items.statement: Targets double-digit EBITDA margin (excl. other income) by H2 FY26
items.quote: I think maybe in the second half of this financial year.

items.statement: Expects FY26 EBITDA to grow ~30% YoY in absolute terms
items.quote: Overall 30% increase in the EBITDA. If you see as an absolute number, last year, we did around INR257 crores. So 30% around over and above that, we should do a year as a whole in this year.

items.statement: Expects FY27 EBITDA to grow ~30% YoY over FY26, potentially more
items.quote: Because we are adding capacity, we are also -- will be having power also, all these projects, which we are doing will be on stream. So we could have much better than 30%.

items.statement: Yarn capacity expansion of ~48-49k tons (POY 19,800, DTY 14,400, FDY 28,800 tpa) at Dahej for ~INR235 cr, operational by Aug 2026, adding ~INR70 cr annual EBITDA
items.quote: additional yarn capacities at Dahej plant, POY capacity of 19,800 metric tons per annum, DTY capacity of 14,400 metric tons per annum. FDY capacity has been doubled from what was initially planned. FDY capacity addition will be now 28,800 metric tons per annum instead of 14,400. FDY market is gaining ground in domestic market. The capacity addition envisages a capital expenditure of around INR235

items.statement: Funding: Recycling INR200 cr term loan + INR100 cr equity; Yarn expansion INR125-126 cr ECB + internal accruals; Steam & Torrent from internal accruals
items.quote: Recycle project, we are taking a term loan of INR200 crores, INR100 crores will be infused as equity from the parent company. And the INR235 crores, we will be taking a ECB of around INR125 crores, INR126 crores. Balance will be internal accrual. And rest of the other 2, it will be all under internal accruals.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 margins better than Q1 FY25 and Q4 FY25 despite some inventory loss from crude drop
items.quote: Q1 margins are good, but there was some reduction in the raw material drastic when the crude has fell from $75 to $65. So there could be some inventory loss. But overall, we should be better than Q1 of last year, much better than Q1 of last year

items.statement: FDY capacity doubled to 28,800 tpa as FDY gaining ground in domestic market
items.quote: FDY market is gaining ground in domestic market. The capacity addition envisages a capital expenditure of around INR235 crores. This additional capacity will be operational by August 2026 and will give it additional EBITDA of around INR70 crores annually.

items.statement: Chinese PTA cost advantage ~$100/ton; local PTA capacity additions (IOC, GAIL by CY25, Reliance 3.2mt by mid-2027) expected to reduce gap
items.quote: Mainly because of PTA, which is short supply in India, and they have abundance of PTA rather they export a lot of PTA. So their cost and we have to pay a price, which includes transfer to the port, freight, clearance charges, everything. All that comes to around $100. That is what we pay extra over and above what the local in China gets the

items.statement: Minimum import price of $3.5/kg on 9+4 HS codes for knitted fabric reducing imports and boosting domestic yarn demand
items.quote: There was an import of a lot of knitted fabric from China at very low prices, which are below the cost prices. So there the government has put $3.5 as the minimum price. So after that, there is a good demand in the knitted fabrics in India. And that's why the demand for yarn is going up.

items.statement: Recycled polyester yarn sells at INR35-40/kg premium over virgin; pilot operational, commercial plant construction started
items.quote: Yes, recycled yarns are being sold right now also at a higher price than the virgin. The price difference is roughly INR35, INR40 would be than virgin.

items.statement: Stopping guidance for now; will use FY26 to build strength, predictability and stability across portfolio
items.quote: we will be stopping guidance for now. Given the current macro environment, we believe it is prudent to utilize FY26 to build strength, predictability and stability across our portfolio.

items.statement: Margin target recalibrated to stabilizing at 15% over next 24 months from earlier 16% in 12 months
items.quote: previously, we said that we will touch 16% sometime in the next 12 months. That's what we said in January. But we may have to recalibrate this to touching and even staying steady at 15% over the next 24 months.

items.statement: Q4 revenue lower than expected due to macro uncertainties in last 2 months; softer start to Q1 expected
items.quote: This Q4 revenue was lower than the previous expectation, given the rapidly evolving macro situation, which impacted the revenue portfolio and profile, especially in the last 2 months of the quarter.

items.statement: Six large deals won in Q4, two from aerospace and two from communications; three from top 10 clients
items.quote: of the 6 large deals we won in Q4, two were from aerospace and two were in communications.

items.statement: Sustainability vertical split into utilities, energy, and mining & minerals for agility; GCC-focused BU created
items.quote: We also took a decision to break up sustainability vertical into its constituents, which are utilities, energy and mining and minerals.

items.statement: Capex reduced from ~3% of revenue; strong cash generation to continue
items.quote: we also did a lot of work in terms of reducing our capex spend, which at one point is almost 3% of our revenue.

items.statement: Board reviewing dividend policy to ensure cash available for growth investments including M&A and semiconductor business
items.quote: The Board also has taken a decision to review the dividend policy to make sure that we are investing and have enough cash available to support growth.

items.statement: Macro uncertainty causing pause in decision-making; March softer than anticipated; impact expected in Q1 but not structural
items.quote: March was softer than what we anticipated, given some of the global uncertainties that are going on. We do not see any significant challenge because of this.

items.statement: Healthcare and automotive segments showing momentum entering FY26; connectivity and new growth areas impacted in March
items.quote: We definitely have some of the areas which has grown healthily in th e last year. I'll call out health care as one of them. So definitely, it's an area where we have seen momentum. We have seen growth in some of the other segments as well like automotive

items.statement: Cyient Semiconductor Private Limited carved out as separate segment from Q1 FY26; Suman Narayan appointed CEO
items.quote: we have recently concluded the carve-out of a subsidiary, CSPL, Cyient Semiconductor Private Limited. And as previously communicated, CSPL financials will be reported as a separate segment starting Q1 FY26 onwards.

items.statement: DET EBIT margin 13% in Q4 FY25, down 48 bps QoQ; FY25 margin 13.5%, down 261 bps YoY
items.quote: The DET EBIT margin for Q4 FY25 stood at 13% down by 48 bps quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Guidance stop is temporary; will resume when Sukamal has full handle on business and forecasting
items.quote: So the guidance stopping we are doing is temporary. We will come back as to when we are going to release that guidance.

items.statement: No structural change in top 5 clients; top 5 grew 4.5% YoY and top 10 grew 9% YoY in FY25
items.quote: the top 5 customers grew by 4.5% year-on-year for us, and the top 10 clients grew by about 9% year-on-year for us.

items.statement: Green hydrogen project win in Norway for marine transportation; meaningful for energy business, ramp-up in progress
items.quote: it will be significant for the energy business, and the ramp-up is in the process of happening. And we're already seeing some -- we're seeing the first of the revenues that we'll continue to see that over the quarters.

items.statement: DET now long-term debt-free; highest ever cash position at $157M and FCF of INR800 crores in FY25
items.quote: At the end of FY25, our cash position is the highest ever we've had at $157 million for DET and the FCF for DET was INR800 crores, up by INR45 crores year-on-year.

items.statement: Wage hikes planned for FY26; focused investments in technology and sales to support growth strategy
items.quote: we intend to continue with wage hikes to our colleagues and associates, which is what we will do in F Y26. The third thing I'll say is that we'll be a lot more prudent and focused on investments we will make in the current year towards outcomes

items.statement: NIM expected to hold at current level if rate cuts are delayed; further repo cuts will hurt margins
items.quote: To the current level of margins, yes.

items.statement: NIM stabilized at 3.29% in Q4 FY25 after five quarters of decline; one basis point drop despite 25 bps repo cut
items.quote: The NIM for this quarter comes in at 3.29 as compared to 3.3 for the previous quarter. And during Q4, repo rate cut of 25 bps happened from 6.50, we lowered it down to 6.25. Despite that, we have had the impact. It's not a full impact, but the impact on the book has been about one basis point so far.

items.statement: Savings account rate cut to 1.5% on lower bucket; bulk deposit rates cut sharply; retail term deposit cuts ongoing with 12-15 month lag benefit
items.quote: We have already made rate cuts on our savings account. Otherwise, why would the NIM fall only by one basis point in quarter four? There's some immunization actions that we've already taken. Will we continue to drop the savings account rate just to accommodate any future repo rate cuts? Very unlikely. But what has happened is that we have reduced our non-callable retail rates, the bulk term deposit

items.statement: Co-lending growth to match balance sheet growth (not exceed); organic high-yield products (LAP over home loans) to drive incremental growth
items.quote: The percentage growth of co-lending based products where the yield is slightly subdued will be actually on par with the balance sheet, whereas we could have the organic book growth contributing significantly more than what has been contributing till this time. So there is a product mix in terms of organic versus inorganic, and also within organic, higher yield products is where we are focusing upo

items.statement: Mortgage mix shifting from home loans to LAP; LAP yields 150-250 bps higher; journey started five quarters ago and showing results
items.quote: The second product exchange is that there is a needle movement from home loan to LAP. Mortgage is the largest book. Incremental sourcing of home loans is less and of business loans is higher. Business loans will give you anywhere between 150 to 250 basis points higher yield. So that's a journey we started about five quarters back. We're seeing the results of it now.

items.statement: PMAY 2.0 seen as major growth driver; max rate 11.5% matches current yield; 5-year subsidy lock-in reduces delinquency; sweet spot at Rs 25 lakh ticket size
items.quote: We're very happy with it for multiple reasons. One is that the max interest rate on that is 11.5%, which if you were to look at it is almost on par with the yield and advances that we're currently getting at 11.54%. Secondly, the book stays with you, the c ustomer stays with you for at least five years is guaranteed. Thirdly, the incentive for the customer to remain current, non - delinquent is ve

items.statement: Core fee income hit record Rs 161 cr in Q4; five-quarter rising trend (118, 114, 139, 141, 161); driven by third-party distribution, overdraft engagement, penal charges replacement
items.quote: let me take you thro ugh the last five quarters of core fee income growth, starting from March ’ 24. Rs.118 crores, Rs.114 crores, Rs.139 crores, Rs.141 crores, Rs.161 crores. Last three quarters have been our highest ever and the next quarter has been kind of eclipsing the previous quarter

items.statement: MFI portfolio small; no improvement seen; accelerated provisions taken; gross NPA 2.99%, net NPA 1.12%, PCR 74.48%
items.quote: Honestly, I don't see any improvement. At least our portfolio, there is no improvement. It's a small portfolio, so we are okay with it. We have taken accelerated provisions on it, b ut I don't see any improvement

items.statement: Technology spend on core banking (Finacle, FinOne, treasury), cybersecurity (SIEM), customer-facing digital (paperless onboarding, MFI digital journey, RPA, GenAI); employee count reduced to 11,057
items.quote: We have upgraded our core banking system, Finacle a year before last. Last year, we upgraded our instalment letting program FinOne. It's the state-of-the-art, one which we have implemented now. Third item is our treasury management system. TCS, we upgraded it in June of last year. We have totally 4 core banking systems, 3 of them are up and running.

items.statement: Cost to average assets at 2.54% in Q4; target 2.5%; Q1 typically nadir for cost-to-income; trend suggests further improvement
items.quote: Cost to average assets for the quarter has come at about 2.54%. The go-to which we have spoken about albeit in a yearly sense is about 2.5%. So these are within touching distance of where we want to be.

items.statement: Capital raise likely in Q2 FY26; paperwork done; Tier 1 at 14.3%, total CRAR 16.77%; 23 bps capital consumed for 24.7% loan growth
items.quote: we are looking at quarter 2 for that incremental money to come in. But what is more heartening is that, look, any business which can grow by 25 % with 23 bps usage of capital, I think that is a fairly eff icient capital efficient model

items.statement: Provision cost at 33 bps for Q4, 31 bps for FY25; well below 45-55 bps model; supports ROA path despite NIM pressure
items.quote: We are closing this year with close to 31 bps of credit cost and the quarter with about 33 bps of credit cost. So even in an environment where MFI loans that the bank has is going through its problems, we cannot deny that. But the fact is, despite taking accelerated provisions, the overall provision number is healthy at 33 bps for the quarter.

items.statement: Overdraft-focused strategy for SME lending creates moat vs NBFCs; improves engagement, cross-sell, fee income, loan life, reduces attrition
items.quote: We are really going big time on business loans, which are of an overdraft nature. Customers are liking it. They are benefiting from it more importantly. And if we continue on this journey at a similar kind of growth rates over the next few quarters, maybe even years, we will find that as matters stand, the relative white space that we have would continue.

items.statement: Gold loan organic book unchanged post RBI circular; co-lending draft guidelines awaited; no change to current practices
items.quote: Absolutely no change. Whatever was mentioned in some form or the other or perhaps even higher, we are - for organic book, okay, I'm not talking about co-lending at all. I hope you're not referring to co-lending guidelines. On the gold loan proposals, we are on our organic own book. It's pretty much the same.

items.statement: Loan growth 25%, deposit growth 22% in FY25; savings account growth 19%; top 20 deposit concentration down to 6.61%
items.quote: In continuation of the trend of growth momentum, we have seen a balance sheet growth of 22% for the year. Deposit growth was a healthy 22% and the loans growth was 25%.

items.statement: Treasury gains benefited from rate cut environment; core fee income focus remains; treasury gains welcome but not primary driver
items.quote: Usually, when you are in a rate cut environment, NIMs suffer and you make gains on your investment usually. So I'm sure treasury has done a reasonably good job, but the environment has also been favorable. So while you take the stick on the NIM compression, there is some benefit you get on the investment piece as well.

items.statement: Enterprise gross margin target range is 25% to 27%.
items.quote: I think between 25% to 27% gross margin is a narrow band that we have been operating in the last couple of quarters. While we do not guide, but I would say those are the range or range that we want to operate at.

items.statement: SMS pricing pressure has bottomed out; any price increase will help top line and gross margins.
items.quote: I believe that hopefully, have bottom ed out from a pricing perspective and any upside that we get from a price increase would only help both to p line and gross

items.statement: Signed RCS MaaP platform deal with two large telcos outside India; revenue contribution expected from end of Q1 FY26.
items.quote: We have signed a deal to deploy RCS platform with two of the large telcos outside India. So, it's the first large win for us, which is in outside India. So, you should start seeing the contribution of that by end of Q1 onwards as the things ramps up.

items.statement: ILD SMS revenue is now sub-10% of total revenue and not a material headwind for FY26.
items.quote: From an ILD questio n perspective, it continues to be weak. But I think within our portfolio now, it is sub 10%. It is not material enough for us to materially worry for us in a future projection perspective

items.statement: Free cash flow for FY25 was 101% of PAT; Q3-Q4 average free cash flow >150% of PAT.
items.quote: Our free cash flow for the full year was 101% of the PAT and last Q3, Q4 has been on an average more than 150% of the PAT.

items.statement: No formal guidance given; management says exiting FY25 on a high note with Q4 growth of 2%+ and expects tailwind into FY26.
items.quote: We are exiting the year with a very good note, right? If you see from last number of four, five quarters, we have not grown. In Q4, we have grown 2% plus. So, we will have a tailwind from a Q4 growth perspective.

items.statement: WhatsApp utility message pricing in India aligned with SMS rates (~₹0.11); marketing message pricing ~₹0.70-0.75.
items.quote: So, if you look at it here in India, SMS prices are in the range of ₹0.9 to ₹0.11. So, they kept their utility prices at around ₹0.11 and marketing messages, they have kept at around ₹0.70, ₹0.75 paisa.

items.statement: Platform business targets each platform to reach ₹100 crore ARR over 4-8 quarters.
items.quote: Our aspiration is that each of the platform that we work on over four to six quarters or eight quarters, depending on the life cycle and the use case goes to ₹100 CR ARR is the wish list of the ambition that we have put for ourselves.

items.statement: Meta may slightly change utility message pricing; no major impact expected.
items.quote: The only change we foresee what we are getting hints from Meta is that there could be a slight maybe change in the way they charge for the utility messages, but nothing major impact over here.

items.statement: Signed and gone live with largest NBFC, largest gaming company, largest bank, and number two PSU bank on WhatsApp/RCS.
items.quote: We have signed and gone live with one of the largest NBFC in the country. We have gone live with the largest gaming company in the country on WhatsApp as well as on RCS. We have signed the largest bank on WhatsApp and currently the integration is going on.

items.statement: Plan to start charging for services on OTT channels in FY26 to improve revenues and margins.
items.quote: In nutshell we are going to start charging for our services as well to these customers this year and we would see that our OTT revenues would definitely go up and our number of customers will go up on these channels and our margins will also Improve.

items.statement: M&A strategy: selective, culturally aligned assets to accelerate growth; no rush to deploy cash.
items.quote: We continue to look out for the assets. We do not want to rush. But whenever we believe that there are the right assets, which will help grow us faster, which will fit with us from a cultural perspective, I think we will not shy away from making those investments.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance for FY26 is 11-12%
items.quote: next year I think we should be better than that, maybe between 11% - 12%.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance for FY26 is around 27%
items.quote: Going forward, I think, since we have to make a lot of investment in newer geography, newer talent and some digital initiatives and so on and so forth , so around 27% kind of margins we are looking or we are confident to maintain.

items.statement: Maintenance capex for FY26 expected at Rs. 60-70 crore
items.quote: Normally our maintenance CAPEX is about Rs. 60 – Rs. 70 crore a year. And I believe in next year, FY26, similar kind of CAPEX will be there.

items.statement: Specialized tests contribute about one-fifth of portfolio
items.quote: the specialized portfolio is something which each company would be defining differently. But the way we define our specialized portfolio; it is about one -fifth of our portfolio comes from the specialized test.

items.statement: Tier-3 and Tier-4 revenue grew mid-teens in FY25
items.quote: We have had a good growth in our Tier-3 revenues even in this year. We had a healthy, mid-teens kind of growth.

items.statement: No price hike taken in FY25; pricing in Tier-3/4 similar to Tier-1/2
items.quote: Our pricing approach in Tier-3, Tier-4 is not really different compared to whatever are the contiguous Tier-2 or Tier-1 markets. Our pricing is similar, it's not essentially lower pricing on an MRP basis.

items.statement: Reagent supply from China is negligible (<1%)
items.quote: In pathology diagnostics, no reagent in our case comes from China. None.

items.statement: Lab expansion tempo of 15-20 labs per year to continue for FY26 and FY27
items.quote: We have added 18 new testing labs last financial year. And for this financial year and maybe one more, we definitely would like to keep up the tempo at this pace.

items.statement: Collection network maturation takes 18-36 months
items.quote: It could be anything between 18-36 months that would take for the collection network or a new collection center and a lab network to really start maturing and contributing significantly to the volume and the revenue numbers.

items.statement: Cash of Rs. 1,229 crore kept for inorganic opportunities in South/West
items.quote: we are keeping this cash with us for any opportunity which will emerge and as earlier mentioned , I mean, obviously we are growing organically and we have started our own efforts in South, particularly South and West, but if there is any opportunity there, definitely we will be keen to do that opportunity.

items.statement: Suburban integration impacted Q4 revenue; recovery expected in 1-2 quarters
items.quote: We did the whole IT stack changeover in Suburban in Q4 and also the voluntary liquidation process was carried out in Q4. So, because of that, there has been a bit of an impact in terms of the revenue for Suburban in Q4. And we have already started recovering and we believe that we should be able to recover quickly in the next 1-2 quarters.

items.statement: Radiology revenue less than 5% of total; high-end radiology not a current focus
items.quote: Our revenue from radiology is actually miniscule. It is very low single digits. I mean, it is all pathology revenue only.

items.statement: Management targets double-digit EBITDA margins in the next 7 to 8 quarters.
items.quote: We are confident that in the next 7 to 8 quarters, we will be closer to our aspiration of double-digit margins.

items.statement: Gross margin improved 67 bps YoY to 31.4% in Q4 FY25, sustained in 31-33% range.
items.quote: Our gross margin for this quarter improved by 67 basis points to 31.4%.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expanded 385 bps YoY to 7.8% in Q4 FY25.
items.quote: Our EBITDA margin was at 7.8%, an improvement of 385 basis points.

items.statement: Hyderabad facility scaled up, now producing 50% of TPW fan output with 40% capacity enhancement.
items.quote: Operations in Hyderabad have scaled up and have strengthened our capabilities and market presence. We are now getting 50% of our TPW fan production from Hyderabad, improving our manufacturing scale and efficiency.

items.statement: BLDC fans grew over 50% YoY in Q4 and over 30% for full year; BLDC contribution reached ~20% of ceiling fans.
items.quote: BLDC has grown over 50% year-on-year this quarter and over 30% on a full year basis, with our overall NPDs in fans category now contributing almost 20%.

items.statement: Premium fans contribution at 30%+ vs industry ~20%; aspiration to reach 40%+ in next few years.
items.quote: Premium, the industry would be somewhere around 20%, 21% or closer to 20%. We are at about 30%+ on premium contributing to it. Our aspiration is to take it to 40% and above in the next few years.

items.statement: Channel filling for summer products underway in March; exit trends better; optimistic on Q1 with strong IMD summer forecast.
items.quote: March, however, recorded a better exit trend, particularly for summer products like fans, with channel filling currently underway for most brands across the industry.

items.statement: Air coolers grew ~33% YoY in Q4 and ~37% for full year FY25.
items.quote: Air coolers saw a robu st growth of almost 33% in Q4 and about 37% for the full year basis

items.statement: B2B lighting order pipeline stronger; B2B lighting grew over 20% for full year FY25.
items.quote: We have successfully delivered marquee projects in th e B2B lighting segment with an even stronger pipeline of orders, resulting in our B2B business growing by over 20% on a full year

items.statement: Commodity prices (copper, aluminum) rose Feb-Mar but softening now; unpredictable due to tariff wars.
items.quote: Moreover, the quarter experienced fluctuations in key commodities such as copper and aluminum with prices rising through February and March. However, it is softening now, but very much unpredictable given the current tariff wars.

items.statement: RoHS compliance effective April 1 increased costs; industry expected to pass on to consumers.
items.quote: One big change is the RoHS compliance, which has increased the cost -- and hopefully, I think the industry will pass it on to the consumers.

items.statement: Project Sanchay delivered INR 75 crores cost savings in FY25.
items.quote: This has helped us in witnessing a cost saving of INR75 crores for the financial year '25.

items.statement: DTM expanded to 11 states (added Kolkata/West Bengal); DTM revenues grew high double-digit in Q4 and FY25.
items.quote: We have expanded our DTM coverage in Kolkata, thereby completing our full presence in West Bengal and taking our total DTM states to 11 as we speak by end of Q4. Our revenues from DTM states grew high double digit for this quarter and for the full year.

items.statement: B2C lighting registered high double-digit volume growth for FY25; lighting is fastest-growing segment.
items.quote: Our B2C lighting business has registered a high double-digit volume growth for the year.

items.statement: Pricing headwinds persisted across most categories compressing margins, except cables and wires.
items.quote: Pricing headwinds for the industry persisted across most categories, compressing margins, except for cables and wires segment.

items.statement: Revenue INR 862 crores in Q4 (+9.4% YoY, +5.5% QoQ); FY25 revenue INR 3,094 crores (+10% YoY).
items.quote: We concluded quarter 4 with a revenue of INR862 crores, reflecting a 9.4% year-on-year increase and a 5.5% sequential growth. For the full year, our top line reached INR3,094 crores, demonstrating a robust 10% growth compared to the previous year.

items.statement: FY26 AUM growth estimated at 24-25% aided by new business lines
items.quote: The AUM growth estimates of AUM remain at 24 to 25% aided by new lines of businesses launched in last two to three years.

items.statement: FY26 NIM expected to remain stable with cost of funds declining 10-15 bps
items.quote: Cost of fund is estimated to go down by 10 to 15 bps in FY26. Overall we estimate NIM to remain stable in FY26.

items.statement: FY26 fee income growth estimated at 13-15% after moderating fees and stopping co-branded cards
items.quote: The company has moderated its fees and charges and stopped its co-branded card business. The company estimates its fee and charges to grow by 13 to 15% in FY26.

items.statement: FY26 OPEX to NTI estimated to improve by 40-50 bps from current level
items.quote: OPEX to NTI is estimated to improve by 40 to 50 bps from our current level, and some of that we are talking about our AI progress.

items.statement: FY26 credit cost estimated at 1.85-1.95% of average AUM
items.quote: Our credit costs for FY26, the company estimates the loan loss to average AUF in the corridor of 185 to 195.

items.statement: FY26 ROA estimated at 4.4-4.6% and ROE at 19-20%
items.quote: Return on asset is estimated to be in the range of 4.4 to 4.6. Return on equity given excess capital, ROE metric is estimated to be between 19 to 20% for FY26.

items.statement: FY26 customer franchise addition target of 14-16 million
items.quote: The customer franchise we remain confident to add 14 to 16 million customers in FY26.

items.statement: Long-term ROA guidance widened to 4.3-4.7% from 4.6-4.8%
items.quote: The only change you principally see here is return on assets, which used to be 4.6 to 4.8%. We're creating a little wider ROE range of 4.3 to 4.7%.

items.statement: Long-term ROE guidance lowered to 19-21% from 21-23% due to surplus capital
items.quote: ROE from a long-term guidance standpoint, pre-COVID were 19 to 21. We went up from 21 to 23 and we think this is one of the last remaining residues of COVID that we think, on a long-term basis, will compound between 19 and 21%.

items.statement: Invested 65 crores for 12% stake in cybersecurity firm Protectt.ai
items.quote: In the fourth quarter, in the quarter gone by took a 12% stake in a company called Protectt.ai investing 65 crores.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 cost of funds at 7.99%, up 3 bps; expect gradual decline to 7.75-7.85% by end FY26
items.quote: Cost of funds came in at 7.99, a marginal increase of three basis points. Overall from a direction standpoint, we expect cost of funds to gradually go down to 7.75 to 7.85 by end of FY26.

items.statement: Opened 137 standalone Gold Loan branches and 30 MFI branches in Q4; total Gold Loan branches 964, MFI branches 333
items.quote: The company opened 137 standalone Gold Loan branches in the quarter that went by and added 30 MFI branches. Overall, Gold Loan branches are now 964 and MFI branches are now 333.

items.statement: Additional ECL provision of 359 crores taken in Q4 for annual model redevelopment, primarily in stage 1 assets
items.quote: Given the higher flow-forward rates that we've actually seen through the year and elevated rate costs in the last three quarters, the redevelopment of the ECL model resulted in an additional ECL provision of 359 crores. And primarily, rather mostly, in stage 1 assets.

items.statement: Credit cost missed FY25 guidance at 2.07% vs 1.75-1.85% target; optimistic on FY26 improvement
items.quote: Credit cost was a clear miss as per our assessment. The company took significant credit action through FY25 and is optimistic about its impact for P&L FY26.

items.statement: Rural B2C business recovering; early vintage metrics (3/6/9 MOB) improving to pre-COVID or better levels
items.quote: The early vintage 3 MOB 6 MOB in rural B2C is improving. As Sandeep spoke about, even the ECL that is also clearly calling out, we remain very confident from here to grow the rural B2C business.

items.statement: Expect 11-15% top-line growth excluding ethanol; overall double-digit growth including ethanol
items.quote: So we expect a growth of around about, say, 11% to 15% in the top line and apart from ethanol. And in the margin guideline also, it will be on the similar lines or slightly higher.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected around 11-13% for FY26
items.quote: It will be similar on the similar lines around 11% to 13%.

items.statement: Planned capex of INR100 crore for FY26 primarily for malt plant maturation facility and operational efficiencies
items.quote: For FY '26, we have planned a capex of around INR100 crores, primarily to set up a maturation facility for the malt plant and undertaking other operational efficiencies improvements.

items.statement: Proprietary IMFL EBITDA margin sustainable at 15-18%; premium share currently 10-15% of proprietary IMFL revenue

items.statement: INR14,000 crores of loans won or sanctioned in current calendar year including April
items.quote: In this calendar year, including the month of April, we have already done more than INR14,000 crores of loans.

items.statement: INR14,000 crores cumulative sanctions from non-IR railway ecosystem since Q4 FY25
items.quote: the numbers we have already flagged. In fact, it is flagged by the Government of India also that w e have already mopped up INR14,000 crores as of

items.statement: Total addressable market of INR2.5 lakh crores including metro railways within MOA mandate
items.quote: the whole business is around INR2.5 lakh crores, including the metro railway.

items.statement: Diversified from single client Indian Railways to multiple railway ecosystem clients with backward/forward linkages
items.quote: We are only limiting ourselves to the MOA, which gives me the legroom for giving loans to anything which is having backward or forward linkages to the railways.

items.statement: Earning 2x to 3x margins on new railway ecosystem loans compared to Indian Railways lending
items.quote: We are becoming lowest in this beating all banks and NBFCs and still making margins of 2x to 3x to what we used to get from Indian Railways.

items.statement: Expect most of INR14,000 crores sanctioned loans to be disbursed in FY26 despite 2-year period
items.quote: we expect that most of the disbursement will be done in this FY itself.

items.statement: AUM rundown of ~INR10,000 crores per annum from 15-year Indian Railways loan maturities
items.quote: the 15th year, to be precise, if it is 2025, then 2010 loan will come out to be going out of my books, which is in terms of INR10,000 crores per annum.

items.statement: Operating cost less than 0.1% with high capital adequacy and quick turnaround as competitive advantages
items.quote: You must have seen our operating cost is one of the lowest in the industry, about 0.1 -- we don't have 0.1%, even less than 0.1%.

items.statement: Aim to improve SSSG and SCSG and achieve positive SSSG in FY26
items.quote: For FY26, our aim is to improve our SSSG and SCSG (1:50) and achieve positive SSSG in FY26.

items.statement: CAPEX for new concept pilot at Rs.2,000-2,500 per square feet for additional space
items.quote: So for example if I am having a store which is 1,500 square feet and currently I am using 600 square feet for bottom-wear, the balance 900 square feet is where the CAPEX is not done, I will be incurring say Rs.2,000 to Rs.2,500 per SFT for the additional 900 square feet.

items.statement: Mapped out and finalized over 30 stores for Q1 FY26
items.quote: We have already mapped out and finalized over 30 stores in Q1 FY26 ensuring that we are well positioned for a strong start of the year.

items.statement: Gross margin target range of 62-63% for FY26
items.quote: From a gross margin perspective, I see our gross margins maybe in the range of 62% to 63% or maybe a little higher, but. I think maintaining gross margins and maintaining P&L margins will be our endeavor in FY26.

items.statement: New category pricing targeted between Rs.800-1,800
items.quote: So the pricing also what we are targeting for this is going to be between Rs.800 and Rs.1,800.

items.statement: April SSSG flattish, expecting improvement in May and June
items.quote: From what I see April SSSG has been flattish. So, we are expecting May and June to be good, but April has been a little slow.

items.statement: Pilot of 15 stores in H1 and 10 stores in H2 FY26 for new women's topwear and men's casual categories
items.quote: We would be looking to have 15-stores of this new concept in the first six months phase and 10 stores in the second six months' phase.

items.statement: Full price sales ratio for new categories unknown, will be determined after pilot
items.quote: Even I don't visualize that the full price sales ratio will be more than 95. It might be for all you know. But today as of now, I don't know what will be the full price sales ratio.

items.statement: Target net addition of 120 stores annually starting FY26
items.quote: With these closures done, we aspire to do an addition on a net basis 120 stores annually, starting FY26.

items.statement: Conservative estimate of 100 gross LFS store additions in FY26
items.quote: On a conservative basis, I would say about 100 stores we should be adding in FY26. 100 stores is more from a gross perspective.

items.statement: No separate warehouse CAPEX needed for pilot, existing Tirupur warehouse extended and well equipped
items.quote: Prerna, we have been doing in our existing warehouse for some time now. See, we had a 1,00,000 square feet warehouse in Tirupur. There was some space behind which we extended. So that we had extended regardless of this pilot or not. So our current location is well equipped to handle any future growth.

items.statement: Strong free cash flow of Rs.50 crores in FY25 sufficient to fund pilot and store expansion without debt
items.quote: So this year, the business has generated Rs.50 crores of free cash flow, which is much higher than what I would be investing in this pilot. Let me put it that way. So even after doing this pilot, there would still be free cash flow.

items.statement: Early signs of gradual demand improvement at ground level, momentum expected to build
items.quote: We're beginning to see some early signs of gradual improvement in demand at the ground level. Encouraging by the trends, we believe the momentum will continue to build and we expect further strengthening of demand as we move forward.

items.statement: First Middle East store in Dubai Silicon Central Mall expected by May or June end
items.quote: We expect our first store to open either by May end or by the June end marking an exciting milestone in our international expansion. This store is going to be planned to open in Silicon Central Mall in Dubai.

items.statement: Inventory days maintained at 102 days, target to optimize to 90-95 days
items.quote: Usually our inventory spikes a little bit in March because of summer season, but through the year, we target inventory days between 90 days and 95 days.

items.statement: Combined ratio on NEP basis improved 1.4% YoY to 110.8% for FY25; Q4 FY25 NEP combined ratio 110% vs 110.9% in Q4 FY24.
items.quote: When we see this for '24-'25, this combined ratio would be 110.8. So basically, you can see, there is an improvement of 1.4% on the combined ratio. On a quarter-by-quarter basis, the combined ratio in Q4 F '24 on a NEP basis would be 110.9%, while in Q4 FY '25 the combined ratio is 110 %, an improvement of 0.9%.

items.statement: IRDA combined ratio (with 1/n) for FY25 was 109.3% vs 108.7% in FY24; Q4 FY25 111.3%.
items.quote: Combined ratio, including 1/n is 109.3% for the year and Q4 is 111.3%. And compared to the full Financial Year last year it was 108.7%.

items.statement: PAT more than doubled to Rs 425 crore for FY25; Q4 PAT Rs 116 crore vs Rs 53 crore in Q4 FY24.
items.quote: Overall profit for the year increased to Rs. 425 crore, for the quarter Rs. 116 crores, ROE in the 4th Quarter is 3.5%, for the entire year it is about 13%.

items.statement: No realized equity capital gains in FY25; booked a capital loss of Rs 3.4 crore.
items.quote: In the case of Digit, if we look at in our entire year, which is the whole Financial Year '24-'25, we actually have no capital gains. In fact, we have a capital loss of Rs. 3.4 crores.

items.statement: GWP without 1/n grew 15.6% YoY in FY25 (with 1/n: 14%); Q4 FY25 GWP growth 13.5%. Industry GWP growth ~6% in FY25.
items.quote: If you look at GWP for the entire year, without 1/n, our growth rate would be 15.6%, with 1/n growth rate for the year is 14%. And for the quarter, the growth rate is 13.5%.

items.statement: Motor TP market share stable at 5.92% in FY25 vs 5.96% in FY24.
items.quote: In TP, as I already mentioned, the market share last year for the whole year was 5.96%. This year, the market share is 5.92%.

items.statement: Expect industry growth 3-4% higher in FY26 vs FY25 due to fire rate hikes from Jan/Feb and anticipated TP rate increase.
items.quote: I would still expect the growth rate of the industry to be about 3 % to 4% higher compared to last year.

items.statement: Group Health April 1 renewals saw very high competition; smaller policies later in April showed some pricing improvement.
items.quote: What I am hearing is that on April 1 when the big renewals were due, we have actually seen, I would say, that we have seen very high competition on April 1. But I think the smaller policies which were due now, say, during the month, not exactly on 1st of April, there I would say we have seen some improvement in the pricing.

items.statement: Equity allocation increased from 2.9% (Dec 31) to 6.4% (Mar 31); target up to 10% of assets.
items.quote: As of December 31st, if you see the note below, the bottom most line, our equity allocation was only 2.9% , and as of 31st March equity allocation has actually now moved to 6.4%.

items.statement: Non-Motor proportion increasing year-on-year for last 4-5 years; Motor mix: cars ~40-42%, two-wheelers ~30%, commercial vehicles ~30%.
items.quote: Our mix in the last four or five years in terms of Motor and non-Motor has actually been moving anyway more and more towards non-Motor.

items.statement: Reserving robust: whole account and TP triangles show adequate reserves every year; only Rs 60 lakh adverse development from one old TP claim.
items.quote: Again, I think to refresh memory, first year the earned premium was very small. We had got one large claim where, I believe, the claim amount was close to was Rs. 4.5 crores or Rs. 5 crores. The claim is still not settled. So overall, if you actually look at , the reserves have come down, but we still have a small Rs. 60 lakh of unfavorable development coming in only from one claim.

items.statement: Fire gross loss ratio improved to 56.8% in FY25 from 84% in FY24 (which had 5 nat-cat events); net loss ratio volatile due to small net retention.
items.quote: This year, the loss ratio , on a gross basis , is only 56.8%. So , just wanted to bring across the overall profitability of this commercial line of business is driven more around gross loss ratios.

items.statement: Expense of management (EOM) ratio reduced to 33.4% (without 1/n) in FY25 from 36.3% in FY24, a ~2.9% improvement; with 1/n EOM 33.9%.
items.quote: Last year, as per EOM, our expense ratio was 36.3%. This year, on the same basis, that is without 1/n, our expense ratio is reduced to 33.4 %. So there is a reduction of 2.9% on the overall expenses for the whole year.

items.statement: Expect IRDA to take corrective action to reduce retail commissions as EOM guidelines intended; most peers saw EOM increase in FY25.
items.quote: However, in reality, since in both '23-'24 and '24-'25 commissions actually went up. Now , IRDA obviously would be very serious about this, and this is my personal opinion, that I would expect IRDA to take some corrective actions on EOM so that they can actually achi eve the objective of lower commissions.

items.statement: No formal guidance given; management expects TP rate hike (timing uncertain), fire rate hikes already visible, and private car renewal book maturity to aid profitability over next 3-5 years.
items.quote: We would also expect some increase in the third-party premium rates. We would not hazard a guess whether this would happen from July or September, but there should be some increase in the third-party rates.

items.statement: Management will not give specific guidance on SSSG or store openings for FY26, but expects store openings to be in the same ballpark as FY25 (90 stores).
items.quote: In FY '26, I would not give any specific guidance, Vivek, if you can understand that. But we will be in the same ballpark.

items.statement: Store expansion opportunity includes 17 virgin towns above 1 million population and 800+ stores in smaller towns, with logical focus on Tier-2/3.
items.quote: So. the total opportunity in the smaller towns is 800 , in the larger towns its 300 to 400. So. I guess it will be logically more in the Tier-2, Tier-3 towns.

items.statement: Gross margin improved 80 bps YoY driven by sourcing leverage, private label mix increase (135 bps), and customer shift to higher price points.
items.quote: The first and the obvious one is that our business is growing well , resulting in greater leverage with us in terms of sourcing and buying. So that's an important component of what's led to that margin improvement. Secondly, as I mentioned slightly earlier, and you also alluded to that, the private label contribution has gone up by 135 bps over last year and that has also contributed to improvemen

items.statement: Not reducing private label discount to national brands yet; focus remains on driving category penetration and affordability.
items.quote: Not immediately as yet, because you see , there are two factors which go into the pricing of private brands. One of course is , as you mentioned, the discount over the market leaders and so on. Secondly, our goal is also to drive penetration in these categories which still have no penetration . And one element of pricing is completely focused on seeing what is the price point at which they will be

items.statement: Same store sales growth of 12.3% for FY25 and 13.7% for Q4 FY25 was broad-based across all three categories and all regions (East, North East, South, West) with no significant divergence.
items.quote: Firstly, our same store sales growth, just minor correction, is 12.3% for the full year, for Quarter 4 it is 13.7% (Note: these are adjusted SSSG ). Secondly, our growth across all our three businesses is pretty similar and in the same ballpark. And lastly, you will be happy to know that we have not seen any significant divergences of growth between East, North east, South and West. Of course, the

items.statement: Category mix stable: Clothing 43.9%, General Merchandise 28.2%, FMCG 27.7%. Private label contribution rose to 73.1% (+135 bps YoY).
items.quote: The private brands ' contribution grew to 73.1%, which is a clear 135 bps improvement over the last year. The category mix remain ed broadly the same or similar . Clothing contributes to 43.9% of our business, general merchandise 28.2%; and FMCG 27.7%.

items.statement: Real estate availability in small towns remains a challenge; compliance and build-to-suit models used to mitigate. Labor training is a continuous challenge due to nascent retail industry.
items.quote: The availability of suitable properties, especially as you go into smaller towns becomes lesser and lesser . And therefore, players like us are also open to build-to-suit properties which are specifically made for us because there are no suitable properties available.

items.statement: Quick commerce available at 656 stores across 429 cities; 8.7 million registered users. Contribution 3-5% of store revenue in underserved Tier-2/3 markets, 1.5-2% in saturated metros. Business near cash break-even.
items.quote: Now our quick commerce initiative is available to the customers who live in the catchment of 656 stores across 429 cities in the country . And now registered users on quick commerce have increased to 8.7 million folks around the country.

items.statement: Management aims to maintain current margin levels while growing fast; sourcing benefits may be reinvested for growth sustainability rather than passed on as price cuts.
items.quote: So. our general view on margins is that we wish to continue to grow aggressively. So. therefore, if reinvesting our sourcing benefits, which will become more and more with growth, we would generally speaking first look at the option of reinvesting them to ensure sustainability of growth, if it does make any difference . I n some cases, like you could take the example of clothing , passing on every

items.statement: Store breakeven (payback) typically 18 months, consistent across Tier-2/3 towns which already represent 70% of store base.
items.quote: So, our typical breakeven in 18 months , and even in the smaller towns it is in the same range . Do recognize that 70% of our stores even today, which is let's say more than 450 stores are in Tier-2 and Tier-3 towns.

items.statement: New state expansion (Kerala) proceeding at full speed; Maharashtra and Gujarat pilots launching in next 30-60 days. Margin targets validated before rapid rollout in new states.
items.quote: I am very happy to inform you that we have double digit stores in Kerala now, and we are moving with speed in terms of expansion into Kerala. At the same time, we have also started small pilots which will just be rolled out, I suppose , in the next 30 to 60 days , both in Gujarat and Maharashtra , to learn about that those two markets , b ecause as you know, historically we have not been there.

items.statement: No significant difference in SSSG across Tier-1, Tier-2, Tier-3 towns; all categories growing in same ballpark.
items.quote: Now Jignanshu, fair observation, but we have not seen any significant differences between Tier-1, Tier-2 and Tier-3 in terms of growth, and specifically the same store sales growth, pretty much in the same ballpark across the country. And ye s, I mean, that's been true of all our categories actually.

items.statement: Top private brands: Brink (apparel/GM, >Rs1,000 cr, doubled FY22-25), Home Select (GM, near Rs1,000 cr, >2x growth), Yellow Hippo (kids). Growth expected at similar pace.
items.quote: The number one brand in the Company is a brand called Brink which straddles apparel and general merchandise. So the biggest category under Brink would be T-shirts. And this brand has doubled in terms of its revenue from FY '22 to FY '25. And I think currently it is signi ficantly more than Rs. 1,000 crores in terms of our revenue. The second biggest brand is a brand called Home Select, which is es

items.statement: No specific forward guidance on SSSG, store count, private label share, or category mix; management advises using historical trends to model future.
items.quote: See, again, I would request you to not expect me to comment on specific numbers. My advice would be that the historical trends a re all available on all the things that you have mentioned, the same store sales growth, the category mix, the margin performance, store opening numbers for full year '25 we have made available today. I would repeat that , we opened 90 new stores this year. So , whilst I

items.statement: Kumbh Mela provided temporary positive impact in Allahabad/Varanasi/Lucknow; no adverse impact anywhere; stores in those towns continue double-digit SSSG post-event.
items.quote: So you see, inevitably, there was some positive impact in Allahabad, Varanasi, even Lucknow, etc., all the towns which are in the neighborhood of Allahabad. But it was temporary and , obviously, it's gone now. But they do not see any negative impact in any which way any where in the country.

items.statement: Smaller format store pilot (4-5 stores, ~6 months old) showing good response; cautious expansion pending 30-40 store validation.
items.quote: So. firstly, yes, I will speak about the smaller format. But we started the new store sometime in the last quarter of last year, so currently the earliest store would be probably six months or thereabouts in terms of its aging . And I am, in a qualitative sense, happy to tell you that the response has been good . A nd as we speak, we have four or five of these stores, so we are expanding in the tw

items.statement: Aspiration to achieve double-digit growth or stay ahead of industry segment growth
items.quote: But aspiration still continues to be there that we try and get it to at least a double-digit growth or stay ahead of the industry or the segment growth.

items.statement: Capex for Q1 CY25 was INR 82.5 crores, about half of same period last year
items.quote: And as you can see, for the quarter, we have just invested INR 82.5 crores, which is almost at half the level when compared to the same period last year.

items.statement: Full year capex expected to be slightly above Q1 run rate
items.quote: By end of this year, it will be slightly above the run rate. So, we will be doing slightly more in the coming quarters.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved to 19.3% in Q1 CY25, highest ever registered
items.quote: And I guess, this is the highest EBITDA that we have registered so far, bringing in an EBITDA of INR 407 crores into the system.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin dipped to 18.3% due to KRSV impact
items.quote: At a consolidated level, Schaeffler India, both the companies put together, our revenue stands at INR 2,174 crores with an EBITDA of 18.3%, which is a dip of 1 % because of the impact of KRSV.

items.statement: Export order book for short term is being cautiously monitored but expected to sustain current performance level
items.quote: As of now, the order book is for the short term, we are very cautiously looking at the developments that are happening around the world, but we expect to sustain this level of performance.

items.statement: Strong demand uptick seen in renewable energy (wind), construction equipment, and raw material sectors
items.quote: We definitely have seen some uptick in our business and demand, at least, particularly if you see the renewable energy sector, wherein we play a big role in the wind energy market, we saw a pretty strong demand coming in.

items.statement: Tractor production grew 19% in Q1 CY25 on good monsoon forecast
items.quote: Incidentally, on the forecast of reasonably good monsoons, we are seeing the demand strongly bouncing back and the tractor production went up 19% in the country.

items.statement: Export share of sales increased to 15% in Q1 CY25 from 11-12% previously
items.quote: And then, of course, our export, which was down to around 11%, 12% has gone up to 15% in this quarter.

items.statement: Localization ratio improved to 76% of revenue from own production in India
items.quote: So, whatever we are selling, 76% is manufactured in our 4 plants in India.

items.statement: No impact seen in India from European job cuts or Vitesco merger synergies so far
items.quote: Now, what is happening in the group remains. And I am happy to share that in India, so far, we have not seen any impact due to what is happening in Europe coming in India.

items.statement: Tariff situation fluid; no strategy shift to China-plus-one for India exports to US yet
items.quote: The situation has been very, very fluid that first announcements and then withdrawing that. And also, that currently, U.S. is in talk actively with China on diluting actually the complete tension.

items.statement: Auto bearing portion within Bearings & Industrial Solutions segment is close to 17%
items.quote: If we talk about the segmental mix on bearings, within that, auto bearing is close to 17%.

items.statement: Free cash flow strong at INR 237 crores in Q1 CY25 vs INR 163 crores in Q4 CY24
items.quote: So hence, you will see that our free cash flow also registered a strong numbers at INR 237 crores compared to the preceding quarter, which was INR 163 crores.

items.statement: Working capital target is to bring it down to last year's level
items.quote: This is going to be a focus area for us. And our target and our actions are to try and get it down to last year's level.

items.statement: Housing Finance AUM expected to grow at 20% in FY25, achieved
items.quote: And we had already guided that our AUM is expected to grow at 20% in FY25, and that's what we have achieved in FY25.

items.statement: Housing Finance disbursement run rate will increase further with higher RM base
items.quote: Going forward, with higher RM base, the disbursement run rate will only increase further.

items.statement: AMC market share in net sales expected to continue improving in FY26
items.quote: We are confident that with the current run rate of flows that we've seen in the months of February, March and the early trends in the month of April, our AUM market share could continue to rise in FY26 over the exiting FY25 numbers.

items.statement: Wealth Management distribution revenue share expected to continue inching up
items.quote: And we would like to believe that the share of distribution in the total revenues of this business should continue to inch up like they went up from 11% in FY24 to 19% in FY25.

items.statement: Private Wealth Management expected to contribute larger share of group profitability in coming years
items.quote: We believe Private Wealth Management business will contribute larger share of profitability for the group in the coming years due to higher growth as we continue to penetrate more customers with differentiated products a nd services that the clients demand in this

items.statement: Investment Banking pipeline more than 2x FY25 revenues providing strong visibility
items.quote: Our IB pipeline is more than 2x the revenues that we booked in FY25, providing us reasonably strong visibility of growth in this business, notwithstanding the recent volatility that we've seen in the market.

items.statement: Technology spend increased to 4.5-5% of net revenues, up ~100 bps YoY
items.quote: In terms of our tech spends also, we spend almost about 4.5% to 5% of our net revenues on technology, and this number is growing. Over last year, this number is up almost 100 b ps.

items.statement: Marketing costs substantially higher in FY25
items.quote: Same is the case with our marketing costs this year, subs tantially higher spend on that

items.statement: Incremental cost of funds 50 bps lower than overall cost, spreads and margins to improve in lending businesses
items.quote: Our incremental cost of funds is now 50 b ps lower than the overall cost currently. We are already seeing the positive impact of favourable rate cycle coming to us on both of the lending business, whether it is on the margin trade finance segment or on the housing finance. To that extent, we will see the improvement of spreads and margins in the coming periods.

items.statement: Net interest income spread improved from 5.9% to 6.5% in FY25
items.quote: Third part of the Wealth Management business is the net interest income, which grew by 37% YoY due to higher lending book, as well as improvement in spreads from 5.9% in FY24 to 6.5% in FY25.

items.statement: Wealth Management net flows grew 3x to Rs. 10,279 crores in FY25
items.quote: This is reflected in our FY25 growth wherein our net flows grew 3x to over Rs. 10,279 crores in FY25 on a YoY basis.

items.statement: AMC gross flows grew 290% YoY to Rs. 68,007 crores in FY25
items.quote: Coupled with expansion in our distribution presence, our gross flows grew by 290% YoY in FY25 to Rs. 68,007 crores.

items.statement: AMC net flows grew 10x to Rs. 48,450 crores in FY25
items.quote: In terms of net flows of the asset management business, it grew multi -fold from Rs. 5,191 crores FY24 to Rs. 48,450 crores, increased by 10x in FY25.

items.statement: Housing Finance disbursements grew 78% to Rs. 1,794 crores in FY25
items.quote: Our disbursements grew by 78% to Rs. 1,794 crores.

items.statement: Fee-based revenue contribution increased from 31% to 37% of total revenues in FY25
items.quote: Our fee-based revenue contribution to our total revenues increased from 31% same time last year to 37% now.

items.statement: Annual recurring revenue as percentage of total net revenue grew to 56% at end of FY25
items.quote: Our annual recurring revenue as a percentage of total net revenue grew to 56% at the end of FY25.

items.statement: No FY26 revenue or EBITDA guidance given; management will provide outlook once macro settles in a quarter or two
items.quote: we are not giving any particular time. But I would also say that during the year, as the things settle, we will certainly come back and give the outlook for the res t of the

items.statement: Q4 FY25 deal closures $280M; sequential increase from $236M in Q3, $207M in Q2, $202M in Q1
items.quote: in the first quarter of this year, the deal closures were $202 million, in second quarter $207 million, in the third quarter, $236 million. And in the last quarter, that Q4, our deal closures were $280 million.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA margin 21%; management aims to maintain margins in FY26 via platforms, automation and AI productivity
items.quote: we believe that many of these things will help us not only that we want to continue having the margins, same margins, but we would like to invest in terms of many areas for future and really making a transition to the new models, business models.

items.statement: H1 FY26 growth expected positive quarter-on-quarter; H2 pickup anticipated as tariff clarity emerges in 3-4 months
items.quote: We don't talk about quarter-to-quarter growth, but it would be positive.

items.statement: Vertical adjacency expansion: started work with 4 of 8 new clients (2 truck OEMs, 1 off-highway, 1 passenger car); Europe pipeline largest
items.quote: Out of those 8, we have started working already on 4. And out of them, 2 are commercial vehicles and 1 is off highway. And the last one is, of course, passenger cars.

items.statement: Some clients giving rate increases; others seeking cost-effective solutions; shifting to productivity-based offshoring model to protect margins
items.quote: in some customers, we have got the increment that is increased rates in some customers. And of course, there are clients which are coming back for a better cost -effective solution.

items.statement: Investing in AI transformation, hiring AI team, building automotive-specific AI agents, platforms, tools and accelerators
items.quote: We are also making a meaningful investment into AI transformation. It is in terms of hiring the team, then we are also building solutions as I said, AI is not just AI because that any company can come up with.

items.statement: Tariff uncertainty may slow order-to-revenue conversion for a quarter or two; some small project closures seen but no significant ramp-downs
items.quote: the speed at which the things will get executed is still not fully clear in the short term. While we believe it is a question of a quarter or 2 at the most.

items.statement: M&A discussions in advanced stages for strategic adjacencies (vertical or offerings); not for pure growth; financing approach not specified
items.quote: we are looking at certain acquisitions also in advanced stages of discussion, but till it doesn't happen, it doesn't happen. So those opportunities are there.

items.statement: Mercedes-Benz SDV deal: multi-year (3-4 years), similar scope to Honda/Renault deals, not included in Q4 $280M TCV
items.quote: absolutely, it is a similar scope we are doing, but I think we came a little bit late, but absolutely, it is the same contract. And it will be a longer -term deal. It's a multiyear deal, which we are looking at 3 to 4 years deal.

items.statement: China strategy progressing: building local organization, partnerships; expect meaningful engagement in second half of FY26
items.quote: I believe in the later part of this year, we should have something going. But we are progressing on some conversations there.

items.statement: QORIX JV contributed INR14 crore profit in Q4; quarterly volatility expected; medium-term positive outlook
items.quote: there will be quarter-on-quarter variation because it's a product company, QORIX itself. We do believe that in coming times in medium-term, it will be positive.

items.statement: Europe pipeline solid; 2 truck OEMs and 1 passenger car OEM from Europe among new wins; expect at least one large deal closure in Q1 FY26
items.quote: The 2 truck OEMs that Mr. Pandit talked about, they are from Europe. The passenger car OEM also happens to be from Europe. The pipeline keeps getting better.

items.statement: US growth to be broad-based across passenger cars, trucks and off-highway; new passenger car OEM engagement started
items.quote: we've started an engagement with the new OEM in U.S., which is a good thing for us. And we believe that we'll grow, we'll have substantial growth from that particular pass car OEM in the US.

items.statement: Commercial vehicle and off-highway base building in FY26; meaningful growth expected from FY27
items.quote: In this year, we would build a base. And from the next year, we will see meaningful growth is what we see as of now.

items.statement: Adjusted EBITDA margin range guided at 25-27% for FY26, with near-term blend of 27% core and 18% railway business implying 24-25% blended margin

items.statement: ISTS waiver ending June 2025; company following policy and not taking risk on assumptions

items.statement: Increasing wind share in merchant portfolio; post-June 2025 solar merchant capacity to serve C&I or pumped storage
items.quote: We have been increasing share of the wind in our merchant portfolio, and you would see more and more such capacities being there.

items.statement: Refinanced $1.06 billion construction facility at AA+ rating with 19-year door-to-door tenure
items.quote: Adani Green refinanced its new construction facility of $1.06 billion. This long-term refinancing, rated AA+, represents door-to-door tenure of 19 years.

items.statement: All operations now water positive, achieved a year ahead of target
items.quote: You'll be happy to note that all of our operations are now water positive, and this goal has been achieved a year before our own target.

items.statement: Maharashtra 5 GW PPA: 2 GW in 2 years, then 1 GW every 6 months
items.quote: It starts from two years and then every six months we have additional 1 gigawatt, 1 gigawatt each.

items.statement: FY25 capacity addition of 3.3 GW vs 5 GW target due to environmental challenges at Khavda; learnings applied for FY26
items.quote: Our assumptions with respect to the environment remain there and the soil conditions there and the effect of the rains beyond the months where it was raining. I think there was some effect to it, which has now been taken care of.

items.statement: No FY26 revenue or EBITDA guidance given; will provide outlook once macro settles
items.quote: we are not giving any particular time. But I would also say that during the year, as the things settle, we will certainly come back and give the outlook for the res t of the

items.statement: Q4 FY25 deal closures $280M, up sequentially from $236M in Q3
items.quote: In the first quarter of this year, the deal closures were $202 million, in second quarter $207 million, in the third quarter, $236 million. And in the last quarter, that Q4, our deal closures were $280 million.

items.statement: Intend to maintain FY25 EBITDA margin level while investing in AI, platforms, automation
items.quote: we believe that we are in a good position to do that. There are many things we have been focusing a lot on things such as platforms, the automation as well as AI together.

items.statement: Expect positive Q-on-Q growth in H1 FY26; pickup in H2 as tariff clarity emerges
items.quote: We don't talk about quarter-to-quarter growth, but it would be positive.

items.statement: Started work with 4 of 8 new vertical adjacency clients: 2 truck OEMs, 1 off-highway, 1 passenger car
items.quote: Out of those 8, we have started working already on 4. And out of them, 2 are commercial vehicles and 1 is off highway. And the last one is, of course, passenger cars.

items.statement: Some clients giving rate increases; others want cost-effective solutions; shifting to productivity-based model
items.quote: in some customers, we have got the increment that is increased rates in some customers. And of course, there are clients which are coming back for a better cost -effective solution.

items.statement: Investing meaningfully in AI transformation, hiring, automotive-specific AI agents and platforms
items.quote: We are also making a meaningful investment into AI transformation. It is in terms of hiring the team, then we are also building solutions as I said, AI is not just AI because that any company can come up with.

items.statement: Tariff uncertainty may slow order-to-revenue conversion for 1-2 quarters; some small project cancellations seen
items.quote: the speed at which the things will get executed is still not fully clear in the short term. While we believe it is a question of a quarter or 2 at the most.

items.statement: M&A discussions in advanced stages for strategic adjacencies; financing approach not specified
items.quote: we are looking at certain acquisitions also in advanced stages of discussion, but till it doesn't happen, it doesn't happen.

items.statement: Mercedes-Benz SDV deal is multi-year (3-4 years), similar scope to Honda/Renault deals, not in Q4 TCV
items.quote: it is a similar scope we are doing, but I think we came a little bit late, but absolutely, it is the same contract. And it will be a longer -term deal. It's a multiyear deal, which we are looking at 3 to 4 years deal.

items.statement: Europe pipeline solid; 2 truck OEMs and 1 passenger car OEM from Europe in new wins
items.quote: Europe pipeline looks solid. The 2 truck OEMs that Mr. Pandit talked about, they are from Europe. The passenger car OEM also happens to be from Europe.

items.statement: US growth broad-based across passenger cars, trucks, off-highway; new passenger car OEM engagement started
items.quote: we've started an engagement with the new OEM in U.S., which is a good thing for us. And we believe that we'll grow, we'll have substantial growth from that particular pass car OEM in the US.

items.statement: Asia growth to be broad-based: India reasonable growth, China positive, Japan positive, Korea flattish
items.quote: India will be a growth market. We see a reasonable growth in India. , China has been a small part. So we will see at least something positive there than what it was last year. Japan will be also positive. And Korea is probably flattish as of now.

items.statement: Commercial vehicle and off-highway base building in FY26; meaningful growth expected from FY27
items.quote: In this year, we would build a base. And from the next year, we will see meaningful growth is what we see as of now.

items.statement: Validation and integration programs accelerating; discretionary R&D/POC work being deferred by OEMs
items.quote: some of these further in the timeline activities start falling into discretionary activities and they start getting tuned. They're not necessarily cancelled, but they start getting tuned in terms of deferment.

items.statement: QORIX JV profit INR14 crore in Q4; quarterly volatility expected; medium-term positive outlook
items.quote: there will be quarter-on- quarter variation because it's a product company, QORIX itself. We do believe that in coming times in medium-term, it will be positive

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions remain a significant near-term risk despite India's strong macroeconomic position

items.statement: Strategic shift from transactional broking to wealth management focusing on asset accumulation and annuity products
items.quote: The big shift I would say in the mindset is that the focus will be more on asset gathering, focus will be more on selling, I would say, annuity products like mutual funds, AIF and PMF.

items.quote: Yes, of course, it will have some impact on the cost to income ratio in the short term simply because as the build-out is happening, there will be an increase in manpower cost and that has been evident because our manpower cost has risen.

items.statement: Retail broking faces headwinds for next 1-2 quarters due to regulatory changes and volatility, but long-term outlook positive given low equity penetration
items.quote: My view is that the short term, I would still say that there will be some amount of recalibration happening. items.statement: Ultra-HNI RM count to grow from 50 to 100-120 in next year as part of wealth management expansion
items.quote: I think in the next one year, the headcount will go from 50 to about 100 or 120.

items.statement: Asset management AUM at Rs. 800-900 crores expected to double in next year; no mutual fund launch planned in next 12 months
items.quote: So, we have already recruited a fund manager for equities and he has joined us. And so, at this point in time, I would say that we are roughly close to about Rs. 800 crores –Rs. 900 crores of assets under management and this we think should easily double in the next one year.

items.statement: Income tax search conducted in January 2025; no subsequent communication received, impact on financials not determinable

items.statement: Management not providing forward-looking statements including cost-to-income ratio guidance for FY26
items.quote: We are not giving any forward-looking statement. That's why I won't be able to comment on the cost to income ratio for FY '26.

items.statement: Blended yield on MF, PMS, AIF distribution assets approximately 0.75-0.9%
items.quote: Actually, on a blended basis, I think the yield will be about 0.75, 0.8, 0.9x.

items.statement: Life insurance premium business expected to grow slowly in mid-teens after recent decline
items.quote: See, actually we think that this business will not show a big spike, but it should get back to a slowly upper sloping graph in the mid-teens.

items.statement: NIM guidance for FY26 is between 3.75% and 4.00%, likely close to 4%
items.quote: Our NIM for this quarter is 3.75%, and for the full next year, the guidance will be somewhere in between 3.75% and 4.00% and probably somewhere close to 4% is what will be there.

items.statement: Credit cost guidance for FY26 kept below 30 basis points
items.quote: We are keeping our credit cost guidance below 30 basis points for next year. We sh ould be able to comfortably achieve this - is our

items.quote: On return on assets, our guidance is between 1.5% to 1.8% and return on equity between 15% to 17%.

items.statement: Asset growth anticipated between 20% to 25% for FY26, constrained by liability growth
items.quote: Overall, I think anything between 20% to 25% growth is anticipated as of now. But of course, we have to see.

items.quote: We are migrating our CBS to Oracle system along with the implementation of various surr ound systems. items.statement: NIM bottomed out at 3.75% in Q4 FY25; FY25 full year NIM was 4.13%; FY26 guidance 3.75-4.00%
items.quote: I think from a NIM perspective, we have definitely hit the bottom. We will not go below where we are right now. But on a year-on-year, the NIM is 4.13% and we need to see. items.statement: All verticals contributing to asset growth; wholesale, SME, gold, retail scalable post tech migration; liability growth is the constraint
items.quote: Frankly speaking, the growth is absolutely not a problem for us, e xcept for the funding part. items.quote: our long-t erm philosophical thinking is wholesale will be 30%, SME will be 20%, retail will be 30% and gold will be 20%. That's our FY 2030 journey

items.statement: Key risks: tech migration execution (biggest risk and opportunity), legacy unsecured book tapering down, liquidity risk easing, global tariff uncertainty
items.quote: the biggest risk for us is this migration and the entire tran sformation and biggest opportunity is also that and we are waiting for that. Otherwise, I don't see any major risks

items.quote: We have every year, grown by anything between 50 to 100 branches. We will retain that kind of a pace for our acquisition because we cannot invest at a very large scale till, we have the product services and processes. You will see a significant expansion from FY '27 onwards.

items.quote: Because of the global uncertainty, tariff war and all of that happened, the hedging costs went up because of which, while we are expecting the FCY borrowing cost to come down as these are all SOFR linked, SOFR didn't come down that much last quarter and hedging costs temporarily went up, which took our cost of funds a little higher.

items.statement: Tech migration dry runs successful; main migration in May; stabilization expected in 3-4 months; full scaling from H2 FY26

items.quote: On a stand-alone, we believe that it should be in the range of around 250 to 300 basis points. And this projection number does not include any additional ESOPs, which may be granted by NRC in this particular financial year.

items.statement: Book tax rate expected in 23-24% range from FY26 onwards
items.quote: Yes, on a book rate, we see in the range of around 23% to 24%.

items.quote: Going forward, we expect maybe a dilution of max to max 1 or 2 basis points in yield, mainly because of the higher proportion of ETF AUM that we have.

items.quote: Yes, the Capex amount should go down. I don't think we will be opening such high number of offices in FY '26.

items.quote: Our SIP gross sales and folio account on a year -on-year basis have also grown by around 23% and 14%, respectively. So we still have some comfort level there.

items.quote: Our quarterly average AUM for the index and ETF funds stood at ₹ 1,41,492 crores, up by 23% in the 4th Quarter. ETFs and Index fund net inflow stood at ₹ 19,605 crores.

items.statement: Hybrid funds driving flow turnaround; large & mid-cap also seeing good traction
items.quote: A significant part of the traction we have seen in turning around flows during the course of this year has actually come from the hybrid funds.

items.quote: We have recently got a regulatory approval to launch a multi-cap fund, and that fund is already open for subscription from 29th of April till 13th of May. Apart from multi-cap fund, we don't see any pipeline as far as the diversified equity is concerned.

items.quote: Both on Innovation Fund and Dynamic Equity fund, you need to appreciate that apart from the market impact, there is also a currency impact. Currency has fallen sharply over the last year.

items.statement: UTI Pension Fund AUM crossed ₹3.6 lakh cr; Max Life Pension Fund schemes transferred to UTI Pension Fund by PFRDA
items.quote: We are very proud of our subsidiary, UTI Pension Fund. This company crossed the milestone of ₹ 3.6 lakh crore AUM at this point of time.

items.quote: UTI Alternatives Private Limited has a total AUM of ₹ 2,648 crores as of March '25, a 34% growth from March '24.

items.quote: Which brings me neatly to a net order book which at the end of FY25 stands at 24.2 thousand crore rupees or $2.8 billion. The EV contribution to this order book remains high. It's at 77%.

items.statement: Adjusted EBITDA margin range guided at 25-27% for FY26, blending 27% core business with 18% railway business
items.quote: So end of next quarter we will give you a range, but if you just do the ma th that you take 27% is what we did 27 %x80 and do 18 x20, you will come to somewhere closer to between 24 to 25
