items.quote: At this moment, we are looking to invest a number which is below $10 million. That's the first stage.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 adjusted EBITDA margin 27.6%, down 130 bps YoY due to product mix change; full year margin 28.2%, down 60 bps
items.quote: Adjusted EBITDA margin was 27.6%, which is a drop of 1.3% compared to fourth quarter of last year, and it's primarily on account of change in the product mix.

items.statement: US tariffs expected to adversely impact auto demand short-term; 3% of total revenue at medium risk over next 12-18 months

items.statement: Entering humanoid robot components market leveraging motor, gear, sensor capabilities; actuators represent >50% of $35-50k BOM; exploratory work begun, commercial success binary

items.quote: 25% tariff is not something that can be absorbed by anyone because nobody makes 25% net margin. Which is why eventually the consumer, the end consumer pays for it in the form of higher end product prices is what eventually happens.

items.statement: Starter motor RFQs increasing unexpectedly as US OEMs refocus on ICE projects; won large starter motor orders last quarter
items.quote: Strangely, yes, so that's been one of the I'd say weird second order impact of all of this which is going on, that we are now suddenly getting starter motor RFQs which had kind of dried up, pretty much completely. Last couple of years we were not getting any starter motor RFQs. We have suddenly have a lot of starter motor RFQs.

items.statement: Edible oil EBITDA per ton guidance of INR 3,500-3,600 for full business including other income
items.quote: I think we should be able to deliver the margin structure in per ton terms, which we have been delivering earlier, except for the last year. items.quote: on growth front, e dible oil consumption we are hopeful of anything between 7% to 8% growth, although the country consumption is growing by only 3%, but we expect to do better than average industry, and we will continue to do, one

items.quote: On margin front, I think we have been saying this for quite some time that food will remain into an investment phase or a growth phase for next 2 years to 3 years and we'll continue to operate at an EBITDA neutral.

items.statement: Palm oil prices expected to soften in April-June, overall stability expected in FY26
items.quote: And going forward, April, May, June, the prices will soften little bit further. But one doesn't know about any policy that Indonesia or Malaysia will bring on B40. items.quote: And I mean, we are hopeful that in the next couple of years itself, we can make the top line 2x of what it is today.

items.statement: Gohana food park commissioning expected by August 2025, wheat flour capacity 15,000 tons/month
items.quote: Only project that will come by August is the wheat flour project, which is a good, big project and that we will get only 6 months. I think that is around 15,000 tons per month capacity.

items.statement: FY25 profitability benefited from one-off commodity cycle gains not expected to repeat in FY26
items.quote: For the quarter 2, quarter 3, we did saw a favorable commodity cycle gain, one-off kind of cycle gain, which actually resulted into a better number for us in Q4 -- in Q3, particularly and to some extent, and Q2 also. items.statement: Differential duty of 15% between CPO and refined palmolein requested from government to support Make in India
items.quote: Now, we have been requesting the government that Make in India is something that is being talked about, but it needs a differential duty of at least 15%. And in that case, only we can import more CPO and process and make olein in India.

items.statement: Food & FMCG growth expected to return to 18-20% going forward after FY25 slowdown to 9-10%
items.quote: I think going forward, we should continue to deliver 18%, 20% growth in food.

items.statement: Effective tax rate of 25.8%, assume 25% for next year
items.quote: Yes. So today, the effective tax rate of company is 25.8%. I think you can continue to assume 25% tax rate effectively.

items.statement: Branded share: edible oil ~60%, food >75%, overall ~70%

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved from 17% to 20% annually; PAT margin improved from 6% to 9% in FY25.
items.quote: the EBITDA margin has jumped from 17 to 20 on an annual basis. And if you look at the PAT margins, it has jumped from 6 to 9%.

items.statement: Demand has improved; revenue grew 5.5% YoY on constant currency in FY25 and 8% QoQ in Q4 FY25.
items.quote: On constant currency terms, we have grown 5.5% annually.

items.statement: Revenue split: 52% product engineering, 48% digital transformation; InfoBeans Cloud Tech share decreasing in parent.
items.quote: Revenue breakup for segment, digital transformation, product engineering, more or less similar, 52 percent product engineering, 48 percent digital transformation.

items.statement: Expenses tightly controlled through cost optimization measures, supporting margin expansion.
items.quote: the expenditure is trying to be, we are trying to be more prudent and trying to control the expense by applying a lot of cost optimization measures.

items.quote: Quilo is one, so we have one customer on Quilo. But there are other pieces that we're doing with other clients, where there's an AI piece involved. And we are currently on three projects on AI right now.

items.quote: I am happy to also tell you that we have now reached 100 contracts in our international business.

items.statement: M&A due diligence cost Rs.12 crore in FY25; cloud/license expansion added Rs.12-13 crore
items.quote: There is some impact of M&A due diligence cost of about Rs.12 crores that we incurred during the year which has reduced the EBITDA.

items.statement: AUM market share ~33-34%, targeting 39.4-40%; SIP market share ~40%; AIF AUM Rs.1.5 trillion, up 50% YoY
items.quote: Overall industry has been growing at about 12%, whereas KFintech's market share, which has been growing at nearly three times that, close to about 33%, 34%.

items.statement: Value-added solutions revenue up 57% YoY; Webile mobility stack revenue up 150% YoY; wealth platform mPowerWealth signed 5 large wealth managers
items.quote: I am very happy to inform you that the previous year saw a 57% increase in value added solutions revenue year-on-year.

items.statement: Large M&A ambitions closed for foreseeable future; focus on integration of Ascent Fund Services (51% stake)
items.quote: With this, we would have summarily close our large M&A ambitions for the foreseeable future. There will be minor plug-ins which may still continue to evaluate.

items.statement: Dividend Rs.7.5 per share declared; Rs.305 crore for Ascent 51% acquisition funded from cash (Rs.660 crore)
items.quote: We have cash and cash equivalents as of 31st March close to about Rs.660 crores and dividend of Rs.7.5 per share has been declared by the board and subject to shareholders' approval shall be disseminated so.

items.statement: KRA platform ready, awaiting final SEBI approval; expect launch this quarter
items.quote: We have completed our platform build at this point in time. We are awaiting SEBI's final approval. Our readiness at this very moment is we are literally a minute away from launching our KRA Solutions the moment we get approval from the regulator.

items.statement: Management maintains guidance of 18% to 20% top line growth and 40% to 45% EBITDA margin
items.value: 18% to 20% top line growth; 40% to 45% EBITDA margin
items.quote: We continue to maintain guidance of 18% to 20% top line growth and 40 % to 45% of EBITDA margin.

items.statement: Ascent integration expected to be EBITDA neutral in near term and accretive in FY27
items.quote: While we will see the integration of Ascent in the coming three, four months we believe that it will be neutral in terms of EBITDA margin impact, and it will become accretive in FY27

items.statement: KFintech Southeast Asia deal pipeline is close to $25 million revenue potential excluding Thailand
items.quote: Our KFintech deal pipeline in Southeast Asia is close to about $25 million at this point in time.

items.statement: Ascent deal pipeline is larger than KFintech international pipeline and expanding faster across 18 countries
items.quote: Ascent, their pipeline is larger in the context of multiple geographies that they are present in 18 different count ries and of course we are still in the early stages of integration

items.statement: Management does not anticipate materially high compression from AMC renegotiations
items.quote: There can be some compression, but I wouldn't anticipate it to be materially high.

items.statement: Tech spend as percentage of revenue rose from 7-8% five years ago to 23-24% in FY25
items.quote: If you see our spend of tech as a percentage of revenue, which is a parameter we track to , five years back, it used to be about 7 % to 8%, the year that had gone by, it has risen to almost 23 % to 24%.

items.statement: ESOP cost was Rs.11.3 crores in FY25; expected to increase to Rs.18-20 crores in FY26
items.quote: We also have ESOP cost of about Rs.11.3 crores, which was incurred as an addition to what was incurred last year and next year again, you will see an increase in the ESOP cost because more employees will get covered in a new scheme which new brands will come in and we do expect anywhere around 18 to 20 crores of ESOP expenses to come in the next year.

items.statement: Issuer Solutions added 9 million folios in FY25, nearly all organic from existing clients and IPOs
items.quote: On the Issuer Solutions, the total folio addition in the previous year was 9 million folios, which is pretty robust. And I think with the exception of one specific transition, nearly all of it is organic

items.statement: AIF revenue is purely annuity with no one-time revenue; revenue lags fund launch by 1-3 months
items.quote: In AIF usually there is no episodical one-time revenue at all. So, this is purely annuity. In fact, you will always see a lag of revenue because it usually takes a month to t wo to t hree months where a fund house when it launches and onwards and RTA for us to set ourselves keep ourselves operationally ready for them to go live and then they get the

items.statement: BlackRock Aladdin partnership integration underway; revenue expected in 1-2 quarters
items.quote: It is probably a quarter to 2 away in terms of clocking revenues. But obviously, it's important to go that far to be able to understand because there even the tiniest of conversion in terms of our clients can be of materially a large contract for KFintech.

items.statement: M&A expense of Rs.12 crores split between Q3 and Q4 FY25
items.quote: The M&A expense is broken up into two quarters, Q3 and Q4.

items.statement: Volume expansion expected to outpace AUM expansion; investing in cloud, data, AI and cyber security
items.quote: We believe that the volume expansion will probably even outpace the expansion of the AUM in times to come. And the cyber security related aspects are extremely important for the nature of the work we perform.

items.statement: Employee headcount grew 5-7% while volumes grew 33% YoY; hiring driven by transaction volume, new funds, new clients
items.quote: While the volumes have gone up by 33% year-on-year, the increase in the number of employees has been marginal of about 5% to 7%.

items.statement: Expect EBITDA growth close to 25% with at least 100 bps margin expansion in FY26
items.quote: And for the financial year FY '26 also, our focus remains on increasing the profitability, and we expect that the growth in our profitability in terms of EBITDA would be close to 25%, with at least a 100 basis point increase in the margin.

items.statement: Target 20-25% minimum bottom-line growth for FY26; no specific top-line guidance given
items.quote: But our aim is that on the bottom line, we expect at least 20% to 25% minimum growth for the next financial year -- sorry, for the current financial year.

items.statement: FY25 capacity expansion completed ahead of schedule and below budgeted capex
items.quote: The planned capacity expansion that we had planned for the last financial year, which is FY '25, was completed seamlessly and fully integrated with our existing operations and executed ahead of the schedule and also below the originally budgeted capex.

items.statement: Expanding flexible hose capacity from 16.5 to 20 million meters; 16 million commissioned end of Q3 FY25
items.quote: And also with that, we are expanding from 16.5 million to about 20 million.

items.statement: Metal bellows Phase 1 capacity 120k pcs/yr; revenue potential INR85-90 cr at peak; miniature bellows INR25-30 cr
items.quote: So at full capacity, the metal bellows project would be having a top line of about INR85 crores to INR90 crores at peak utilization. And the miniature metal bellows would have a top line of about INR25 crores to INR30 crores at peak utilization.

items.statement: Short-term tariff pain possible (1-2 months); medium-long term opportunity for Indian manufacturers
items.quote: there might be short-term pain, but I think over the course of the entire year, I think we'll see a much better opportunity for Indian manufacturers who are exporting to the U.S. because I think the demand for Indian products is going to increase

items.statement: Revenue potential ~INR650 cr at 20M meter hose capacity with 70% assembly mix at current steel prices
items.quote: So at a 20 million meter annual capacity and say, I just assume that, say, if 70% of the business comes from the assemblies, right? So we can see a revenue potential of about INR650 crores.

items.statement: Metal bellows optimum utilization by FY27; miniature bellows commissioned by Mar'26, optimum by FY28
items.quote: I think for the metal bellows, we can expect that by '27, we will reach an optimum utilization. And I think miniature metal bellows our project would be commissioned in by March of '26. So the optimum utilization for that particular project would may happen in FY '28.

items.statement: Long-term: metal bellows could contribute 25-30% of revenue in 4-5 years
items.quote: I would say, 25% to 30% of our business, if not more, would come from metal bellows 4, 5 years from now. It's just a ballpark figure, right?

items.statement: Working capital cycle ~120 days export vs ~75 days domestic
items.quote: For example, if an overall working capital days, say, for example, for an export is just assuming, say, for example, 120 days overall working capital cycle. In India, that comes down to about 75 days.

items.statement: Credit cost expected to stay around 1% plus or minus 10 bps in FY26
items.quote: I am expecting it to stay around 1 % plus or minus 10 bps. So I am seeing the credit cost hovering around that range.

items.statement: AUM growth target 12-15% including BL base, 25-30% excluding BL base for FY26
items.quote: If you take that in the base, then you will see around 12 % to 15% growth. If you remove that from the base, you will see about 25% to 30% AUM growth is what we are targeting.

items.statement: Net interest margin expected to be stable going forward
items.quote: Ajit, we expect the net interest margin to be stable.

items.statement: Doorstep gold loan share target 18-22% in next 1-2 years from current 15%
items.quote: In the next one year to two years, we want to take it up by 3% or 4% points. That means you will see that 15% number going to about 18% to 22% in the next one year to two years.

items.statement: Investing in collection infrastructure, middle and field hiring to complete by Q1 FY26
items.quote: The middle layer and field level hiring is in progress and we expect to complete it by Q1.

items.statement: Small ticket LAP disbursals Rs 270 crore in Q4 FY25, up 58% QoQ
items.quote: With the new processes in BRE, our small ticket LAP disbursals for Q4 touched Rs. 270 crores, a growth of about 58% quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Pure spread expanded 13 bps in FY25 as yields rose 43 bps and cost of borrowings rose 30 bps
items.quote: While on an average, our cost of borrowings have gone up by 30 bps. Consequently, we have seen a pure spread expansion during the year of 13 bps.

items.statement: Weighted average cost of borrowings up 3 bps QoQ to 8.72% due to MCLR resets; incremental cost lower
items.quote: On a quarter-on-quarter basis, our weighted average cost of borrowings has marginally gone up by three basis points from 8.69% to 8.72%. And this is primarily due to MCLR linked interest resets on existing borrowings. Our incremental borrowing cost continues to be less than this.

items.statement: Gold loan tonnage grew 18% YoY to 11.3 tons; added 35,000 new customers in Q4
items.quote: Tonnage growth for the year came in at 18 % YOY reaching 11.3 tons. We have added 35,000 new customers in Gold loans during the quarter.

items.statement: Elevated Stage 2 and 1+ delinquencies in ST LAP; flows expected next two quarters then plateau by year end
items.quote: The Stage 2 also you will see elevated this time. So there are likely to be flows in the quarters coming and we see those flows coming in the next two quarters. And thereafter I am seeing a plateau and then by year end we will normalize.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio sticky historically; BAU OPEX on downward trajectory but tactical growth investments continue
items.quote: See, there is always going to be some amount of spend in the OPEX line, which is building muscle. And we will not shy away from that. What we are trying to tell on this call is that the part of the OPEX which is BAU, which is maybe flat or just a going on kind of cost, that consciously we are trying to put it on a downward trajectory.

items.statement: Capital adequacy improved 30 bps to 21.9% via DA Rs 531 cr and CLM Rs 256 cr in Q4
items.quote: During the quarter, our AUM grew by Rs. 900 crores. We moved Rs. 787 crores of loans off book which constituted a DA of Rs. 531 crore across the mortgage book and a CLM of Rs. 256 crores on the gold loan book. Through this, in spite of growing AUM at a rapid pace, we were able to improve capital adequacy levels by 30 bps from 21.6% to 21.9%.

items.statement: Off-balance sheet book Rs 3,973 crore, up 75% YoY; gold partner book Rs 1,131 cr, BL securitized Rs 440 cr, mortgage Rs 2,408 cr
items.quote: Our off balance sheet book as of March 31, 25 stands at Rs. 3,973 crores, up 75% year-on-year from Rs. 2,276 crores in the previous year. Of this, gold loans held in partner books accounted for Rs. 1,131 crore, unsecured business loans secu ritized stood at Rs. 440 crores and mortgage loans accounted for Rs. 2,408

items.statement: Branch expansion continues; 52 branches opened in FY25 with 28 in Q4; first branch opened in Andhra Pradesh (Guntur)
items.quote: If you look at the slide #18 we have opened roughly about 52 branches last year. 28 of the 52 have come in Quarter 4. So we are expanding branch networks. I also mentioned we opened the first branch in Andhra, which is in Guntur.

items.statement: NIMs expected to improve in FY26 driven by lower cost of deposits, unsecured growth recovery, and stable secured NIMs despite higher funding costs
items.quote: So yes, Manish, we should expect NIMs to improve as we go into this financial year, and I mentioned all the right reasons for that.

items.statement: CASA cost reduced to 4.36% while CASA grew 18% to Rs 5,235 cr; deposit cost rose from 7.7% to 8% but one rate cut already done in April
items.quote: I must tell you that from a 7.7% to an 8%. But here we are sitting in April and we have already had one cut in the deposit rates, we have had one cut in our savings rate.

items.statement: Unsecured MFI growth expected at 3-5% in FY26; secured assets to continue 40% growth; gold loans and two-wheelers now mature profitable businesses
items.quote: Will it grow at 10%? Unlikely. But certainly in the 3% to 5% range, we see it growing because we are very conservative. So again, if there is nothing which surprises us, you will obviously see a pe aking out

items.statement: Secured book now 70% of advances; gold loans grew 237.6%, two-wheelers 105%, affordable housing 37.8%, micro-LAP 21.6%, MSME 29.1%
items.quote: Overall growth in secured assets is 40%. And where we sit, we would like to continue the same growth rate and there is no reason why we should not continue the same growth rate of secured asset growth.

items.statement: MFI book 28% under guarantee programs (CGFMU/CGTMSE); target 90% by September; Karnataka MFI slippages in Q4 (Rs 560 cr book); Rs 305 cr accelerated provisions taken
items.quote: The MFI book, 28% of which is now under the guarantee program. As we all know that this guarantee program takes in new disbursements, so we will complete the balance 70 %-odd through this year. So by September, we will mostly be 90%-odd under the guarantee program.

items.statement: No capital raise needed; capital adequacy improved to 20.7% from 20.3% without raising capital; further strengthening expected from profits, guarantee programs, and gold loan book
items.quote: Our capital adequacy has moved upto 20.7%. It was 20.3% last year and we have not raised capital. It only tells you that we do not need to raise any more capital.

items.statement: DTA balance Rs 550 cr at FY25 end; final DTA utilization year is FY27; Rs 185 cr DTA added in FY25; expect Rs 20-40 cr more in FY26
items.quote: Abhilash Sandur: Rs. 550 crores. Ajay Kanwal: Rs. 550 crores, yes.

items.statement: ARC sales used for both secured and unsecured; provisioning identical for ARC and on-book; will continue as tool based on NPA flows
items.quote: Yes, we have done ARC sale this year, both on secured and unsecured. And mainly unsecured. As you know, the provisioning for an unsecured book with ARC or within the Bank has to be identical.

items.statement: Universal Bank application to be filed within 30 days after meeting gross NPA <3% and net NPA <1% for two consecutive years
items.quote: With that, we would like to file in our application for the universal Bank within the next 30 days.

items.statement: RBI gold loan circular creates level playing field (75% LTV including interest for all regulated entities); bank moving part-time valuers to full-time and adding karatometers
items.quote: I think the impact is very positive because it says that all regulated entities, which includes NBFCs and banks, should have 75% loan to value, including the interest. And as you know, that was the difference between banks and NBFCs where NBFCs were able to do 75% without the interest, so I think there is a level playing field.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA guidance of INR5,500-6,000 crores
items.quote: We are projecting an EBITDA range of INR5,500 crores to INR6,000 crores, a substantial growth from FY25.

items.statement: Order book at INR47,000 crores as of March 31
items.quote: Our order book remains robust at INR47,000 crores.

items.statement: INR9,000 crores capex for 6 GW integrated ingot-wafer-cell-module PLI project by 2027
items.quote: The PLI project, which is an integrated 6 gigawatts of ingots and wafers, cells and modules, that's the one which we would be commissioning by 2027. And that is on time. We are on time for that. And that's that, the capex for that, on your question for capex, that's around INR9,000 crores of capex that we'll be spending to get that done.

items.statement: 3.2 GW module expansion at Chikhli to come online in 3-4 months
items.quote: However, 3.2 gigawatts of Chikhli facility, we are going ahead and executing that project at breakneck speed because that is really tied to a lot of our customer requirements and needs. And so that we would like to get online in the next, I would say, 3 to 4 months here.

items.statement: Board approved additional 1.6 GW module line in US; deployment timing flexible
items.quote: Our 1.6 gigawatts of module facility in the U.S., we have got the approval from the Board. We are closely watching the situation as it is evolving. And at the right time, we will go ahead and we will deploy the resources that are there at our beck and call.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA margin 21.04% vs 15.56% prior year; Q4 margin 25.59%
items.quote: EBITDA for the year stood at INR3,123 crores, representing a strong increase of 72.59% year-on-year with margins of 21.04%. Last year, the same margin was at 15.56%.

items.statement: Gross margin improvement driven by raw material cost decline and local cell integration
items.quote: So, as the prices are coming down, you will see our raw material prices are coming down faster and therefore we are able to manage a good margin and that's something that we hope to do as we continue into the future.

items.statement: DCR market expected to grow to 10-15 GW in FY26 from 3-4 GW last year
items.quote: Based on the allocation increased by the government and their own government spend structure, we expect this market itself to go up to anywhere between 10 to 15 gigawatts this year.

items.statement: Pipeline of ~100 GW for module business and ~30 GW for EPC contracts
items.quote: We are actually seeing a pipeline of about 100 gigawatts ahead of us which gives us the confidence that 2026 booking numbers are going to be solid and the same goes for 2027.

items.statement: 5.4 GW cell factory ramping; full rated capacity expected in 45-60 days
items.quote: So, I mean, our expectation is that in the next 45 to 60 days, the entire factory of 5.4 gigawatts will be fully on stream and manufacturing it at its rated capacity.

items.statement: In-house cell cost ~7-8 cents vs 11.5-14 cents for externally sourced cells
items.quote: The domestic DCR market also is something around that. So these two segments with our own cell when it comes online, which is expected to be something around 7 to 8 cents.

items.statement: US revenue share 17-20%; natural hedge via US and India manufacturing to manage tariff risk
items.quote: In the revenue stack that we have at this point in time, anywhere between 17% to 20% is U.S. bound, directionally. And so, as you can see, there's a very substantial 80% of our revenue coming from India market.

items.statement: Current US tariff 14%; potential additional 26% paused; will manage via dual manufacturing footprint
items.quote: So, at this point in time, it is 14%, right? And the flat rate that was going to be imposed on India was an additional 26%. That is what we know at this point in time, right? But we will need to see the evolution of all of this.

items.statement: INR790 crores equity committed for ENEL acquisition; typical IPP structure 65-70% debt, 25-30% equity
items.quote: We have committed an equity value of around INR790-odd crores of money plus there are other small pricing mechanism which shall uncover by the time we close the transaction which is expected probably within this quarter itself.

items.statement: Advances from customers ~INR4,300-4,400 crores per contract liabilities
items.quote: currently roughly about I can say around INR4,300 crores or INR4,400 crores is what we have as advances. Difficult t o give you the breakup, but yes that's the broad number and it sits in the head contract

items.statement: Retail revenue share 23-25%; utility share north of 60%
items.quote: Like I said directionally we have about 23% to 25% from our retail business.

items.statement: PAT expected to be INR800-plus crores by FY27
items.quote: So, by FY '27, we expect a PAT of INR800-plus crores.

items.statement: Cash capex for FY26 expected around INR600-700 crores through internal accruals
items.quote: Cash capex will be around INR600 crores to INR700 crores.

items.statement: LFP cathode plant capex INR1,130 crores with INR300 crores in FY26 and balance in FY27
items.quote: I think INR300 crores will be in FY '26 and balance, most of it will be in FY '27.

items.statement: Specialty carbon black expansion from 60,000 to 130,000 MTPA at Singur expected operational by Q3 FY26
items.quote: At Singur, our work on brownfield expansion of special ity carbon black line from 60,000 metric ton per an num to 130,000 metric ton per annum is progressing as planned and is expected to be operational by Q3 FY '26

items.statement: Anthraquinone and carbazole plant scheduled to go live in Q2 FY27
items.quote: The high value-added specialty product line is scheduled to go live in Q2 FY'27.

items.statement: Order book and contractual agreements place company in good position for next 2-3 years
items.quote: With our order book and our contractual agreements, we are placed in a very good situation for next 2 to 3 years, clearly.

items.statement: Specialty carbon black margins range from INR20,000 to 50,000 per ton depending on grade and application
items.quote: specialty carbon black margin differs from 20,000 to 50,000, depending on what grade you are producing, what application you are selling to.

items.statement: Volume trajectory expected to hold and grow further in FY26
items.quote: Yes, definitely, we expect the volume trajectory to hold on and grow further.

items.statement: Export opportunity for liquid coal tar pitch very bright with volumes ramping up in current year across Middle East and Southeast Asia
items.quote: The export opportunity is very bright in pitch. We are supplying material to different geographies. And in the current year, we expect the volumes to ramp up.

items.statement: LFP cathode active material plant first phase 40,000 MTPA operational by Q3 FY27, targeting 200,000 MTPA by 2030
items.quote: Our vision is to build a capacity of 200,000 metric ton per annum of electric cathode active material plant sufficient to power 100 gigawatt per hour of lithium-ion batteries with the first phase of 40,000 metric ton per annum expected to be operational by Q3 FY '27.

items.statement: LFP segment first full year revenue expected INR2,200-2,400 crores at full capacity utilization
items.quote: So in first full year of operations, it will have a top line of around INR2,200 crores to INR2,400 crores at full capacity utilization.

items.statement: Birla Tyres modernization operations to begin in phases starting end of Q1 FY26, focusing on off-highway and specialty tyres
items.quote: Modernization and revamping efforts are well underway with operations set to begin in phases starting end of Q1 FY'26. We will focus on building a comprehensive product portfolio of specialty tyres to serve off-highway tyre segment.

items.statement: Business model not based on opportunistic markets; no impact from China or Russia sanctions due to integrated cost advantage and long-term customer relationships
items.quote: Our business model and business that we have built is not based on opportunities. So unlike other companies, a lot of companies being impacted with what China is doing. And you will be pleased to know that there is no impact of China on Himadri business model.

items.statement: Board vision to achieve Rs. 15,000 crore topline on group basis by 2030 through organic growth and strategic acquisitions
items.quote: The Greaves Board had set itself a vision to achieve Rs. 15,000 crore topline on a group basis by 2030 through a blend of organic growth and strategic acquisitions and the management of Greaves Cotton and Greaves Electric Mobility remain committed to the same.

items.statement: Approximately Rs. 100 crore capex planned for coming year for internal growth in standalone business
items.quote: We will outlay approximately Rs. 100 crore capex even in the coming year for our internal growth purpose.

items.statement: Rs. 100 crore capex plan for Excel Controlinkage over 3-4 years for de-bottlenecking and capacity expansion
items.quote: We have outlaid almost Rs. 100 crore capex plan when we invested in this Company and this was something that we were planning to undertake over a 3 to 4-year period.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin at 14.7% in Q4 FY25; combined GCL and Excel EBITDA margin at 16.4% in Q4 FY25
items.quote: Standalone EBITDA for Greaves Cotton was Rs. 84 crore with margin at 14.7%. The combined Q4 EBITDA for Greaves Cotton and Excel is at Rs. 107 crore with margins at 16.4%.

items.statement: Full year FY25 combined EBITDA of GCL and Excel at Rs. 338 crore with 15% margin
items.quote: The combined EBITDA of GCL and Excel stood at Rs. 338 crore with a margin at a healthy 15%.

items.statement: Genset market share improved from ~2.7% to around 4% over last 6-8 quarters; non-auto applications dominate growth
items.quote: In gensets, our market share had been in the region of approximately 2.7% some time back. And we currently are below 4% or around 4%.

items.statement: Electric two-wheeler industry grew ~20% to 1.3 million units in FY25; GEML expects growth trajectory to continue
items.quote: The electric two-wheeler industry last year has grown by close to 20%, reaching 1.3 million units, and we expect that growth trajectory to continue.

items.statement: GEML launched three new electric two-wheelers in FY25: Ampere Nexus, Magnus Neo, and Ampere Reo; also launched Eltra in L5 segment
items.quote: This year, we introduced three electric two-wheelers, new two-wheelers, Ampere Nexus, Magnus Neo, and Ampere R eo, each engineered to be safe, smart, stylish, and affordable

items.statement: Engineering business diversified into multi-product, multi-application with gensets, CNG, hydrogen concept, e-powertrain for L3/L5, and exports
items.quote: We have tried to diversify our portfolio from a single engine, single application Company to multi product, multi-application Company and we continue on this journey.

items.statement: GEML constrains forward-looking statements on profitability and burn rate due to DRHP filing and awaiting SEBI approvals
items.quote: Going forward on the profitability part, as you are aware, we are waiting regulatory clearances from SEBI on our DRHP. So, I think I would constrain myself from giving any forward-looking statements.

items.statement: GEML preparing for subsidy-free environment next year; current subsidy at Rs. 2,500/kWh capped at Rs. 5,000 per vehicle for two-wheelers
items.quote: We are working towards a subsidy-free environment where it is the value proposition of the product and the consumer connect which you build through your quality, reliability and after sales service.

items.statement: GEML filed DRHP on December 23, 2024 for proposed IPO subject to SEBI approval, market conditions, and commercial considerations
items.quote: As you are aware, we have filed a draft red herring prospectus dated December 23rd, 2024, for a proposed initial public offering, which is subjected to receipt of regulatory approvals from the SEBI, market conditions and other commercial considerations.

items.statement: Greaves Cotton standalone cash reserves of Rs. 379 crore; near zero debt balance sheet; ROCE at 19% for FY25
items.quote: We continue to operate with a near zero debt balance sheet supported by standalone cash reserves of Rs. 379 crore. Our return on capital employed for FY25 stands at a healthy 19%.

items.statement: Excel Controlinkage plant utilization approximately >80% overall; some pieces at 60-70%, others at 90%+
items.quote: We would be approximately at an overall level more than 80% of plant utilization.

items.statement: Retail business building scalable tech-enabled model across auto, non-auto, EV components with 10,000+ retailers and 21,500+ mechanics
items.quote: A nationwide network of 10,000 plus Retailers and 21,500 plus mechanics ensures strong service delivery while digital tools enhance the operational efficiency.

items.statement: GEML market share in electric two-wheeler increased from 3.4% to 4.3% QoQ in Q4 FY25; Vahan registrations grew 15% QoQ
items.quote: Our Vahan registration grew by 15% quarter-on-quarter, resulting in an increase in our electric two-wheeler market share from 3.4% to 4.3% in this quarter.

items.statement: Expect strong double-digit growth across retail portfolio in FY26
items.quote: Overall, we remain confident of delivering strong double-digit growth across our retail portfolio in FY26 underpinned by sustained demand, proactive planning and the continuing evolution of our brand and experience proposition.

items.statement: Expect material office leasing in FY26 with 1.2-1.4 million sq ft pipeline
items.quote: I think in terms of leasing, Puneet, you will see material leasing happening in FY26, especially I think if I add the pipeline that are under active discussions between Pune, Bangalore and Chennai, we are talking about 1.2 to 1.4 million sq. ft. of leasing discussions going on across these three new offices and we should see significant conversions during this year.

items.statement: Expect meaningful office rental contribution from Q3 FY26
items.quote: Yes, I think considering the both agreement timelines and the fit out timelines, I would presume that you should see a more meaningful contribution from quarter three of this financial year.

items.statement: FY25 aggregate capex Rs 2,600 crores; Rs 1,600 crores for land/FSI, Rs 1,000 crores for construction
items.quote: Our aggregate CAPEX in FY25 was around Rs. 2,600 crores. Out of this , around Rs. 1,600 crores has been invested in th ree land parcels, namely Coimbatore, Chandigarh, and Bangalore i.e. Mittal Land and the FSI, which we have bought recently in the Lower Parel area and around Rs. 1,000 crores we have incurred toward s the construction at various places across the country and to densify our growth

items.statement: Annual construction capex ~Rs 1,000-1,200 crores for next 5 years
items.quote: I think this will be maintained even for next five years for sure. I mean of course this will, I mean any other acquisition or a bigger FSI purchase will be over and above that but on a construction side the number should be restricted to around Rs. 1,200 crores every year for next 5 years.

items.statement: Pre-leasing pipeline of 500,000 sq ft at Millennium Towers Pune
items.quote: Pre-leasing activity is underway with an active pipeline of over 500,000 sq. ft. in discussions at this moment.

items.statement: Pre-leasing conversations for ~800,000 sq ft across Bangalore and Chennai offices
items.quote: Between Bangalore (Phoenix Asia Towers) and Chennai (One National Park), we have pre-leasing conversations ongoing for almost 800,000 sq. ft.

items.statement: Hotel portfolio EBITDA margin 46% in FY25
items.quote: The hotel portfolio has delivered a strong performance once again this year with income rising to Rs. 580 crores up 6% year-on-year and EBITDA is growing by 11% to Rs. 266 crores reflecting an overall healthy margin of 46%.

items.statement: Cost of debt reduced from 9.2% to 8.5% over last few years
items.quote: We are putting a lot of efforts to reduce the cost of the debt which has come down from 9.2% to 8.5% in the last few years.

items.statement: April 2025 retailer sales expected to cross Rs 1,130 crores, up 14% YoY
items.quote: April is typically a lean month, but we have continued to see strong momentum in retail sales, with retailer sales expected to cross Rs. 1,130 crores for this month. This reflects a 14 % year-on-year growth, and to our minds, it confirms the depth and consistency of consumer demand across our portfolio.

items.statement: Revamping Phoenix MarketCity malls to improve brand mix and shopper experience
items.quote: All our Phoenix MarketCity Malls are being revamped deliberately to improve brand mix, shopper experience, and long-term rental profile. While this has resulted in short-term dips in trading occupancy, we expect these interventions to unlock meaningful consumption and rental upside over the next 12 to 18 months.

items.statement: Adding ~7 million sq ft retail leasable area by 2030, taking portfolio to ~18 million sq ft
items.quote: We are looking to add around 7 million sq. ft. of leasable area to our operational retail portfolio by 2030. This will take us from 11.5 million to around over 18 million sq. ft. in the retail side.

items.statement: Indore mall access constrained by highway construction; expect strong growth after completion in 12 months
items.quote: There is a bit of a constraint in access to the mall at this point in time, but with the highway activities scheduled to be completed in the next 12 months, we believe that access to the mall will improve multi -fold, and we should see very strong growth in consumption going forward in Indore in FY27 and beyond.

items.statement: Consumption impact from macro risks expected to be transitory
items.quote: So, from that perspective, if the catchment profile is strong and India macro story remains intact, we believe that consumption impact, if any, would be transitory in nature.

items.statement: Secured additional FSI of 136,000 sq meters at Lower Parel for Rs 586 crores in Q4 FY25
items.quote: We have secured additional FSI of approx. 136,000 sq. meters at our Lower Parel development for a premium payment of approx. Rs. 586 crores during Q4 FY25.

items.statement: Residential launches Tower 8 & 9 at One Bangalore West and Alipore Kolkata planned for Q2/Q3 FY26
items.quote: We continue to evaluate the timing and approach for future residential launches, including Tower 8 and 9 at One Bangalore West and our Alip ore project in Kolkata , and both of these projects are scheduled to launch during FY26, maybe in the Q2 and Q3 around that time.

items.statement: Expect credit growth 2-3% above systemic growth in FY26
items.quote: If you see the visibility, we would be 2%-3% more than the credit growth.

items.statement: Target slippages of Rs 650-700 crore for FY26 with recoveries exceeding slippages
items.quote: So we gave a guidance of Rs. 800 crores for the current year and we closed at Rs. 815 and for the next year, we will be around Rs. 650-Rs. 700 crores. That is the number we are looking at. But in terms of provisions, we will also have, D1, doubtful 1 to doubtful 2 extra provisions we will have for the year which we may have to take. Otherwise, we are quite confident of recovery, will be more than

items.statement: NIM guidance of 3.5-3.7% for FY26 with +/-10 bps range
items.quote: Yes, I will confirm we will be around 3.5-3.7. This is what we are looking at and 2%-3% more than the industry growth is what we are looking at if the visibility is good for the current year.

items.statement: NIM expected to stay at 3.6% +/-10 bps despite rate cuts due to deposit repricing benefits and fixed rate gold loans
items.quote: As discussed in earlier calls, our NIM is in the range of 3.60% for the past few quarters and we hope to maintain the same trend with (+/-10) bps.

items.statement: Plan to open 50-75 branches in FY26 taking total to 925-950
items.quote: We opened about 75 branches in the current Financial Year '25. We had been consistently opening about 50-75 every year except during the COVID years. So this year, from 875, probably we will be taking it to about another 50-75 basis points, 75 branches. If let us say, things are favorable, we may also open few more branches.

items.statement: Retail book target exit of Rs 3,000 crore in FY26 from ~Rs 1,000 crore currently
items.quote: So to be precise, we are looking to exit this year with Rs. 3,000 crores. Rs. 3,000 crores should be the exit number for retail for this year as we speak.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio expected at 48-50% in FY26 due to retail investment, then declining
items.quote: Our cost-to-income ratio for FY '25 is at 47.77% as against the expectation of 48%-50%. This is mainly due to some expenses we have planned for retail vertical in FY '24-25 were postponed for the next year that is FY '25-26. Hence this year CIR will be around 48%-50% and start reducing once the benefit of retail vertical starts showing results.

items.statement: MSME outstanding growth was 23% in FY25 driven by digital lending platform
items.quote: Actually speaking, the outstanding MSME growth was 23% for the current Financial Year.

items.statement: Low exposure to export-oriented units; Coimbatore textile exposure improving after Bangladesh competition eased
items.quote: See, currently, we did not have significant exposure to the export oriented units- it is low to middle single digit only. Within that, Coimbatore built textile exposures for the last 3-4 years, they had the impact because of the strong competition from the Bangladesh. After the regime change and things like that, there was some advantage for them and currently and it is better than what it was the

items.statement: Gold loans migrated from floating to fixed rate in July 2024 to protect margins in falling rate cycle
items.quote: We moved on July from floating to fixed, the gold loan rate.

items.statement: Risk-weighted assets at Rs 39,900 crore as of Q4 FY25
items.quote: Rs. 39,900 crores, the overall risk weighted assets.

items.statement: Deposit growth to align with credit growth targeting LDR of 85%
items.quote: We wanted to keep the LDR at 85. So that is the number which we are looking at and our growth will also be basis the same.

items.statement: Savings bank rate cut by 25 bps in Feb 2025 and term deposit rates cut in April 2025; benefits to reflect in 2-3 quarters
items.quote: During the middle of the quarter, we have also decreased our Savings Bank rate by 25 bps and during the month of April, we have reduced our term deposit rate in line with the reduction in repo rates. The benefits of rate reduction and deposits will start reflecting in the coming quarters.

items.statement: EBLR portfolio saw ~10 bps yield impact from 25 bps repo cut; cumulative 100 bps cut may transmit 50-75 bps to yields
items.quote: It could be 50-75. Some lag will have.

items.statement: Personal loans of Rs 1,200 crore are secured loans to existing MSME borrowers, not unsecured
items.quote: This is not an unsecured loan. This is a loan given to my existing borrowers or MSME under the personal loan headline, which also collateral with us.

items.statement: Credit growth target of 14% to 15% for FY26
items.quote: Sir, credit growth for this year also, we would like to grow at around 14% to 15%. That will continue.

items.statement: Deposit growth target of 12% to 13% for FY26
items.quote: We have got our strategy in place and our plan is to grow deposit to the tune of 12% to 13% in this financial year.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio target of around 44% or 42% by end of FY26
items.quote: And going forward, since income is increasing, we are expecting to maintain it at around 44% or maybe 100 or 200 bps lower than that, around 42% by the end of this year.

items.statement: NIM target of around 3.50% for FY26
items.quote: NIM, we are looking at maintaining at around 3.50%. There will be some pressure. And I think around 3.5% we'll be able to maintain at year-end.

items.statement: CASA growth target of around 10% for FY26
items.quote: The plan which is there for CASA growth is around 10%, that is what we are looking at.

items.statement: CD ratio target of around 80% to 81% for FY26
items.quote: We'll try to maintain it around 80%, 81%, sir.

items.statement: Recovery target of around INR4,500 crores for FY26
items.quote: For this year, our recovery target is around INR4,500 crores for the entire year.

items.statement: ROA target to maintain 1.12% and improve by few basis points by end of FY26
items.quote: We will try to maintain it. And by the end of this financial year, we'll try to improve it by an additional some few basis points.

items.statement: IT budget approved at INR1,700 crores plus for FY26
items.quote: This year, we have got the budget approved from the Board amounting to INR1,700 crores plus.

items.statement: Plan to raise INR1,400 crores via QIP to reduce government shareholding
items.quote: And going forward, to comply with the SEBI guideline of minimum shareholding, we are raising capital from the market to bring down Government of India shareholding further.

items.statement: International book NIM expected at 3.42% to 3.43%
items.quote: 3.42% to 3.43%, yes, around that, yes, almost.

items.statement: MTNL account of INR2,332 crores became NPA in Q4 FY25; 100% provision made
items.quote: One account of MTNL that is already there in the public domain, all of you know that. So, INR2,332 crores of MTNL account became NPA in February this year in Q4.

items.statement: No stress seen in MSME portfolio; slippages around INR200-250 crores per quarter in RAM segment
items.quote: Whatever slippages a re happening it is happening every quarter around INR200 crores, INR250 crores of slippage happening and it's mostly in RAM only, a small value

items.quote: We will be maybe last quarter of this financial year. In this year, we will be shifting to new tax regime.

And in second half, you should see a significant climb back in.

items.quote: We are very cautiously optimistic about H2 of the coming year when we should come back to growth. items.statement: BALIC structural margin improvement from cost cuts and operating leverage; full benefit expected by FY27, visible from H2 FY26
items.quote: We have also taken significant calls on cost structures, looking at more productive investments, removing wastage, inefficiency and in some places significant cost cuts. This is helping us leverage to an extent. You saw that operating leverage show up in Q4.

items.quote: Overall, on an RWRP basis, the mix of business for Quarter 4 stood at : par with 21%, non-PAR savings at 27%, term at a very healthy 6%, annuity 6% and ULIPs at about 40%.

items.quote: During the quarter, BALIC's new business growth was muted, which is in line with the industry, largely impacted by the new surrender regulations and the stock market volatility.

items.statement: Bajaj Markets: 8.6 lakh consumers on digital platforms in Q4 FY25; BFSI lending disbursements Rs.1,865 cr vs Rs.1,636 cr YoY; 96 unique partnerships; cash profitable for two consecutive quarters; no capital infusion since Mar'22

BFSI lending disbursements, including secured, unsecured and both through BFL and outside partnerships for the quarter stood at 1,865 crores for the quarter as against 1,636 crores for the same period last year.

items.quote: the second one first, Axis is 22% of our business and overall, if you notice that most of our peers their largest bank is upwards of 40% to 50% to 60% as well, and it was a studied strategy that we shall not be dependent on

items.statement: Volume CAGR over 25%, profitability growth exceeding 35%, ROIC above 25% targeted for Vision 2029
items.quote: The company has set ambitious targets including a volume CAGR of over 25%, profitability growth exceeding 35% and ROIC above 25%.

items.quote: The company has capex planning totaling INR1,500 crores to be deployed by FY '28. Encompassing both expansion of existing operations and investment in new verticals, including lithium-ion, paper, rubber and steel recycling.

items.statement: FY26 capex of around INR375 crores planned across lead, rubber, plastic, Dominican Republic and Romania expansion
items.quote: So we are planning to do a capex of around INR375-odd crores this year and the overall plan is to do a capex of around INR1,500 crores in the next 3 years.

items.statement: Rubber recycling capacity of 60,000 MTPA in FY26, split between H1 and H2, including pyrolysis and crumb rubber/sheet plants
items.quote: So it's around -- the total capacity in this year would be around 60,000 metric ton per annum. Part of it will come in H1 and part of it will come in H2.

items.statement: Sustainable EBITDA per kg guidance: Lead INR18-19, Aluminium INR14-15, Plastic INR10-11 for FY26
items.quote: So currently this year as we've been mentioning that we had certain arbitrage opportunities, so the total EBITDA per ton is around INR20 per ton -- or INR20 per kilogram or INR20,000 per ton. But our guidance is that on a sustainable basis, we can expect a INR18 to INR19 per kg in lead with a slight improvement of say around INR0.25 or INR0.50 every year based -- because of better economies of sca

items.statement: Aluminium EBITDA per kg guided at INR14-15, Plastic at INR10-11 for FY26
items.quote: So aluminum also would be around INR14 to INR15 per kilogram going forward. And for plastic also it is going to be INR10 to INR11 per kilogram, at least for this year.

items.statement: Domestic scrap sourcing rose to 43% from 30% YoY due to BWMR and EPR regulations, 48% in Q4 FY25
items.quote: Stringent government regulations under BWMR and EPR have driven a significant 60% rise in domestically sourced scrap. 43% of the total scrap was sourced from domestic market as compared to 30% in last year.

items.statement: Value-added products contributed 46% of revenue in FY25, targeting 50% by Vision 2029
items.quote: 46% of the revenue came from value -added products which is in line with our Vision 2029 of achieving 50% revenues from this category.

items.statement: Trump tariffs may cause short-term logistics cost increases but impact limited due to global operations flexibility
items.quote: Yes. So definitely because what will happen is that a lot of containers would get stuck in China because -- so that definitely on a short term basis, logistic cost could go up and would impact the profits if -- but right now it's not having any impact right now as we speak.

items.statement: RCM notification for battery scrap expected in upcoming GST Council meeting, could accelerate formal sector shift to 75% in FY26
items.quote: We are expecting that to come in this year in lead scrap also, in battery scrap also which got delayed because of some omission that government omitted by mistake battery scrap in this. So once that will come into picture, I think the shift over will take faster than we were expecting earlier.

items.statement: Tax rate guided at 12-13% blended globally, India standalone at 30% with MAT credits of INR30 crores over 6-7 years
items.quote: So the blended tax rate should be closer to 12% to 13% on a global basis. So as we are already considering the MAT credit in India also, so the tax rate for India is also going to be same. No change.

items.statement: ROCE benchmark of 25%+ for all businesses, consolidated ROCE expected in 25-30% range
items.quote: So it would be prudent to assume ROCE in the range of 25% to 30% over the period of time. Yogesh Malhotra: Yes, sir.

items.statement: Lithium-ion battery recycling pilot and rubber recycling facility in Mundra to be operational by H1 FY26
items.quote: We are progressing steadily with the setup of a pilot lithium -ion battery recycling project and our inaugural rubber recycling facility in Mundra, India. Both are scheduled to be operational by the first half of FY '26.

items.statement: Acquired waste tire recycling plant in Romania with 18,000 MTPA capacity for INR40 crores (INR32 crores by GNBV)
items.quote: A special purpose vehicle in Romania has been formed with Gravita Netherlands holding an 80% equity stake and management control, while local partners hold the remaining shares. With a total investment of INR40 crores of which INR32 crores is contributed by GNBV.

items.statement: Capacity target of 700,000+ MTPA by FY28 from 334,000 MTPA in FY25
items.quote: Gravita continues to scale operations having reached 3.34 lakh metric ton per annum in capacity in FY '25 and is aiming for a significant milestone of 700,000 plus MTPA by FY '28.

items.statement: FY26 expected to be a strong year of growth with a strong order book currently
items.quote: See, I think we remain confident that FY26 will also connect to a strong year of growth. While I can't comment specifically on what the operator plans are. But I believe our order book is quite strong that I'm seeing currently.

items.statement: Capex declined ~24% in FY25 vs FY24; management not confirming if FY25 is new normal but expects tower and tenancy growth to remain strong
items.quote: Again, I don't specifically talk about any numbers. This year, we had a significant tower rollout and tenancy rollouts as well. Obviously, higher the tenancy is lower the -- tenancy is not the same cost as putting a new tower. So, I don't want to say what specific trend you will see. But all I can say, the tower and tenancy growth will remain strong in the coming year.

items.statement: Order book is quite strong currently
items.quote: But I believe our order book is quite strong that I'm seeing currently.

items.statement: Reported EBITDA margin flat YoY at 56.9% in Q4 FY25; down 35.8 pp QoQ due to Q3 one-time write-back of Rs. 30 billion
items.quote: The EBITDA margin was largely flat year -on-year at 56.9%, but declined by 35.8 percentage points sequentially. items.statement: Reported energy margin -5.2% in Q4 FY25; adjusted for common control transaction impact, energy margin improved to -2%
items.quote: Our reported energy margins were -5.2% in Q4, which includes accounting impact of common control transaction as explained earlier. Adjusted for this, energy margins improved to -2%, driven by seasonality and reduction in diesel consumption.

items.statement: Diesel consumption reduced 6% YoY in FY25; added 15,000+ solar sites taking total base close to 30,000
items.quote: Through electrification of non -electrified sites, deployment of energy storage solutions and a continued expansion of our renewable energy portfolio, we further reduced the diesel consumption by 6% year -on-year in FY25. We also added more than 15,000 solar sites during the year, taking the total base close to 30,000.

items.statement: Industry added ~40,000 5G base stations in FY25; total base ~475,000; 5G loading continues to contribute meaningfully to loading revenues
items.quote: When it comes to 5G, close to 40,000 5G base stations were rolled out in the industry in the last financial year, with a total base now standing at close to 475,000. While the pace of deployment has moderated, 5G -related loading continues to contribute mea ningfully to our overall loading revenues.

items.statement: Average data consumption per user grew 15% YoY to 27.5 GB in Q2 FY25; 5G data consumption grew 18% QoQ and contributed 26.5% of total data usage in Q3 FY25
items.quote: The average data consumed per user per month across the top three operators grew 15 % year-on-year to 27.5 GB for the quarter ended September 2024, with the total data consumed growing by 20% year-on-year. items.quote: So typically, if you see Q4 is the time where we are setting ourselves for monsoon as well. items.quote: See, the number that you see is roughly a 1.1% growth sequentially that probably without the acquisition would have been something like a 2.5% growth sequentially.

items.quote: We would continue with our similar growth rate of between 17% to 20% overall level and have the trust in us.
