items.quote: Going forward, I believe the gross margin should not grow any further but may remain largely range bound as we stand ready to grow market share in core growth categories.

items.statement: Apparel ASPs degrew marginally due to seasonal mix; no further correction planned
items.quote: Apparel ASPs degrew marginally primarily due to lower winter and higher summer seasonal mix in the quarter. There is no further correction planned in ASPs, which should remain in the similar range going forward.

items.statement: Youth share increased from 22-23% to 30-33%; Gen Z driving consumption
items.quote: Relatively, we used to receive around 22%, 23% of youth, which is under 25%. And now we see that has gone up to 30%, 33%.

items.statement: Expect continued growth from rural income improvement and good monsoon
items.quote: We believe the farm income and then the rural income is supposed to grow. There's going to be more employment. There's definitely going to be more economical betterment or better consumption that the consumers would have.

items.statement: Non-apparel categories like beauty, jewelry, wearables launched but will remain small; 2-3% mix shift possible
items.quote: There could be a 2% or 3% shift which can happen over the period of time.

items.statement: Risk of manufacturer constraints if export opportunities draw capacity away
items.quote: there is one risk that we see that the amount of manufacturers available -- good manufacturers available in the market could be a little constrained going forward if cont inued overexpansion or overinvestment doesn't happen in this particular sector

items.statement: GST credit accumulation growing; added INR 14-20 crores this year; difficult to resolve for growing business
items.quote: There is a net addition of probably INR 14 crores or INR 15 crores in this year as well, almost INR20 crores this year. So that remains a challenge.

items.statement: No long-term debt; growth financed through internal accruals and working capital limits
items.quote: There is no long -term debt on t he books, and we remain comfortable on the cash front with ample working capital limits available to leverage future growth, which will be financed through internal accruals

items.statement: ESOP expense normalized to INR 8-10 crores annually going forward
items.quote: But largely, you should have around INR8 crores to INR10 crores of expenditure on ESOP going forward, which is agai n coming from the actuarial valuation

items.statement: Double-digit volume growth expected for CY2025 in India
items.quote: We have always said that we can grow in double digit, and this is what we are expecting happening this year and we are quite comfortable with that guidance.

items.statement: Capex guidance of ~Rs 3,100 crore for CY2025, ~Rs 900 crore remaining to be spent
items.quote: We have given the guidance of ~ Rs. 3,100 crore for this year and we are on track and appx. Rs. 900 crore out of which is yet to be spent.

items.statement: Bihar plant commissioning May 1, 2025; Meghalaya plant by end of May 2025
items.quote: Well, Bihar is getting started tomorrow, May 1, 2025 and Meghalaya will be by the end of May 2025.

items.statement: South Africa EBITDA margin at 14.4% in Q1 CY2025, expected to be maintained for the year
items.quote: No, it used to be ~ 10% odd, and we have reached ~ 14.4% and we expect to maintain 14.4% for the year.

items.statement: India EBITDA margin guidance floor at 21%, currently above that with backward integration driving improvement
items.quote: We have always said that 21% in soft drink industry is a very good EBITDA margin. So, we have stuck to that but we keep trying and making sure that we achieve better than that.

items.statement: South Africa volumes grew ~13% over trailing four quarters to 141 million cases
items.quote: We achieved 141 million cases in South Africa over the trailing four quarters marking a growth of ~13% over the same period last year.

items.statement: Low/no sugar products mix increased to ~59% of consolidated sales volumes in Q1 CY2025
items.quote: Aligned with our growing focus on healthier beverages, the mix of the low sugar , no sugar products increased to ~59% on consolidated basis of the total sales volumes in Q1 CY2025.

items.statement: Raw material costs stable; packaging slightly lower due to oil prices, sugar slightly higher, overall comfortable
items.quote: We don't see the raw material prices going up significantly. Fortunately for us oil prices are not going up, so our packaging material pricing are quite stable or rather even slightly lower. Sugar slightly has gone up, so it balances out and we are quite comfortable with our production costs.

items.statement: India beverage market underpenetrated with ~12 million FMCG outlets, VBL reaching ~4 million, significant headroom for growth
items.quote: There are ~ 12 million FMCG outlets and we are reaching out to about ~ 4 million only. So there is still so much room for everyone to add new outlets through increased GTM and by putting more chilling equipment.

items.statement: Tanzania and Ghana deals on hold due to pending clearances; will not proceed without full regulatory approval
items.quote: It's just that we have not got the clearances what we were supposed to get. And in the African countries, till we get full clarity, being a listed company, we are not going to take control of the company.

items.statement: Interim dividend of Rs 0.50 per share (25% of face value) approved, cash outflow ~Rs 1,691 million
items.quote: In line with our dividend policy, the Board of Directors has approved an interim dividend of 25% of face value, i.e., Rs. 0.50 per share, resulting in a total cash outflow of ~Rs. 1,691 million.

items.statement: CRISIL upgraded long-term credit rating to CRISIL AAA Stable
items.quote: Lastly, we are pleased to share that CRISIL has upgraded our long-term credit rating to CRISIL AAA Stable.

items.statement: PepsiCo brand salience in South Africa increased from 15% to ~20%, growing faster than own brands
items.quote: Our Pepsi brand sales are going up from 15% and it's close to 20% now. All our products are growing including our homegrown brands. PepsiCo product our growing at a faster pace.

items.statement: Zimbabwe volumes expected to normalize from Q2 CY2025 after sugar tax impact absorbed; not expecting huge growth
items.quote: We think from this quarter onwards we expect it to come back to normal. However, we are not expecting huge growth.

items.statement: Domino's account loss less than low single digit volume impact, no material effect on overall growth
items.quote: It was less than low single digit.

items.statement: International Security booked AUD 150 million of permanent revenue new wins in FY25, impacting FY26 and beyond
items.quote: Over the last year, they have booked AU$150 million of permanent revenue, which will obviously impact not just FY '26, but also the subsequent years.

items.statement: India Security contract churning is done; margins at 5.5-5.6% and expected to gradually return to 6% pre-COVID levels
items.quote: I think in Security business in India, I think the contract churning exercise is pretty much done. Therefore, we are reporting 5.5%, 5.6%. And I think gradually, as we gain more operating leverage that will go back to 6% levels, which is the pre - COVID normal level.

items.statement: FM business inching towards 5% EBITDA margin; expects to be out of the woods on margin in coming first quarter
items.quote: In FM, it has taken more time than before, but even FM now is inching towards 5% EBITDA margin. And I think hopefully, in the coming first quarter, you will see that even the FM business is out of the woods as far as the margin is concerned.

items.statement: International Security EBITDA margin back near 4%, expected to operate in 4-4.5% band going forward
items.quote: As far as international is concerned, on the international side, the pre-COVID EBITDA margin level was roughly 4.5%. International is back at close to 4% already, and you can expect it to operate at that 4%, 4.5% band going forward as well.

items.statement: Labour law implementation timing uncertain due to national security focus; wage reset for security workers delayed
items.quote: But I think the whole country's focus now is on different and more pressing national security matters. So, it's very hard to say, when the labour laws will get implemented, and the labour laws effectively are the trigger for minimum wage reset for security workers.

items.statement: No formal guidance given; references historical quarterly revenue and EBITDA CAGR of ~15% over last 7 years
items.quote: I don't think we give any guidance, but your last 7 years of listed performance will tell you that our quarterly CAGR for revenue is close to 15% and our quarterly CAGR for EBITDA also is close to 15%, 16%.

items.statement: Goodwill impairment of INR 306 crores taken for Henderson, SLV, Uniq, ADIS acquired in 2019; no further significant impairment expected
items.quote: Now what we've decided is that we have taken the pending impairment requirements with regards to Henderson and also the two other major acquisitions that happened in 2019, which are SLV and Uniq. So, we have taken all those impairments, and that's the reason why you see this INR 306 crore impairment entry.

items.statement: Remaining INR 700 crores goodwill relates to MSS, DTSS, RHPL; auditors confirm enough headroom, no further impairment indicated
items.quote: The remaining INR 700 crores goodwill which is appearing in the books is mainly related to the past acquisition like MSS, DTSS, RHPL. And during the process of account finalization, the auditor has done the impairment testing of all the entities. And other than these three entities for which we have taken the impairment, there is no indication, there's enough headroom available as per the impairme

items.statement: Australia order wins (AUD 180M in FY25) result of 2-3 years BD investment; includes defence and Sydney Trains contracts; such large wins may not repeat annually
items.quote: So what you're seeing this year is a result of 2 to 3 years of investment that we have done. And we have landed on some meaty contracts, one being defence and another being Sydney trains locally. So, these kinds of events don't happen every year.

items.statement: Australian labour cost pressure driven by manpower shortage, not minimum wage increases; early signs of easing
items.quote: And that situation, as and when it eases, we are seeing early signs of that easing. But as and when it eases, will reduce our pressure on the cost of labo ur as we move forward. So it has got nothing to do with the minimum wage side. It is more the availability of manpower

items.statement: No equity dilution needed; net debt/EBITDA at 0.7x, average debt cost 7-7.5%, negotiating rates down
items.quote: We don't need equity dilution at this point in time to the best of my understanding. We are operating at 0.7x net debt to EBITDA. There is enough headroom for debt, and there is no pressure on us.

items.statement: Cash Logistics DRHP filed with SEBI in Q4 FY25; received first feedback from SEBI yesterday; listing aims to bring capital back to SIS to reduce net debt
items.quote: The cash business, DRHP, we received first comments or first feedback from SEBI just yesterday. So, I think that project is coming along well. That listing exercise also aims to bring back capital into SIS to further reduce our net debt situation.

items.statement: Management priorities: revenue growth (currently 8-10%, want faster), margin improvement, better free cash generation (OCF/EBITDA), higher return ratios (ROCE 15%, want upward)
items.quote: As regards to the management priorities, I think management priorities always are on four metrics for us like any other business, revenue growth, margin improvement, better free cash generation, which is OCF to EBITDA and higher return ratios. So we continue to work on all four metrics. We are growing at roughly 8%, 10%. We want to grow faster.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 consolidated EBITDA INR 165 crores (4.8% margin), highest ever; India Security 5.6%, FM 4.7% (+80bps YoY), International 4% (up from 3.8% Q3)
items.quote: On a consolidated level, EBITDA grew by 10.1% year -on-year to INR 165 crores, which is the highest ever reported by SIS and it translates to an EBITDA margin of 4.8%. India Security reported an EBITDA margin of 5.6%, up from 5.5% in Q4 FY '24. FM has reported an EBITDA margin of 4.7%, which is 80 basis points higher on a year -on-year basis.

items.statement: Targeting advances growth of 15-17% CAGR over next three years with secured mix over 55% by FY27
items.quote: Given the current macro-economic environment, we are targeting an advances growth of 15 – 17% CAGR over the next three years, with a strategic focus on increasing the secured mix. We expect secured advances to constitute over 55%+ of the total advances by FY27.

items.statement: Targeting credit cost of 1.5-1.6% over next 2-3 years
items.quote: While credit costs are expected to remain elevated in H1FY26, we are targeting to reach 1.5–1.6% of credit cost over the next 2-3 years, based on our relentless focus on improving portfolio quality through robust risk management and aided by improving MFI cycle

items.statement: Targeting RoA of 1.8-1.9% over next 2-3 years
items.quote: Our focus remains on a steady and sustainable improvement in profitability, with a clear glide path toward improving RoA to 1.8–1.9% over the next 2-3 years, driven by better asset quality, improvement in other income and operating leverage

items.statement: Expect NIM to moderate by 50-60 bps over next 2-3 years as secured mix increases
items.quote: I think as our secured mix increases further, over the next 3 years, we should expect, I think, the NIMs to come down by, say, another 50 to 60 basis points over the next 2-3 years.

items.statement: Expect operating expenses to assets ratio to increase by 10-20 bps over next two years
items.quote: As a result of these investments, we expect the operating expenses to assets ratio to increase by 10–20 bps from current levels over the next two years.

items.statement: Targeting net EEB portfolio growth of INR 5,000 crore in FY26
items.quote: We have also kept a guidance of around INR5,000 crores of incremental growth in this EEB segment.

items.statement: Q4FY25 NIM at 6.7%, down from 6.9% in Q3FY25; full year FY25 NIM at 7.1% within guided 7-7.5% range
items.quote: Net interest margin for Q4FY25 came in at 6.7%, down from 6.9% in Q3FY25, reflecting similar pressures from the secured loan mix and higher slippages. However, on a full year basis, the NIM remained resilient at 7.1%, just 28 basis points lower year-on-year and within the guided range of 7% to 7.5%.

items.statement: Secured book growth expected to moderate margins on risk-adjusted basis
items.quote: The planned increase in the share of our secured loan book is expected to have an impact on NIM. As a result, we anticipate some moderation in margins over the coming years on a risk adjusted basis.

items.statement: EEB portfolio declined 9% YoY but grew 1% QoQ to INR 56,544 crore; non-EEB book grew 29% YoY
items.quote: The EEB portfolio saw a decline of 9% year-on-year, although there was a marginal increase of 1% quarter-on-quarter, reaching INR56,544 crores. This decline is primarily due to portfolio controls we implemented in response to the elevated risk in the microfinance industry. On the other hand, growth in the non-EEB book, which now represents 59% of our total advances, was strong at 29% year-on-year

items.statement: MFI sector stress expected to gradually improve in coming months; EEB disbursements muted in Q1FY26, pickup from Q2, normalization by Q3-Q4
items.quote: I think the first quarter is going to be a muted one. And I think quarter 2 onwards, the disbursal should pick up. But by the end of quarter 3, I think we will have, hopefully, a normal year -- quarter the way it was there prior to a couple of years, and that should stabilize over quarter 3 and quarter 4.

items.statement: Credit costs elevated at 3.9% in Q4FY25 but improved from 4.1% in Q3; FY25 credit cost at 2.9% down 50 bps YoY
items.quote: Credit costs, including the standard assets, for the quarter stood at 3.9% of advances, down from 4.1% in the previous quarter. For FY '25, the credit cost declined to 2.9%, representing nearly 50 basis points year-on-year reduction.

items.statement: Gross NPA stable at 4.7%, Net NPA at 1.3%; PCR including write-offs at 86.5%
items.quote: Despite an increase in slippages and higher upgrades & recoveries, our headline asset quality remains largely stable with Gross NPA at 4.7% and Net NPA at 1.3%. PCR (incl. the technical write-off portfolio), was higher at 86.5%.

items.statement: EEB DPD pool (SMA 0,1,2) improved to 3.4% of EEB advances from 3.8% in Q3, absolute reduction of INR 223 crore
items.quote: The overall EEB DPD pool, SMA-0, 1, and 2, stood at INR1,895 crores, representing 3.4% of EEB advances in Q4 compared to 3.8% in Q3 FY '25, representing a 40 basis points improvement. This reflects an absolute quarter-on-quarter reduction of INR223 crores

items.statement: Investing in people, technology, branches; opened many branches in Q4FY24; investing in core banking upgrade, loan origination systems, credit card launch
items.quote: So actually, yes, basically, 3 things. One is that we have opened many branches in the last quarter of the previous financial year, not this year. And that expenses are adding up, but we will definitely get the benefit of business from these branches going forward. The second is that the investment in IT. The depreciation cost is a major opex cost, but that's, as Rajeev has said that both were nec

items.statement: Reduced savings and term deposit rates effective May 1; top term deposit bracket cut 30 bps from 8.05% to 7.75%; 40% of loan book EBLR-linked with immediate transmission
items.quote: So we have also reduced our interest rates on both savings bank and term deposits. So the rationalization has already been taken place. It will come effect from 1st May onwards. So we are expecting that around 30 basis points where we were giving on t he highest term deposit bracket, so 8.05%, it has come down to 7.75

items.statement: Secured book grew 32% YoY to 50.5% of advances; retail term deposits grew 30% YoY; retail deposits (CASA+TD) at 69% of total deposits
items.quote: In this quarter, our secured book grew by 32% YoY, improving the secured mix to 50.5%, compared to 42% in FY24. Retail term deposits grew strongly at 30% YoY, highlighting the growing trust and engagement from individual customers. CASA deposits now represent 31% of the total deposit base, bringing the total share of Retail Deposits (CASA + Retail Term Deposits) to 69%.

items.statement: Board recommended dividend of INR 1.50 per share for FY25
items.quote: Furthermore, I am pleased to inform you that the Board of Directors has recommended a dividend of INR 1.50 per share, subject to the approval of the shareholders at the forthcoming Annual General Meeting.

items.statement: Vadraj acquisition will enable total cement capacity of 31 million tons per annum by Q3 FY27
items.quote: This acquisition will enable us to reach a total cement capacity of 31 million tons per annum by the third quarter of FY'27, further strengthening our position in the industry.

items.statement: Vadraj refurbishment and new Kutch grinding unit capex increased to Rs 1,500 crore phased over 3 years at Rs 600 crore, Rs 600 crore, Rs 300 crore
items.quote: Hence the overall CAPEX needed to rebuild Kutch facility, Surat facility and also put up a GU in Kutch will now be turned up from the original number of Rs. 1,200 crores to about Rs. 1,500 crores but the timeline to do all these things will be in three calendar years of 2025, 2026 and 2027 and the phasing of the investments would be in the tune of about 600, 600 and 300 in the next 3 years, 24 to

items.statement: Maintenance capex for existing operations limited to Rs 100-150 crore per year to fund Vadraj capex from internal accruals
items.quote: And along with that, to fund this CAPEX from internal accruals, we will pare down our capital expenditure to run the current operations to a max of 100 crores to 150 crores so that we have adequate cash flow in the organization to fund the CAPEX of Vadraj.

items.statement: Vadraj acquisition funded via Rs 600 crore long-term debt, Rs 1,200 crore via CCDs and CCPs, plus Rs 1,200 crore bridge loan for up to 6 months
items.quote: Out of this Rs. 1,800 crores of financing which we need to do upfront, we will take a long-term debt of Rs. 600 crores in Nuvoco's books and then the balance Rs. 1,200 crores will be through instruments like CCDs and CCPs which will be on a long-term maturity.

items.statement: Targeting additional Rs 100-150 per ton cost savings over next 2-3 years from railway sidings, AFR ramp-up, productivity programs
items.quote: We are targeting close to about Rs. 100 to Rs. 150 per ton in the next 2 to 3 years.

items.statement: Net debt target maintained at Rs 3,500-4,000 crore at end of Vadraj capex cycle despite Rs 3,000 crore investment
items.quote: But suffice to say, the target which we have is 3 years cycle from now, we certainly will be back at anywhere between Rs. 3,500 to Rs. 4,000 crores.

items.statement: Vadraj ramp-up plan: 0.3-0.4 million tons in FY27 H2, 2 million tons in FY28, higher thereafter; supported by Project White channel expansion in Gujarat
items.quote: In FY'27, half month, probably 0.3 mt - 0.4 million tons from Vadraj will be sold in Gujarat. And in FY'28, we are targeting a full year, 2 million tons sale in Gujarat and in FY '29 this will go to higher number and then on the build up average.

name: Star Health and Allied Insurance Company Ltd

items.statement: Medium-term vision to double top line and triple profit on IFRS basis by FY2028
items.quote: We have also guided for an FY' 2028 medium term kind of vision where we would be doubling our top line and tripling our profit on the IFRS basis. We continue to stand by that guidance.

items.statement: Confident of profitable FY2026 but no specific loss ratio guidance given
items.quote: We are geared up and confident for a profitable FY '2026.

items.statement: Price corrections of 20-40% on Banca portfolio and over 60% of retail portfolio repriced
items.quote: We have done pricing corrections on our Banca portfolio as well, in the range of 20% to 40%, and along with that, w e have taken a lot of measures on micro segmenting our markets, focusing on profitable markets, ensuring that we are picking up risks more

items.statement: Soft annual price increases planned to keep up with medical inflation

items.statement: Combined ratio 101.1% in FY2025 vs 97.3% in FY2024; claim ratio 70.7% vs 66.5%; expense ratio 30.4% vs 30.7%
items.quote: Our combined ratio in Financial Year '2025 stood at 101.1 % compared to 97.3% in Financial Year '2024. items.statement: Retail loss ratio ~68%; group loss ratio 89.8% in FY2025, group contribution reduced to 7% of GWP
items.quote: We are an 18 year old organization, and we are operating currently at 68% loss ratio on the retail side, and overall 70%.

items.statement: Fresh retail GWP grew 25% in FY2025; digital fresh business grew 71%; agency fresh growth 16% (19% in Q4)
items.quote: We saw strong growth in our fresh retail GWP, which grew by 25% for the year. This success was driven by renewed agent productivity, sharper campaign and the acceleration of our digital channels.

items.statement: Superstar policy garnered Rs.550 crore in FY2025; long-term policies 10% of portfolio vs 7% in FY2024; average sum insured up 10% to Rs.16 lakh
items.quote: A key product innovation this year was the launch of our superstar policy, which has garnered more than Rs.550 crore in Financial Year '2025.

items.statement: Group segment contribution reduced to 5% of premium in Q4 FY2025 from 9% in Q2; large group business to reduce significantly from Q1 FY2026
items.quote: Coming to the retail and group split just in Quarter 4, our retail contribution to the total premium was 95% and the group was only 5%.

items.statement: Claim frequency increase ~7-10% annually; severity held below 10% vs industry 10-15% medical inflation; elevated surgical claims in cancer, gynae, obstetrics, urology
items.quote: On frequency, the increase, while still in single digits, is closer to 10%, on the higher side of the single digits and that's a bit of an increasing trend than what we have earlier observed in the previous year.

items.statement: Reserves strengthened in Q4; outstanding claims reserve + IBNR at 14% of claims paid vs 11-12% earlier
items.quote: Yes, we have strengthened our reserves this quarter. See we don't have to go by one particular quarter. This business is no t about quarterly numbers , its annual business is in fact more than annual

items.statement: Core claim system transformation to complete by Q2 FY2026; >50% hospital billings digitized; app downloads 1 crore
items.quote: We are also undertaking a complete transformation of our core claim system, which will happen by Q2. That will again help us for better efficiencies in claims processing, preventing leakage and better fraud control.

items.statement: Agent network target: 1 million agents over next 3 years from current 7.75 lakh; added 74,000 agents in FY2025
items.quote: Over the next three years, we aim to expand this network to a million agents. This expansion is a key lever in our strategy to deepen insurance penetration, particularly across non-metro cities and emerging towns.

items.statement: Investment income Rs.1,260 crore in FY2025 (yield 7.7%); investment assets Rs.17,898 crore (+15.5%); equity allocation raised to ~15% of AUM
items.quote: Investment income in Financial Year '2025 has grown to Rs.1,260 crore versus Rs.1,171 crore in Financial Year '2024. The yield for Financial Year '2025 stood at 7.7%, our investment assets have grown by 15.5% and has reached Rs.17,898 crore in Financial Year '2025.

items.statement: PAT Rs.787 crore in FY2025 vs Rs.1,103 crore in FY2024; ROE 9.5%; solvency 2.21x vs 1.5x regulatory requirement
items.quote: Our PAT for Financial Year ‘2025 stood at Rs.787 crore, compared to Rs.1,103 crore in Financial Year ’2024. Our ROE for Financial Year ‘2025 stood at 9.5% . Solvency of the company as on March 31 st, 2025 was 2.21 times compared to the regulator y requirement of 1.5 times

items.statement: Claims NPS improved to 55 from 47; cashless claims <3 hours at 96%; claim rejection down to 10% from 13%; preventive health checks up 48%
items.quote: Our claims NPS stands at 55 for Financial Year ‘2025 versus 47 in Financial Year ’2024. Star Health and Allied Insurance Company Ltd. – 30th April, 2025 In terms of claims amount , our cashless claims lesser than 3 hours at 96% in Financial Year ’2025. Our claim rejection has come down to 10% in Financial Year ‘2025 versus 13% in Financial Year ’2024

items.statement: FY26 annual revenue growth guidance of 20% year-on-year
items.quote: In the press release, you have stated that the guidance for FY '26 is a 20% growth in revenue. Is that correct? Umang Soni: Yeah, that is annual guidance.

items.statement: Aspirational target of 30% annual revenue growth for next three years from FY27
items.quote: Our understanding was that for the next three years, we have an aspiration to grow 30% every year in revenue. Is that correct, Umang? Umang Soni: Correct.

items.statement: Double-digit revenue growth expected in Q1 FY26 with strong growth in subsequent quarters
items.quote: we w ould be achieving a double-digit growth in the next quarter as per the guidance given. Following that, in the coming quarters, quarter two , quarter three and quarter four also, we would be having tremendous growth

items.statement: EBITDA margins expected to remain in the range of 25% in coming quarters
items.quote: EBITDA margins expected to remain in the range of 25%.

items.statement: Management does not expect operating margins to return to 40% due to larger base and higher salaries
items.quote: It was very small; base was very small. I was not taking the salaries and all. So that's why we were getting that. So now I don't think that we are going to reach that number.

items.statement: Shift from T&M model to project-based delivery with resource selection freedom
items.quote: We have shifted the business approach also. What we have Ksolves India Limited (KSOLVES) Q4 & FY25 Post Earnings Conference Call May 3, 2025 realised that our major revenue is coming from the T&M model. T&M model is something where you supply the resources, but customer accept the resources after they taking

items.statement: Strong pipeline developed after strategic sales changes; customers discussing projects
items.quote: After these strategic changes, okay, now I can say that we have a good pipeline also for the next few quarters, and we can see that customers are now coming to us, they are talking to us, they are discussing their projects.

items.statement: No tariff impact; clients reducing on-site teams and requesting more offshore resources
items.quote: Honestly speaking, tariff effect could not or I can say that I do not see any impact of tariff till now, because our customers are reducing the team size on site, because they don't want to stop the work.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 revenue dipped 11.6% sequentially due to US holiday season delaying deal closures
items.quote: On a sequential basis, revenue saw a bit dip by 11.6%, primarily due to the holiday schedules in December and January, which extended the deal closures.

items.statement: Longer sales cycles for larger deals; $600K deal took 6 months for approval
items.quote: We have received approval for a project. The cost is approximately $600,000, and it took approximately six months, means we were chasing them continuously for six months.

items.statement: Working capital loan of ₹9 crores taken for short-term cash flow mismatches; to be repaid
items.quote: The working capital loan was availed during the year just to manage short-term cash flow mismatches on account of overall growth in the business.

items.statement: Dividends to continue but not on fixed policy; will adjust based on opportunities and cash generation
items.quote: On dividends, yes, we'll continue to give dividends, but not on a fixed policy or like we'll give it. But as and when we generate and we see any other opportunities, we'll be reducing or increasing the dividends.

items.statement: AUM growth guidance of 25% for FY26
items.quote: So this year also, I think we are giving a guidance of 25% what we gave last year after October till things get settled.

items.statement: Gross Stage 3 assets guidance to remain sub 2%
items.quote: Our guidance will be -- our Stage 3 assets will be sub 2%. That's where our guidance always stands.

items.statement: Overall credit cost guidance to remain sub 1%
items.quote: Having said that, the overall credit cost, our guidance will be sub 1%. This is where the range that we like to operate.

items.statement: Branch expansion guidance of 75-100 branches for FY26 including split branches
items.quote: So in general, we are good to open about close to 75 to 100 branches every year, including the split branch. So I think we will stick to that same guidance as far as this year is also concerned.

items.statement: Capital work in progress of INR62 crores for head office building construction
items.quote: See, the capital asset is a building that we had purchased for construction of head office premises. So that will come up over the next few years because this is a place that we have purchased, you need to demolish the existing building and construct.

items.statement: Incremental cost of funds dropped to 9.29% from 9.56%, a 27 bps decline
items.quote: On the cost of borrowing, our incremental cost of funds have dropped to 9.29% from 9.56%, nearly 27 bps drop.

items.statement: Expect 25-30 bps reduction in incremental cost of funds in FY26
items.quote: So our belief is that on an incremental basis, we should at least see 25 to 30 basis points of benefit coming through to us.

items.statement: Bank borrowing proportion may increase to 65-70% from current 63%

items.quote: Sell.do aims at revenue growth of 30% year -on-year in FY '26.

items.statement: Analytica aims to increase client base by 60% to 350+ in FY26
items.quote: We aim to increase client base by 60% and take it to 350 plus, still far off from the vast TAM of 40,000 -plus real estate RERA registered developers.

items.statement: Rental units under management to grow 15-20% incrementally over the year
items.quote: So we will keep on adding around 15% to 20% incrementally, and this will play out over the year in terms of rental units under management.

items.statement: HelloWorld targets 80% occupancy in existing supply base
items.quote: In FY '26, HelloWorld aims to achieve 80% occupancy with operational excellence, competitive offerings, and superior service.

items.statement: NestAway manages 37,500 rental units at 77% blended occupancy across 15 cities
items.quote: Our Rental busines s comprising of student living, co-living, family rentals and rental management software now operates across 15 cities in the country, managing 37,500 rental units at an average blended occupancy of 77

items.statement: PBT, EBITDA and adjusted EBITDA margins improved 17%, 15% and 12% year-on-year respectively
items.quote: Our PBT , EBITDA and adjusted EBITDA margins have shown improvement of 17%, 15% and 12%, respectively, year-on-year.

items.statement: Distribution segment delivered 14% net margin in FY25
items.quote: Being core tech business es, the segment delivered a healthy 14% net margin, underscoring strong profitability.

items.statement: Co-living growth is purely demand-led with 1 crore rental units needed in top 8 cities
items.quote: We have identified that there's close to 1 crore rental units that are required to be serviced for the co-living and student living community in top 8 cities in the country.

items.statement: Revenue mix expected to remain 55-60% Rental, 30-35% Distribution, 10-15% Capital for next couple of years
items.quote: Probably 25% to 35% will be the Distribution business and 10% to 15% will be Capital business. So we have seen this trend over the last few years, and we be lieve they will be in this range for next couple of years as well

items.statement: Rental and Capital segments will delay profitability to gain market share, targeting 50,000 then 1 lakh rental units
items.quote: This will require us to sort of spend on teams, spend on new markets, spend on new geographies, spend on new micro markets and will delay profitability for certain quarters. But this is essential because getting this market share in control first is our first goal.

items.statement: Rights issue concluded with final tranche providing ample growth capital to more than double revenues over 30 months
items.quote: This final tranche provides us with ample growth capital to expand our verticals and more than double our revenues over the next 30 months.

items.statement: SM-REIT license application at fag end, expecting real execution on new schemes in current quarter
items.quote: We are at the fag end of our application. And I think in this quarter we should have our real execution going on the new schemes front. So this year should be adding onto revenues from the SM-REIT space as far as FY '26.

items.statement: Plan to liquidate non-core buildings (INR 34 crores) in current or next financial year to unlock capital
items.quote: We would likely liquidate these assets, sell these assets, bring that capital in our balance sheet which should create some value in our existing business.

items.statement: IntraEdge AI intraday product in pilot; full rollout expected by early Q2 FY26
items.quote: It is in the pilot phase and you know we'll have full rollout shortly

items.statement: IntraEdge full rollout targeted for early Q2 FY26
items.quote: Yeah. So, I think by early Q2, it should be ready.

items.statement: Industry new customer additions fell 28% QoQ to 71.3 lakh in Q4 FY25
items.quote: Industry overall added 71.3 lakhs new customers in Q4 FY '25 compared to 98.7 lakhs in Q3 FY '25, which is a 28% QoQ, quarter-on-quarter decline.

items.statement: 5paisa new customer acquisitions dropped 19% QoQ to 91,000 in Q4 FY25
items.quote: Further for Q4 FY '25, we acquired 91,000 new customers, which is a 19% QoQ decline reflecting the broader industry trend of reduced retail participation.

items.statement: MTF interest rates cut effective Nov 1 leading to ~11% QoQ decline in MTF income
items.quote: In an effort to remain competitive, we reduced our MTF interest rates effective November 1st leading to about 11% decline in the MTF income of the quarter.

items.statement: FY25 revenue Rs 360 cr (-9% YoY), profit Rs 68 cr (+25% YoY), margin improved from 14% to 19%
items.quote: For the full fiscal year, FY '25, which is closing 24-25, we recorded revenue of 360 crores, which is a 9% decline from last year on YoY basis and a profit of INR 68 crores, which is a 25% increase on a YoY basis with our margins improving from 14% to 19%.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 total expenses reduced 9% QoQ to Rs 58 cr
items.quote: We've aligned our variable expenses with income trends and with further optimized cost resulting in a 9% reduction in total expense to INR 58 crores for this quarter.

items.statement: Client funding book stable at Rs 260 cr, down 2% QoQ
items.quote: Our client funding book remains stable at 260 crores, which is a very minor 2% QoQ drop.

items.statement: Mutual fund AUM crossed Rs 1,392 cr
items.quote: Our mutual fund AUM crossed thirteen hundred ninety-two crores.

items.statement: Launched F&O 360 upgrade, QTV live streaming, IntraEdge AI intraday tool, SIP via UPI autopay, charting upgrades, 15ms latency reduction
items.quote: Some of the key product rollouts have been an F&O 360 upgrade which is a completely enhanced upgraded F&O trading platform ordering advanced option strategies, expert research call, and a launch of QTV, which is a live expert led streaming and trading module.

items.statement: SEBI F&O regulations and muted markets caused 23% QoQ broking revenue decline and 36% QoQ ADTO drop
items.quote: Our broking revenue declined 23% QoQ primarily due to industry wide drop in derivative volumes.

items.statement: Net worth crossed Rs 600 cr on March 31, 2025; expects business to normalize over next few quarters
items.quote: Our network crossed INR 600 crores on March 31, 2025 and we believe in the markets and our business will normalize over the next few quarters allowing us to return to historical profitability levels.

items.statement: Management expects to maintain historical growth rates of around 20% in FY26 and plans for similar growth with corresponding expense budgeting.
items.quote: We've historically delivered about 20% or near 20% growth. In this year, we don't think our plans don't change much. We still expect to do that.

items.statement: Annuity revenue growth expected to recover to healthy rates within the next two quarters as delayed large deals go live.
items.quote: We do think that in next 2 quarters, we should be back on the track so that the growth rates can be restored on those annuity side of it.

items.statement: Order book stood at INR 1,664 crores at end of FY25, growing around 10% year-on-year.
items.quote: I think at the end of FY '25, our order book stood at -- yes, it is INR1,664 crores.

items.statement: Unexecuted order book expected to grow more than 20% year-on-year, relevant for FY26 execution.
items.quote: I expect more than 20% growth in that.

items.statement: Margins expand with growth above 20%; cost base loaded at 16-18% growth annually. FY26 margins depend on achieving healthy growth rates.
items.quote: Somewhere between 16% to 18% is what we load cost in the beginning of year as a part of the plan. So any growth which we hit in above 20%, our market -- margins should keep on expanding.

items.statement: No Y-o-Y margin compression expected in H1 FY26; costs are flat and growth momentum remains healthy.
items.quote: No, I don't think so. See when you are saying Y -on-Y, it will not have a compression. I don't think there's any reason because our costs are flat, and we are still growing at a good healthy growth momentum.

items.statement: Support revenue dip in Q4 due to quarterly adjustments and timing of contract renewals; churn remains minor at 1-2%.
items.quote: It's a marginal dip. I think it is a kind of a correction in certain accounts. We have some -- in terms of quarterly adjustments.

items.statement: ATS/AMC revenue correlates at 18-22% of license revenue when it kicks in; support revenue varies by engagement complexity.
items.quote: ATS/AMC have direct correlation. They're somewhere between 18% to 22% of our revenue when they kick in.

items.statement: Company pursuing rate revisions and price renegotiations to enhance support revenue stream over next 1-2 years.
items.quote: We are looking at rate revisions. We are looking at again price renegotiation in certain cases. This should also give a few percentage points going into next 1 or 2 years.

items.statement: US market saw 10 large deals in Q4 across banking, insurance, and health insurance; expects US to be a growth driver in FY26.
items.quote: This was the first quarter we got 10 deals from U.S. and some are very marquee deals. Now that we have got these wins, we expect now the growth rate and the momentum to continue building.

items.statement: APAC revenue reached ~15% of total; driven by government wins in Singapore and banking across Malaysia, Indonesia, Philippines; expects momentum to continue.
items.quote: It has become a substantial part of our revenue. It is almost now reached around 15% of our revenue, which is a good thing. And we are quite hopeful that I think the APAC can maintain a growth momentum.

items.statement: India revenue target of INR 1,000 crores in next 2-3 years; market share >20% in addressable space; expanding into NBFCs, payments, trade finance.
items.quote: I think we really would like that India it is 1,000 crores in the next 2, 3 years. That's our plan.

items.statement: Launched AI agents LumYn, Harper, Marvin; AI driving deal wins in content ingestion, early warning systems, underwriting automation.
items.quote: During the year, we have launched our groundbreaking AI agents, LumYn, Harper, and Marvin.

items.statement: Macro uncertainty acknowledged but diversified across geographies and segments; India less affected, financial services have second/third degree impact.
items.quote: Having said that, as I said, we are pretty diversified. There's not a single market or a single client segment on which we are dependent.

items.statement: Effective tax rate for FY26 expected at 23% due to partial SEZ benefits; new norm unless government policy changes.
items.quote: Now the current base of 23% is going to be the likely base which will continue going forward. And so last year, we had roughly around 17.5%, I think more close to 18% tax. This year, we are operating at 23%. So this is the new base.

items.statement: Invested nearly 10% of revenue in R&D and around 21% in sales and marketing during FY25; plans to continue prudent investment.
items.quote: During the year, we have invested nearly 10% of our revenues in R&D initiatives and around 21% of revenues on the various sales and marketing activities.

name: Home First Finance Company India Ltd

items.statement: Raised Rs 1,250 crores via QIP in April 2025 issuing 1.3 crore equity shares to institutional investors
items.quote: In April 2025, we successfully raised Rs. 1,250 crores through a qualified institutional placement, issuing 1.3 crore equity shares to market institutional investors, details of which are available on our website and exchanges.

items.statement: Targeting 20-25% disbursement growth for FY26 with 20-25% from new branches and 75% from existing branches
items.quote: Disbursement growth, we are targeting it on 20% +; somewhere in the range of 20% to 25% is what we are looking at for disbursement growth. And the trend will be similar – about 20% to 25% will come from new locations, branches, expansion, distribution and 75% will continue to come from existing branches.

items.statement: Confident of achieving Rs 20,000 crores AUM by FY27 and Rs 35,000 crores by FY30 with no major hindrances seen
items.quote: No, we are fairly confident of achieving the Rs. 20,000 crores mark in the next 2 years. At this point, we don't see anything which could be a hindrance to achieving the Rs. 20,000 crores.

items.statement: Guiding spread excluding co-lending at 5%+ (5% to 5.25% range) and expect to maintain it due to floating rate book
items.quote: Our expectation is that we will be able to hold on to the cost of borrowing moving ahead. So, we are comfortable with that 5% plus guidance on the spread, excluding co-lending.

items.statement: Asset yields expected to hold in 13% to 13.5% range for incremental origination
items.quote: Asset yields will largely hold in the 13.5% kind of a range. 13% to 13.5% we normally maintain the yields.

items.quote: We continue to maintain our conservative medium-term credit cost guidance of 30 to 40 bps.

items.statement: Branch expansion to grow 20-30% annually from higher base; expect 30-40 new branches per year vs 20-25 previously
items.quote: The number of branches will increase because of the base being higher. We would like to expand at about 20% to 30% every year. The AUM is expanding at about 25% to 30% every year. The branches also will expand at the same pace. So, we were growing at about 20 - 25 branches every year. That number will go up slightly maybe 30 to 35 or 35- 40 every year.

items.quote: As far as the overall market is concerned for FY26, we think it should be another year of good or decent demand because affordable housing demand has largely been secular. items.statement: Proforma leverage post-QIP at 3.3x, proforma CRAR at 51%, net worth Rs 3,751 crores; capital sufficient for ~4 years until FY30 unless faster growth
items.quote: Given our enlarged equity base post the capital infusion, our proforma leverage has come down to 3.3x. Proforma capital adequacy (CRAR) post capital raise will be 51% and a net worth of Rs. 3,751 crores.

items.quote: Run-off we have assumed is around 17% to 18%. With the 20% to 25% disbursal growth, we should be able to get to about 26%-27% to about 30% range of AUM growth.

items.quote: Yes, broadly in the same range . You can say last 2 years average productivity is what we will be able to maintain.

items.quote: on a very conservative side, we expect a minimum growth year -on-year of 25% or maybe even 30%. And our profits would always -- should be in line with what our current numbers are i the same ratios as we go forward to 20% to 30

items.quote: See primarily, we would be doing capex of INR500 crores, of which more than INR350 crores would be for equipment. We would be adding a few more rigs and other processing equipment in this financial year.

items.quote: FY '26, we are expecting revenue of almost INR100 crores, for sure. we can book more than this if we will add a few more projects in Dolphin.

items.quote: So land is having value of around INR1.5 crores to INR1.75 crores.

items.quote: And 20%, therefore, is more a long-term 4-5 year CAGR guidance. I'm just clarifying that even in the past, we have stated that it's not an immediate every year growth guidance.

items.statement: Quick commerce contribution margin flat QoQ due to competitive intensity preventing expected margin expansion
items.quote: The impact of competition is visible in the lack of significant margin expansion that we would have otherwise expected.

items.quote: There has been significant competition for the same real estate in most of the cities that we are in.

items.statement: Zomato Everyday shut down as it wouldn't move the needle for food delivery at scale; Bistro separate early-stage business

items.quote: I wouldn't be surprised at all if that 18%, 19% today becomes closer to 30% or even higher, right, when we get to year 3 from now.

items.quote: Our goal is to achieve 70% contribution from CRAMS and CEM, with 30% from large-scale manufacturing. And we are well on our way to realizing this vision.

items.statement: Personal finance 38% of loan book (government employee loans under MoU); MSME 18% (micro 15%, small 3%, medium 1.1%); financial markets exposure to NBFCs Rs. 11,749 crores (92% rated AA+); no credit card, microfinance, or personal loans out

items.statement: GNPA 3.37%, NNPA 0.79%, PCR >90%; slippage ratio 0.92%; no material impact expected from Pahalgam incident as tourism exposure <1% of credit portfolio; SMA-1 increase technical (70%+) due to salary-installment misalignment, corrected 3rd Ma
items.quote: We do not anticipate any material impact on our business or financial performance as our credit exposure to the tourism sector in Kashmir Division, is not even 1% of our overall credit portfolio.

items.statement: May raise debt and equity in FY26 for growth funding; comfortably placed at CRAR 16.29% (CET-1 12.95%); no final decision on quantum or mode (QIP, government, etc.)
items.quote: Though at present the Bank is placed comfortably, however, the Bank may consider raising both debt and equity capital in this fiscal for funding its growth.

items.statement: TWO recoveries Rs. 390 crores in FY25 (Rs. 168 crores in Q4); Rs. 3,000 crores TWO remaining; expect Rs. 250 crores+ recoveries in FY26; OTS scheme mixed response, another OTS possible
items.quote: Rs. 250 crores expected in this FY. So, that is going to continue.

items.statement: Dividend 215% approved for FY25; digital transactions >90%; mobile app upgraded, loan journeys digitized for all products including agriculture to be completed this quarter

items.statement: 5-year vision: profit Rs. 5,000 crores, business >Rs. 5 lakh crores; retail-focused with all-round growth across sectors; process corrections to strengthen foundation
items.quote: We are looking at a profit level of Rs. 5,000 crores, maybe a business level of more than Rs. 5 lakh crores in 5 years' time.

items.statement: Global clients curtailing discretionary spending; transformation spends continue in cloud, data analytics, AI/ML, regulatory automation
items.quote: Globally, while the banks are maintaining their measured stance towards discretionary spends, we are seeing clients going ahead with transformation initiatives, with spends continuing in areas such as cloud data analytics, AIML automation requirement on the regulatory side, if they are to handle any.

items.statement: Elevated uncertainty may lead to tighter client budgets and delays in discretionary spending by global clients
items.quote: However, elevated uncertainty may lead to tighter client budgets and delays in discretionary spending by global clients.

items.statement: India GDP expected to grow at 6.5% in Fiscal 2026 with downward bias
items.quote: India's GDP is expected to grow at 6.5% in Fiscal 2026, with a downward bias.

items.statement: Bank credit likely to grow 12%-13% in Fiscal 2026 vs 11-11.5% estimated for Fiscal 2025
items.quote: Bank credit is likely to grow to 12%-13% just Fiscal, compared with 11-11.5% estimated for Fiscal 2025, given three tailwinds viz. the recent supportive regulatory measures, a boost to consumption from tax cuts, and softer interest rates.

items.statement: Corporate bond issuances might see greater traction driven by easing monetary policy
items.quote: Corporate bond issuances might see greater traction, driven by easing monetary policy, provided the impact of macro and geopolitical issues is minimal.

items.statement: Crisil expects at least two more repo rate cuts of 25 bps each in rest of fiscal 2026

items.statement: Expect slight uptick in bank credit growth by 100-200 bps YoY in fiscal 2026
items.quote: We expect a slight uptick in the bank credit growth by 100 to 200 bps on-year in fiscal 2026 with the growth supported by rollback of risk weights for NBFC, a boost to consumption from tax cuts, and softening of interest rates.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 PBT and PAT grew approximately 16% YoY

items.quote: Segmental profit, on the other hand, witnessed a strong uptick in Q1 2025, growing approximately 16% on year, on the back of changing product mix and continued focus on margins.

items.statement: Rating Services segment grew about 32.5% YoY in Q1 2025
items.quote: Overall, the Rating Services segment grew by about 32.5% Y-o-Y in Q1 2025.

items.quote: Nashik capacity would go to 4.5 lakh tons, and we would add about 1 lakh ton in Haresamudram.

items.quote: Uber-Luxury is definitely doing much better than Premium-Luxury and Premium-Luxury is doing much better than Aspirational-Luxury. So, our major focus will be on Premium-Luxury as well as Uber-Luxury to drive this growth

items.statement: Planned launches in FY26 include Nepean Sea Road (>Rs 5,000 cr GDV), 5th Avenue ODC (>Rs 1,500 cr), Skypark tower (~Rs 700 cr), Vasai, SBR towers (Rs 400-450 cr), Naigaon phase (~Rs 350 cr)
items.quote: we are looking forward for the formal launch of Sunteck Nepean Sea Road project which is of GDV value of, on the current status more than Rs.5000 crores and the 5th Avenue at ODC Goregaon West which is for one tower of GDV value of more than Rs.1,500 crores and Sunteck's Skypark one more tower which we look to launch in this current financial year which is again close to GDV value of Rs.700 crores

items.statement: Dubai project delay due to approvals and design changes for optimal product mix
items.quote: will be the approvals, nothi ng else obviously approvals and it is that the designing stage work we were contemplating the mix of the projects that is why we had to change the design once or twice

items.statement: Net cash surplus of Rs 125 crores, net debt to equity improved to -0.04x
items.quote: Our balance sheet remains strong with a net cash surplus of Rs. 125 crores. Our net debt to equity has improved from (-0.02x) in 3rd Quarter of FY25 to (-0.04x) at end of 4th Quarter of

items.statement: Generated net operating cash flow surplus of Rs 374 crores in FY25
items.quote: We have generated a strong net operating cash flow surplus of Rs. 374 crores in FY25

items.statement: Bandra redevelopment project launch targeted for end of FY26 or early FY27, not factored in guidance
items.quote: I can give you on a conservative side towards the end of this financial year or toward the early next financial year we will be able to launch that project. But that is with a not very big GDV value, so we are not even considering that in our whatever numbers we are contemplating for the next

items.statement: EBITDA growth guidance of 15% to 20% year-on-year at absolute level
items.quote: we have already and have been giving a guidance that our profitability, because that's a metric that we want all of us to kind of concentrate on that will kind of grow between 15% to 20% year-on-year basis

items.statement: EBITDA absolute growth guidance of 15% to 20% year-on-year
items.quote: we are committed to delivering that 15 %, 20% EBITDA CAGR.

items.statement: Vietnam expansion completed at Ngon Coffee Company Limited subsidiary
items.quote: We also have completed the expansion at Ngon Coffee Company Limited, our subsidiary in Vietnam.

items.statement: Q4 EBITDA margin jump due to high proportion of high-margin contracts and avoiding low-margin business
items.quote: In Q4, we had a very high proportion of high-margin contracts. And a lot of end customers, which we had talked about in the last 4 quarterly updates that we are working on a lot of them.

items.statement: Coffee prices still high and choppy but showing signs of stability in last 2-3 months
items.quote: The coffee prices are still high and they're still choppy as of now. But we are seeing some signs of stability in the last 2 - 3 months.

items.statement: B2C price increases of 30-35% on larger packs taken in line with industry
items.quote: probably on the larger packs, 30% to 35% industry has taken, and we have also taken similar price increases.

items.statement: Short-term demand stress in domestic B2C due to price increases but long-term outlook positive as India converts from tea to coffee drinking nation
items.quote: are looking, and we are experiencing certain stresses in the demand. But I believe these are short-term stresses because the amount of consumption that is, the amount of consumption that is being driven, especially the out-of-home player in the cafes

items.statement: Small pack contribution increased to around 20% for full year, up from 17-18% last year
items.quote: So entire year, now we have crossed around 20%. So that's an increase. We were at around 18% or so, 18%, 17% to 18% last year.

items.statement: Working capital at ~45% of revenue and debt at INR 1,800-1,900 crores driven by 5x coffee price increase from $1,000 to $5,000 and seller's market squeezing payment cycles
items.quote: The single most contributing reason has been the prices. So from that $1,000 that used to be there in between '15 to '20, it is now $5,000, yes.

items.statement: Long-term contracts not normalized yet; customers still giving 3-month contracts instead of 1-year due to high choppy prices
items.quote: Not much there because they still are at high levels and at choppy levels. So we haven't seen normalization there.

items.statement: Long-term customer profile at 60-70% but they are giving short-term 3-month contracts instead of annual contracts
items.quote: my long-term customer profile will be approximately 60% to 60%, 70%, yes. So these are my long-term customers who buy from me always. But the only thing is that instead of saying that, okay, the next 1-year quantity is this much, they would say that, no, let me buy only for 3 months.

items.statement: Volume growth ~10% for full year FY25, down from 20-22% in prior years due to avoiding low-margin contracts
items.quote: the volume trajectory for last 3 years has been a lot closer to 20%, 22%. This year, it's closer to 10%.

items.statement: Newer capacities at 10-15% utilization on yearly basis; Vietnam extended capacity just announced, utilization to be seen next quarter
items.quote: The newer capacities last year because they came at different points of time. But on a yearly basis, if you see, there was 10% to 15% utilization of the newer capacities.

items.statement: Freight costs uncertain due to Red Sea tensions and tariff announcements; difficult to predict stabilization
items.quote: it's very difficult to comment right now where things will go forward with. Then again, when Trump had decided tariffs and all that, suddenly, there was a slump for a few days.

items.statement: Blend library expanded from 500-600 to 1,000 blends, enabling market share gains in new markets and products
items.quote: Today, we have 1,000. So that probably speaks of the fact that every day is a day when we kind of develop something new for some client or the other.

items.statement: Vietnam tariff risk mitigated by Vietnam's proactive 0% tariff on US imports and India-US trade deal progress; production flexibility between Vietnam and India plants
items.quote: Vietnam has already kind of made all imports as 0 tax from U.S., urging them to go back to status quo. So I'm sure there will be some settlement there.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 EBITDA margin improved to 11% from 10% in Q4 FY24 and 7.63% in Q3 FY25
items.quote: EBITDA margin improved to 11%, up from 10% in Q4 FY '24, and significantly higher than 7.63% in Q3 of FY '25.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA margin was 9% with EBITDA at Rs. 125 crores
items.quote: EBITDA margin was at Rs. 125 crores, which increased by 9.5% on a year-on-year basis. EBITDA margin stored at 9% percent.

items.statement: NBR expansion ready but waiting for anti-dumping investigation conclusion before proceeding
items.quote: In the rubber segment specifically for NBR, nitrile butadiene rubber, so as I have mentioned before that we are sort of waiting on the anti-dumping investigation final conclusions before taking a call and going ahead with it.

items.statement: Non-nitrile latex volumes grew 8-10% in FY25; expect slightly higher growth next year
items.quote: So even in the non-nitrile latex segments we have grown at about 8% to 10%. Jaspreet Walia: Volumes? Abhiraj Choksey: Volumes, yes. And it will be probably a little bit more

items.statement: US tariff uncertainty creating customer hesitation; Chinese glove oversupply pressuring nitrile latex margins
items.quote: Given the US tariffs and the uncertainty around that issue, what we are seeing in the market is a lot of uncertainty from some of our businesses that are more US-focused. So, for example, we do not have much exposure to the US, but indirectly some of our customers have exposure to the US, they export to the US.

items.statement: India-Pakistan situation adds to uncertainty; tariffs remain main concern for outlook
items.quote: Of course, there are certain uncertainties right now with the tariffs from the US, I think that's the main issue right now. And of course, the India-Pakistan situation, I do not want to comment because it's too recent and no one knows how that will play out.

items.statement: Crude price decline not directly beneficial short-term due to inventory lag; focus on raw material-finished goods delta
items.quote: Lower crude prices, once they are steady, if it remains steady, it does help of course from a working capital angle, also from a pricing angle it helps a little bit. But while they are falling, as we have seen in the last couple of months, it's actually a little bit not great for the company.

items.statement: Nitrile latex running at 75-80% monthly capacity in Q4; targeting 100% utilization as industry capacity absorbs
items.quote: For the new nitrile latex project which we are at about 75% plus now, I am talking about monthly run rate. For the year as a whole we were lower of course, but Q4 we were at about 75%, 80%, between 75% and 80%.

items.statement: APCOBuild growth slowed to single digits in FY25 after years of 18-20% growth; remains small profitable business
items.quote: Difficulty year in the sense that we have been used to 18%, 20% or maybe more growth earlier. This year the growth is in single digits.

items.statement: Hybrid renewable power project in Gujarat to cover 65-70% of plant consumption; Rs. 3.27 crore investment yielding significant savings
items.quote: We will be sort of moving at least 60% to 70% of our current consumption, 65% to 70% of our current power consumption in our Gujarat plant to renewable energy, and therefore reducing our green house gas emissions.

items.statement: Expect to sustain double-digit revenue growth and strive to deliver double-digit operating profit growth in FY26
items.quote: Moving into next year, we expect to sustain double -digit revenue growth and will strive to deliver double -digit operating profit growth.

items.statement: Expect India business volume growth of more than 5% annualized in FY26, with 6-7% as base case
items.quote: We expect the volume growth next year , full year annualized, as more than 5%. 6-7% growth has almost become a base case for us.

items.statement: Expect Foods portfolio to grow 25%+ over medium term to reach about 8x of FY20 scale
items.quote: The Foods portfolio has reached 5x of the FY20 scale, and we expect 25% + growth over the medium term to reach about 8x of the FY20 scale, while we continue to improve profitability in the category.

items.statement: Expect Foods and Premium Personal Care to expand to ~25% of domestic revenue by FY27
items.quote: We will continue to aggressively diversify the portfolio through these portfolios in line with our medium -term strategic priorities and expect these portfolios to expand to ~25% of domestic revenue by FY 27.

items.statement: Expect Digital-first portfolio exit ARR to be 2.5x of FY24 ARR in FY27, up from previous target of 2x
items.quote: We now expect this exit ARR to be 2.5x of FY24 ARR in FY27, up from the previous target of 2x.

items.statement: Expect Digital-first portfolio to achieve double-digit EBITDA margin by FY27
items.quote: We continue to see marked improvement in profitability in the Digital-first portfolio and maintain our aspiration to achieve double-digit EBITDA margin by FY '27.

items.statement: Expect Beardo and Plix combined ARR to cross ₹1,000 crores in FY26 with focus on operating profitability
items.quote: We expect these two brands to cross ₹1,000 crores in combined ARR this year with a clear focus on driving operating profitability with scale.

items.statement: Expect Just Herbs and True Elements to focus on sustainable 20-25% growth and achieve breakeven in 18-24 months
items.quote: Just Herbs and True Elements, though not yet at breakeven, will focus on sustainable 20% to 25% growth and leveraging scale and synergy to achieve breakeven at the earliest over the next 18 to 24 months.

items.statement: Expect gross margin pressure to ease starting end of Q2 FY26 as copra prices soften
items.quote: Hopefully, from quarter two onwards, we can start seeing some improvement.

items.statement: Consolidated operating margin ended just shy of 20% in FY25; A&P spends up 35% in Q4 and 18% in FY25
items.quote: The consolidated operating margin of FY 25 ended just shy of 20%, and we have delivered resilient bottom line performance without any negative surprises despite input cost pressures being significantly higher than for the rest of the sector.

items.statement: Foods gross margins structurally expanded ~1,000 bps cumulatively over FY24 and FY25
items.quote: In Foods, we have structurally expanded gross margin s by ~1,000 bps over FY 24 and FY 25, on a cumulative basis, and we expect gradual margin expansion as the business scales in the medium term.

items.statement: Took cumulative ~30% price increase in Parachute (23% through Q4 FY25 plus 8-9% recently) with 1% volume decline
items.quote: Very recently, we've taken another round of price increase of about 8% to 9%.

items.statement: Expect gradual pickup in core category growth through FY26 aided by improving consumption sentiment and easing hyperinflation
items.quote: In India, core category growth was subdued in FY 25, but we expect a gradual pick up through FY26, aided by improving consumption sentiment across urban and rural, and easing of hyperinflation pressure across key commodities.

items.statement: Copra prices expected to remain firm until Q2 FY26 due to lower arrivals; margin pressure to continue for next 1-2 quarters
items.quote: Given the extended firmness in copra prices due to lower arrival in the market, the awaited correction is most probably going to happen towards Q2.

items.statement: FY26 credit growth guidance 12%, deposit growth 10%, CASA target at least 48%, NIM 3.70-3.80%, ROA maintained at current level, ROE 16-17%, GNPA below 3%
items.value: 12% credit growth, 10% deposit growth, CASA 48%, NIM 3.70-3.80%, ROE 16-17%, GNPA <3%
items.quote: Now, for March 2025-26 market guidance, we expect the credit growth to be at 12%, deposit growth to be at 10%. We want to improve the CASA to at least 48%. NIM, we will be satisfied with 3.70 to 3.80. ROA, we will try to maintain the ROA at the moment. Return on equity expected in between 16% to 17%, and GNPA below 3%.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio target around 50% in a year and a half
items.quote: Our target is to reach to around 50% in a couple of years, maybe in a year and a half. So, that is the guidance we have.

items.statement: Corporate CAPEX pipeline in J&K UT tied up at Rs 2,500-3,000 crore including Rs 1,000 crore sanction likely to disburse soon and Rs 500 crore under sanction
items.quote: I think the pipeline in the CAPEX where we are tied up, I guess it will be around Rs. 2,000 to Rs. 2,500 crores at the moment because many of the projects are yet to be commissioned. So, one of the projects, already we have given a sanction of Rs. 1,000 crores, which is likely to be disbursed anytime now. I mean, the disbursement is likely to start anytime now. And there is another project which w

items.statement: NIM guidance for FY26 at 3.70-3.80% vs 3.92% in FY25; 52% loan book floating rate, 38% personal loans to govt employees with protected rates, high CASA provides cushion
items.quote: At the moment, the guidance I have given is around 3.7 to 3.8. It may be around that, maybe better. But I feel that we still have sufficient opportunity in this Bank to have better NIMs than many others in the industry.

items.statement: No increase in employee cost expected for 1-2 years as salary revision done, no recruitment planned, retirements lined up
items.quote: Since immediately we do not have any plans of recruitment, and there are some retirements lined up, and also the salary revision thing is over and out by now, so I do not see any increase in the employee cost going forward at least for a year or two.

items.statement: Credit growth guidance 12% for FY26 factoring downward revision in India GDP forecast; aiming to reduce concentration risk by growing retail book in rest of India (housing, car loans)
items.quote: The business growth might appear a bit moderate, but it takes into consideration the recent downward division in India's economic growth forecast for '26 and is in alignment with the broad growth predictions for Indian banking sector in 2026.

items.statement: Retail focus to continue; corporate book second line of defense; targeting housing and car loan growth in rest of India; personal finance 38% of book (govt employee loans), MSME 18% (mostly services)
items.quote: We are now aiming at improving the retail loan book of rest of India. That is something which we are really looking at. The corporate loan book growth will remain as a second line of defense for us.

items.statement: GNPA 3.37%, NNPA 0.79%, PCR >90%; slippage ratio 0.92%; no material impact from Pahalgam incident as tourism exposure <1% of credit portfolio; SMA-1 increase technical (70%+), corrected by aligning installment dates with salary dates from 3
items.quote: We continue to remain focused on our asset quality as is evident from our numbers, which are in line with our guidance, in fact better than that. GNPA at 3.37%, NNPA of 0.79% and provision coverage ratio of above 90%.

items.statement: May raise debt and equity capital in FY26 for funding growth; comfortably placed at CRAR 16.29% (CET-1 12.95%); no final decision yet, will evaluate all options if credit growth demands
items.quote: Though at present the Bank is placed comfortably, however, the Bank may consider raising both debt and equity capital in this fiscal for funding its growth.

items.statement: 5-year vision: profit Rs 5,000 crore, business >Rs 5 lakh crore; retail-focused with all-round growth; ALM discipline; process corrections to strengthen foundation
items.value: Profit Rs 5,000 crore, business >Rs 5 lakh crore
items.quote: We actually see the Bank at a very, very strong position 5 years from now. I don't think that this should be taken as guidance or anything. But we are looking at a profit level of Rs. 5,000 crores, maybe a business level of more than Rs. 5 lakh crores in 5 years' time.

items.statement: Dividend 215% approved for FY25; third consecutive year of dividend; digital transactions >90% in FY25; mobile app upgraded, loan journeys digitized for all products including agriculture to be completed this quarter
items.quote: Also, I am pleased to share that Board has approved a dividend of 215% for the Financial Year 2025, marking our third consecutive year of rewarding our shareholders and showing our gratitude for their confidence in us.

items.statement: Credit cost increase not significant, likely 20-30 bps max; ROA sustainment levers: TWO recoveries, forex income, robust credit growth, expense control
items.quote: If you consider 20 to 30 bps as an increase in credit cost, I would say that there will be an increase. But it is not likely to be more than 20 bps or 30 bps. So, no significant increase in the credit cost is expected by the Bank going forward.

items.statement: FY26 deposit growth guidance 8-10%, advances growth 10-12%
items.quote: If I talk of the guidance for the FY 2025-26, we are giving guidance for deposit of 8-10% and advances of 10-12%.

items.statement: FY26 CASA ratio guidance around 40%, LDR around 80%
items.quote: We are giving guidance to maintain CASA around 40%. We would like to maintain LDR around 80% range.

items.statement: FY26 Gross NPA guidance <3%, net NPA maintain current 0.19%
items.quote: Gross NPA , we are giving guidance to maintain less than 3% and we’ll maintain the current levels of n et NPA, because we have already reached 0.19

items.statement: FY26 recovery guidance Rs.5,500-6,500 crore
items.quote: Further, we are giving recovery guidance of Rs.5,500 crores to Rs.6,500 crores.

items.statement: FY26 NIM guidance revised to 3.15-3.30% due to rate cuts
items.quote: We will have some moderation on yield on advances and NI Ms because of rate cuts . Since inflation is within comfortable range, we see there may be some more rate cuts, so we are giving a revised NIM guidance in the range of 3.15% to 3.30

items.statement: FY26 RoA guidance 1.20% due to asset growth and profitability moderation
items.quote: Although we have achieved RoA of 1.32%, but because of the increased asset or some moderation in the profitability, we are giving RoA guidance in the range of 1.20%.

items.statement: FY26 cost-to-income ratio guidance around 45%
items.quote: We will be able to maintain cost-to-income ratio around 45%.

items.statement: FY26 credit cost guidance <1%, slippage guidance <1%
items.quote: Credit cost, I am giving guidance of less than 1%, slippage also we are giving guidance of less than 1%.

items.statement: FY26 corporate loan growth target ~9%
items.quote: Corporate, we have kept a target of around 9% growth.

items.statement: Annual digital/IT spend maintained at Rs.1,300-1,400 crore
items.quote: Our annual expenditure on digital and IT is in the range of Rs.1,200 crore to Rs.1,300 crore. So, we are maintaining, similar budget of Rs.1,300 crores to Rs.1,400 crores per year going forward.

items.statement: Digital business projected at Rs.2,25,000 crore for FY26
items.quote: We are projecting Rs.2,25,000 crore for the financial year 2026.

items.statement: Yield on advances declined 28 bps due to EBLR-linked book and WCDL rate cuts
items.quote: The yield on advances has declined by 28 basis points and is mainly due to the impact of the EBLR only, as 40% of my book is linked to external benchmark. We have already passed on 50 basis point. We've observed a significant rate cut in WCDL loans, and that's primarily what's driving the impact.

items.statement: Supreme Court judgment on resolved account may require reversal but management views it as net positive
items.quote: We have received a copy of the judgment very recently. And of course, it is a landmark judgment and how it will impact, only time will tell. But one thing I can tell you, if at all, we have to reverse, I think it will be good for the Bank, because if you see, we have got our resolution at 40%, that means 60% haircut was there. Now that the asset is up and running, the enterprise value must have go

items.statement: Draft RBI gold loan guidelines may impact growth and earnings if implemented as proposed
items.quote: Yes, of course, there will be impact both on growth and income, but it is draft guidelines, and we have given our feedback. Let us see how, in what shape the final guidelines comes. But if it comes as it is, yes, there will be some impact on both, growth and earnings.

items.statement: Credit demand met via infrastructure bonds and refinancing, not wholesale deposits
items.quote: We could have achieved this deposit growth even in this year, but we have taken a conscious call because we raised some fund from other sources at competitive rate, like infrastructure bond and other refinancing options. So, credit demand was met by these sources, that's why we did not go for the deposit growth, because wholesale deposit, we ended at flat Rs.1.04 lakh crore to Rs.1.06 lakh crore,

items.statement: Endeavor to maintain 65:35 RAM:corporate loan mix, recently sanctioned Rs.38,000 crore in Q4
items.quote: See, endeavor will be to maintain the same, around 65:35, but we are already looking for the opportunity and wherever we are getting good opportunity, we are according sanctions also. And recently, in Q4, we have been able to accord sanction of around Rs.38,000 crores.

items.statement: Plan to expand branch network in underpenetrated regions like western region
items.quote: One more point on branch expansion is that we plan to expand our branch network, particularly in regions where our presence is currently limited, such as the western region.

items.statement: FY26 AUM target INR1,000 crore plus, disbursement around INR400 crore, branches to remain at 90
items.quote: Sir, now for FY26, we will do INR1,000 crores plus. I am not saying it will increase from INR1,000 crores to INR1,200 crores. But it will be more than INR1,000 crores. And our disbursement will be around INR400 crores. And our branches, we have 90 branches. We will work on those 90 branches.

items.statement: FY27 AUM target around INR1,300-1,350 crore, disbursement around INR500 crore, branches to increase to 100 after crossing INR1,000 crore AUM
items.quote: And our target for next year will be around INR1,300 INR1,350 crores. And our disbursement will be around INR500 crores, and our branches we will increase above INR1,000 crores, so there the branches will become 100.

items.statement: Medium-term AUM target INR1,500 crore after FY27
items.quote: And after that, if there is next year, then we will reach around INR1,500 crore.

items.statement: NIM expected to increase as repo rate cuts benefit fixed-rate book and operating cost per unit declines with scale
items.quote: Sir, the impact of the repo rate will have its own benefit. NIM will increase. Next quarter will have a good impact. Because we are on a fixed rate. The rate that has come down and the book that has already been made, in the last few years, the loss was also on a fixed rate. Now when it has reduced we will get the benefit.

items.statement: Housing loan portfolio yield maintained at 18%, LAP at 20%; no reduction in lending rates despite repo rate cuts
items.quote: No, no. Our average housing loan, that portfolio is maintained at 18% only. And our LAP sits around 20%.

items.statement: Branch expansion capped at 100 branches; only 8-10 more branches after crossing INR1,000 crore AUM, no further expansion for 2-3 years
items.quote: No, our target is 100 branches. We have done 90 branches. If our INR1,000 crore loan book target is achieve, then we will only make 10 more branches. Then we will not increase any branch from 100 branches for the next 2 years.

items.statement: No demand slowdown in rural/semi-urban areas; business driven by branch network and venue marketing, not digital channels
items.quote: The rest is that the business is good in rural areas. Demand is also good in rural areas. People do not look or do everything runs according to them.
