Their earnings are not too much that anyone can make an impact. Their business is like a regular business. So, there is no problem in business.

items.statement: Housing loans 73%, LAP 27%; salaried 26%, self-employed 74%; 100% secured against property; average ticket size INR8 lakh, average LTV 44%
items.quote: In FY25, housing loan was 73% and loan against property was 27%. Salaried loan was 26% and self-employed loan was 74%. Our 100% loan book is secured against property. The average ticket size of the housing loan book is INR8 lakhs and the average LTV is 44%.

items.statement: ROA expected to cross 3.5% in FY26 and reach 4%+ as equity base leverages up; current ROA 3.17%
items.quote: Sir, the ROA has reduced due to the increase in equity, but the expansion plan and the growth of the business and the growth of the PAT, the ROA should cross the 4% which has been taken by the equity, and it will cross 3.5% in the next year.

items.statement: Credit rating upgraded to BBB+; expected to reach A- at INR1,000 crore AUM, lowering borrowing costs
items.quote: And in today's date, all the things that had to be done have been completed. Now our rating has also become BBB plus. And as soon as it comes around INR1,000 crores, then our rating will also come in A minus. If we come in that rating, then it will be a little easier to take money from the bank. And as the rating increases, we will get a little benefit in the borrowing cost.

items.statement: Balance transfer activity at 10-11% of book, largely offset by reverse transfers
items.quote: Sir, balance transfer is 10%, 11%. And the same come back. The same goes and comes back. There is a difference of 1%, 2%.

items.statement: Borrowing mix: 46% banks, 48% FIs, 6% NHB; NCDs not used due to higher cost and bullet repayment structure
items.quote: Sir, 49% is from FI, 48% is from banks, 6% is from NHB. And NCD has a higher cost that is why they are not able to take it. And if NCD is available for more than 5 years because we are a housing finance company, then we do not take NCD in the short term. And secondly, we do not take bullet payment NCD.

items.statement: Total confirmed order book stands at INR 1,197 crore as of March 31, 2025, with INR 1,019 crore in water domain and INR 178 crore in geospatial enterprise solutions.
items.quote: As at the March, the total order book confirmed order book stands at around INR 1,197 crores. Of this, projects in the water domain account for INR 1,019 crores and the geospatial enterprise solutions services contribute to around INR 178 crores.

items.statement: Order book pipeline typically ranges INR 300-400 crore per quarter; currently INR 355 crore bid pipeline with expectation of INR 280+ crore conversion in next month.
items.quote: So even as we speak, we have a pipeline for which we have bid in the range of around INR 355 crores. So and that is what we expect something to happen within next one month or so. About these out of INR 355 crores, we expect the disposal of at least two of the large projects, which could be aggregating to more than INR 280 crores in the next one month or

items.statement: EBITDA margin was 18.82% in Q4 FY25 and 18.63% for full FY25; management aims to maintain and improve margin profile going forward.
items.quote: we said consistently over the last year is we do not see any headwinds and we should be able to maintain and improve our margin profile as the quarters and quarters starts unfolding

items.statement: Technology solutions revenue grew 3.5x to INR 213 crore in FY25, increasing share of total turnover from 24% to 51%.
items.quote: The execution of technology solutions projects witnessed a 3.5-fold increase during the year 2024-2025, rising from INR 60 crores of last year to INR 213 crores of the year 2024-2025, which reflects a strong demand and enhanced delivery capabilities.

items.statement: Technology solutions contributed 51% of FY25 turnover vs 24% in FY24; focus remains on growing higher-margin technology solutions.
items.quote: The share of Technology Solutions total turnover increased significantly from a 24% of the total turnover of last year to 51% of the turnover of this year, underscoring the company's strategic focus on the high value digital initiatives.

items.statement: Invested INR 12 crore in US business development expensed in FY25 P&L.
items.quote: We have invested around INR 12 crores towards the business development for expansion into U.S. market, and this has been expensed out in the profit loss account for the year 2024-2025.

items.statement: Vidarbha river linking project execution may face compounding delays due to upcoming rainy season affecting survey and soil testing.
items.quote: Because we have received order late, there are also and we have discussed this with government, there are also possibilities of compounding delays because with the rainy season coming up, the work will be affected in terms of survey and soil testing and all of that for API.

items.statement: Company holds investable surplus of INR 105 crore for inorganic opportunities plus INR 45 crore operational cash surplus.
items.quote: As of year-end, it holds an investable surplus of around INR105 crore for inorganic opportunities along with our operational cash surplus of INR 45 crore.

items.statement: Management does not provide forward revenue or margin guidance; expects continued growth trajectory without specific targets.
items.quote: We generally don't give futuristic numbers, but we can tell you we expected substantial growth in the current year.

items.statement: Board recommended dividend increased to 35% from 25% previous year.
items.quote: Infused with the performance, the Board has recommended a higher dividend of 35% as compared to 25% last year.

items.statement: Appointed Mr. K.P. Surej as CEO Designate and Additional Director; Mr. Vanish Moorthy appointed as Additional Director for international growth.
items.quote: Besides as informed, the Board has also appointed Mr. K.P. Surej as the Additional Director at its meeting on 3 of May 2025 and is a CEO designate of the company.

items.statement: Jal Jeevan Mission center allocation reduction not seen as headwind; company's share remains 3-5% of annual budget with significant untapped potential across states.
items.quote: So I think the Jal Jeevan mission is not the only source. But in any case, Jal Jeevan mission is also still a lot of potential to be tapped. Right now, we are only focused into Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, and we are tapping into some other states.

items.statement: M&A discussions ongoing for two targets; due diligence expected to complete in next 1-2 months for customer and competence acquisition.
items.quote: So we are on the process. Hopefully, in next one or two months, we will be able to get some headway on those two targets, which we are actually working on.

items.statement: International technology solutions expansion underway; signed one large contract with small execution started, pipeline expected to expand in FY26.
items.quote: We signed one large contract and we started small execution of that already. And we expect that pipeline as well as those contracts in terms of longer term to expand during the current year, which is FY 2026.

items.statement: Data center plans put on back burner to focus on existing segments with more immediate opportunities.
items.quote: If we decide to move forward, we will definitely come back and improve. But right now, we are trying planning to put them on back burner because there are more orders and more business being pursued with the existing segments.

items.statement: Company optimistic about achieving 40-50% revenue growth in FY26 supported by increased capacity utilization, improved logistics, and focus on high-margin value-added products
items.quote: Because of this factor the Company's optimistic about achieving 40-50% revenue growth in FY '26 supported by increased capacity utilization improved logistics and continued focus on high margin value-added product.

items.statement: Capex guidance for FY26 is Rs 75-100 crores, primarily for Pakhajan capacity expansion and R&D facility
items.quote: For this year, we have said about between Rs. 75- 100 crores.

items.statement: Large long-term supply orders and quarterly orders from committed customers are converting at Pakhajan facility
items.quote: Well, we have certain large long-term supply orders, but orders come every quarter-on-quarter, not in one go. So yes, there are few orders, few customers who have come on board which need a large quantity on a regular basis

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 17-19% for FY26 due to pricing uncertainties from geopolitical issues
items.quote: Well, as of now, we don't want to increase the guideline because there are a lot of uncertainties on the pricing front because of the geopolitical issues, so we still want to maintain between 17%-19% EBITDA margins for FY '26.

items.statement: Sustainable gross margin expected at 40-42% long-term, with 40% being more reasonable
items.quote: Sustainable should be about 40%-42%. 40% should be more reasonable margin one should look at it as a long run business.

items.statement: Quarterly pricing with customers allows pass-through of both cost increases and decreases, minimal margin impact from 10-15% price changes
items.quote: We have done some that analysis of 5% open, 5% down, how does it impact, but it has a very minimal impact as we have quarterly pricing with our customer, so we don't see a major impact.

items.statement: Business approvals completed, converting to actual orders giving confidence for 60-70% Pakhajan utilization in FY26
items.quote: Already, there all are there in place. That is why we are giving you the guidance of utilization for 60%-70% on FY '26 basis.

items.statement: Focus on high-margin value-added products and improving product mix to drive growth
items.quote: We are well positioned to capitalize on this evolving landscape. Because of this factor the Company's optimistic about achieving 40-50% revenue growth in FY '26 supported by increased capacity utilization improved logistics and continued focus on high margin value-added product.

items.statement: Global economic uncertainty, geopolitical tensions, and policy shifts creating price volatility in raw materials and finished goods
items.quote: The global economy remains uncertain unlike evolving geopolitical tension and policy shift impacting the chemical industry. These uncertainties are expected to drive price volatility across both raw material and finished goods

items.statement: Raised Rs 125 crores through preferential equity issuance for industrial segment opportunities and long-term debt reduction
items.quote: We have raised Rs. 125 crores through the issuance of equity shares on a preferential basis. This new funding will be strategically invested in promising opportunities within the industrial segment and to reduce long-term debt.

items.statement: Pakhajan facility Phase-2 expansion decision premature, depends on FY27 cash flows and funding
items.quote: 27, we are not given thought yet, how much we would respond, what is the cash flow and how you are going to raise fund, everything to be come in the future, so it is too premature to talk about Phase-2 today.

items.statement: Debt target to reduce to Rs 450 crores by FY26 from current Rs 470 crores, with debt/EBITDA ratio target of 3.5x
items.quote: See, current debt is in the range of about Rs. 470 crores, current debt and we expect that to come down to somewhere in the range of about Rs. 450 crores.

items.statement: Working capital days target of 110-115 days by end of FY26, inventory normalization expected by September quarter
items.quote: Yes, 110 is our target, 110-115 days as the overall control should be target one, should be achievable by FY '26 definitely.

items.statement: Incremental capacity expansion at Pakhajan for products with good traction and forecast
items.quote: We do see some good traction in some of our product where we build up the capacity and we see good forecast and good opportunity, so we decided to do some incremental capacity.

items.statement: US tariff impact mixed - some customers accepting revised prices, others in wait-and-watch mode
items.quote: Some segment customers we are seeing, they are just wait and watch, they also want to see the overall US economy, how they perform, so someone has a little bit slow down and some are doing well.

items.statement: Revenue growth momentum expected to continue in FY27 with new capex impact visible from Q1 FY27
items.quote: I think so. We are very much confident about that because there will be enough space for further growth too and as we are also looking for new CAPEX, so that we only kick in 27, not in 26.

items.statement: Management expects topline growth of over 25% in FY26 with EBITDA margin around 20-21% for the full year.
items.quote: Looking ahead, FY26 is poised to be a turnaround year. With new products entering the commercial phase, demand improving across key markets, and capacity utilisation forecasted to be at optimal levels, we anticipate a topline growth of over 25%. This, coupled with better operating leverage, is expected to drive a meaningful improvement in EBITDA.

items.statement: SDA segment revenue expected to grow 40-70% in FY26 driven by volume recovery and Euro 7 implementation.
items.quote: So considering that we are remaining at the same levels in terms of product pricing, same levels in terms of raw material prices, but in terms of revenue that this can bring in, it would range between 40% to 70% growth in terms of volume and value.

items.statement: PASC segment expected to grow at least 40% in FY26 with major contribution from Q3 onwards.
items.quote: So we will cross at least 40% in terms of growth that is what we clearly foresee.

items.statement: Electrolyte salts segment forecast to grow at least 200% in FY26 but from a small base of Rs 6 cr to Rs 23-26 cr.
items.quote: So we expect the electrolyte salt segment to grow by at least 200% this year. But what significant impact will it have is hardly anything because it will go from, let us say, from Rs.6 crores to Rs.23-26 crores in terms of revenue is what we forecast.

items.statement: PTC segment expected to grow consistently at 10-12% annually.
items.quote: Basically, in terms of growth if we see, PTC is technically expanding 10% to 12% on a year.

items.statement: New facility for major agro intermediate under construction with capex of Rs 105-110 crore, targeting operational readiness by January 2026.
items.quote: No, so this will be about Rs. 105 Cr., anywhere between Rs. 105 Cr. and Rs. 110 Cr., And we are striving very hard to get it operational before January of 2026.

items.statement: Secured bulk commercial order for major agro intermediate; commercial supplies to commence in Q3 FY26.
items.quote: We have secured a bulk commercial order for one of our major agro intermediates, marking a crucial step forward in this vertical. The commercial supplies for this product will commence in third quarter of FY26.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guided at 20-21% for full year FY26, with significant H1 vs H2 difference due to production-sales timing.
items.quote: want more of a precise answer to this, would say a ballpark number of around 20% should be more realistic for the current year. I am expecting there would be certain challenges when we are scaling up each of these new large value products. We are talking of increasing the topline with new products, that is also a significant part of the overall growth. So, when this is happening, am suspecting tha

items.statement: Four agro intermediates commercialized in Q4 FY25 causing operational inefficiencies; expect to master production by end of June 2025.
items.quote: So I probably believe by the end of June 2025, most of the processes we should be on the optimum level.

items.statement: Semiconductor-grade ultra-pure chemicals achieved below 10 PPB purity in reactor; awaiting qualified packaging from Germany/Japan to send first commercial lot.
items.quote: Yes. So we are sending our samples. So basically, we have achieved the desired quality. Absolutely everything below 10 PPB levels has been achieved inside the reactor. Now we are waiting for the right packaging material.

items.statement: SDA demand recovery visible with customer engagement improving; Euro 7 and hybrid vehicle shift provide tailwinds; China demand may reverse as gas prices rise.
items.quote: Over the past few months, customer engagement has improved meaningfully and we are seeing a consistent uptick in demand volumes. Furthermore, we will witness offtake from customers who approved our products during past couple of years. This development, combined with the approaching EURO 7 implementation, provides a strong tailwind for growth.

items.statement: Electrolyte salts volumes picking up from Q1 FY26; third product sample approved, commercial validation in Q2 FY26; second strategic customer qualification progressing well.
items.quote: The customer using our electrolyte for energy storage devices has been gaining momentum and the volumes have started to pick up from first quarter of FY26. Besides the electrolyte salts for energy storage devices, our pilot scale sample for the third product required to make the electrolyte solutions has been formally approved by the customer. We are now undergoing minor modifications to our exist

items.statement: Flame retardant development halted due to unfavorable market; capacity reallocated to agro intermediates.
items.quote: The challenges in flame retardant market are continuously increasing and it does not make a prudent commercial sense to venture into this market as of now. So, we have decided to withheld the production and development activities of these products.

items.statement: US tariff exposure minimal as nearly all products fall under global exemption list; no significant customer inquiries about supply shifts.
items.quote: You see, that is something they called there is some annexure that is published that these are the products or categories which are exempt from this special duty. And I believe almost all, barring a couple of products, almost all the products what we are into is under that exemption list.

items.statement: SDA plant capacity utilization improved from 29-32% to ~60% recently; conventional plant at 83-84% occupancy.
items.quote: The SDA part of the plant, so the plant where we expanded and then we saw this sudden drop in terms of volume and the challenging type of phase in the SDA part, so that plant had been running at about 29% to 32% capacity which since last one month we are seeing it operating at about 60% level.

items.statement: No major capex planned for foreseeable future; only marginal capex for wear and tear
items.quote: But for the foreseeable future, we don't have any major capex planned this year.

items.statement: Capex focused on cane development and bottling capacity, not distillery expansion
items.quote: Our capex is only on the bottling capacity, not so much on the distillery capacity.

items.statement: Sold 99% of export obligation; small quantities to institutional clients pending
items.quote: We, as a company, decided to sell our export obligation. We've sold pretty much 99% of our export obligation.

items.statement: Ethanol margins lower due to reduced recovery increasing cost of production for syrup and B-heavy molasses
items.quote: The impact of recovery, which increases the cost of production of sugar, also increases the cost of production of ethanol, especially when you're making it with syrup of B-heavy.

items.statement: Ex-mill sugar prices rose ~INR 3/kg after export announcement; FRP increased INR 15/quintal to INR 355/quintal for season 25-26
items.quote: Following the export announcement, the ex -mill sugar prices rose by approximately INR 3 per kg, which was a much-needed boost required to cover the cost of production.

items.statement: Domestic sugar prices expected to remain firm; closing stock manageable
items.quote: On the domestic front, I think the prices should remain firm. They have been holding steady. The closing stock is manageable and the FRP increase should also help keep the prices stable to firm.

items.statement: Grain distillery starting by end of month/early next month; 25.5 lakh liters FCI rice ethanol contracted; plant can run on rice or corn
items.quote: Now we are contracted to supply the Q3 cycle of FCI rice. So I think we should be starting a grain distillery by end of the month, early next month.

items.statement: Expect 25-30% of distillery capacity to supply grain ethanol in coming year; unlikely to divert sugar to syrup
items.quote: In the coming year, we do anticipate being using at least 30% or 25% to 30% of our distillery capacity to supply ethanol with grain.

items.statement: Red rot disease impact uncertain; true impact known post-monsoon; hoping for lesser impact this year
items.quote: It is a little early to say because the true impact of red rot is only a certain post monsoons. It's a waterborne disease. But if all the measures that all of us are taking, including the farmers, we hope the impact will be lesser this year.

items.statement: Cane acreage may drop 2-3% overall due to farmer shift to other crops in some units; aiming to offset with better yields
items.quote: Yes, you could s ay 2%, 3% drop overall, but we hope to make that in with better yields.

items.statement: Expect 1000-1500 tons additional sugar release from export quota sale
items.quote: So the quota that we have sold, we will continue to get the additional release on account of the sugar that got exported out of our quota. So we expect 1000 to 1500 tons of sugar to be coming into our releases on account of the quota sale.

items.statement: Cane availability expected stable to slightly up next season; clearer picture by August-September
items.quote: So whatever increase we will get will be on account of better yields. And if the weather continues to remain favorable and our cane development efforts bear fruit, we should hopefully remain stable, stable to a little bit up.

items.statement: No buyback planned until debt reduces further; debt-equity comfortable; no major capex ahead
items.quote: So at this point of time, once again, like we said, let's bring our debt down and let's get the numbers and then we'll look at buyback post that.

items.statement: Dividend of INR 1.25 per share approved for FY25 per dividend policy
items.quote: The Board has approved a dividend of INR 1.25 per share for the current year.

items.statement: Revenue growth of 14% to 15% projected for FY26
items.quote: At this point of a time, the way we have projected, this could be around 14% to 15%.

items.statement: Target 2x FY25 turnover in 3-4 years with 30% from value-added products
items.quote: In the next 3 to 4 years of time, we will have around 30% of our revenue coming from an expanded base on the current base, it will be double, and on that 30% will be coming from value-added of knitting and weaving and processed fabric.

items.statement: INR114 crores cash capex budgeted for FY26
items.quote: INR114 crores we are projecting to be spent in FY '25, '26.

items.statement: 25,000 new spindles commissioning by June 2025, costing INR215 crores
items.quote: The addition of 25,000 new spindles is progressing as scheduled, and we expect operations to commence by June '25.

items.statement: 40 knitting machines project initiated with INR38 crores capex, first 10 machines by September 2025
items.quote: We also initiated a new project to install 40 knitting machines at our existing location with a total capex of INR38 crores. Work on the first phase involving 10 machines is already underway.

items.statement: Inquiries increasing due to US tariffs but conversion delayed by 90-day pause
items.quote: This has started Jatin initially, and because of this 90 days pause period by the US. Now there's a little bit of -- the people are wanting to wait that, okay, let's wait these 90 days because after 90 days what will happen because by the time they give the order now.

items.statement: Long-term EBITDA margin target 17-20%, currently at ~10%
items.quote: We are very confident that you will start seeing these benefit maybe hopefully -- because, we right now, we can't commit on the kind of volatility we have in t he market, you know because of geopolitical, because of US tariff this thing, but once things become normal, definitely, we believe that this 17%, 18%, we will be able to deliver on that

items.statement: Cotton yarn spread currently INR119, up from INR109 in Q3
items.quote: The cotton spread at this point of time is around INR119.

items.statement: Expect demand improvement post 90-day tariff clarity, optimistic on medium-term outlook
items.quote: I'm very optimistic tha t the outlook of the textile industry in the medium term, because if you look at the tariffs. The way it has been announced by the US small advantage to India will definitely have a small -- even if a small portion of the volume shifting from other countries to India will definitely have a big boost into the business of textile

items.statement: Fabric revenue share increased from 6.5% to 7.8% in FY25, exports share from 15% to 16%
items.quote: The share of revenue from fabric increased from 6.5% in FY '24, to 7.8% in FY '25. Similarly, the share of exports has also increased from 15% noted in FY '24 to 16% of revenues in FY '25.

items.statement: US tariff uncertainty and 90-day pause creating order conversion delays
items.quote: But only because of this 90-day period, a little bit conversion of the inquiry into the orders is getting a little longer time.

items.statement: Peak debt projected at INR600 crores by FY29, debt-equity ratio maintained at 0.35
items.quote: Approximately around INR600 crores of the overall peak debt once we complete our entire process.

items.statement: Kaveri section discontinued in March 2025, incurred INR2 crores loss in FY25, benefits from April
items.quote: Broadly, we have spent around INR2 crores. The benefit of this, we could see in the month of April, the benefit has started coming in.

items.statement: No plans for garmenting currently, focus on ready-to-cut fabric first
items.quote: See, at this point of a time, we don't have any plan to go for garmenting. First, we want to establish. You know that past experience of our home textile. So we want to be firs t establish ourselves as a ready -to-cut fabric to be supplied to the garment manufacturer

items.statement: Cotton prices expected range-bound near INR55,000 per candy, CCI holding 100 lakh bales
items.quote: Domestic cotton prices are currently stable, averaging around INR55,000 per candy and international prices have also shown steady trends. We expect cotton prices to remain range bound in the near term.

items.statement: No specific guidance for FY26; will share detailed guidance mid-year as progress is made
items.quote: As of now, we are not giving any specific guidance for FY '26. We will share detailed guidance in mid of the year as we progress further.

items.statement: MBBL portfolio expected to grow faster; non-microbanking secured portfolio to see healthy growth in FY26
items.quote: Expect good growth in MBBL portfolio (individual loan). We are expecting healthy growth trend to continue for non-microbanking portfolio, which is largely secured loan portfolio in FY '26 as well.

items.statement: Profitability to remain under stress in H1 FY26, material improvement expected post H1
items.quote: Profitability is expected to remain under stress in H1 FY '26, post which we expect material improvement in profitability profile.

items.statement: SMA book in microbanking reduced from 10% (Dec'24) to 5% (Mar'25); expect SMA normalization by Q1 FY26 and meaningful reduction in fresh NPA generation
items.quote: SMA book in microbanking portfolio reduced from 10% as on December '24 to 5% as on March '25. And accordingly, we expect fresh NPA generation to reduce meaningfully in some time.

items.statement: Stress expected for another 2 quarters (Q1 and Q2 FY26); credit cost on declining trajectory but pain to continue
items.quote: We expect that this pain, whatever, pain or stress is expected to be there for another 2 quarters, so quarter 1 and quarter 2 of FY '26.

items.statement: Opened 200+ new branches in FY25, total >1,000 branches; may not need much expansion in FY26 as franchise adequate for target growth
items.quote: We have significant large franchise which is adequate for our target growth, and hence, we may not need much expansion of branch network in FY 2026.

items.statement: Reduced savings deposit rates for certain slabs and highest retail term deposit rate by 25 bps; will lead to gradual reduction in cost of funds
items.quote: Recently, we have reduced interest rates for savings deposits for certain slabs as well as highest rate for retail term deposits by 25 basis points, which will lead to reduction in cost of funds gradually.

items.statement: Approved up to INR 750 crore Tier 1 capital raise; not in hurry as capital adequacy >20% vs 15% requirement; timing and mode (rights/QIP/etc.) open based on market conditions
items.quote: We have taken approval for up to INR 750 crores Tier 1 capital that we can raise for market. So we'll certainly look at market. The moment market is receptive and good, then certainly, we'll go for this. But we'll not be in hurry because we are adequately capitalized as on date.

items.statement: No direct JLG exposure in Karnataka and Tamil Nadu; negligible presence in Karnataka via BC partnership
items.quote: Furthermore, with respect to state level ordinance and related disruption, we do not have any direct exposure towards JLG lending in Karnataka as well as Tamil Nadu.

items.statement: Non-microbanking portfolio NPA ~2.4%; credit cost 1-1.5% after FLDG benefit; profitability improving year-on-year
items.quote: NPA in non-microbanking portfolio is close to 2.4%. And credit costs in these businesses have been in the range of 1% to 1.5%.

items.statement: Reverse merger: RBI NOC received, exchange NOCs received, SEBI approval awaited; NCLT process may take 7-9 months post SEBI approval
items.quote: We have got the NOC from RBI. We also know that the two exchanges through which SEBI ultimately is in okay. So both of them have given their NOC. Currently, we have already responded queries to SEBI. I think, we are in the queue.

items.statement: Unexecuted order book of INR 120 crores carried forward to FY26; INR 243 crores L1 positions pending work orders; INR 44 crores tenders awaited; INR 450+ crores bid in April 2025
items.quote: Our order book stands robust as at the end of 31st March 2025 with INR 120 crores worth of orders being carried forward to FY25 and tenders bidded results awaited amounting to INR44 crores. Tenders worth INR 243 crores have already been declared with Solarium being declared as L1 but pending work orders till now.

items.statement: L1 orders of INR 243 crores from NTPC tender (part of INR 270 crores total); INR 27 crores received by March 2025; INR 35 crores received post-March; expecting INR 54 crores more in next 1.5 months
items.quote: Yes, so out of this INR 243 crores, this is part of a larger contract which we have won out of NTPC's tender. This is in total about INR 270 crores worth of orders out of which we have received INR 27 crores by the end of March 2025.

items.statement: INR 363 crores visibility (INR 120 crores carried forward + INR 243 crores L1); expects execution within FY26
items.quote: So, these are the numbers which we kind of foresee if we only total this up to say INR 243 crores as L1 and INR120 crores as revenue to be booked, it stands at about INR363 crores.

items.statement: Residential rooftop monthly revenue grew from INR 5 crores to INR 10 crores (2x); March 2025 alone INR 56 crores total revenue; H2 residential revenue INR 45 crores
items.quote: In terms of numbers, if we talk about, so residential rooftop, we were at INR 5 crores per month revenue at the start of the year, which has been increased to INR 10 crores at the end of the year, which is March 2025 standalone.

items.statement: PM Surya Ghar Yojana driving adoption: 9 lakh homes installed solar in last 1 year vs 10 lakh in prior 15 years; REC is nodal agency; multiple states adding subsidies
items.quote: Like if I will say, in the last 15 years, there was adoption by 10 lakh homes w ho have gone solar. But in the last only one year, around 9 lakh homes have installed solar at theirs

items.statement: Overall EBITDA margin guidance anchored at 11-13% range; residential rooftop gross margins ~20%, EBITDA margins ~10% in H2
items.quote: 11% to 13% is the range which we want to probably anchor at this point in time.

items.statement: Geographic expansion offsets margin pressure: higher gross margins in new states (UP, Delhi, Maharashtra, MP) balance maturing states (Gujarat); execution learnings from Gujarat replicated
items.quote: But good part for us is that we already started going to the other part of the country which is UP, which is Delhi, which is Maharashtra, which is Madhya Pradesh, where the adoption rate is very, very low at this point in time. And we are able to make much higher margins in those states.

items.statement: Aggressive expansion: 15+ new warehouses planned in next 6 months; opened Jodhpur warehouse recently; Solar Saarthi channel partner program (200 partners, INR 11,000 fee) enables low fixed cost city entry
items.quote: Over the next six months, there are very aggressive growth plans across India. When we say across India, largely within these states which we have already opened, going deeper into the same states with a larger number of cities. So, there are more than 15 new warehouses to be opened which are planned.

items.statement: DCR panel supply constraint delayed INR 17 crores residential orders to Q1 FY26; corporate tie-up with leading manufacturer secured; cell capacity additions by large players (Adani 3GW) expected to ease supply
items.quote: We faced challenges like limited availability of DCR panels, which delayed about INR17 crores of residential orders to Q1 of financial year 2026.

items.statement: IPO proceeds deployed in working capital; leveraging balance sheet with bank funding for growth; no IPP entry planned for next couple years
items.quote: Largely, we foresee to deploy those funds within the working capital space at this point in time as our business is growing. So, largely, the fund utilization we foresee in the working capital space.

items.statement: Strategic shift to turnkey EPC model: turnkey revenue grew from INR 100-105 crores to INR 200 crores (100% growth); trading reduced from INR 70+ crores to INR 30 crores; residential 37% of revenue, institutional ~50%
items.quote: We strategically shifted our business model towards a higher EPC share, aiming to strengthen margins and long -term profitability. This move is aligned with our f ocus on delivering more accretive value-driven solar solutions while continuing to build our own distribution

items.statement: No formal guidance given; foresees continuing growth trajectory similar to past years; residential rooftop monthly run rate of INR 10 crores expected to continue; order book visibility INR 363 crores for FY26
items.quote: In terms of the future growth, we want to refra in from any sort of guidance. But at the same point in time, we foresee to continue our growth trajectory in a similar fashion as it has happened in the past couple of years

items.statement: Employee strength grew from <200 to 309; ESOP pool >50% allocated (INR 84 lakh expense); hired segment heads, CFO, 60 IIT/IIM interns; ESOP cost to increase in absolute terms but decrease as % of revenue
items.quote: We have also strengthened our leadership by appointing segment heads, hiring an experienced individual as CFO, and bringing around 60 interns from top IITs and IIMs to support our next phase of growth. Moreover, being L1 in around 38 categories out of 45 under NTPC-distributed rooftop programs for various Indian ministries highlights our strong position in the sector.

items.statement: Receivables spike due to March revenue skew (INR 56 crores); residential AR INR 7.5 crores vs INR 10 crores revenue; subsidy transfer now within 45 days (portal transition causing temporary delays)
items.quote: March 25 alone has contributed INR 56 crores revenue. So if you see, it is largely because of the skewness, which has happened in terms of revenue of March numbers.

items.statement: Profitable since inception (2017 bootstrap); competes with Solar Square (PE-funded, losses) but state-level leadership varies (Gujarat ahead, Maharashtra behind)
items.quote: We understand our business. We are being profitable since day one, which is since the company being started as bootstrap from 2017 itself.

items.statement: Difficult terrain execution capability: executed projects near Hanle telescope (Leh), Manipur, Silchar; authorities requesting 10 more projects in Leh region; niche strength in distributed solar for government/defense
items.quote: We installed two projects there. Now, we are already in talks or rather the respective authorities are wanting us to execute 10 more projects in the same territory because no other player has been able to execute those projects.

items.statement: FY26 guidance maintained at Rs.7,000 crores revenue, Rs.1,100 crores EBITDA, and Rs.650-700 crores EBIT
items.value: 7000 crores revenue, 1100 crores EBITDA, 650-700 crores EBIT
items.quote: the guidance given during the last quarter earnings call for the first time for FY26, we have given Rs.7,000 crores top line and Rs.1,100 crores EBITDA levels and a wide range of say Rs.500 crores to Rs.700 crores EBIT, we have already reached Rs.512 crores EBIT in the current year itself. So, we are expecting in the region of Rs.650 crores to Rs.700 crores EBIT going forward in the next financial

items.statement: FY26 group capex guided at Rs.750-800 crores
items.quote: Our CAPEX guidance as a whole for a group will be only around Rs.750 crores to Rs.800 crores totally in that region.

items.statement: Standalone capex expected at Rs.550 crores in FY26
items.quote: I think Rs.550 crores for Craftsman is what we expect in the current condition.

items.statement: New powertrain business order book filling up; three-digit revenue expected in FY27, peaking at $100 million by 2029-30
items.quote: the order book is filling up, but the development cycle time is around 18 to 24 months. So, we will not see any three-digit revenue, the three-digit revenue will only come in FY27 on the new powertrain business. But as I mentioned, I think it will peak in 2029, 2030 for $100 million revenue for this business.

items.statement: Sunbeam FY26 EBITDA margin expected at 8-10% blended average
items.quote: on a blended average we can say between 8% to 10% EBITDA is what we expect for the full financial year

items.statement: Powertrain margins to creep up with better operating leverage; double-digit growth expected in FY26
items.quote: Our margins also will start creeping up with better operating leverage but depends on one quarter to another quarter there may be some changes, always Q1 will have some challenges, but we don't see much challenge this year, Q3 will be always a challenge. So, Q2 and Q4, we expect very strong quarters. So, overall, I think the run rate on the powertrain will continue to grow. It will have a double-d

items.statement: Storage business growth expected at high teens (~20%) in FY26
items.quote: High teens I would say, almost 20% we can expect the growth on the storage business.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue mix: PV 32%, 2W 18%, CV 17%, storage 10%, off-highway 5%, tractor 4%
items.quote: the commercial vehicle portion is coming to 17%, two wheeler is coming to 18%, passenger vehicle is 32%, storage is 10%, off-highways is 5% and tractor is 4%.

items.statement: No tariff impact as exports are Ex Works/FOB; no customer has requested price reduction
items.quote: All the business what we do, we are either doing Ex Works or FOB, very rarely I think hardly 5% of the business may be CIF whatever exports we are doing at Craftsman. So, similarly for DR Axion, I think the only export is back to Korea that is also FOB or Ex Works… I don't remember exactly, it is not CIF. US exports as far as Sunbeam is concerned, it is negligible. It is more towards Mexico there.

items.statement: Land sale of Sunbeam Gurgaon expected in Q3/Q4 FY26 to add ~Rs.300 crores
items.quote: aided by possibly the land sale in Q3 or Q4 of Sunbeam, that will add around Rs.300 crores plus depending on that market value at that particular point of time.

items.statement: Alloy wheel: Bhiwadi ~Rs.300 crores, Hosur ~Rs.150 crores revenue in FY26
items.quote: Bhiwadi will be around Rs.300 crores plus for FY26 and Hosur will be around Rs.150 crores. This is as per the earlier earnings call.

items.statement: Consolidated aluminum revenue run rate ~Rs.1,000 crores/quarter; FY26 expected Rs.4,300-4,500 crores
items.quote: Q4 has been Rs.1,000 crores. So, we will be anywhere between Rs.4,300 to Rs.4500 crores overall.

items.statement: Sunbeam consolidation year; no new order pipeline until FY27-28
items.quote: Sunbeam, as I mentioned, it was in an insolvency situation, so there was no order pipeline when we took over Sunbeam totally. So, it is the question of stabilization for the next one year before we get in any new order pipeline and that will get into any sort of revenue only in FY27 and FY28 only.

items.statement: Powertrain utilization ~70%; aluminum utilization 70-75%; targeting 80-85% by Q2
items.quote: have touched around 70%- odd. So, I think the upper limit will be 85% to 90% because of the seasonality as well as there will be some customers losing market share or they will have some inventory correction, which will happen. So, there is the headroom. So, I think I will not say 70, slightly below 70, very difficult to exactly put a number to it. Even in the aluminum side, we are at operating at

items.statement: Fronberg repair & maintenance capex ~Rs.40-50 crores under evaluation
items.quote: there is some repair and maintenance for a very old equipment at Fronberg, which may be around Rs.40 crores, Rs.50 crores, may be there, we're evaluating that.

items.statement: FY26 AUM growth 20-21%, disbursement growth 18-19%, PAT growth 20-21%, GNPA 1.10-1.15%
items.quote: So Abhishek, in terms of growth targets or guidance we will maintain our AUM guidance of 20%-21%, disbursement growth of about 18%-19% and a PAT of about 20%-21%. And on the NPA front we believe that we should be around 1.10% to 1.15%.

items.statement: Cost-to-income improved 104 bps in FY25 to 36.4%; target further 30-50 bps reduction in FY26
items.quote: I think when we reduce 120 bps of cost to income, I think I have said that we want to reduce about 150 bps in 2 years, to be very honest. And we have already done about 120 bps in year 1. I think to be very honest, next year, we will have around 30 to 50 b ps sort of a drop in cost to income

items.statement: Exit spread 5.7% in FY25; aim to maintain yields at current levels (minus 5-6 bps) in FY26
items.quote: And as Rishi said, the reason of us going on emerging A, B and C is primarily to ensure that our next year yields also fall into the same range as we exited in the current financial year. So we would like to maintain yields at similar levels, may be minus 5 to 6 basis points, but otherwise we would like to maintain at similar levels.

items.statement: ECB of $50M at SOFR+156 bps, fully hedged all-in cost ~8.1%; blended borrowing cost 7.9% for NHB drawdowns
items.quote: The ECB that we did was for US $50 million. We did it in Quarter 4 FY'25 and this is a fully hedged transaction that we have carried out. This is carried out at a SOFR plus 156 bps and the full all-in hedged cost comes in around 8.1%.

items.statement: Demand similar across urban and emerging; competitive intensity lower in emerging A/B/C driving higher conversion
items.quote: So demand, whether it is urban or whether it is emerging, not rural again, it is more or less similar. It is all about how do we reach there, where is competition playing a larger role?

items.statement: Emerging mix to rise from 45% to 55% of AUM in 2 years; self-employed and self-construction share to increase in emerging
items.quote: Urban and emerging split, I can tell you is about 55% current is from the urban locations and the balance is from the emerging locations. And we would look at maintaining 55% should eventually in a couple of years should go to about from emerging and 45% from urban, so it will reverse as we move ahead.

items.statement: GNPA improved 3 bps YoY to 1.05%; Stage-2 at 4% includes 0.6-0.7% COVID restructured assets; no early stress in Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, MP
items.quote: GNPA as at 31st of March is 1.05%, and this is one of the best performances in terms of GNPA in the last 3 to 4 years that the company has demonstrated. There is an improvement of 3 bps of GNPA on an AUM basis.

items.statement: Incremental borrowings INR 5,024 cr in FY25; first ECB $50M; undrawn sanctions INR 891 cr; liquidity INR 2,200 cr (10.7% of book)
items.quote: Our incremental borrowings for FY'25 stood at INR 5,024 crores. We have around 43 borrowing relationships among national housing bank, banks, housing finance banks, mutual funds and DFIs.

items.statement: In-house sourcing rose to 59% (from 54%); Aadhaar Mitra referral contribution ~30% of disbursements (up from 22% in FY24)
items.quote: Broadly, if I can tell you, in-house, which was 54% last year, has grown to 59%. So almost 60% is now in-house. And the balance is external split between DSAs and connectors.

items.statement: State concentration cap maintained at ~14% of AUM; no plan to raise threshold
items.quote: We as management, we have strategically decided whether it is distribution whether it is incremental disbursement or whether it is AUM we will not breach the 14% mark, maybe 50 bps here and there 14-14.5 but that's the range we will be around.

items.statement: Credit rating upgrade discussions ongoing with both agencies; recent meetings held; decision at agency level
items.quote: We are already engaged with both the credit rating agencies. And I don't foresee that this rating upgrade should be prolonged for too long, while obviously, it is a decision that will be taken at their management level or the rating committee level.

items.statement: Write-offs INR 8-9 cr in Q4 FY25, INR 32 cr full year; no prudential write-off in Q4
items.quote: This would be approximately INR 8 crores to INR 9 crores in Quarter 4. Siraj Khan: Full year? Rajesh Viswanathan: INR 32 crores would be the full

items.statement: MFI overlap customers fell from 9,096 to 7,077; Tamil Nadu operations normal with government support
items.quote: Our numbers were about 9,000-odd customers, 9,096 customers who had MFI exposure. That number has dropped to about 7,077 customers now. So loans have been foreclosed

items.statement: Domestic jewellery EBITDA margin was 11.6% in Q4 FY25, aided by operating leverage and hedging gains; 11-11.5% guidance maintained for FY26.
items.quote: Actually 11.9% if you think about domestic jewellery business, it's kind of 11.6%. You can see in our disclosure that there has been higher primary for international business and they had some positive impact on the reported number. But 11.6% nevertheless had element of, small element of operating leverage as well as some hedging gains sitting it.

items.statement: Jewellery EBIT margin guidance maintained at 11-11.5% for FY26 despite uncertainty.
items.quote: As far as coming to 11% to 11.5% margin guidance, I think that stays. We are not guiding you for any upside. Considering the uncertainty of gold prices and many, many uncertainties for future, 11% to 11.5% seems to be more reasonable to think about.

items.statement: Targeting healthy double-digit jewellery growth in FY26 (15-20% range), driven by ticket size or buyer growth; Q4 retail growth ~20%.
items.quote: Certainly, what you said is true. When gold prices are going up sequentially there is a benefit there is a value growth and therefore there's a ticket size growth that we see. And in our mind, as I mentioned in an earlier question, we are certainly planning and targeting and also hoping for a healthy double-digit growth, either driven by ticket size or by buyer or by both.

items.statement: Plan to open 40-50 new Tanishq stores in FY26; also renovate/relocate/expand 50-60 existing stores.
items.quote: 40 to 50 stores. But more importantly, we are also looking at 50 to 60 stores of existing stores being either renovated or relocated or adding additional space.

items.statement: Gold price rise impacting sub-₹50k segment sentiment; consumers shifting to lighter, lower-caratage, lower-making-charge jewellery.
items.quote: As gold prices have kind of clipped up so sharply, we are seeing in the sub ₹50,000 price band, very specifically, more in gold and little bit in studded also, there is an impact on the consumer sentiment there. Now some of it is us vacating price points because simply gold price goes up, the same product goes into a certain higher price band. That is one part of the story. But there is continued,

items.statement: Studded buyer growth outpacing gold buyers; small solitaire sizes seeing whopping buyer increase; portfolio play across Tanishq, CaratLane, Mia driving sub-₹1L studded growth.
items.quote: On Studded, small stones, I don't think this story is at all playing out the way we might be imagining. And that is more than 90% of the studded. So different stories sitting here and different kinds of segments and very, we are also leveraging that. And by the way, on the Solitaire side, smaller stone sizes, we are seeing a whopping increase in buyers. And at overall level, studded buyers is outp

items.statement: Gold metal loan rates doubled temporarily but settling ~75-80 bps above historical; gold price rise increases financing cost 30-40%.
items.quote: Of course, you are right that as a knee jerk reaction, gold on lease rate (GOL) has gone up almost doubled and more than doubled and it is settling down now. But more than that even gold price, you know, gold rate also impact our financing cost because now the same quantity of GOL is far more expensive 30%-40% and I have to pay interest on that 30%-40%.

items.statement: Exchange policy risk low; cash exchange incidence in decimals; diamond-to-gold exchange very low; store-of-value culture supports policy.
items.quote: In India, the category of jewellery is so much about store of value and in a way the exchange policies reflect that customer need and therefore even the lower, relatively lower gross margins in this industry in India because of the store of value concept because customers don't want to lose when they exchange.

items.statement: LGD wholesale and retail prices falling sharply (retail ~₹30k/carat); market choppy; Titan evaluating customer relevance and economic viability before entry.
items.quote: Most certainly the wholesale price was anyway coming down continuously and it continues to drop. And I think that will not stop because even automation will happen and many other tech developments and productivity developments will push costs down like any tech product. But interestingly, even on the retail side, many of the players were retailing LGD products at roughly ₹60,000 to ₹50,000 a carat

items.statement: East and South leading growth; West and North sluggish in FY25.
items.quote: I think East and South continue to lead the growth and West and North have been a little more sluggish and within that again West maybe a little bit more than North, has been sluggish. But that seems to have been the trend of the previous Financial Year that just ended 31st March.

items.statement: Competitive intensity high; unhedged players discount making charges; Titan responds with brand, experience, design, making charges.
items.quote: Those who don't hedge do sit on inventory gains and they are willing to let go of margin and they play it out in the form of heavy discounting on making charges. And it is not just restricted to small players, it is also even larger players. Not every large player is hedging 100%. So it does play out. So yes, but we also then respond in whichever way is appropriate for that market.

items.statement: Balance sheet capable of leveraging for working capital if gold prices keep rising; will increase GOL usage.
items.quote: If gold price continue to rise like this, while we have some levers of increasing our GOL level, etc. etc. but it would certainly require some more capital investment from our side and for which our balance sheet can be leveraged, it is capable, but idea would be then to leverage GOL more.

items.statement: Hedging gain in Q4 from contango on international forwards; part permanent, part phasing; not significant enough to quantify separately.
items.quote: Gold is volatile at this point of time and we have, if I can use the word contango gain, when you are doing forwards in gold thing, when you do the future, there is a different economics. When you do the forwards with the gold on international exchanges, then there is a different economics. And we have been able to do some of that transactions in Quarter 4, which gives us contango gain. And that i

items.statement: Positive tailwinds for FY26: good Q1 wedding season, infra spending, tax relief liquidity; outlook bullish for next few years.
items.quote: See this year there is a very good wedding season in Quarter 1. Last year there wer elections in Quarter 1 and there were no wedding dates. Infrastructure spending by government has continued and will continue for the first 4-5 months, which was not there last year. There is also the largesse from the finance ministry on the IT for a large number of people in the country. Maybe not directly, but a

items.statement: CaratLane launched 9-carat jewellery (non-hallmarked); good response; 9-carat hallmarking likely soon.
items.quote: We launched this 9-carat jewellery sometime around valentine and we saw good response. This is not hallmarked. We are not claiming it is hallmarked. But it is stated as 9 carat diamond jewellery, it is sold as 9 carat diamond jewellery. But it is also quite likely that 9 carat is going to come under hallmarking very soon. It is in advanced stage.

items.statement: US tariff impact minimal so far; no price hikes taken; monitoring; bilateral trade agreement progress likely positive.
items.quote: Tariffs, as of the way we are seeing things now in both in the US market, it's not really cost any significant thing, but that we have not taken any price increases as yet. We're waiting. We will watch how the whole situation unfolds and then basis that depending on what competition also does, it's quite likely that if tariffs go up, then we will take price increases.

items.statement: Vacuum salt and bromine projects scheduled for commissioning in FY26, commercial production expected to start in Q3 FY26
items.quote: Commissioning of our vacuum salt and bromine project remain scheduled for FY '26. We expect these projects to begin contributing to our growth from FY '26, while enhancing our product portfolio and competitive positioning.

items.statement: FY25 growth capex of INR311 crores spent on greenfield, vacuum salt, bromine, Zara Zumara, seawater pipeline, compressor and salt drilling
items.quote: On the growth capex, we have spent around INR180 crores. That covers greenfield, vacuum salt, bromine and Zara Zumara. And then on the existing plant, the remaining figure has been spent, of which largely is seawater pipeline and compressor.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 EBITDA margin at 30.2% vs 23.8% in Q4 FY24, full year EBITDA up 7% YoY to INR966 crores due to operational efficiencies and cost reduction
items.quote: EBITDA margin came in at strong 30.2% compared to 23.8% in Q4 FY '24. For the full year, EBITDA came in at INR966 crores, which is an increase of 7% ye ar-on-year. Our margins remained resilient due to higher production, operational efficiencies and innovation resulting in reduction in input

items.statement: Soda ash prices expected to be softer in near term due to weak demand in China, Europe and US, but structural tailwinds from solar glass duty and renewable energy focus
items.quote: Madhav, like I said, it is very difficult at this point of a time to kind of predict what will happen. But yes, like I said, China is softer. Globally, Europe is also softer. Even US demands are also not picking up. So the prices will be softer.

items.statement: Vacuum salt and bromine projects on existing salt field and plant, commercial production starting Q3 FY26, will enhance product portfolio and competitive positioning
items.quote: See, in terms of bromine, we are doing this bromine, current bromine, which is likely to be commissioned in FY '26, is on the existing salt field, and that project is going as per the schedule. Likely production, means commercial production, will start in third quarter. Vacuum salt also likely to be in the third quarter.

items.statement: Geopolitical uncertainty, US tariffs, China demand moderation, and potential surplus in China creating pricing pressure; minimum import price benefit limited, anti-dumping duty application filed
items.quote: The global macro setup has been marked by rising uncertainty and volatility, influenced by recent impositi on of tariffs by the United States. These events have had broader implications on global trade dynamics, economic activities and market sentiments

items.statement: PBDIT margin guidance maintained at 18-20% despite competitive intensity
items.quote: we are still very confident that today, as we are going ahead, there are series of things as an organization which we have taken up, whether it is a very big area of backward integration which we have built in.

items.statement: White cement plant at Fujairah (2.75 lakh tonnes) operational by June 2025
items.quote: The plant should be operational by June of this year, and we will continue to look at white cement coming from this plant for us which is our first foray into cement.

items.statement: Futuristic emulsion plant with Capex over Rs 3000 crores, partially operational March-April 2026, fully by April 2027
items.quote: It is futuristic and only about four players in the world have technology for it. So, this is the first plant we are putting up with a C apEx of more than Rs 3000 crores

items.statement: Standalone Q4 gross margin at peak 44.9%, PBDIT margin 18.5% within 18-20% guidance
items.quote: From point of view of gross margins, have gone up which is a combination of some deflation and some of the work which has been done by sourcing of formulation efficiencies what we have brought in.

items.statement: Consolidated FY25 gross margin 42.3% down ~100bps, PBDIT margin 17.8%
items.quote: Gross margins are at about 42.3%, almost about 100 bps decline. And in terms of PBDIT margins, it is 17.8%.

items.statement: Deflation of 0.5-1% expected in current quarter (Q1 FY26)
items.quote: We see in the current quarter also there would be a deflation of about 0.5% to 1% what would happen.

items.statement: Cautiously optimistic for Q1 FY26; Tier 3-4 cities better than Tier 1-2; government spending returning
items.quote: Overall, I think there is an element of flux which is happening from the geopolitical situation which is going around. We'll have to wait and see how things really mature there in terms of their normalcy.

items.statement: Innovation contributed 14% to Q4 topline; 300+ new products and 130+ patents in last 5 years
items.quote: This trajectory has contributed almost 14% to the top line in Q4. So, very strong initiative from a innovation point.

items.statement: Impairment provisions: White Teak Rs 77.8 cr (consolidated), Rs 78.5 cr (standalone); Indonesia divestment loss Rs 83.7 cr; Sri Lanka Causeway Paints impairment Rs 21.5 cr
items.quote: If you look at it, the total impairment provision on goodwill consolidation is Rs77.8 crores. On standalone, the impact is about Rs 78.5 crores.

items.statement: FY25 decorative volume growth 2.5%, value decline -5.7%; industrial volume growth 2.8%, value decline -4.6%
items.quote: On a 12 monthly basis, we are up by about 2.5% on volume terms and on a value we are down by about -5.7%.

items.statement: Dividend payout maintained at 60% for FY25
items.quote: Just a quick point, the dividend payout has been consistent. We have been able to grow and maintain. We have taken a dividend payout at 60% as well for this year.

items.statement: White Teak billing halted for 4-5 months due to BIS specifications and China input dependencies
items.quote: we have been stuck in W hite Teak and not able to look at any selling which has happened in a big way in the last 4-5 months leading to possibly a degrowth which has happened

items.statement: AP Global Q4 -1.5% reported, +6% constant currency; FY25 flat; Africa underperformed due to currency devaluation
items.quote: In quarter four, we were at about -1.5%, although in constant currency terms, we were still at about 6%. However, from a yearly perspective, we are just at base.

items.statement: Distribution network expanded to 1.69 lakh touch points
items.quote: We have almost about 1.69 lakh touch points created over a period and that is a fairly strong number of how this keeps on increasing quarter to quarter and over the years.

items.statement: Home Decor: 67 Beautiful Home stores across 53 cities; #1 in modular kitchens and decorative lighting; Nilaya Anthology luxury store launched in Mumbai
items.quote: Today this is a very strong spread of offering Home Decor under one roof. These are initial stages; I would say it may take time to build up this category.

items.statement: Home Decor categories (kitchens, bath, White Teak, Weatherseal) making losses in Q4 and FY25
items.quote: In both the categories there is a certain loss which we are making in quarter four and as well as for the year. And that is something which we need to set it right as we are going ahead.

items.statement: Aiming for single digit value growth for Asian Paints in FY26
items.quote: But the idea is to aim for single digit value growths for the year FY26.

items.statement: Consolidated CapEx of Rs 700-800 crore expected in FY26 and similar in FY27
items.quote: We are expecting about Rs 700 to 800 crores outflow this year and probably a similar number next year.

items.statement: Government spending returning, mid-to-luxury housing flaring up, rural demand improving with good monsoon
items.quote: First, what we are seeing from the last third and the fourth quarter is the government spending is coming back which was disrupted in the first half because of elections or otherwise.

items.statement: Gross margin improvement driven by raw material deflation and raw material efficiencies
items.quote: The gross margin improvement came at two levels. One was the deflation which happened in the market and second, what we see is that the raw material efficiencies which have been built in, with the work which we have done.

items.statement: New product contribution 14% of sales, largely from interiors (65%) and premium to luxury space (60%)
items.quote: Largely it would come from interiors about 65% would be interiors roughly.

items.statement: Competitive intensity from both existing players and new entrant, not just new entrant
items.quote: So, possibly it is a combination of existing players and some of the new players who have come in, which are adding to the competitive intensity, not these two.

items.statement: No immediate price cuts despite crude correction; waiting to see geopolitical developments and anti-dumping duties
items.quote: At this moment I don't think it would be really appropriate to take stances in looking at either decreasing or looking at prices in very different ways.

items.statement: Volume-value growth gap at 7-7.5%, target to bring within 6% band
items.quote: I had commented last time also that we are aiming that this should not be more than 6%, as we see it this time it is between 7 to 7.5%.

items.statement: White cement plant CapEx complete in FY26; VAM/VAE plant CapEx of Rs 3000 crore to continue till FY27
items.quote: It's only part of the VAM VA E plant CapEx which is going to go till FY27 which would be left out of Rs 3000 crores.

items.statement: B2B business expected to gain from government infrastructure spending on airports, tunnels, bridges
items.quote: And we feel that is going to give us a good gain from our whole B2B business which is going to come up.

items.statement: Down trading observed due to liquidity crunch and postponement of repainting
items.quote: Given the fact that there is a little bit of a crunch, there is a postponement which is happening. T his year possibly on the repainting there has been a bit of a postponement which has also happened

items.statement: Distribution reach at 169,000 dealers; potential to expand beyond 2.5 lakh with new touch points in Northeast, J&K, smart cities
items.quote: So, if you ask me frankly saying that will it stop at 2.5 lakh? No it will not.

items.statement: Industrial margins strong in auto and refinishes; pressure in powder, protective paints, road marking paints
items.quote: I think the margins basically come under some pressure when you look at categories like powder and 38 | Page protective paints or even a R oad marking

items.statement: Not willing to irrationally defend market share at cost of sustainability; focus on brand building and value proposition
items.quote: Just irrationally going after saying that I want to prevent the share at any cost whatsoever might not be a good approach.

items.statement: Confident of delivering double-digit revenue growth in FY26
items.quote: We remain confident of delivering double -digit revenue growth in FY '25-'26.

items.statement: Target to open 30-plus hotels in FY26 with 3 on balance sheet
items.quote: We expect to deliver strong growth with sustained margins and continued portfolio growth, with a target of opening 30-plus hotels in FY '26, 3 of which will be on our balance sheet.

items.statement: Pipeline of 134 hotels as on date, over 95% capital-light signings
items.quote: Over 95%, I repeat, 95% of these signings are capital light, resulting in an industry-leading pipeline of 134 hotels as on date.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin expanded to 35% in FY25, hotel segment margin 35.9%
items.quote: Our consolidated revenue stood at INR 8,565 crores, and our EBITDA margin expanded to 35% in FY '25.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin expanded 260 bps to 43.9% in FY25
items.quote: Our standalone performance in FY '25 was also the best ever with 12% growth in revenue to INR 5,145 crores and EBITDA margin expansion by 260 basis points to 43.9%.

items.statement: ARR-driven growth with high flow-through of 80-100% on rate increases
items.quote: See, if the business comes through rate increase, the flow-through is very high. It could be 80%, 90% or even 100%, depends on what rates we are talking about.

items.statement: Demand outpacing supply with 6% room nights sold growth vs under 3% supply growth in FY25
items.quote: In FY '24-'25, demand represented by room nights sold grew 6% as against supply of room nights available, growing only under 3% versus last year for industry.

items.statement: April 2025 consolidated revenue grew ~17% YoY with strong business on books for Q1
items.quote: We have begun the new financial year on a stro ng note with April 2025, consolidated revenue growing by approximately 17% over April 2024, and strong business on books for Q1

items.statement: New businesses (Ginger, Qmin, Ama, Tree of Life) grew 40% to INR 602 crores at 37% margin
items.quote: Our new business is vertical comprising Ginger, Qmin, Ama Stays & Trails and now Tree of Life delivered a 40% growth in FY '25, resulting in a consolidated revenue of INR 602 crores. New business continues to be margin accretive with a consolidated margin of 37%.

items.statement: TajSATS margin impact of ~1% in FY26 due to new levy accounting, but revenue to grow 3-5% extra
items.quote: Overall, if you look at how we are looking at their numbers, the next year, FY '26, we expect because of this, there could be a 1% impac t on the margin, but this will also help in growth in the revenues because this levy now gets added to the revenue

items.statement: Liquidity of INR 3,000 crores to tackle headwinds and pursue consolidation opportunities
items.quote: IHCL has liquidity of INR 3,000 crores, which will not only help us tackle headwinds, if any, I repeat tackle wins any kind of headwinds, if any, but will also give us an advantage for any consolidation opportunities that may arise in due course.

items.statement: Dividend proposed at ~20% of consolidated PAT, INR 2.25 per share
items.quote: Reflective of the company's sustained financial performance, a dividend of ~ 20% of consolidated PAT amounting to INR 2.25 per share is proposed, subject to shareholders' approval.

items.statement: Direct booking share rising, each percentage saves INR 700-1,500 per booking
items.quote: Each percentage increase or each room night that we don't have it going through there saves us anything around INR 1,000 to INR 1,500 based on the total mix. But as the growth is coming more in the upscale and mid-scale brands, so you can safely assume around INR 700, INR 800 per booking that is channeled directly through our website.

items.statement: Target 30% revenue growth conservatively for FY26
items.quote: Yes. So our statement is that we will target 30% growth conservatively. That's what we are making as an official statement.

items.statement: Target EBITDA margin in mid to late teens over next few years
items.quote: So we have an ambitious plan that we would like to have at least our EBITDA, maybe in the range of mid -teens to late teens.

items.statement: Order book of INR893 crores as of March 2025, executable within 12 months
items.quote: We ended the year with an order book of INR893 crores, up from INR534 crores in FY '24 and INR307 crores in FY '23.

items.statement: Capex of INR43 crores incurred in FY25 for backward integration and new products
items.quote: During the year, we incurred a capex of INR43 crores primarily to strengthen backward integration and accelerate new products manufacturing at our Sinnar and Satpur plant.

items.statement: Board approved backward integration expansion at Sinnar with estimated investment of INR52 crores
items.quote: The estimated investment for the proposed expansion is approximately INR52 crores.

items.statement: Board approved land acquisition of INR50 crores for potential future expansion
items.quote: Further, the Board has also approved acquisition of land within India and amount of INR50 crores in aggregate for potential future expansion.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved to 10.9% in FY25 from 8.7% in FY24
items.quote: EBITDA stood at INR71.8 crores with a margin of 10.9%, up from 8.7% in FY '24.

items.statement: Backward integration of aluminum tank (30-35% of BOM) enabled 45% market share in traction transformers
items.quote: This is the backward integration that we have done for the transformers, where we were importing the aluminum tank from Switzerland and that constituted about 30%-35% of the BOM cost.

items.statement: Propulsion system (4 components) developed in-house, field trials underway, eligible for 20% development order after 50,000 km
items.quote: We have supplied. It is commissioned and it is running in the field.

items.statement: Propulsion system realization INR1.75-1.8 crores per set; hotel load converter INR1-1.15 crores
items.quote: About INR1.75 crores to INR1.8 crores.

items.statement: Indian Railways produced 1,400 locomotives in FY25, expects ~1,500 in FY26; INR455 billion allocated for rolling stock
items.quote: Last year was 1,400 locomotives. So that's 1,400 propulsion systems. And this year will be pretty much the same, maybe around 1,500 locomotives.

items.statement: Future expansion to be funded by debt and internal accruals; no equity raise planned
items.quote: Yes, it will be debt plus internal accruals.

items.statement: New products expected to commercialize from H1 2026 including next-gen converters, braking systems, HVAC for coaches
items.quote: Many of the solutions we are developing, are at advanced stages and expected to go commercialize from the first half of 2026.

items.statement: Two wholly-owned subsidiaries incorporated: Coincade Studios (IT/AI/Web3) and Hirect FZ-LLC (Middle East power sector)
items.quote: During the year, our Board approved the incorporation of two wholly-owned subsidiaries, Coincade Studios Private Limited which is aimed at developing next -generation solutions in the field of IT, AI and Web3 & other emerging technologies and Hirect FZ-LLC strategically positioned to expand our presence in the power generation, transmission and distribution sectors in the Middle East.

items.statement: AMC for propulsion systems estimated at 3-5% of realization value (INR1.8 cr)
items.quote: It will be somewhere around between 3% to 5% or something like that.

items.statement: Full-year FY25 EBITDA margin was about 13.5%, noting prior year included INR 8 crore pre-tax profit on sale of investments.
items.quote: For the full year, we've had EBITDA margins of about 13.5%.

items.statement: No major capex planned; only INR 10-15 crore for incremental/debottlenecking investments.
items.quote: We have a plan of about INR 10 crores to INR 15 crores, but no thing major compared to what we have done, the major expansion at Dahej, which happened over the last few years

items.statement: Specialty chemicals capacity utilization is 50-60% on average, with headroom to double current specialty sales.
items.quote: On the average, I would say we are between 50% to 60% in our Specialty Chemicals business in terms of capacity utilization.

items.statement: European export demand has declined structurally due to high energy costs; company is developing Latin America and China markets to offset.
items.quote: We could see the European demand coming down and particularly impacted by the increasing costs, not only for energy, but for everything else as well. And we are looking at and we have been active in developing new markets.

items.statement: Sulfur price jumped ~40% in recent months; pass-through to specialty contracts will reflect in Q1 FY26.
items.quote: What happened in the previous quarter is an unusual jump in the sulfur price, which will get reflected in the contract pricing in Q1 of this financial year. So we will be able to pass it on. And normally, it's not this much, so it doesn't reflect like that. But this time, it was substantial. So I think 40% or so was a change in the price just across the last few months.

items.statement: Upcoming Kutch copper smelter (expected in 3-6 months) will add sulfuric acid supply, pressuring sulfur-based producers.
items.quote: We expect in the next 3 to 6 months, it will come online. But it is not in our control or anything.

items.statement: Full-year FY25 revenue split roughly 50% specialty, 50% bulk; boron business ~INR 90-100 crore (70% commodity, 30% specialty).
items.quote: So roughly 50-50, I would say.

items.statement: Management refuses to give forward margin or revenue projections, citing commodity dependence and volatility.
items.quote: No, there is no such thing, and I don't like to give forward projections because we are still heavily de pendent on commodities, very difficult to project future margins and too many fluctuations, too many variables at any given time and becoming more and more variable every day, as you can

items.statement: Specialty volumes grew 15-20% in FY25; bulk volumes flat at 90-95% utilization.
items.quote: But main change is in the volume of the specialties. And while we don't publish individual product numbers or anything like that, but you can say at least 15% to 20% jump in the specialties.

items.statement: Annual maintenance capex includes INR 1.5-2 crore for sulfuric acid plant shutdown every 1-2 years plus regular upkeep.
items.quote: And the other part is, say, once in a year or once in 2 years, we need to shut down our su lfuric acid plant for maintenance. So that's when we spend about INR 1.5 crores to INR 2 crores depending on what equipment needs to be

items.statement: Dahej shutdown cost 10-15 days in Q4 FY25; Roha shutdown of 20-25 days planned in Q1 FY26 will impact production.
items.quote: And we have a shutdown in Roha in Q1 of '25-'26, and that will be a slightly longer shutdown. That is about 20 days to 25 days total shutdown time.

items.statement: Long-term borrowings below INR 60 crore; working capital comfortable; no major capex planned.
items.quote: In terms of our debt and things like this, we a re quite comfortably placed. We are repaying debt, and our long-term borrowings are now below INR 60 crores

items.statement: US tariffs not expected to impact as few US producers exist; any tariffs can be passed on as competitors face same or higher tariffs.
items.quote: But as far as our products are concerned, there don't appear to be too many producers in the U.S. Therefore, we do not expect any impact of the tariffs and if the tariffs do come into play, we will be in a position to pass them on to the customers in the U.S., as all our competition as well will face the same tariffs or higher tariffs.

items.statement: Three specialty products in commercial trials; expect full acceptance in current year; new products for next year commercialization.
items.quote: And we expect that the products which we've recently launched will get fully accepted in this current year. And in this current year, we will develop some new products, which we'll take up in the next year for commercialization.

items.statement: Company currently under old tax regime; expects to move to new regime (25-26%) next year or year after.
items.quote: So both plants are in the same company, and we are currently under the old tax regime, but we expect by next year, we'll go to the new tax regime next year or the year after.

items.statement: Overall top line growth expected 12% to 15% and bottom line growth 15% to 20%
items.value: 12% to 15% top line, 15% to 20% bottom line
items.quote: And the growth we can expect in top line 12% to 15%, as we already told you. And the growth which we are expecting in bottom line is around 15% to 20% based on -- and this is...

items.statement: PU business expected to increase minimum 15%-20% in next two years
items.quote: Minimum 15%-20 % will increase.

items.statement: Mexico unit postponed for 3-4 months due to US tariff uncertainty
items.quote: Future capex, we have told that we wanted to open a unit in Mexico. But because of this USA problem, we are waiting for another 3 months to see whether the -- what is the outcome.

items.statement: No order cancellations; order size increasing on 2-year basis
items.quote: No cancellation. In fact, we are getting some increase on year -- 2-year basis.

items.statement: Gross profit jump driven by increase in automotive and general exports
