items.quote: Because of increase in automotive exports, especially and other exports, general export. This growth in margin has come mainly because of that.

items.statement: Chemical price decline impacted margins 10%-15% but not significantly
items.quote: Whatever is there, prices of course chemical down, has affected, but it is not much, 10% -15%, not that much affected.

items.statement: Domestic demand described as okay, not very high
items.quote: In terms -- it's okay. Vinod Kumar Sharma: It's okay. Suresh Kumar Poddar: Yes, okay. It's not very

items.statement: US tariff impact currently nil; waiting 3-4 months for clarity on Mexico expansion
items.quote: We have no effect of this tariff -- change in tariff. Because we are exporting directly from India to U.S. through the port of Mexico. That's it. So therefore, this tariff change is not affecting to us.

items.statement: Export OEM INR253 crores, Export General INR91.4 crores, Domestic OEM INR175 crores, Auto Replacement INR142 crores, Footwear INR182 crores, Furnishing INR24 crores for FY25
items.quote: Export general, INR91.40 crores; Export OEM, INR253 crores; and Domestic OEM, INR175 crores: Auto Replacement, INR142 crores; Footwear INR182 crores; Furnishing INR24 crores.

items.statement: Other income spike of INR40 crores includes non-recurring government grants for Gwalior plant; recurring grant ~INR3 crores/year
items.quote: Basically, this INR40 crores is inclusive of government grants, which we were expecting for last -- it was applied for, for last 3 to 4 years. And that we have received. But for every year, it is not more than INR3 crores.

items.statement: Capacity setup takes minimum 12-15 months plus local approvals and OEM quality process
items.quote: Minimum, it takes 12 months to 15 months minimum, it takes to put up a capacity, anywhere. And permission and other approvals depends on the local laws of the country.

items.statement: Lithuania subsidiary set up for European general and furnishing retail; trading to start soon
items.quote: Further to start general and furnishing retail business segment in European market, we have already set up a subsidiary company in Lithuania and trading activities is also going to start soon in this quarter to Lithuania and nearby countries in Europe.

items.statement: US export OEM sales ~INR180 crores out of INR250 crores total export OEM; general exports >INR90 crores worldwide
items.quote: Our total export OEM sale is INR250 crores, okay, total at consolidated level. Out of that, around INR70 crores is in South Africa and INR180 crores nearly is in US.

items.statement: Targeting double-digit revenue growth on CAGR basis for next 2 years; aim to cross INR3,000 crores then INR3,500 crores by FY27
items.quote: We still are optimistic of achieving a double-digit growth as far as revenues are concerned on a CAGR basis for next 2 years at least. The thing is initially -- our initial target would be to cross INR3,000 crores on an immediate basis. And then from there, we will try to reach INR3,500 crores.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin target 14-15% for FY26
items.quote: 14% to 15% is the stable guidance what we are giving here.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin target 14-15% for FY26
items.quote: So we are hoping that in the s tand-alone company, we'll be maintaining that at least around 14% to 15% -- between 14% to 15%, we'll try to maintain

items.statement: Formulation revenue growth target 20-25% for FY26
items.quote: So we are targeting about between 20% to 25% of revenue growth in formulation.

items.statement: FY26 capex guidance INR150-200 crores consolidated; similar amount in FY27
items.quote: I would say roughly around INR 150 crores to INR 200 crores would be the range of capex, which we might do in FY '26. And then again, similar kind of amount probably in FY '27 when more newer products are identified.

items.statement: FY25 capex incurred INR177 crores
items.quote: The capex incurred during full year of FY '25 amounted to INR177 crores.

items.statement: USFDA import alert 66-40 removed for Tarapur facility; key APIs cleared for US export
items.quote: We are also pleased to share that company received letter from U SFDA on 14th February 2025, which has officially removed our API manufacturing facility located at Tarapur from import alert 66-40

items.statement: Gross margin improved over 200 bps to 35.8% in FY25; expect further improvement from regulated sales and backward integration
items.quote: For the full year, one of the most significant positives for the year was marked the improvement in gross margins, which improved over 200 basis points to 35.8%.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 consolidated EBITDA margin 14%; standalone API+spec chem+intermediates 14.5%
items.quote: In Q4 FY '25, revenues grew by 9% to INR679 crores with EBITDA margins improving to 14%.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 rate variance -4% to -5% YoY; Q1-Q2 FY26 expect -3% to -4% negative rate variance; H2 FY26 stable
items.quote: Rate variance, we have seen around minus 4% to 5% year-on-year for the quarter.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 API volume growth 15.5% YoY driven by exports; targeting double-digit volume growth FY26
items.quote: During the quarter, we witnessed strong global demand for APIs, driving a 15.5% growth in volumes, primarily led by exports.

items.statement: Saykha greenfield antidiabetic backward integration trial production started; Tarapur greenfield targeting 700 tons/month by June 2025, 1,600 tons/month by end FY26
items.quote: The Tarapur Greenfield project had certain initial operational challenges, which have now been largely resolved. The company remains focused on a gradual production scale-up, targeting over 700 tons per month by the month of June 2025 and aiming to reach a cumulative capacity of approximately 1,600 tons per month by the end of FY '26.

items.statement: Pakistan exports ~2.9% of sales; monitoring trade ties, will divert volumes if needed
items.quote: So our exports to Pakistan is a little less than around 2.9% or so. Definitely, we are keeping a close watch on the progress of the trade ties between India and Pakistan.

items.statement: Investing INR8.05 crores in 26.25% stake in Pro-Zeal Green Power Nine for 24.4 MW solar plant
items.quote: The total investment committed amount to INR8.05 crores to be invested in a phased manner.

items.statement: Power & fuel savings INR10-15 crores FY26, INR25-30 crores annually from solar and cogen boiler
items.quote: However, for FY '26, we feel around INR10 crores to INR15 crores might -- of benefit might come in this year itself. And from next year onwards, it should be around INR25 crores to INR30 crores.

items.statement: Fill-finish facility expected to be capitalized by Q2 FY26
items.quote: for fill finish activity, the expected timeline to have a capitalization is by Q2 this year considering the remaining batches to be commercialized and the regulatory approvals in the place.

items.statement: Hester Africa breakeven expected in two years
items.quote: We hope that not this year, the next year, we hope two years we should take to breakeven at Hester Africa

items.statement: No concrete new capex plan for FY26 beyond fill-finish commissioning and maintenance
items.quote: For the CAPEX, right now there is not much plan on it. As mentioned earlier, our fill finish is going to get commercially used now by Q2, latest Q3. And apart from that, we are just planning on our CAPEX plans. It's right now mostly to do with maintenance, etc.

items.statement: Targeting return to 25% net margin levels over time
items.quote: Definitely. And that is our endeavor. This year, as you can see, has been a strong base in wanting to reach that level.

items.statement: Hester Africa has tender for Tanzanian government business and expects tenders from 1-2 more countries
items.quote: we are already having the tender for Tanzanian government business, we see other 1 or 2 countries also tenders coming up.

items.statement: Avian Influenza vaccine launch expected by beginning of Q2 FY26
items.quote: We have always maintained Q2. If I have mentioned Q1, I probably don't recollect. But yes, it would be the beginning of Q2 for sure.

items.statement: H9N2 vaccine market estimated at Rs 80-100 crore in India, larger globally
items.quote: In India, I think the H9N2 market I am not sure totally but it would definitely be approximately say Rs. 100 crore, around Rs. 80 crores to Rs. 100 crore market and world market is much bigger than that.

items.statement: BSL-3 facility awaiting administrative approval from BIRAC; commercialization timeline uncertain
items.quote: in case of BSL-3 facility, we are awaiting some administrative approval from the BIRAC which is an authority for that.

items.statement: Cash flow from operations ~Rs 70 crore sufficient for current debt repayment; no new working capital needed
items.quote: if you see our cash flow for the year ended March '25, I think the cash generated from the operations are roughly around Rs. 70 Cr. So I think we are able to manage right now the repayment which is for the current debt from our operations only.

items.statement: Hester Africa accumulated losses at Rs 45 crore; recoupment expected 1-2 years after breakeven
items.quote: As of now total accumulated losses at Africa is roughly around Rs. 45 Cr. that is accumulation but as we mentioned that in 2 years will be at a breakeven and for accumulation to be recouped, I think will be needing 1 or 2 more years more than the 2 years

items.statement: Management targets minimum 20-25% average growth rate for FY26
items.quote: We don't want to give a very forward -looking statement, but we will minimum try to maintain our average growth rate of 20% to 25%.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target maintained north of 20% with potential 1-2% compromise as company grows
items.quote: So, Mr. Bheda, I would think that north of 20 % will always be our target. We'll always try to be above 20% for sure. As we grow, we may have to compromise to a certain extent by 1 % or 2%, but we will try to maintain north of 20% for sure.

items.statement: Capex of Rs 250-300 crores planned for FY26 for debottlenecking and expanding major products
items.quote: You mentioned in the PPT is for FY26, the number is Rs. 250 to Rs. 300 crores. So, is it entirely for debottlenecking or any other plans? Narayan S. Iyer: Yes, it is basically for debottlenecking or expanding on our major products in that.

items.statement: Capacity expansion from 48,000 to 54,000 metric tons expected to complete by March 2026
items.quote: As has been informed, we are actively working to expand our production capacities for our key products and take it up from 48,000 metric tons to 54,000 metric tons. We expect this expansion to be completed by March 2026.

items.statement: Confident of 20-25% growth based on order book position and commitments from six key customers
items.quote: Well, we are confident of our growth as we see our order books position and we also are working closely with the clients, we have much more clients right now, customers who have given commitments.

items.statement: Margin improvement driven by superior product mix, high-value products over $100/kg, and side-stream valorization
items.quote: So as I already explained, it is the product mix that now that we now have which includes products which are high value products selling over $100 per kilogram as well as the products that we make from the site streams.

items.statement: Expect to maintain record EBITDA margins of 23.5% in near future
items.quote: EBITDA margins once again is at a record high of 23 .5% for the quarter and we expect to maintain similar EBITDA margins in the near future.

items.statement: Healthy demand for core products with plants operating at 85-90% capacity and further debottlenecking underway
items.quote: All our key products are currently operating at optimal capacity as demand for all key products are very healthy. Our units have all been operating at close to 85% to 90% of our capacities.

items.statement: No significant impact anticipated from US tariffs as US market exposure limited to ~10% and India has tariff advantage
items.quote: We really do not anticipate any significant impact from the ongoing US tariffs as our presence in the US market is limited to around 10%. At the moment, almost all countries supplying to US have to bear higher tariffs than India.

items.statement: PRIGIV JV plant commissioned in Feb 2025, expected breakeven in FY27, potential Rs 300-350 crores top line in 3-4 years
items.quote: PRIGIV has just started its operation somewhere in February '25. So there's hardly any contribution coming on to the revenue front , about Rs.4 crores or so. And as Mr. Mahesh bhai indicated in his initial opening remarks , PRIGIV will start possibly a breakeven from somewhere around a year from now, maybe '26-27

items.statement: Gross margin expansion driven by yield improvements and side-stream valorization, not raw material cost reduction
items.quote: Input cost as in you have to see it in terms of improved yields. It is not that the cost of raw material has substantially gone down. It is improved yields which is resulting into lower material cost.

items.statement: Asset turnover expected to improve from 1.4x to 1.7-1.8x in coming years through debottlenecking and working capital reduction
items.quote: As far as the Gross fixed asset turnover that you talked about, it should be in the range of around 1.4 x and we are moving towards going to 1.6 x, 1.7x in the coming few years.

items.statement: Peak debt not to exceed 3x Debt-EBITDA, currently at 2x
items.quote: Our overall debt will not be exceeding a Debt-EBITDA of 3x. Currently it is at 2x odd on Debt-EBITDA.

items.statement: Product prices at $7-7.5/kg, potential 5-10% average price increase going forward
items.quote: Today the prices we are at now $7-$7.5, going forward, I think it could be even 5%, 10% higher, average price.

items.statement: Structural demand growth from rising hygiene awareness in India, Africa, Asia driving volume growth beyond GDP
items.quote: The awareness of cleanliness is coming , awareness of hygiene is coming all over the world. Actually after COVID this has taken a fast track to increase our share, and the demand is much higher.

items.statement: Sustainability and supplier reliability becoming more important than customer relationships in chemical industry
items.quote: I also want to tell you today the market scenario where especially the chemicals are panned out , sustainability is the keyword and supplier in coming times I can tell you, will be more important for a customer than his customer.

items.statement: Revenue growth outlook 15-20% for next few years
items.quote: So like our projection growth outlook for next few years would be in the range of 15% to 20%.

items.statement: EBITDA margin to expand ~100 bps per 10% revenue growth
items.quote: I think with every 10% increase in the top line, we will have around 100 bps increase in the EBITDA margin.

items.statement: Kolkata modernization facility targeting Q2 completion, Q3 safe date
items.quote: The modernization work which we are doing for a new facility near Kolkata is progressing quite fast. And we expect it to be get it completed by -- we are targeting quarter 2, but I think quarter 3 will be a safe date for the completion, although we are targeting quarter 2.

items.statement: Pentonic revenue share rose from 34.3% to 35.6% in FY25
items.quote: This was enabled by a favorable product mix with the higher-margin Pentonic brand expanding its revenue share from 34.3% to 35.6%.

items.statement: Pentonic gross margin 40%+
items.quote: 40-plus GP in Pentonic range of products. So it continues to be that way.

items.statement: Average selling price rose 10% to INR6.21 in FY25, expect similar growth
items.quote: We had a 10% increase this year. And going forward, we expect a similar growth in the average ASP.

items.statement: Export growth to slightly outpace domestic market
items.quote: We will come back with a more specific guidance in the next quarter, but our endeavour is to grow the export market slightly faster than the Indian market.

items.statement: Stationery segment growth to outpace company 15-20% top-line growth
items.quote: We believe that the growth in the stationery segment should be outpacing the growth of the company.

items.statement: E-commerce JV approved at 65:35 shareholding, small initial equity
items.quote: we are looking at a 65:35 shareholding ratio, majority being with Linc. So it's goi ng to be a small capital equity

items.statement: Mitsubishi JV project on schedule for Q2 FY26 operations and launch
items.quote: Our project is on schedule, and it is planned for quarter 2 operations and launch itself.

items.statement: Export margins higher than company average of 11.5-12%
items.quote: Yes. So export margins are actually higher than the company average definitely.

items.statement: Dividend proposed at INR1.5 per share, 23.5% payout ratio
items.quote: The Board of Directors has proposed a dividend of INR1.5 per share, implying a payout ratio of 23.5%, subject to shareholder approval.

items.statement: No legal restriction from Mitsubishi stake to onboard other brands
items.quote: No, there is no legal agreement that binds us, and it's our strategic call.

items.statement: Total addressable market expanded from INR6,640 cr to INR38,500 cr
items.quote: We are also actively exploring opportunities across the broader stationery market, increasing our total addressable market from INR6,640 crores to INR38,500 crores.

items.statement: Guiding for high single-digit to low double-digit revenue growth in FY26
items.quote: We are guiding this year for a high single digit, low double -digit kind of guidance.

items.statement: EBITDA margins expected to improve by 1-1.5% in FY26
items.quote: EBITDA margins should improve by 1% - 1.5% if that happens.

items.statement: Only routine capex planned for FY26, no major expansion
items.quote: There will be only routine capex. Of course there is no major capex required.

items.statement: Channel sales to decline from 80% to 75%, project sales to rise to 25% in FY26
items.quote: In FY 26, the channel will go down to 75% and project will go up to 25%.

items.statement: Demand optimism based on Q4 improvement, better April, project completions, deferred purchases ending, and export recovery
items.quote: My optimism comes from quarter 4. It was slightly better than quarter 2 and 3. And then also April has been slightly better than last year.

items.statement: Max plant at 55% utilization in Q4; expected to reach 75-80% by H2 FY26, driving margin improvement
items.quote: Max plant, which is getting stabilized, 55% capacity utilization and the minute this ranges betw een 75% to 80% capacity utilization, which is very soon in a couple of quarters, we will have a complete reversal over

items.statement: No pricing increase strategy; stricter on receivables and discounting; gas cost at INR47/scm in Q4, INR44/scm for FY25
items.quote: Overall gas pricing, I'm sure that would be a question. INR47 is the overall gas pricing. This is purely gas and no other mixed fuel in this.

items.statement: Morbi overcapacity: 70-80 plants may shut due to financing drought, high land costs, tax issues, and quality/pricing erosion
items.quote: We believe that all of these put together, we think another 70, 80 plants, if not more, will get shut in Morbi again this year.

items.statement: Brand spend to increase to 2.5% of sales in FY26 from 2% in FY25
items.quote: Brand spend will also increase in proportion to about 2.5%.

items.statement: Employee cost as percentage of sales to be lower in FY26 vs FY25
items.quote: So, if it is as a percentage, it will definitely be lower. So, I can only talk as a percentage. I can't talk in absolute terms. But yes, in percentage terms, it will be lower than FY '25.

items.statement: Consolidated debt at INR288 crores, up from INR233 crores; standalone debt-free and no working capital borrowing
items.quote: If you see our debt levels, our total debt levels are INR288 crores, down from last year from INR233 crores.

items.statement: Domestic demand pain across all tiers; green shoots in Tier 2-4 towns in MP, Bihar, UP; metros mixed with Delhi/Pune/Mumbai strong, Hyderabad slower
items.quote: I think the pain has been across the Board has been across the Board. Small towns have been ailing as much as big towns.

items.statement: Gross margin pressure from 5% capacity utilization drop, 4-5% gas price rise, and higher discounting; expected to recover
items.quote: All these three put together almost resulting in almost 4%, 4.5% gross margin reduction, decline in gross margin.

items.statement: Bathware sales grew 18% in Q4 and 11% for FY25; targeting double-digit growth again in FY26
items.quote: Bathware sales is something which we are very bullish about. The sales grew by 18% in quarter 4 and 11% in the whole year of 2025. This is very encouraging, and we hope to do again double-digit growth in Bathware for next year.

items.statement: Refused to launch lower-priced SKUs to chase volume; will protect mother brand pricing despite 81% utilization
items.quote: No. No. I think if I were sitting at 60%, 70% capacity utilization, maybe you would have thought of it. But at 81%, I'm quite sure that a little bit of patience will prove a much more beneficial situation for the long run.

items.statement: Management expects strong top line growth and improved EBITDA margin in FY26 driven by distribution expansion, stable commodity prices, calibrated pricing, and cost rationalization.
items.quote: These initiatives coupled with stable commodity prices and a calibrated approach to pricing, rationalization of cost structures, places us well to deliver strong top line growth as well as improved EBITDA margin in FY26.

items.statement: EBITDA margin of 16-18% is considered a bare minimum; management targets higher margins going forward with gross and EBITDA margin improvement expected.
items.quote: I think that EBITDA margin of 16% was a very bare basic minimum range. I think we are looking anywhere at a much higher EBITDA margin than that.

items.statement: Two price increases taken in Q4 FY25 for coconut oil followed by a mid-teens increase in April 2025; further increases will depend on copra price movement.
items.quote: In response to copra price inflation, two prices increases were implemented in Q4 FY’25 though they remained at a lag and hence it was followed by a preteen price increase in April 2025 again

items.statement: General trade showed 7% sequential growth in Q4 driven by wholesale and rural recovery; wholesale channel grew 15% QoQ after prior weakness.
items.quote: During the quarter general trade registered a growth of 7% on a sequential basis while on the year-on-year basis it still remained negative.

items.statement: Non-ADHO portfolio saliency is ~20%; long-term target is ~40% with coconut oil and Almond Drops Hair & Skin Care as key drivers.
items.quote: Almond Drops is at 80% or so. That is where the saliency is. And now the saliency of the products beyond Almond Drops, all the new products as well as a bit of traditional products that we had is around close to 20%.

items.statement: Project Aarohan Phase-II expanded to Rajasthan, Haryana, Delhi, Chhattisgarh; implementation expected to complete by May 2025 with 24,000 new outlets and 1,300 new towns added in Phase-I.
items.quote: During the current quarter Phase-II of Project Aarohan has now been expanded in states of Rajasthan, Haryana, Delhi and Chhattisgarh where reach and representation improvement opportunities have been identified, and implementation is expected to be completed by May 2025.

items.statement: Banjara's acquisition 49% completed; balance 51% expected in Q1 FY26; post-merger integration commenced April 2025 with consultant engaged for 3-month design phase.
items.quote: During the quarter, the Company completed the acquisition of 49% of equity share capital of Vishal Personal Care Private Limited, the Company holding the Banjaras brand, balance 51% is expected to be completed in Q1 FY26.

items.statement: Copra prices increased over last two quarters due to higher downstream demand and supply shortages in Sri Lanka; prices expected to remain bullish in short term.
items.quote: Copra prices increased over the last two quarters primarily due to higher demand for downstream products and supply shortages in markets like Sri Lanka with prices expected to remain bullish in the short term.

items.statement: International business grew 30% YoY in Q4 and 20% for FY25; Rest of World markets grew 107% YoY in Q4 and 49% for full year led by Canada, Malaysia, USA, Tibet, New Zealand.
items.quote: The international business recorded a robust growth of 30% year-on-year in Quarter 4 and 20% for FY'25.

items.statement: E-commerce channel grew 33% YoY in Q4 and 29% for full year; quick commerce grew 60% YoY and 21% QoQ with saliency at 12% in Q4 vs 10% in Q3.
items.quote: The E-commerce channel grew by 33% year -on-year in Q4 '25 and 29% for the full year.

items.statement: Almond Drops Hair & Skin Care range grew 73% YoY in Q4 and 46% for FY25; targeting Rs 4-5 cr monthly turnover in next 2 years.
items.quote: We are looking at the latest about Rs. 4 to 5 Cr kind of a turnover coming out of this on a monthly basis in the next 2 years or so.

items.statement: Cost savings of nearly Rs 6 cr achieved in FY25 through specification optimization, alternate vendor development, and raw material sourcing; productivity improved 6% in Guwahati and 17% in Paonta Sahib.
items.quote: These efforts have resulted in nearly 6 crores savings in FY'25. Additionally, productivity improvements have been driven through automation on select product lines, smart manufacturing initiatives to reduce non-value-added activities and enhance manpower productivity with improvement of 6% in Guwahati and 17% in Paonta Sahib.

items.statement: US business expected to grow mid-teens (~15%) in FY26; ROW 12-15%; API ~10%
items.quote: I expect the U.S. business to grow on mid to high te ens, it should grow for F Y'26 depending on how the launches pick up and what kind of erosion, which I don't know, but I expect that from what we are seeing, a mid-teen, like a 15%-odd should be a good growth for the U.S. market

items.statement: India business targeting double-digit (10%+) growth for FY26
items.quote: For India business, we are quite positive to get a double-digit growth for the whole year. There might be some quarter -to-quarter where ability based on onset of monsoon, but ex of that, we are quite confident that we have a plan in place to drive a 10% plus growth.

items.statement: R&D spend guided at Rs 600-650 crore for FY26
items.quote: Next year again, we'd look at about 600 to 650, depends on how the project goes.

items.statement: Maintenance/regular capex budgeted at Rs 400-450 crore for FY26 including spillover
items.quote: Roughly I am budgeting about Rs. 400 crores-Rs. 450 crores. This should include some spillover of expense which will come from those existing projects that is Indore and others included.

items.statement: Gross margin target around 70% acceptable; EBITDA margins expected to improve over next couple of years as new facilities ramp up and R&D optimizes
items.quote: Actually, Mr. Baheti what he had said earlier, is that margins of around 70% is what we find acceptable and I think this is what we will look at strive at being around for that.

items.statement: ~30-35% of R&D spend towards peptides and complex injectables; ~40% including complex ophthalmics; ~45% of new filings on injectables
items.quote: Amongst that, I would say about 30%, ye s, about 30 %-35% would be towards peptides a nd complex injectables. If you add complex ophthalmic also, about 40 % would be towards complex products and

items.statement: US pricing pressure remains; Q4 QoQ dip due to Q3 one-time buy opportunities and new launch stocking
items.quote: Yes, so the pricing pressure remains in the U .S. market and it's still there, product to product if you look at it.

items.statement: No significant US manufacturing capacity industry-wide; tariff impact would be macro issue; only ~10% volumes can be made in US
items.quote: No one has enough capacity in the U.S., even our peers who have plants in the US, it is a fraction of the volumes that they are supplying. So, I think it's going to be a macro issue that everyone will face with and the buyers in the industry.

items.statement: 4-5 US product launches planned for Q1 FY26; 15+ launches lined up for FY26; 20-30% could be interesting opportunities
items.quote: We will launch 4 to 5 products in Q1 as well.

items.statement: Pithampur formulation facility commissioned; peptide block at API 2 and additional injectable line at F3 completed; major projects done
items.quote: On the domestic side, we have commissioned Pithampur. So '24-'25, we have spent a good amount of money on Pithampur manufacturing facility , cumulatively about Rs. 200 odd crores.

items.statement: Inventory buildup due to US launch preparation and one delayed launch; not tariff-related; efforts to restrain inventory going forward
items.quote: have built inventories, because we had scheduled multiple launches in the previous year to be launched products, at U.S. So, inventories at U.S. level is high

items.statement: API business faced pricing pressure from Chinese competition; lost some business but compensated via relationships and new products
items.quote: It was just pricing pressure and erosion. We lost out some business because of lot of pricing pressure. Chinese are back in the market and even through India.

items.statement: Receivable days expected to normalize to ~75 days in next few quarters from current elevated levels
items.quote: Receivable we have been for a long time, we have been around between 70 and 80 days, this has gone up slightly on account of last quarter sales and some new launches, while the collection days is little higher for the new launches, that would also go back to about 75 days or so in the next few quarters.

items.statement: Bosutinib launch uncertain due to technical issue; Tirzepatide targeting day-one launch in all markets pending NCE-1 date
items.quote: Bosutinib, it may be there. We have a technical issue, so it may come, I am not committing to that as yet.

items.statement: Injectables facilities not fully utilized creating EBITDA drag; operating leverage expected as utilization improves
items.quote: As we get more capacity utilization in those facilities, as we start getting more v olumes out of those facilities, that will automatically give a lot of operating leverage because these are not fully utilized right now

items.statement: MR count stable at ~5,500; only ~100 incremental additions planned for FY26
items.quote: It's pretty much the same. There might be some incremental balancing, but no major expansion is expected. Maybe there might be a hundred odd people we will add.

items.statement: Management guided for Rs. 10,000 crores revenue in the next four years from current Rs. 3,400 crores.
items.quote: Yes. So we have actually given guidance saying that we will reach Rs. 10,000 crores in the next four years. And yes, that's the guidance that we have given.

items.statement: Routine hygiene capex expected at Rs. 40-50 crores annually for the next two years; Bhagyalakshmi farm capex largely completed.
items.quote: So from that perspective, as we look ahead for the next two years, I think the routine capital expenditure, which was likely in the past like around Rs. 40 crores to Rs. 50-odd crores, we can foresee annually a Rs. 40 crores to Rs. 50 crores of capital outlay.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expanded 130 bps to 8.5% in FY25; management aspires to take it higher but gives no specific number guidance.
items.quote: We continue to thrive on that and we aspire to take it to higher levels. But genuinely, we do not give any specific number wise guidance.

items.statement: Milk procurement prices rose 12% YoY to Rs. 37/litre in Q4; management expects prices to stabilize for the next six months.
items.quote: Milk procurement, what we anticipate to be more or less stabilized now onwards, because milk is the seasonal commodity and we have a supply /demand gap, in the summer where the milk production naturally goes down.

items.statement: Core categories (ghee, cheese, paneer) grew 17% volume in FY25; growth driven by branded dairy demand, distribution expansion (15 to 29 warehouses), and brand equity.
items.quote: So basically it is a natural demand for the branded good quality products as well as our distribution network expansion, along with the brand equity what we command and because of that we have more demand for these dairy products.

items.statement: New age business (Avvatar, Pride of Cows) margins are roughly 2x company average gross margins; Avvatar grew 41% YoY and 6x in three years.
items.quote: maybe indicatively I can share that the new age business margins are relatively almost 2x of the company's average gross margins.

items.statement: Raised Rs. 161 crores via convertible warrants; Rs. 70 crores for debt reduction, Rs. 40 crores for working capital, Rs. 20 crores for capex, rest for general corporate purposes.
items.quote: Out of the Rs. 160 crores, we, as per the explanatory statement provided, we have mentioned Rs. 70 crores will be utilized towards debt reduction , almost Rs. 40 crores will be used towards the working capital , almost Rs. 20 crores will be used towards the capital expenditure, and the remaining as a corporate general purpose.

items.statement: Ingredient business (SMP) degrew 9% YoY as management consciously deprioritized this low-margin commodity segment.
items.quote: We have consciously taken this call , because it is a very low margin business , so we have consciously chosen this strategy of growing the other segments and more focusing on the core and the new age.

items.statement: Cheese plant operating at 98-99% capacity utilization; further expansion only via adjacencies with marginal capex.
items.quote: And now we are almost using our capacity. There will be a adjacency which we will bring in. So we are almost doing 98 %, 99% capacity utilization.

items.statement: Direct milk procurement is one-third of total 15 lakh litres/day; two-thirds via aggregators through 300+ BMCs and chilling centers.
items.quote: Almost two-thirds of the same is procured through aggregators , and almost one-third is through our direct own network through our BMCs, which is bulk milk coolers; and CC, which is chilling centers.

items.statement: Bhagyalakshmi farm has 5,000+ Holstein Friesian cows targeting 20,000 in five years; 2,000 acres silage production for captive feed.
items.quote: And the way the breed is, we have our self-progeny, so in coming five years we are going to touch about 20,000 cows. They are the same breed of Holstein Friesian which is very productive and very rugged breed in Indian conditions.

items.statement: Inventory days reduced from 72 to 61 days; net working capital days down from 74 to 62 days driven by inventory reduction.
items.quote: Number two, it is mainly on account of the reduction in the inventory which we have shown the trend that from 72 days it has gone down to 61 days.

items.statement: Net debt stands at Rs. 561 crores (gross debt less fixed deposits and cash); debt-to-equity improved from 2.4x to 1.9x.
items.quote: On the borrowing side, of course, the net debt of the company is Rs. 561 crores, it is a gross debt less of all the fixed deposits and the cash balances.

items.statement: Operating cash flow of Rs. 212 crores in FY25; used for Rs. 120 crores capex and Rs. 80 crores interest outflow.
items.quote: So entire proceeds if we were to dissect in two parts, one part is usage of the capital expenditure in the capital expenditure item, which is both for Bhagyalakshmi. Farm as well as for Parag Milk Foods largely. I think that completes all the capital expenditure obligations which were there in terms of whatever were the routine hygiene CAPEX which were required. So it is almost close to Rs. 120-od

items.statement: Other current assets of Rs. 400-450 crores largely comprise government receivables (PSI/PLI incentives) and advances to milk aggregators for procurement infrastructure.
items.quote: With respect to the other part of the assets, it is largely the receivable from the government which is on account of the PSI and PLI incentives which government provides. So , of course, that cash flow is dependent on the overall larger cash flows from the state government or central government.

items.statement: Biological asset revaluation income decreased YoY in FY25; constitutes 11% of PAT; valuation by independent certified valuer per IndAS.
items.quote: just to apprise you again that this year the income has decreased on a year-on-year basis and it is not growing that every year this income is growing

items.statement: Consolidated top-line growth of 16-18% backed only by volume growth for FY26
items.quote: Overall, we are expecting between 16% to 18% top line growth in GAVL backed only by volume growth.

items.statement: Consolidated profit growth of 16-18% for FY26 driven by Astec loss reduction
items.quote: As far as profitability is concerned, again we have taken a growth of 16% to 18% profit.

items.statement: Astec CDMO business expected to grow 35% year-on-year for the next couple of years
items.quote: More or less it will be around 35%. Year-on-year the growth will be 35%.

items.quote: 20%-23% is the gross margin.

items.quote: My expectation is that our EBIT per ton will remain between INR1,900 to INR2,000 on an average.

items.quote: It will go up to almost 40% plus in the next year, the saliency of value-added product.

items.quote: We will definitely try to get 30% plus margins and more than 30% plus growth over last year in top line.

items.quote: But my sense is that between 25% to 30% is something which we try to maintain 3 years out also.

items.statement: Astec targeting EBITDA positivity in FY26 with losses halved from FY25
items.quote: We are saying that on a conservative basis our loss should come down to less than half of last year and that will definitely drive profitability of Godrej Agrovet.

items.quote: No capex in Astec. In GAVL, we are only putting capex in high margin businesses now, particularly Oil Palm Plantation.

items.statement: Astec contract manufacturing POs and negotiations for H1 completed, giving confidence of normal demand
items.quote: most of the contract manufacturing POs and negotiation has been over. So this gives u s a confidence that almost most of the contract manufacturing will be coming back to the normal demand

items.statement: Vegetable Oil forward integration investments to add 2-2.5% to overall profitability over time
items.quote: So these 2 investments will add close to anything between 2% to 2.5% to our overall profit depending on the price of the product.

items.quote: Apart from that, in certain value-added products we have taken a price increase of about 4% to 5% to 10% in certain areas; but that constitute only 10% to 12% of our total portfolio.

items.statement: Crop Protection kharif placement very good on expectation of normal monsoon; expecting good volumes
items.quote: So placement is very good on the back of expectation of normal monsoon. So I think we are fully geared up. I think dispatches are happening. Placement is happening at the retail level. So we are expecting a good season and we are also expecting very good volumes.

items.statement: Non-MF revenue projected to grow in excess of 20%, closer to 25% in FY26
items.quote: Non -MF, even for this year, we're projecting in excess of 20%, closer to 25% growth.

items.quote: We are expecting that AUM growth will be more moderate, will be maybe 11%, 12%.

items.statement: Exit yield for FY26 expected at ~2.15% (down 8-9 bps from Q4 FY25 2.24%)
items.quote: 0.08% to 0.09% is what we expect.

items.quote: I expect overall from a capex perspective, we will spend around INR100 crores on the overall -- meaning on the rearchitecture part of it, and we'll spend another INR70 crores on the other capex part of it.

items.quote: So nothing major. We do have, as a part of regular couple of smaller sized contracts coming up as they do in every year. Probably there are 2, 3 that are coming up in the current year.

items.quote: So to have 32% of overall revenue to be -- it is around 33% is currently to be the employee cost would be a good assumption to make, and that's what we are working towards.

items.quote: Our CAPEX guidance as a whole for a group will be only around Rs.750 crores to Rs.800 crores totally in that region.

items.quote: the order book is filling up, but the development cycle time is around 18 to 24 months. items.statement: Sunbeam FY26 EBITDA margin expected 8-10% blended, Q1 muted, Q4 strongest
items.quote: on a blended average we can say between 8% to 10% EBITDA is what we expect for the full financial year, but Q1 will be quite muted.

items.statement: Powertrain margins to creep up with better operating leverage, double-digit growth expected in FY26
items.quote: Our margins also will start creeping up with better operating leverage but depends on one quarter to another quarter there may be some changes, always Q1 will have some challenges, but we don't see much challenge this year, Q3 will be always a challenge. items.statement: Aluminum business consolidated revenue run rate Rs.1,000 crores/quarter, FY26 revenue Rs.4,300-4,500 crores
items.quote: Q4 has been Rs.1,000 crores. So, we will be anywhere between Rs.4,300 to Rs.4500 crores overall.

items.statement: Storage business growth expected at high teens, nearly 20% in FY26
items.quote: High teens I would say, almost 20% we can expect the growth on the storage business.

items.statement: Revenue mix diversified: PV 32%, 2W 18%, CV 17%, storage 10%, off-highway 5%, tractor 4%
items.quote: the commercial vehicle portion is coming to 17%, two wheeler is coming to 18%, passenger vehicle is 32%, storage is 10%, off-highways is 5% and tractor is 4%.

items.quote: All the business what we do, we are either doing Ex Works or FOB, very rarely I think hardly 5% of the business may be CIF whatever exports we are doing at Craftsman. US exports as far as Sunbeam is concerned, it is negligible. It is more towards Mexico there.

items.statement: QIP of Rs.1,200 crores raised last year to capitalize on opportunities and tariff disruptions
items.quote: we went last year with the mandate to raise Rs.1,200 crores QIP sensing the opportunity and also sensing the disruption coming from tariffs and the geopolitical situations also in Europe.

items.statement: Alloy wheel Bhiwadi FY26 revenue ~Rs.300 crores, Hosur ~Rs.150 crores, operational breakeven achieved at Rs.40 crores quarterly revenue
items.quote: Bhiwadi will be around Rs.300 crores plus for FY26 and Hosur will be around Rs.150 crores. This is as per the earlier earnings call.

items.statement: DR Axion Q4 revenue Rs.376 crores, FY26 growth 8-10% CAGR, FY27 slightly above 10%
items.quote: Revenue for DR Axion was Rs.376 crores.

items.statement: Sunbeam consolidation year, no new orders until FY27-28, Gurgaon plant 75% emptied, VRS provisioned Rs.160 crores at acquisition

items.statement: Fronberg Foundry repair & maintenance CAPEX ~Rs.40-50 crores being evaluated
items.quote: there is some repair and maintenance for a very old equipment at Fronberg, which may be around Rs.40 crores, Rs.50 crores, may be there, we're evaluating that.

items.statement: Land sale of Sunbeam Gurgaon expected Q3/Q4 FY26, estimated Rs.300+ crores proceeds
items.quote: aided by possibly the land sale in Q3 or Q4 of Sunbeam, that will add around Rs.300 crores plus depending on that market value at that particular point of time.

items.statement: Target PBT margin in excess of 5% for FY26
items.quote: I think we should target for a PBT margins of in excess of 5%.

items.statement: Debt reduction target of INR300-400 crores for FY26
items.quote: We have to beat our target for this financial year, debt reduction will be in the range of INR300 crores to INR400 crores.

items.statement: FY26 capex expected at INR200 crores plus for Kalyan and INR60-80 crores for Candere
items.quote: INR 200 crores plus for sure, because INR 200 crores will be for Kalyan itself. So, INR 200 crores plus Candere will be the right way to look at it

items.statement: Candere mature store margins 30-35% with 2% stock churn
items.quote: Margins, you know that it is in the range of 30%, 35%. Okay that is a store which is almost matured that is the store 's economics.

items.statement: Robust demand continuing from previous quarter with strong Akshaya Tritiya sales
items.quote: We witnessed robust growth in our Akshaya Tritiya sale this year, and we continue to see encouraging momentum in consumer demand, especially around the wedding purchases during the current quarter.

items.statement: Studded ratio target 30-32% for FY26, no sharp increase expected

items.statement: Gold metal loan interest rate increased from 3-3.5% to 5-5.5%
items.quote: It was in the range 3% - 3.5% now it is in the range of 5%, sorry 5% - 5.5%.

items.quote: But that was because of the uncertainty around GML. Now I told you last two, three months, GML had a huge turbulence because of other reasons, right? So, there was GML uncertainty around GML, especially over th e last one or two months, that is why the GML limits was not reduced

items.statement: Candere targets PAT profitability in FY26 with 70% studded mix at store level

items.statement: Targets 30-35% top-line growth and 15-20% EBITDA margin for next year and longer term

items.statement: Expects higher EBITDA margins due to lower cost structure from AI leverage

items.quote: We currently have three partners on DLG. There'll be a DLG disclosure that will go up on our website, which is already on our website.

items.statement: Consumer user base growing without marketing spend due to product improvements; cut marketing to prove product-led growth works
items.quote: the growth in user base did happen without, in fact, we cut the marketing in these quarters to show only and give the confidence to the team that your product matters.

items.statement: Wallet reintroduction under active discussion; board discussed today; multiple options on table; decision expected within months

items.statement: Targeting 25-30% revenue growth for FY26 assuming organic and inorganic growth
items.quote: we are targeting a revenue growth of 25% to 30% assuming both organic and inorganic growth

items.statement: Targeting to maintain current EBITDA and PAT margin levels in FY26 despite one-off expenses

items.quote: we have an enterprise solution order book of INR 190 crores
