items.quote: We ended this year at about Rs. 485 crores and we expect next year to deliver between Rs. 1,300 and 1,500 crores.

items.statement: Medium-term retail opex-to-AUM guidance of 3.5% to 4.0%
items.quote: We aim to continue this trend, in line with our medium-term guidance of 3.5% to 4.0%.

items.statement: Expect margins to expand slightly in declining rate cycle
items.quote: We do expect that our margins to expand slightly in general, first of all, only 50% of our lending is variable rate and even within that a lot of them we hav e some leeway in terms of reset dates etc

items.statement: Cost of borrowing to moderate 10-20 bps through FY26; cost of funds to remain flat
items.quote: expect the cost Piramal Enterprises May 06, 2025 of borrowing to moderate through the course of the year, anywhere between 10 and 20 basis points. However, the cost of funds for us will remain roughly flat to where we are right now

items.statement: Unsecured growth higher in FY26 vs FY25 in disbursement and AUM terms
items.quote: I think FY26 will be higher than FY25 in terms of growth rate in unsecured. I think we have had some severe challenges in at least I would say two and a half quarters out of four in this year.

items.statement: Target Wholesale:Retail mix of 20:80 going forward
items.quote: I think our objective is that the righ t mix for Wholesale : Retail would be in Piramal Enterprises May 06, 2025 the range of 20 :80 and that is where we would want to be as we optimize this business going forward

items.statement: Microfinance 90+ DPD at 6.9% on reduced AUM; likely peaked in Q4 FY25
items.quote: which we classify within our Business Loans segment witnessed the sharpest deterioration in the last six quarters. (90+) days past due in microfinance remains at 6.9% on a much-reduced AUM size

items.statement: Growth business credit cost ex-POCI stable at 1.9% in FY25; assume ~2% trajectory
items.quote: From a credit cost perspective, we have had a very stable year in financial year '25. We have not had any jerky movements. We have not had any significant dramatic deltas in credit costs.

items.statement: Opened 27 branches in FY25 vs ~90/year previously; focus on branch productivity
items.quote: In FY25, we opened 27 branches versus about 90 branches per year that we used to open in the prior 2 years. Our focus this y ear has been on raising productivity of existing branches and increasing the number of products offered per

items.statement: Dividend of Rs. 11 per share at 50% payout ratio announced; buybacks not feasible due to leverage
items.quote: We have announced a dividend of Rs. 11 per share and a payout rati o of 50%. So, we are going to the max level that we can in terms of paying dividends because that is a way for us to return capital to shareholders

items.statement: Tax shield of Rs. 14,500 crores carry forward losses available post PEL-Piramal Finance merger
items.quote: With the merger of PEL and Piramal Finance, a tax shield of Rs. 14,500 crores in assessed carry forward losses will be available. This would make our PBT equal to our PAT for several years in the future.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 profit dropped versus previous year due to lower tanker earnings and impairment on 3 MR product tankers
items.quote: We had a drop in profit versus the previous year, and we will come to the main reasons for that.

items.statement: Impairment of just short of INR 70 crores taken on 3 MR product tankers bought in last 18 months
items.quote: Out of the MRs that we bought, 3 of them had some impairment, and we have taken that impairment into our accounts, just short of INR 70 crores.

items.statement: Tanker earnings dropped significantly from Q4 FY24 to Q4 FY25, impact of about INR 400 crores
items.quote: So, we have about a INR 400 crores drop from Q4 last year to Q4 this year.

items.statement: Crude tanker earnings dropped by about $22,000 per day from Q4 FY24 to Q4 FY25
items.quote: We dropped from Q4 FY '24 to Q4 FY '25. We dropped by about $22,000 a day.

items.statement: Product tanker earnings dropped by almost 1/3rd from $37,000 to $24,700 per day
items.quote: Product tankers also, we dropped by almost about 1/3rd from $37,000 to $24,700.

items.statement: LPG carrier rates increased from $35,500 to $43,000 per day as all 4 are on time charters
items.quote: LPG carriers, all 4 of ours are on time charters and those pricings have gone up, and therefore, our rates have gone up from $35,500 to $43,000.

items.statement: Global crude oil demand in Q4 grew by about 1%, Chinese crude imports grew slightly with stock building
items.quote: Global crude oil demand in Q4 grew by about 1%. Chinese crude oil imports also grew slightly. They have been building stocks as far as we can see.

items.statement: New OFAC sanctions tightening crude tanker capacity, with ships added to sanctions list every week or two
items.quote: We had some new sanctions from OFAC, that's a U.S. sanctions authority, which tightened the crude tanker capacity. So, that's 1 factor, which we might see playing out. Every week or 2, we are getting a few more ships being added to the sanctions list.

items.statement: Tanker asset prices dropped about 5% during quarter, product tankers down ~20% from year ago, crude tankers down less
items.quote: Tanker asset prices during the quarter dropped by about 5%. But over a longer period of time from a year ago period, you could see product tankers dropping by about 20%, and we will see that graph and crude tankers by a little less.

items.statement: Order book remains low especially for crude tankers; product tanker order book 21%, crude 11%, dry bulk 11%, LPG 29%
items.quote: You have an order book of about 29% for LPG ships, and you have 21% for product tankers, while around 11% for crude tankers and dry bulk.

items.statement: Company is net cash on standalone basis, awaiting opportunities to buy while prices have dropped but not yet at comfort levels
items.quote: We are still net cash on a standalone basis. So the results of all the CAPEX that we did and the levering up that we did, we are awaiting opportunities to buy while prices have dropped. They have not yet reached our comfort levels, and we will wait for that to happen.

items.statement: One rig coming off contract around December 2025, awarded 3-year ONGC contract expected to start Q4 FY26
items.quote: We have another rig coming off contract sometime around December this year. We have bid into a 3-year contract in India, and we have been awarded that contract as well. So, she will come off the contract in December and do the usual work between 2 contracts and go back on to a 3-year contract, hopefully within Q4 of FY '26.

items.statement: Offshore market mood not positive due to Saudi Aramco actions, talk of more renegotiations or cancellations
items.quote: While it's not gone down, the mood in the market is not very positive with all the Saudi Aramco actions, which have been happening and there is talk of even more renegotiations or cancellations.

items.statement: Offshore assets gross value estimated at $500-600 million, with rigs comprising 60-70% of that value
items.quote: Yes, that should be between $500 million and $600 million. $550 million and $600-odd million. Yes, $500 million to $600 million.

items.statement: Rigs represent 60-70% of offshore asset value
items.quote: Rigs will probably be about 60% plus of the value. 60% to 70% of the value.

items.statement: In-chartered MR tanker has 3.5 years remaining on 5-year contract; Suezmax has 2 years remaining
items.quote: One was originally about 5 years. So, that has about 3.5 years to go. That's for the MR tanker. The crude tanker has about 2 years to go.

items.statement: Growth target is to deploy all capital into fleet, potentially growing fleet 50% from current size at right prices
items.quote: So if we can grow the fleet to 50% higher than it is today, deploying all our capital, we will be happy to do so. But it's a question of having as much capital as possible employed into ships at good prices.

items.statement: Dry bulk asset prices historically cheaper than tankers, closest to purchase levels but not there yet
items.quote: the dry bulk is historically cheaper than the tankers. So maybe it's the closest to our purchase prices, although not there yet.

items.statement: OPEC increasing supply by 800,000 bpd over two months; Atlantic Basin supply growth positive for crude tankers
items.quote: OPEC has announced that they're going to push up quotas by about 400,000 barrels a day in June, 2 months in a row, which means that's 800,000 barrels a day more of supply coming into the market.

items.statement: Saudi Aramco canceled 24-25 jack-up rig contracts a year ago, causing day rates to fall from $80-85k to ~$35k
items.quote: The big factor which happened was the Saudi Aramco actions of about a year ago where they canceled contracts. I think the latest count is for some 24 or 25 jack-up rigs, which obviously had a big impact on the availability.

items.statement: Long-term offshore drilling contracts at lower rates than a year ago; short-term rates similar to year-ago levels
items.quote: The long-term contracts are at lower rates. That is the 3-year contracts are at lower rates than the previous contracts, which are awarded maybe a year ago. So the short-term contracts are about the same level as they were maybe a year ago.

items.statement: Non-ONGC players awarding short-term rig contracts, indicating market widening beyond ONGC
items.quote: We have actually landed contracts for 2 players and this is not ONGC. The 2 short-term contracts which we have got for our 2 rigs, the Chetna and the Chaaya are both for non-ONGC contracts.

items.statement: Insurance covers most eventualities via Hull & Machinery and P&I; only uncovered risks are deductibles
items.quote: Typically, deductibles, things like deductibles.

items.statement: Target minimum 10% IRR in USD terms on ship acquisitions, lowered from previous 15% hurdle
items.quote: We would like to make at least a 10% IRR on the ships that we buy in U.S dollar terms. Yes.

items.statement: Asset prices remain high historically across all segments; dry bulk 10-30% off peaks but still expensive
items.quote: But still, the prices are still very high from a historical context. The other thing also to keep in mind is that just to clarify on the impairment, right, is that we did sell a ship against this purchase.

items.statement: Impairment on 3 MR tankers less than 10% of original cost; written down to higher of market value or value in use
items.quote: First, just to clarify, you wanted the impairment amount as a proportion of the total of these 3 ships or proportion of the total? It's less than 10%? First, it's less than 10% of the original cost, okay?

items.statement: LPG carriers all on time charter (4 ships); crude ~90% spot, products ~80% spot, dry bulk 60-70% spot
items.quote: The 1 outlier in this is that our LPG carriers, we have 4 of them, all of them are on time charter. The other 3 sectors of shipping, that is crude products and dry bulk, crude and products tend to be much more on the spot.

items.statement: Preferred share redemption from Great Ship India to GESCO started this FY with first installment received last month
items.quote: Yes, it has started from this year. So we have already had that first installment last month.

items.statement: Cash split: ~55% in USD bank deposits, ~45% in INR (1/3 bank deposits, 2/3 debt mutual funds)
items.quote: About a little over 50%, about 55% of our cash is in U.S. dollars, the rest is in rupees. U.S. dollars are just in bank deposits. They just sit in our bank. The rupees are typically about 1/3rd of it is in bank deposits, the rest is in mutual funds, typically debt mutual funds.

items.statement: Expect 15% plus revenue growth in current year with higher growth in operating profits and improved margins
items.quote: Amid evolving market dynamics and global trends, we expect to achieve 15% plus revenue growth in the current year, with a higher growth in our operating profits with improved margins.

items.statement: Maintain earlier guidance of 12-14% revenue growth beyond FY26 with potential 100-150 bps margin improvement year-on-year
items.quote: Beyond FY26, we continue to maintain our earlier guidance of revenue growth of 12% -14%, with a potential 100-150 bps margin improvement year-on-year.

items.statement: Gross margins around 65%, 95% of costs between gross margin and EBITDA are fixed, operating margins to expand with growth
items.quote: Because most of our costs are fixed costs. So other than costs, we are about a 65% margin gross-margin business. But between gross-margin to EBITDA, I would say 95% of our costs are fixed costs.

items.statement: Gross margins to improve by 100 bps annually, operating margins to keep expanding with fixed cost base
items.quote: Gross-margins will improve by 100 bps every year. And with operating costs not g rowing in line with that top -line growth, our operating margins will keep expanding

items.statement: Therapeutic mix shifted to 50% Gynae, 15% each Ortho, Derma, Pedia after Yash Pharma acquisition
items.quote: As we speak, Gynae now is about 50%. We still continue to be a gynae-dominated company. So we are 50% in gynae with the rest of the other three therapeutic segments contributing about 15% each.

items.statement: Organic growth was 8% in FY25, accelerated from 1% in H1 to 15% in H2, targeting 15% organic growth in FY26
items.quote: 8% of our growth is organic growth and the rest is inorganic. So while we have reflected a 28% growth during the year, 8% of that has come from organic. However, what is very important to note is this growth was 1% in H1, which has increased to 15% in H2.

items.statement: Follow asset-light model with no manufacturing capex, only investment in IT infrastructure, cash deployment focused on acquisitions or shareholder returns
items.quote: If you notice, we follow an asset light model. We are purely in India. And therefore, all our products for India are using CMOs, which have plenty in this country. We do not have really any capex plan. Our only investment is in computer infrastructure, the laptops and all that we have in offices and in some select field force locations.

items.statement: Divatrone (Dydrogesterone) franchise declined 75% due to competitive intensity and counterfeit issues, now stable at <INR10 crores annually
items.quote: Both the competitive intensity and wherein there was a lot of push and as I said, there was very little pull element, we took a backseat as far as this molecule is concerned and it has dropped by almost 75% for us. Our business is now stable, but at a much lower level and less than INR10 crores or about INR1 crores a month.

items.statement: No pricing pressure in India branded generics market, prices generally increase, positioned as mid-to-high price specialist-focused brand
items.quote: We don't see any pricing challenges at all in India, because that pricing pressure that you're referring to a competitive intensity that you're referring to is more outside India, which are unbranded generic markets or generic-generic markets. India is a branded generic market.

items.statement: MR productivity at INR2-2.1 lakhs PCPM, targeting INR3-3.5 lakhs PCPM over 3-4 years without increasing field force
items.quote: MR productivity, as we speak, is in the region of INR2 to INR2.1 lakhs PCPM or per capita per month. And the 8% growth that we are talking of actually has come from increased MR productivity.

items.statement: Working capital at 3.5% of sales (13 days), extracted INR24 crores over 3 years, limited further reduction expected
items.quote: In last 3 years, we have extracted almost INR24 crores from our working capital. I don't foresee much extraction going forward.

items.statement: Cash balance INR145 crores, will return to shareholders if no suitable acquisitions found at disciplined valuations
items.quote: If we do not find any good targets in the next couple of years, of course, this cash belongs to the shareholders. And we would be rather returning this cash in an appropriate form to the shareholders rather than doing anything not in line with our strategy.

items.statement: Yash Pharma acquisition added 250 reps, expanded doctor reach by 50%, contributed 10 months revenue in FY25 vs 12 months in FY26
items.quote: We have not really changed our field force strength, excepting for the acquisition that we did. So obviously, new field force came in with about 250 reps through Yash Pharma acquisition.

items.statement: Gross margin improvement driven by product mix, cost reduction from timely vendor payments, and price increases
items.quote: No. So, it's always a mix of many things. One is product mix. We, of course, also rationalize and keep producing better procurement. As I mentioned, we pay on time, and therefore, we are able to extract better value from our vendors. We, of course, do take price increases wherever we can.

items.statement: Operating margin guidance refers to pre-ESOP numbers, post-ESOP EBITDA will improve as ESOP costs decline per Black-Scholes model
items.quote: Actually, that refers to pre-ESOP numbers. Post-ESOP numbers automatically will improve because ESOP cost is continuously going down. And that's the way Black-Scholes model works.

items.statement: AUM growth target of 27% to 30% CAGR and target AUM of INR 50,000 crores by FY28
items.quote: In the next few years, we are going to be growth in the range of 27% to 30% kind of range and we intend to reach INR50,000 crores of AUM book by FY '28.

items.statement: Steady state ROE target of around 16% in next few years despite new branch opex impact
items.quote: About overall ROE, we should be in the range of about 16% despite these new branches opex will get absorbed.

items.statement: ROE contribution of 1.5% to 2% from pure fee income play
items.quote: About our ROE, while we will remain in the growth phase, but 1.5% to 2% ROE we intend to generate from pure free income play.

items.statement: Annual technology, data science and cybersecurity spend of INR 90-100 crores
items.quote: If you see that we are spending close to about INR90 crores to INR100 crores a year on our technology, data science and other things on this aspect.

items.statement: Board resolution approved for INR 2,000 crores fundraising; timing depends on market conditions
items.quote: We have taken the board resolution, as all of you guys would know, for the INR2,000 crores. And the timing of the fundraising would be based on the market conditions.

items.statement: Cost of funds expected to soften on incremental borrowing as repo rates come down; no scenario of interest rates going up
items.quote: We clearly see there is no scenario of interest rate going up based on these indicators. And we believe that rates will soften on our incremental borrowing.

items.statement: RBI draft gold loan LTV norms (75% including accrued interest for bullet loans) seen as positive for sector; short tenure (4-6 months) limits impact
items.quote: Overall, it is a positive, while the gold has not depreciated in a drastic manner whenever in the future it happens it create extra safety buffer LTV for these kinds of loan-to-value loans.

items.statement: MSME segment to resume 15-20% growth in FY26 with branch additions after FY25 focus on gold loan
items.quote: This year, we intend to grow that segment again the normal growth about 15% to 20% kind of a growth in the MSME segment.

items.statement: South India expansion planned in H2 FY26 for housing finance, MSME and gold loan branches in Andhra, Telangana, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka
items.quote: This year, we'll be entering in the South by adding more housing finance, MSME, and gold loan branches. So, in the second half, you will see that these segments will have branch network in Southern states.

items.statement: Co-lending AUM at 18% of total AUM (INR 4,079 crores) in FY25 vs 12% a year ago; remains efficient for high ROE, capital conservation and liability diversification
items.quote: As of FY '25, our co-lending AUM stood at INR 4,079 crores, accounting for approximately 18% of our total AUM compared to 12% a year ago.

items.statement: Gold loan ticket size to remain granular around INR 1 lakh; not changing dramatically
items.quote: Our ticket size in gold is going to be more or less so granular that it will be in the range of INR1 lakh only. And it is not going to change dramatically.

items.statement: Leverage (debt-to-equity) maintained at ~3.5x; will not exceed 4x
items.quote: Currently, we are around 3.5x, on a debt-to-equity basis. We will not go above, 4x kind of a level.

items.statement: Construction finance to remain conservative at not more than 20% of book; growth supported by residential real estate demand and healthy pipeline
items.quote: Overall construction finance will always remain at a conservative level, not more than 20%.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio improved from peak 70.5% in Q4 FY24 to 54.8% in Q4 FY25; trend expected to continue as branches mature
items.quote: cost-to-income ratio improving meaningfully from a peak of 70.5% in Q4 FY '24 to 54.8% in Q4 FY '25

items.statement: FY26 revenue growth guided at 20% overall, with domestic 30-32% and exports 12-15%
items.quote: Again, we have guided this year again for a 20% revenue growth. Overall, we may face some little bit headwinds in export business, but we are very bullish on the domestic market where we are expecting a growth of around 30% to 32% for the whole year

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin guided at 25-27%
items.quote: And of course, after a few months, we will have more clarity how things are shaping up because the current geopolitical situation is pretty fluid right now and of course, we will watch it out, but with the current contracts, we have current visibility. We think we don't see any reason that will not go 12%-15%. So overall, we see average both the growths where one-third revenue comes from India, tw

items.statement: Renal business guided at 50% growth in FY26, targeting Rs. 75 crores incremental revenue on Rs. 150 crores base
items.quote: This is next year we are planning because the base has increased now so we are looking at growing by around Rs. 75 crores over the current base of Rs. 150 crores, so around 50% growth is what we are guiding for Renal business.

items.statement: Critical Care segment expected to grow 2.5x in FY26 over previous year
items.quote: And we are very hopeful that Critical Care segment also grows by almost 2 and 1/2 times in the current year over the previous year numbers.

items.statement: Infusion Vascular business in India guided at 18-20% growth in FY26
items.quote: So I think in Infusion category, we are looking at a growth of over 18% to 20% in the current year and I think that is the number we have internally set as a benchmark

items.statement: Capex of Rs. 500 crores planned over next 2 years across 3 new manufacturing facilities
items.quote: I think next 2 years, we have called out the CAPEX of around Rs. 500 crores across 3 new manufacturing facilities we are building right now and mostly, it will help us in expanding the Renal capacity and look at some new opportunities in the CDMO space

items.statement: New plants expected to commercialize by end of Calendar Year 2026
items.quote: So in the previous call, I mentioned that by the end of Calendar Year 26 we should be able to commercialize this operation.

items.statement: Renal dialysis machine sales target of 500-600 units in FY26 (40-50 per month)
items.quote: So this year, our plans are to sell between 500 and 600 machines between that number, so close to 40-50 machines a month.

items.statement: Domestic revenue mix: Renal grew 60% in FY25 to over Rs. 150 crores; Critical Care and Cardiology are new growth drivers
items.quote: The biggest highlight in the domestic business was the growth in the Renal business and the Renal business had grown significantly by 60% for the whole year and that is what we had called out. We had called out a number of around close to Rs. 140 - Rs.150 crores for Renal business for FY '25 and we have actually did over Rs. 150 crores for the whole year.

items.statement: Launched over 30 new products in FY25 vs 18-19 in FY24, accelerating R&D across Cardiology, Critical Care, Renal
items.quote: Last year, we have launched over 30 products. In FY '24, we launched around 18-19 products. Now, we have moved around 30 new products which were launched in FY '25.

items.statement: Export margins slightly higher than domestic; Renal business operating margin positive, expects PAT positive by end of FY26
items.quote: The margin and export is slightly higher than the domestic business.

items.statement: Renal business not loss-making, operating margin positive, expects PAT positive by end of FY26
items.quote: It is not a loss making. The operating margin is positive. So I think it is all about, I think probably by the end of this financial year, we should be able to be making PAT on this business.

items.statement: Export growth guidance conservative at 12-15% due to fluid geopolitical situation and tariff uncertainty
items.quote: Exports, I think we will see a growth rate between 12%-15%. That is what we will see this year. And of course, after a few months, we will have more clarity how things are shaping up because the current geopolitical situation is pretty fluid right now

items.statement: Europe slowdown seen in South Europe due to supply chain disruption and overstocking
items.quote: But in general there was a slowdown coming mainly from countries in South Europe. So I think that is where we had slowdown. And I think as time progresses I think it should come back because in most of the countries there was supply chain disruption, maybe overstocking.

items.statement: Rs. 900 crores of QIP proceeds unutilized, to be used for capex, working capital, and M&A
items.quote: So basically, if you see out of that Rs. 1,000 crores were raised recently through QIP in august, September, last year, almost 6-7 months ago and this money is still quite unutilized, almost Rs. 900 crores of this money is still utilized and Rs. 300 crores were the previous cash in the Company which was built to internal accruals, so we will be using some of the money in CAPEX this year and some m

items.statement: R&D team expanding from 60-70 to 100+ people in FY26; clinical trial spend increasing over next 2-3 years
items.quote: So yes, we are hiring 40 more people in the R&D team this year. So from a present state of 60-70 people, we will move to around 100 plus people this year. We are adding more and we are going to spend more money on clinical trials which is part of the R&D cost to help us to establish the efficacy of the products we are manufacturing today.

items.statement: Healthcare and BFSI verticals expected to scale to $250 million revenue in next 3-5 years
items.quote: We remain confident that our investment verticals of healthcare, life sciences, and banking and financial services will scale to $250 million of revenue in the next three to five years' time.

items.statement: AI-enabled services expected to contribute 20% of revenue over next 3 years
items.quote: We expect AI -enabled services to contribute 20% of our revenue over the next three years, reflecting strong market traction and focused execution.

items.statement: Newly established SOC business in SITL projected to contribute 20% of growth within next 3-5 years
items.quote: The newly established SOC business in SITL is projected to contribute 20% of growth contribution within the next three to five years.

items.statement: Large TMT deal ($73M) to ramp gradually in Q1, largely in Q2, fully by Q3 FY26
items.quote: The deal that we won recently that we announced, the $73 million deal, that will scale up over the next two to three quarters. We started ramping up gradually in Q1, but Q1 will have a very small effect of the deal, but largely will be in Q2 and fully in Q3.

items.statement: EBITDA margin recovery to 20%+ delayed by at least one quarter due to market uncertainty
items.quote: We have at present we will year outlook for reaching back to the earlier growth. We may think there can be a one quarter of delay to that, but we are in the track of reaching there.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 order booking strong with book-to-bill 1.25x and over $100M bookings for international business
items.quote: For Q4 '25, order book stood at 101.6 million, which is the book to bill ratio of 1.25x.

items.statement: International services EBITDA margin improved to 16.5% in Q4 FY25 from 14.6% in Q3 FY25
items.quote: EBITDA grew sequentially as expected, grew by 1.9% to 16.5% in Q4, which is up from 14.6% in the prior quarter.

items.statement: FY25 international services EBITDA margin at 17% vs 21% in FY24
items.quote: EBITDA margin for FY25 stood at 17 %, compared to 21 % in FY24.

items.statement: Cloud and data deals now comprise 60% of total pipeline with accelerating demand around Microsoft Fabric
items.quote: Cloud and data deals now continue to make 60% of our total pipeline. Demand is accelerating, particularly around Microsoft Fabric.

items.statement: Domestic business faces risk from Microsoft potentially going direct to clients; impact unclear, may take couple quarters for clarity
items.quote: It is an emergent view. They have broadly taken a strategic position. But there is a gap between the strategic position and the execution. And the execution, only when it happens, we will be able to exactly know what will be the position.

items.statement: Quant earnout for Dec 2024 still under negotiation; three-year contract extension being discussed
items.quote: Quant turnout for December 2024 period, it is in the process of we are discussing with the current CEO. We still the discussion is going on. Along with the discussion, we will also be able to finalize the amount payable for December 2024.

items.statement: Depreciation and amortization reduction in Q4 due to fair valuation of Quant liability; may increase in coming quarters
items.quote: There can be an increase in the depreciation and amortization value from here because we had a lot of credit coming in this quarter. There can be some amount of increase from here in the immediate quarters.

items.statement: Board prioritizing debt repayment from Quant acquisition over higher dividend payout; RBI remittance issue nearing resolution
items.quote: However, considering the debt we have taken for the acquisition of Quon, the Board decided that let us manage the cash in such a way that we are able to pay off the debt as early as possible.

items.statement: 97% of workforce trained in Gen AI; active headcount 6,800+ with 14% LTM attrition
items.quote: Today, 97% of our workforce is trained in Gen AI, underscoring our commitment to future -ready skills and broad applicability of AI across our delivery, engineering, and consulting operations.

items.statement: FY26 credit growth guidance 11-12%, deposit growth 9-10%
items.quote: credit growth already we have given the direction that '25-'26 also we are going to grow at a rate of around 11 % to 12% in the credit and deposit also around 10 % growth which we are envisaging

items.statement: FY26 operating profit growth guidance 8-9%, NII growth 7%, NIM 2.8-2.9%
items.quote: operating profit, that is 8% to 9% we are expecting. Net interest income, 7%. NIM 2.8 % to 2.9%.

items.statement: FY26 asset quality guidance: gross NPA below 3%, net NPA 0.3%, PCR ~96%, credit cost below 0.5%, ROA above 1%, slippage ratio below 1%
items.value: GNPA <3%, NNPA 0.3%, PCR ~96%, credit cost <0.5%, ROA >1%, slippage <1%
items.quote: gross NPA we are projecting below 3 % and net NPA 0.3%. PCR already we are at around 96%, so we will be maintaining this level. Credit cost below 0.5% and ROA above 1%. Slippages ratio below 1%.

items.statement: FY26 quarterly slippages expected at Rs 1,500-1,700 crore vs Q4 outlier of Rs 3,001 crore
items.quote: the Rs. 3,000 crore slippage which has happened in the Q4 , definitely that was an outlier and going forward, we are expecting that the quarterly our slippages will be in the range of around Rs. 1,500 crores to Rs. 1,700 crores.

items.statement: FY26 total recovery guidance Rs 16,000 crore, with minimum Rs 1,500 crore quarterly from technical write-offs
items.quote: Around Rs. 16,000 crore of recovery I am expecting in the Financial Year '25-'26. In that, the technical write off - recovery every qu arter, I am expecting that minimum Rs. 1,500 crore will

items.statement: Q1 FY26 NIM to remain at Q4 level (~2.81%), improvement expected from Q2-Q3 as deposit costs decline
items.quote: Q1, mostly we will be at the same level . But definitely going forward, Q2 -Q3 onwards, we see improvement in our NII as well as the NIM.

items.statement: H1 FY26 NIM range 2.8-2.9%, targeting 2.9-3% in H2 as deposit repricing benefits flow through
items.quote: First half we will be in the range of 2.8 to 2 .9 and going forward definitely we will be trying to reach between 2.9% to 3%.

items.statement: Special 400-day deposit scheme withdrawn; deposit costs peaked, new accretion at lower rates; benefit visible from Q3 FY26
items.quote: we have withdrawn that special deposit scheme which was there and the different segment also we are going to revisit our deposit rate and maybe some corrections we will be making in the deposit front. So I am expecting that from the Q3 onwards, definitely that impact will be visible on the NII and the NIM front.

items.statement: Corporate pipeline: Rs 1,15,000 crore sanctioned in FY25 (Rs 85,000 crore pending disbursement) plus Rs 28,000 crore new sanctions in FY26 YTD; NBG pipeline Rs 21,000 crore
items.quote: Rs. 1,15,000 crore sanctions are already there with us. There are disbursement which is going to happen for the loan sanction in '24-'25 is around Rs. 85,000 crores. And in this Financial Year, like from 1st April till today, we have given a sanction of Rs. 28,000 in the corporate book.

items.statement: RAM segment grew 16-17% in FY25; targeting >15-16% growth in FY26 driven by outreach campaigns
items.quote: if you see our RAM sector has also grown at a speed of 16% to 17% in different segments. So we are going to push this Punjab National Bank May 07, 2025 RAM segment very high now and I think there also the growth in the all the retail , agri and MSME I am expecting that there will be a growth of more than 15 % to 16

items.statement: Q4 FY25 slippages Rs 3,001 crore (agri KCC & MSME <Rs 10 lakh) deemed outlier; Rs 288 crore already recovered in April FY26
items.quote: mostly, we have analyzed those slippages and that ha s happened in the agri and the MSME segment. And in the agri and MSME segment also, the slippages which has happened, it is below 10 lakhs segment. So we have strengthened our system now and already in this particular month, April itself, we have made a recovery of around Rs. 288 crore out of those fresh slippages which has happened in the Q4.

items.statement: Board approved raising Basel III AT-1 and Tier-2 bonds of Rs 4,000 crore each
items.quote: We have also taken the board approval for raising Basel III compliant AT-1 bonds and Tier-2 bonds for Rs. 4,000 crore each.

items.statement: Adopting new tax regime by Q2 FY26
items.quote: This financial year definitely we are going to adopt the new tax rule now. Mostly by Q1 or Q2. By Q2 definitely the new tax regime will be in place.

items.statement: Dividend doubled to Rs 2.90/share in FY25 from Rs 1.50; expect continued shareholder rewards
items.quote: this year also if you see with a share of Rs. 2 we have given Rs. 2.90 . Last year it was Rs. 1.5. So almost this year we have doubled. So we are expecting that next year again we will be showing a good performance and definitely all the stakeholders will be rewarded.

items.statement: Wholesale deposits (incl CDs) Rs 2.8 lakh crore (~20% of total); 400-day special deposit scheme was key cost driver
items.quote: Including CD it is Rs. 2,80,000 crore.

items.statement: MCLR cut 10 bps effective 1 May 2025; RLLR loans pass through repo cuts; strategic discounts on retail loans may be revisited if further rate cuts
items.quote: MCLR one cut we have already given of 10 basis point that is from 1st of May.

items.statement: Expect to surpass INR 500 crores revenue from luxury and semi-luxury portfolio in FY26
items.quote: In FY25, we have achieved INR 340 crores and we have grown by 32%. And in our luxury portfolio, like the way Royal Ranthambore is growing month-on-month. And also, how Jaisalmer and Rampur and specially with the 2 new introductions, we are very confident that we'll surpass INR 500 crores.

items.statement: Targeting 15% plus volume growth in Prestige & Above category for FY26
items.quote: See, what he has said that our concentration is more on the P&A category, which we are confident that it will be 15% plus.

items.statement: Expect regular category volume growth of 12% to 13% in FY26
items.quote: And regular volumes are back so I think regular also should grow by 12% to 13%.

items.statement: Expect EBITDA margin improvement of 100 basis points in FY26 with continuous improvement over 3 years
items.quote: I think 100 basis points EBITDA margin improvement will be there, and after that we will have to see how much we will get benefit through reduction in duties. So, our business model is tuned to improve the margin continuously for 3 years.

items.statement: Expect net debt to reduce by 35% to 40% in FY26 and become almost debt-free by FY27
items.quote: For FY26, it will come down by around 35% to 40% and after that, we will be almost debt-free.

items.statement: Sitapur unit commissioned two years ago provides self-sufficiency for next 3 to 4 years, no immediate capex needed for ENA capacity
items.quote: See, about last 2 years back, we had put up our Sitapur unit, which is one of the largest in Asia. And with this, I think we are quite self-sufficient for the next 3 to 4 years.

items.statement: Gross margin improved to 43.5% in Q4 FY25 from 41% in Q4 FY24 and 43% in Q3 FY25 due to premiumization and stable raw materials
items.quote: Gross margin during the quarter was 43.5% compared to 41% in Q4 of last year, and 43% in Q 3 FY25. Gross margin improved both year-on- year basis and quarter -on-quarter basis due to the ongoing premiumization in IMFL business, coupled with relatively stable raw material scenario

items.statement: State governments may raise excise duties but unlikely as it affects brands adversely; wait and watch approach
items.quote: It has been seen in the past that whenever you raise prices beyond a point, it affects the brands adversely. So, it is very difficult to comment as of now. Let's wait and watch.

items.statement: Telangana overdue outstanding below INR 100 crores, lowest in industry; current supplies paid regularly; old dues being released since last month
items.quote: So, the overdue of past period is below INR 100 crores. We are the lowest in the industry.

items.statement: Export volume 5% and value 9% of total business in FY25; exceeded FY24 record levels
items.quote: Fortunately, we exceeded that in FY 25 and we further grew, current export in terms of volume is about 5% of the total business, and in terms of value is about 9%, and it continues to grow.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA per ton guidance for FY26 is Rs. 19,000 to Rs. 21,000
items.quote: And overall, now we are giving the consolidated guidance for the entire year between Rs. 19,000 to Rs. 21,000 EBITDA per ton.

items.statement: Volume growth guidance for FY26 is 9% to 10%
items.quote: So, we are quite comfortable of 9% to 10% volume growth for FY ‘26.

items.statement: Export volume expected to grow 25% to 30% in FY26 over FY25
items.quote: So even though we are announcing a 10% export volume, this is at a higher base. So, compared to last financial year actually we are hopeful that we should get at least a 25% to 30% growth in our export.

items.statement: FY26 capex guidance including investments is Rs. 2,700 crores to Rs. 2,800 crores
items.quote: And just to inform FY ‘26 is going to be around Rs. 2,700 crores to Rs. 2,800 crores.

items.statement: FY25 actual capex and investments were Rs. 4,570 crores vs guided Rs. 5,500 crores with spillover into FY26
items.quote: One, yes, we had given the guidance that we will be making a CAPEX of Rs. 5,500 crores, which the actual number is Rs. 4,570 crores because there is some spillover. So that spillover will come in this year.

items.statement: Indonesia JV for SMS operations half paid in FY25, balance half expected in FY26
items.quote: So, over here half of the payment has already been released in this FY ‘25, the balance half what we expect to release in this FY ‘26.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 EBITDA per ton dropped to Rs. 13,800 due to nickel price dip and trade uncertainty pushing volumes to lower-margin domestic market
items.quote: So again, Q4 definitely was one of the lowest EBITDA per ton that we have witnessed in the last multiple quarters actually. And there were two, three factors to that. One thing is that we saw this in nickel pig iron. Generally when that happens, there are always some ripple effects and it takes time to pass that on to the customer, which is the inventory hit we need to take. Secondly, that was the

items.statement: Q1 FY26 EBITDA per ton already recovering and visible within guidance range
items.quote: And like we said already, in Q1 we are seeing the recovery happening, we are seeing our export bookings also picking up, better margins picking up, which is why we are quite confident of this Rs. 19,000 to Rs. 21,000 for this financial year.

items.statement: Domestic demand growing at 10% to 12%, driven by railways, automotive, infra, oil & gas, power and pipe & tube segment
items.quote: Domestic market in India is definitely the fastest growing market, growing at 10% to 12%, which is exactly why we are planning our next round of expansion in Maharashtra.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 product mix: 200 series 37%, 300 series 47%, 400 series 16%
items.quote: So for the quarter it was 37%, 47% and 16%, yes.

items.statement: Anti-dumping duty application for stainless steel to be filed by end of month; provisional duty expected in 3-6 months
items.quote: So now what we are working with the government is actually on anti-dumping duty for stainless steel, where according to them they are quite confident that this can sale through. We are just currently, I would say, collating the data and we will be applying for it within this month, hopefully.

items.statement: Guidance excludes anti-dumping duty benefit; if implemented, both volume and margin would increase
items.quote: No, as things stand right now, we are quite confident of achieving Rs. 19,000, Rs. 21,000. If anti-dumping or any other macroeconomic factor benefits us, we should be able to come with a higher guidance.

items.statement: Maharashtra greenfield project planned for ~4 million tons over 15 years in phases of 1 million tons; first phase timing and capex not yet finalized
items.quote: It will be bigger, we are looking at close to almost 4 million tons, but over a period of 15 years as you say.

items.statement: Net debt target for end of FY26 is Rs. 3,500 crores to Rs. 3,700 crores
items.quote: So Ritesh, net debt we are estimating in the range of around Rs. 3,500 crores to Rs. 3,700 crores at the end of FY ‘26.

items.statement: Renewable power share to rise from 11% to 30-35% with commissioned projects; 30 MW captive solar in Odisha reducing CO2 by 32,000 tons/year
items.quote: On a group level, currently 11% of our group's power consumption is met through renewable sources. With the commissioning of all our announced renewable projects, this share is expected to rise significantly to around 30% to 35%, marking a major step forward in our sustainable journey.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA improved to Rs 65 crore from minus Rs 13 crore in FY24
items.quote: Our focus on reducing operational costs and improving efficiencies has helped our EBITDA for the year FY2025 to Rs. 65 crores from minus Rs. 13 crores witnessed in FY'24.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 EBITDA was Rs 16 crore versus Rs 13 crore in Q4 FY24
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter stood at Rs. 16 crores as against Rs. 13 crores in Q4 FY24.

items.statement: Gross margin improved by over 12% to Rs 1,149 crore in FY25
items.quote: Gross margin improved by over 12% to Rs. 1149 crores.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 gross margin at 42%
items.quote: Gross margin is at 42%.

items.statement: Capex focused on upgrading infrastructure and machines to remain cost competitive and deliver market-required products
items.quote: CAPEX which we are doing, so basically the spinning process more or less remains the same. What we are putting our CAPEX is more to Sutlej Textiles and ensure we remain competitive in terms of upgrading our infrastructure and moving into machines which are required to deliver the products as per t he market requirements

items.statement: Shifting from commodity yarn to value-added yarn; reducing exposure to core spun and core polyester drag products
items.quote: we have clearly taken a decision that we want to reduce our exposure to the drag products and we want to focus on the hero products which currently are in the category o f cotton dyed and cotton mélange but also work on new blends like aramids or acrylics and create new product heroes for us which can be the contribution driver as we move forward

items.statement: Incubating products for carpet, automotive, technical textiles; quick wins in 3-6 months, certified products in 6-12 months
items.quote: transitions dep ending on the product category we are, takes anything between 6 to 9 months because in certain technical products, there is also this element of certification, because the products have to be certified and the whole certifying process itself is anything between 6 months to a year. But quick wins here will be moving into segments which are lateral, but can give us higher realization

items.statement: Yarn business faces global demand fluctuations; dyed fiber and melange segments show reasonable strength; core synthetics grey segment challenged by shift to filament
items.quote: In those segments, I think there is reasonable strength and we are wanting to build on that. However, on the core synthetics which is grey, there obviously while there is a dem and there is also a general shift from a spun synthetic to what you call as filament which comes out cheaper. So there are reasonable challenges

items.statement: US yarn demand currently stable; retailers cutting channel inventory and seeking cost sharing from converters
items.quote: As of now, our yarn business for US is currently looking stable on the product categories which we operate. But in general, your statement that yes, there is a little bit of cut down from the retailers, that seems to be true.

items.statement: UK home textile business could grow 3x from small base; currently Europe ~6-7% of exports, UK ~50% of that
items.quote: We think that in times to come, this business, at least the UK business, because the starting base is small, can very easily go 3x times for us in Sutlej home business.

items.statement: Adopting highly cautious approach due to India-Pakistan tensions; prioritizing stability and monitoring supply chains and workforce
items.quote: Given the recent escalation in India-Pakistan tensi ons, we are adopting a highly cautious approach. We are prioritizing stability and closely monitoring developments to safeguard our supply chains and

items.statement: US tariff impact shared 50-50 with converters/exporters; Sutlej bears 15-20% of value addition
items.quote: in the end apparel se gment, they have kind of agreed for a 50-50 with the converters or the exporters. In our case, since the value addition is in any case nominal, anything between 15%-20% coming to us and balance b eing borne by them or as the case may be depending on what the requirements are, it's in that range

items.statement: Cotton pricing stable; price differential vs international remains but stability helps plan product mix
items.quote: However, the good thing i s that there is stability in the pricing. Now with this stability, it helps us plan our markets, our product mix and it is definitely much better than what it used to be last year

items.statement: Green fiber (recycled PET) sells at 5-8% discount to virgin fiber; bottle prices fluctuate seasonally
items.quote: selling price is typically in th e whatever the fresh virgin fiber is, this fiber comes at roughly a 5% to 8% discount to that

items.statement: FY25 spindle utilization ~90%, up 4-5% from prior year
items.quote: for the full year '25, our effective spindle ut ilization is close to about 90%, which is about 4% to 5% higher than the previous year

items.statement: Home textiles processing capacity ample; weaving capacity elastic via leasing/contractual weaving
items.quote: capacity also we have within our system. As far as the weaving is concerned, we could always look at leasi ng certain assets based on the market demand and make use of the last mile value addition in processing in-house and cater to the demand as it increases

items.statement: Management confident of 20% YoY volume growth for next 3-4 years
items.quote: As far as the volume guidanc e is concerned, we are highly confident that we can continue to deliver 20 % growth YOY over the next 3-4 years

items.statement: EBITDA spread target near Rs. 5,000 per ton for FY26
items.quote: we are confident that we will come back with EBITDA spreads near Rs. 5,000 per ton in FY'26

items.statement: Capex of INR 15 billion spread over next few years to expand capacity to 7 million tons from current 5 million tons
items.quote: The CAPEX for this is around INR 15 billion, which will be spread across the next few years and it will be easily funded from the internal cash flows.

items.statement: Board approved Rs. 1,500 crore capex; Rs. 500 crore per year phased over FY26-28
items.quote: Rs. 500 crores per year you can factor in.

items.statement: General product EBITDA improved to Rs. 2,800 per ton, Rs. 1,000 higher than last 5 years, commanding 5% premium over nearest competitor
items.quote: Now if you look at the margin in our general product category we reported Rs. 2,800 per ton EBITDA. Now that's almost Rs. 1,000 per ton higher than what we have been reporting over the last five years.

items.statement: Target ROCE of 35% for FY26 and above 50% in next 2-3 years
items.quote: Our focus is more on ROCE, like this year we are targeting, we take the target of ROCE of 35%. Our target is 35% ROCE, which was around 25% this year. And in next 2-3 years, our target is to increase this ROCE above 50%.

items.statement: Incremental growth from new geographies, new products, better sales mix to improve EBITDA spreads without stressing volume
items.quote: The incremental growth is coming from new geographies, new products, better sales mix, which will continue to improve our EBITDA spreads going forward.

items.statement: April volume slightly below target by 5-6%, May going well; expect 1.7-1.8 million tons in H1 and over 2 million tons in H2
items.quote: April is just slightly little bit from our target. Like every year the April is on the downside. We are less than our target, volume target by 5% to 6%. And May is going good. So I don't think like first half of the month we can do 17-18 lakh ton, in the second half we crossed 2 million ton.

items.statement: No hedging instrument available for steel inventory exposure
items.quote: There is no such product to do this. So there is no way, there is no instrument to do this.

items.statement: Export share currently 6%, target to take beyond 10% in next two years
items.quote: As of now we are at 6% and target is to take it beyond 10%.

items.statement: Heavy structural EBITDA sustainable at Rs. 8,000-9,000 per ton
items.quote: It should be in the same range Rs. 8,000 to Rs. 9,000 a ton.

items.statement: EBITDA spreads to improve year-on-year for next 3-4 years beyond Rs. 5,000 per ton due to mix improvement, international sales, operating leverage and cost reduction
items.quote: For FY'26, guidance is near Rs. 5,000 a ton. And over the next few years, EBITDA spreads will continue to improve beyond Rs. 5,000 per ton because of improving sales mix and increasing sales from international markets and getting the operating leverage plus working on the cost reduction factors.

items.statement: Expect 5%-7% decline in stand-alone revenue for FY26 with operating margin of 10%-11%
items.quote: Assuming some order inflows in the next few months, we expect around 5%-7% decline in stand-alone revenue for this fiscal with an operating margin of around 10% -11%.

items.statement: Expect INR15,000-20,000 crores order inflow in FY26
items.quote: So, we are looking at about a INR20,000 crores order inflow this year. INR15,000 crores to 20,000 crores at least what we're expecting because last 2 years have been quite muted.

items.statement: No planned capex for FY26 except small replacement capex
items.quote: Now in terms of capex for the company this year, we are not expecting to do any capex in this financial year per se. So, if there is some very small replacement capex that we have to do, that will happen. Otherwise, we have no targets of any capex. There's no planned capex this year.

items.statement: Coal handling plant capex of INR850 crores to start next quarter, complete in 2 years
items.quote: So, the coal handling plant capex is around INR850 crores. And we will start constructing coal handling plant from next quarter, and it will complete in 2 years' time.

items.statement: Order book of INR14,923 crores executable over 2-3 years; ~INR7,000 crores revenue expected in FY26 from current order book
items.quote: Out of this order book, you can split this into 2 years. So, about INR7,000 crores of revenue should be able to come from this order book alone.

items.statement: Government tightened EPC qualification criteria to pre-COVID levels; similar steps expected for HAM to reduce unqualified bidder competition
items.quote: EPC project, the government has already taken the steps to increase the qualification criteria pre-COVID level. So, they have increased the performance guarantee requirement, the technical requirement, and they have increased in terms of the technical and financial criteria, EPC is done. Now they are considering for HAM also in the similar way.

items.statement: Alpha InvIT: 26% stake transferred in 8 of 18 assets (7 COD, 1 pre-COD); first tranche concluded; remaining 10 assets under construction; InvIT draft offer document filed March 2025, approvals expected this quarter
items.quote: So far, we have transferred a 26% stake in 8 assets out of a total of 18 assets included in the deal. Among these, 7 assets have achieved COD and 1 asset has achieved pre-COD and accordingly, annuity payments have commenced, concluding the first tranche of the Alpha deal. The remaining 10 assets are under construction as scheduled and will be divested upon achieving COD. The formation process of o

items.statement: Interest cost expected around INR400 crores for FY26 at INR8,500 crores revenue
items.quote: So basically, for the revenue of INR8,500 crores, we are expecting interest cost around INR400 crores.

items.statement: NHAI ordering pickup expected from Q2 FY26 onwards
items.quote: Sir, we're expecting second quarter onwards, it should pick up significantly.

items.statement: Revenue expected between Rs. 22,000 crores to Rs. 23,000 crores and EBITDA between Rs. 2,800 crores to Rs. 3,200 crores by FY'27 based on current realization
items.value: Revenue: Rs. 22,000-23,000 cr; EBITDA: Rs. 2,800-3,200 cr
items.quote: basically if you look at the revenue expectation post-27 based on current realization is about anything between Rs. 22,000 crores to Rs. 23,000 crores and EBITDA we are currently this year at about Rs. 1,866 crores. So it should be anything between Rs. 2,800 crores to Rs. 3200 crores.

items.statement: Remaining CAPEX of Rs. 3,904 crore to be spent over next two years; majority of carbon steel CAPEX by FY'26, stainless steel and aluminum by FY'27
items.quote: The remaining Rs. 3,904 crore shall be spend over a period of next two financial years with the majority of carbon steel related CAPEX being completed in the current financial year that is '25-'26. The CAPEX related to aluminum and stainless steel to be completed in the Financial Year '26-'27.

items.statement: FY'26 CAPEX expected around Rs. 2,010 crore comprising captive power, solar, finished steel Rs. 413 crore, stainless steel Rs. 784 crore, aluminum Rs. 126 crore
items.quote: The remaining CAPEX of around Rs. 3,000 crores, out of the Rs. 3,000 crores, the Rs. 2,000 crores of CAPEX will be incurred during the Financial Year '25-'26 which comprising of captive power, solar, and this combined finished steel Rs. 413 crore, stainless steel Rs. 784 crore, aluminum Rs. 126 crore which all conclude there is a CAPEX of Rs. 2010 crores.

items.statement: Launched color-coded roofing sheets under SEL Tiger brand (Royal, Elite, Azure, Alfa variants) and food-grade aluminum foil under SEL Tiger Foil at Jharkhand plant
items.quote: A significant highlight this quarter was launched by our new range of color-coded roofing sheet under SEL Tiger brand introduced in the variant of Royal, Elite, Azure, Alfa, a different brand, a different category and product and price mix.

items.statement: Expect aluminum foil demand to grow 8-10% CAGR by 2030; blast furnace achieved 100% capacity in few months, targeting 110% capacity utilization for FY'26
items.quote: With the demand of aluminum foil in the food business, we expect that we should be growing around 8% to 10% CAGR by 2030 and we will be well positioned to capitalize on the rising demand and emerging opportunity in this sector.

items.statement: EBITDA margin 12.5% in Q4 FY'25, up 30 bps YoY and 40 bps QoQ; FY'25 gross margin maintained at 27.7% vs 28.2% in FY'24 despite 3-5% lower steel realizations
items.quote: Quarter 4 '24-'25 on a consolidated basis, we reported an EBITDA margin of 12.5% which is 30 bps higher on a year-on-year basis and 40 bps higher when compared on a quarter-on-quarter basis.

items.statement: Government imposed safeguard duty on aluminum foil imports from China, supporting domestic manufacturers; company well-positioned to benefit
items.quote: On the regulatory front, we welcome the government decision to impose a safeguard duty on the aluminum foil import from China. This policy is a very positive step to support the domestic manufacture by mitigating unfair pricing pressure.

items.statement: Stainless steel revenue expected Rs. 1,300-1,400 crore in FY'26; wire and bright bar capacity 40,000 tons/year with average EBITDA Rs. 7,000-12,000/ton
items.quote: And this year, we expect that we should be able to do a revenue of close to Rs. 1,300 crores to Rs. 1,400 crores this year.

items.statement: DI pipe plant investment Rs. 350-400 crore for 300,000 tons capacity; targeting EBITDA Rs. 5,000/ton yielding Rs. 150 crore annual EBITDA with attractive ROCE
items.quote: If we invest on 300,000 tons capacity, close to Rs. 350 crores or Rs. 400 crores, and if I am able to gain the EBITDA of say Rs. 5,000 crores, Rs. 5,000 a ton, we make close to Rs. 150 crore EBITDA every year.

items.statement: Steel realizations decreased 3-5% in FY'25 vs FY'24; offset by higher aluminum foil and stainless steel realizations and lower raw material costs per ton
items.quote: There has been a decrease in the realization across steel product in the range of 3% to 5% in the Financial Year '24-'25 as compared to Financial Year '23-'24.

items.statement: Expect Q1 FY'26 volume growth and revenue growth QoQ; market conditions positive and optimistic outlook
items.quote: Market is not bad I would say and I expect that there will be a volume growth. The revenue growth will be also there in this Q1 and I am pretty optimistic like everything is looking very positive.

items.statement: CAPEX funded entirely from internal accruals; net cash position Rs. 1,062 crore as of March 2025; gross debt-to-equity 0.07x; maintenance CAPEX ~Rs. 200 crore in FY'25
items.quote: Our net cash positions is Rs. 1,062 crore as on 31 st March 2025 as against the gross debt of Rs. 768 crore as we have cash and cash equivalent along with the long term investments worth Rs. 1,830 crore

items.statement: Capital allocation policy: 70-80% of cash reinvested, 20% retained as liquidity surplus, 10% returned as dividend; final dividend Rs. 2.25/share declared for FY'25
items.quote: As you all aware that for many years we have been following a prudent capital allocation policy by which 70% of the cash generated is returned back into the business, 20% is retained as a liquidity surplus and 10% is returned to our esteemed shareholder as a dividend.

items.statement: OPVC pipes affecting DI pipe industry below 350mm size (40-50% of market); company restricting to minimal conservative CAPEX to de-risk
items.quote: It is affecting and in the time to come, it will have a great competition with the DI pipe below 300 size. So if you see today a complete DI plant, if you think of establishing a complete DI plant with a center plant blast furnace infrastructure and all, it is not going to cost you less than Rs. 2,000 crores.

items.statement: Commissioned stainless steel wire and bright bar divisions (40,000 tons/year capacity); approved for battery foil supply in EV space; targeting high-value niche products
items.quote: In stainless steel long product, we have recently commissioned the Wire Division and the Bright Bar Division. These wires are all very high precision wires, which has an incredible export market and has a very unique utilization.

items.statement: Target minimum 15% CAGR annually; FY'25 revenue Rs. 15,138 crore (15% YoY growth), EBITDA Rs. 2,097 crore (21.2% YoY growth)
items.quote: we are positioned to achieve a minimum 15% CAGR annually.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 business better due to wedding dates but overall sentiment weak; strategies to show results from Q2/mid-Q2
items.quote: So, overall, we do see green shoots, majorly on account of having wedding dates this year versus negligible wedding dates last year. So, business is better on that account. But overall, in terms of expectations, I w ould say that still overall sentiments we can see from the market are weak and not the best

items.statement: Nine-month July-March FY25 customer sales grew 9.3% with like-to-like growth of 2.9%
items.quote: However, in the nine-month period from July to March FY '25, retail sales grew by 9.3%, with like-to-like sales growing by about 2.9%.

items.statement: FY25 gross margin 67.2%, EBITDA margin 46.6%, PAT margin 28%
items.quote: The Company continued to report industry-leading gross margin of around 67.2% and a healthy EBITDA margin of around 46.6%. The EBITDA during the period stood at around Rs. 646 crores. The Company also reported a strong PAT margin of 28

items.statement: Q4 FY25 gross margin 66.2%, EBITDA margin 45.6%, PAT margin 27.5%
items.quote: The Company continues to report an industry leading gross margin of 66.2%, and a healthy EBITDA margin of 45.6%. The Company reported a strong PAT margin of around 27.5%.

items.statement: FY25 net retail area addition ~85,000 sq ft; FY26 focus on quality retail area, cleanup in H1, decent growth from Q3
items.quote: However, at maybe 3rd Quarter onwards, I think we are quite sure of getting back on decent retail area growth, and, most importantly, one thing which I want to sort of bring some light on is quality retail area will grow tremendously from a complete financial year perspective.

items.statement: Mohey grew ~25% faster than company; shifted from bridal to wedding wear; Mohey ASP Rs 7-8k vs bridal Rs 22-23k
items.quote: And when you sort of talked about Mohey, there has been quite a large delta in terms of growth. So, Mohey would have a close to 25% odd delta in terms of the Company from a growth perspective.

items.quote: The notice -- demand notice was on copper as an element, if you're talking about what particular item was it.

items.quote: And going forward, if you were talking about revenue for quarter 4 and we have grown by about overall 19%, 20% in the category, Commercial Refrigeration category.

items.statement: PLI-linked incentive accrued in other operating income; investment income (interest/MTM) in other income; neither included in UCP segment margins
items.quote: In other operating income we have accrued PLI linked incentive. So therefore, you see a jump in that. That's the only thing.

items.statement: Chennai factory state incentives spread over 15 years; primary objective was market proximity to reduce transit time and transportation costs
items.quote: Actually, there is a state benefit definitely there, which is going to come as we produce. But it is over a longer period, over the next 15 years, I think 15 years, we are going to get the dividends in -- from this factory.

items.statement: Management expects volume growth of around 10% (+/-1%) for FY26.
items.quote: Yes. I think volume growth will be in the range of 10% , (+/-1%), maybe it can be more than 10% also .

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance for FY26 is Rs. 9 to Rs. 11 per SCM, with a possible correction to Rs. 9.5.
items.quote: With respect to the margins, we have just discussed maybe Rs. 9 to Rs. 11 is the right guidance for the next financial year. This year we have got Rs. 10. But one correction is there so we may come down to Rs. 9.5 if that correction is taken into place.

items.statement: Capex guidance for FY26 is Rs. 1,300 crores for MGL and Rs. 150 crores for UEPL.
items.quote: We are expecting around Rs. 1,300 crores CAPEX for FY '26, and again around Rs. 150 crores will be in UEPL.

items.quote: However, our current I &C sale, which is between 0.6 mmscmd to 0.7 mmscmd, we can foresee that going up to about 0.9 mmscmd or 1.0 mmscmd in the next couple of years or so.

items.quote: So, now I think the allocation of APM has come down to around 1.67 mmscmd. B ut correspondingly, there is an increase in the NWG available which is around 0.65 mmscmd, okay. So, bearing the replacement of APM with NWG more or less things should remain

items.statement: Bombay High Court committee on EV transition holding positive discussions; report expected in a month.
items.quote: Several meetings have been held, and we will submit our report, maybe, in a month's time to the High Court, and then it will be disclosed to the public.

items.quote: The committee is still to give their recommendation. It's an internal committee constituted by PNGRB. Further, you must appreciate that the matter is sub-judice under Delhi High Court and the discussions are going on.

items.statement: Final dividend of Rs. 18 per share approved; total FY25 dividend Rs. 30 per share (300% of face value).
items.quote: I am happy to announce that the Board of Directors has approved a total final dividend of Rs. 18 per equity share for this financial year. The total dividend for the year, including interim dividend already paid, is Rs. 30 per share, that is 300% on the face value of Rs. 10 per equity share.

items.statement: UEPL merger process underway; 3EV produced 850 vehicles in FY25; IBC battery plant expected in 12-15 months.
items.quote: We are also in the process of merging UEPL back to MGL. So collectively putting together, Rs. 1,300 crores will be the number expected this financial year.

items.statement: Segment-I margin guidance for FY26 at 7.5%; Segment-II at 8.5% with attempt to reach 9%
items.quote: The guidance for FY26, unless and until something dramatically changes remain, for Segment-I, 7.5%; and Segment-II, 8.5%. And we will attempt to take it to 9%, and that will be with a great difficulty, I think.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 growth outlook revised to 10-15% from earlier 20-25% due to weak April
items.quote: As we sit and see now with a muted April, I would down it to say 10% to 15% growth, and if extremely lucky, it will be 20% growth, because one-month has gone, another seven days have gone.

items.statement: Carried forward order book at record Rs 6,263.4 Cr as of March 31, 2025, up 9.9% YoY
items.quote: Carried forward order book as of March 31, '25, grew by 9.9% to Rs. 6,263.4 Cr as compared to Rs. 5,697.6 Cr as of March 31, '24.

items.statement: Committed to investments in R&D, manufacturing, sales & distribution, digitalization, talent and capacity enhancement
items.quote: The company remains committed to its stated path of investments in research & development, manufacturing, sales & distribution, digitalization, talent development and capacity enhancement in order to strengthen its position in times to come.

items.statement: Price hikes of 3-4% in Jan and 4-5% in April 2025 to pass on input cost increases
items.quote: There was 3% to 4% taken in January, 4% to 5% from April 1.

items.statement: EPR provision ~Rs 10 Cr in FY25, expected to rise to ~Rs 30 Cr in FY26 due to rate tripling from Rs 9/kg to Rs 23/kg
items.quote: As far as Blue Star exact figure, do not worry, it is in the order of Rs. 10 Cr, which will go up to Rs. 30 Cr in the coming year. Last year, midway through it came in, so the differential has been provided for.

items.statement: Compressor supply secured till end of summer 2026; evaluating multiple sourcing options including local assembly and future in-house design
items.quote: On all angles, we believe, at least for FY26, we are fully secured, till the end of summer 2026 we are fully secured. Nothing to worry.

items.statement: R&D investment to continue at 1.5-2% of revenue across all product lines
items.quote: So, clear guideline is that whether it is room air conditioner or a deep freezer or it is a commercial air conditioning system, 1.5% to 2% of our revenue will be invested in R&D. It will keep on

items.quote: We are a manufacturer of chillers, we make a few types of chillers meant for data center applications as well, and we are expanding that range. Now, liquid cooling has not penetrated in India much, and we do not have that, but we are in talks with many players abroad for getting that technology.

items.statement: Management confident of delivering double-digit revenue growth and EBITDA growth ahead of revenue growth in FY26
items.quote: We remain confident in our ability to deliver double-digit growth and continue improving margins.

items.statement: Management expects EBITDA growth ahead of revenue growth and continued PAT growth and ROCE improvement
items.quote: Overall, we remain confident of delivering EBITDA growth ahead of revenue growth and our sharp focus on CAPEX and interest costs positions us well for continued PAT growth and ROCE improvement.

items.statement: Capex for FY26 planned at Rs. 380-390 crore, sufficient for growth plans and Thailand Greenfield
items.quote: Next year, our plan is to spend around Rs. 380-Rs. 390 crore and that should be sufficient to cover for both the growth plans as well as the Thailand Greenfield.

items.statement: Healthy order pipeline in Beauty & Cosmetics with new customer wins across geographies backed by Neo Seam tubes and superior printing capabilities
items.quote: Our order pipeline remains healthy with new customer wins across geographies backed by Neo Seam tubes and superior printing capabilities.

items.statement: India margins showed 100 bps YoY improvement and 170 bps sequential increase driven by operational efficiencies and improved product mix
items.quote: In India, margins have shown a clear recovery in line with our commitment. We saw 100 basis points year-on-year improvement and 170 basis points sequential increase driven by operational efficiencies and improved product mix.

items.statement: Full year EBITDA margin expanded 169 bps to 20%+ with all regions contributing; Europe at 16-17%, Americas at 18-19% with further opportunity
items.quote: This marks the 11th consecutive quarter of EBITDA margin expansion supported by sustained double-digit EBITDA growth . Our margins remain robust at 20% plus, reflecting specific management actions to correct Europe and Americas while ensuring operat ing discipline and product mix

items.statement: Raw material environment benign with key commodities range-bound; most businesses contractual with pass-through mechanisms
items.quote: I would say that raw materials basically have been, I would say, benign, if I can use that word and prices of all the key commodities have been kind of range bound. So I think it is a stable commodity cost environment that we are in right now.

items.statement: Underlying demand trend in tubes remains positive; Beauty & Cosmetics grew over 20% in Q4 and Personal Care & Beyond grew 10.3% for full year
items.quote: Within Personal Care and Beyond, Beauty & Cosmetics witnessed over 20% growth, fueled by focused investments in capability and technology, adoption of new theme, deeper customer engagement as well as sharper execution.

items.statement: Personal Care & Beyond now contributes 48% of total business, growing at 10.3% vs Oral Care at 5.6%; sustainable tube mix risen to 33% from 21% last year
items.quote: Our category mix continued to evolve in the right direction with Personal Care & Beyond growing at 10.3% , nearly double the 5.6% growth in O ral Care. This segment now contributes 48% of our total business

items.statement: Minimal impact expected from US tariffs due to local US manufacturing, small export exposure, and contractual duty pass-through with most customers
items.quote: Further, and importantly, we expect minimal impact of US tariffs as we have local manufacturing in the US. Also, our export to the US is relatively small. Further, EPL has contractual pass through of duties with most customers.

items.statement: Brazil capacity expansion of 40 million tubes/year for Beauty & Cosmetics expected operational in Q1 FY26; Thailand Greenfield to contribute from H2 FY26
items.quote: In Brazil, we are adding capacity essentially for Beauty & Cosmetics because we have already sold out our existing capacity on Beauty & Cosmetics. So we are adding that. items.statement: Steady state tax rate expected at 18-22%; FY25 rate lower due to Europe turnaround and China technology benefit
items.quote: On a steady state basis, I believe that with the countries mix coming in anywhere between 18%-22% is our rightful tax rate that should be delivering.

items.statement: Net debt/EBITDA reduced to 0.54x; ROCE improved to 18% (up 335 bps); EPS grew 44% to Rs. 11.38; proposed final dividend Rs. 2.50/share
items.quote: Stronger EBITDA and PAT combined with solid cash flow generation has helped reduce our net debt to EBITDA ratio to 0.54x with ROCE improving to 18%, expanding by 335 basis points. Consequently, our EPS has improved from Rs. 7.88 in FY '24 to 11.38 in FY '25, an improvement in EPS of 44%.

items.statement: CDP A rating for climate change and water security; UNGC Forward Faster Sustainability Award 2025 for sustainable supply chain excellence

items.statement: China growing at 20% for 5 consecutive years in Beauty & Cosmetics; significant headroom in Europe and Americas where shares are very low
items.quote: In China, we still have a relatively small share, but we have been growing at 20% for 5 years now in a row. So the opportunities are growing much faster than the category.

items.statement: Capex mostly normal with slight increase due to Vizag plant
items.quote: In terms of Capex, most of the Capex is normal Cape x. There's a slight increase in projects because of the Vizag plant. But otherwise, everything is normal and as in the previous years

items.quote: As far as quarter 4 is concerned, results are not yet out but our estimate is that it will be about mid-single digit volume growth is our expectation. As far as quarter one and quarter two concern, it should be in the same range.

items.quote: Ya. So as of now, till quarter 4, actually it is set off. Whatever crude benefit that we got actually got offsetted by the dollar. But yes, beyond this, if it comes, there will be some pass through also will happen as far as industrial is concerned.

items.quote: One is the rupee depreciation. There's a lot of volatility in the rupee, the uncertainty because the kind of changes at the global level. Currently, we are not witnessing anything in the short term, but we really don't know what will happen going forward.

items.quote: And performance coating, we believe, will do well backed by a good order pipeline.

items.statement: Assume 20-25% export volume growth in FY26 over FY25
items.quote: We are assuming 20%, 25% growth this year over last year on export numbers.

items.quote: this year also the exports have been there, but it's not much high, it's only about 100 crores plus which has been done this year and next year we are targeting to double this number.

items.quote: I think will be something similar as you mentioned. As you mentioned the major change will happen once you have this localization I think for Kubota which is still two years away, I think till then I think we will remain in this range only 11.5% to 13% sort of range.

items.statement: FY26 capex guidance of Rs.350-400 crores excluding Greenfield; land acquisition adds Rs.450-500 crores
items.quote: So for FY26, we expect to be somewhere between around Rs.350 crores to Rs.400 crores. And mostly this is excluding any investment towards Greenfield. So the land acquisition gets done, so it will be another Rs.450 crores to Rs.500 crores this year.

items.statement: Railway Equipment order book stands at over Rs.900 crores excluding Rs.383 crores BMBS freight wagon order held by RDSO
items.quote: Order booked for the division at the end of March '25 stands at more than Rs.900 crores. This order book however excludes BMBS order for the freight wagon, approximately Rs.383 crores supply for which have been temporary held by RDSO.

items.quote: I think we do not expect too much upward jump from here. It will remain consistent for some more time until and unless the demand from the market goes up, which is expected in the next one or two years.

items.quote: To the customer it has been to the range of about 10% for products which have moved from BS3 to BS5 and about 7% for products which have moved from BS4 to BS5. All of that impact on the cost for the customer is not fully recovered.

items.quote: Non-tractor revenue comprising of Agri Solution business, engine business, spare parts business in Q4 FY25 constitutes 19% of the Agri Machinery segment revenue as against 18% in the corresponding quarter.

items.quote: So far we have done investment of about Rs.60 crores in the finance Company. The total investment right now I think it is about Rs.200 crores in the initial phase, then finally it will go to Rs.700 crores.

So maybe end of February '28 or '29 beginning is what we are looking

items.statement: Dealer inventory at 4-5 weeks for all tractor brands combined
