items.quote: March end we have almost Rs.6,500 to Rs.6,600 crores of liquidity and this is after paying off the debt of the merged companies, which is almost Rs.350-odd crores. So with railway deal getting close d post taxes will get maybe another Rs.1,400 to Rs.1,500 crores sort of net cash. So maybe by next year end after taking into account the fresh cash generation and the CAPEX and the land investment, ma

items.statement: Management does not provide EBITDA margin guidance for FY26; expects clarity by Q2 FY26
items.quote: We do not give guidance, Aditya. As the year unfolds, by quarter 2, you would have a c lear direction of where we are

items.statement: FY26 capex expected lower than FY25 peak of Rs 2,000 crore; sustenance capex Rs 550-600 crore plus Rs 18 crore prebiotics and ~Rs 60 crore Kenya expansion
items.quote: Our sustenance CAPEX should be clocking anywhere between Rs 550 - 600 Crores or so. And beyond that, I think our biggest CAPEX is increasing capacity in our prebiotics plant at the cost of about Rs. 18 crores and there is no other major CAPEX is being planned during the year.

items.statement: Company fully sold out across all products and expects to remain fully sold out
items.quote: I don't think there's a demand issue in the markets we operate. I think we are fully sold out and will continue to be fully sold out in all our products.

items.statement: US export margins under pressure due to Southeast Asian pricing near $200/ton; no major improvement expected in next few quarters
items.quote: It has been the Southeast Asian market where the prices are hovering somewhere close to, $200 odd per ton and while they have positive contribution margin s, they don’t yield full cost recovery

items.statement: UK business restructuring to be complete by Q2 FY26; Lostock shutdown eliminates losses; pharma salt and bicarb to drive profitability
items.quote: By quarter 2, you would start getting the complete stable profile and our anticipation is in terms of its overall, it should move towards the way Magadi transformed itself.

items.statement: India soda ash demand growth projected at 5-6% for FY26; China demand expected stable to slightly negative after 18% surge in FY25
items.quote: We are factoring anywhere between 5% to 6% growth in India even in the coming year. Indian economy and Indian demand is one of the steadiest we will see for the next couple of years.

items.statement: China soda ash demand grew 18% in FY25 driven by solar and lithium carbonate; expected to normalize to ~6% or flat to -1% in FY26
items.quote: Last year was about 18% surge by mainly solar and lithium carbonate markets. We usually expect about 6% growth. So, we are actually factoring in that China will probably remain stable or maybe have a negative of 1% or so.

items.statement: Kenya expanding 50,000 tons pure ash capacity for float glass; modular plant using green/solar power; expected on stream by end of FY26
items.quote: they have got approval to expand their capacity from the government. NEMA approval has come this quarter. They are pressing ahead with the expansion initially for another 50,000 ton. items.statement: UK commissioned 70,000 tons pharma salt capacity at Middlewich; Lostock soda ash operations ceased; focus on high-grade value-added products
items.quote: Our focus in UK will be to move fully to high-grade value-added products, and in this regard, we have commissioned 70,000 Tons of pharma salt capacity in Middlewich, UK.

items.statement: India commissioned 230,000 tons soda ash and 140,000 tons bicarb capacity at Mithapur in FY25; both fully on stream
items.quote: During the year FY25, the Company commissioned 230 kT of soda ash and 1,40,000 kT of bicarb capacity in Mithapur, both are fully on stream.

items.statement: Tariff uncertainties could shift soda ash production and demand centers; management monitoring but not factoring major shifts yet
items.quote: In our view we have not factored any of the major issues around tariffs. It may lead to rebalancing of supply demand centers and as of now from the centers we manufacture we have not seen a major shift in the way we need to rebalance our market portfolio.

items.statement: Global soda ash supply up 8.9% in FY25 led by China Inner Mongolia ramp-up; prices declined over 25% YoY
items.quote: Soda ash capacity increased by 8.9% and this was the main reason for decline in prices by over 25% from the previous year.

items.statement: US gas costs hedged; 75% energy from coal (stable); gas only 25% of portfolio; conversion to gas by 2030
items.quote: See, gas is fully hedged. I think our big issue, more than the variable cost side in most of the units, it has more been the market pricing and also fixed cost where there are opportunities.

items.statement: US capex being recalibrated; capital allocation prioritized to businesses with good free cash flows
items.quote: When I said recalibration of the CAPEX plan, the bulk of the recalibration in CAPEX is happening in US as we speak. We will be able to grow the momentum in US as soon as we see that it is reasonable levels of free cash flows which then can allow us to invest.

items.statement: Freight costs up 11% YoY due to ANSAC exit; now bearing freight directly but capturing higher revenue; margin impact neutral long-term
items.quote: This year we are getting out of ANSAC in the last year of ANSAC. And which means that now we have to directly get where it see enough price and pay the freight for it. Till last year, we had ANSAC a much higher share. We were delivering at their port in US, and they were incurring the freight.

items.statement: Net debt increased ~Rs 1,100 crore in FY25 due to temporary working capital funding for peak capex; to be repaid from future profits
items.quote: We also had a CAPEX incurred during the quarter, so it is temporary funding for the year for CAPEX and this year we had peak CAPEX in India and all over the place. So that is temporary working capital loan taken to fund the CAPEX, but over a point of time that will be repaid from our equity coming in terms of the profits being made.

items.statement: Targeting INR 500 crore revenue by FY27
items.quote: So, yes, we have given the guidelines of -- we have targeted INR 500 crore 2027, FY2027.

items.statement: Targeting INR 360-370 crore revenue for FY26 with 20-25% growth
items.quote: We are targeting, as I mentioned that 20% to 25% of revenue growth. So, we can say that INR 360 crore, INR 370 crores we are targeting for that.

items.statement: Targeting 25% volume growth for upcoming three years
items.quote: So, we are targeting 25% volume growth. And as I said, our efforts are also in that direction.

items.statement: Adding 1,500 tons/month capacity at existing plant by end of FY26 costing INR 5-7 crore
items.quote: We are targeting for actually this end of the year and maybe early than this. It will cost around INR 5 crore to INR 7 crores max.

items.statement: Long-term EBITDA margin guidance of 22-25%, near-term 25-28% if gross margins hold
items.quote: So, I have always guided for the 22% to 25% of EBITDA in a longer term. So, these maybe if the gross margin remains same and raw material prices remain same, so we can come to the maybe 25% to 28% of EBITDA we can say.

items.statement: VAM prices rose 3-4% last quarter; industry leader and Euro raised prices 1.5-2%
items.quote: Recently in last quarter little rise in the VAM around 3% to 4%. So, as an industry leader has also declared the price rise of just 1.5% to 2% and also, we have declared.

items.statement: Majority of FY25 volume growth from existing five mature states; new states also contributing
items.quote: So majority growth comes from the existing five states. The reason is the volume is higher in these five mature states. And we have also taken the growth from the newer markets also.

items.statement: B2B modular furniture makers currently 5% of revenue, targeting 10-15% in 2-3 years at suppressed margins of 15-20%
items.quote: We have created this model already and that is the modular furniture makers. So right now, 5% of our revenue come from this model and maybe it will be go to the 10% to 15% B2B will get in next 2, 3 years.

items.statement: Receivables jumped to INR 125 crore from INR 94 crore due to March volume spike; expected to normalize in 2 months
items.quote: So, yes, you are very right that from INR 94 crore to INR 125 crores in this March balance sheet, the reason is we have generated a very higher volume in March month and that was around INR 47 crores. So, this is the reason that this jump at this level. But this will be again came back within these two months.

items.statement: Marketing spend targeting 7-8% of revenue (half trade, half brand); currently ~2%, rising to 5-7%
items.quote: So, we are targeting 7% to 8% of revenue. And that will be led by half is trade marketing and half for the brand communications.

items.statement: Brand ambassador Pankaj Tripathi signed for 3 years; campaigns live across TV, print, OOH, digital from May 2025
items.quote: Yes, immediately effect but that is a different strategy for that and the contract is for the 3 years.

items.statement: Carpenter loyalty liability INR 95 crore backed by INR 147 crore fixed deposits; 80% of liability from carpenter program
items.quote: See the company already has a fixed deposit of INR 147 crores. So, we have basically created on this base an asset on the balance sheet where we can serve INR 95 crores regularly or redeem it.

items.statement: Network expanded to 48 branches/stockists across 14 states; 90% revenue from stockist model

items.quote: We are expecting around Rs. 1,300 crores CAPEX for FY ’26, and again around Rs. 150 crores will be in UEPL. And we are also in the process of merging UEPL back to MGL. So collectively putting together, Rs. 1,300 crores will be the number expected this financial year.

items.statement: Current quarter EBITDA margin is around Rs. 10 per SCM; full year FY25 margin is Rs. 10 per SCM.
items.quote: Coming to your EBITDA margin, this quarter we have earned around Rs. 10. And on the whole for the year is again Rs. 10.

items.statement: APM allocation reduced to 1.67 mmscmd; NWG increased to 0.65 mmscmd in April.
items.quote: So, now I think the allocation of APM has come down to around 1.67 mmscmd. B ut correspondingly, there is an increase in the NWG available which is around 0.65 mmscmd

items.statement: I&C volume expected to reach 0.9-1.0 mmscmd in next couple of years from current 0.6-0.7 mmscmd.
items.quote: However, our current I &C sale, which is between 0.6 mmscmd to 0.7 mmscmd, we can foresee that going up to about 0.9 mmscmd or 1.0 mmscmd in the next couple of years or so.

items.statement: Q4 sales volume: CNG 2.934 mmscmd, domestic PNG 0.59 mmscmd, I&C 0.67 mmscmd.
items.quote: Such average sales volume of 4.194 mmscmd consists of CNG of 2.934 mmscmd, domestic PNG of 0.59 mmscmd, and industrial and commercial volume of 0.67 mmscmd.

items.statement: Bombay High Court committee on EV transition holding positive discussions; report expected in a month.
items.quote: Several meetings have been held, and we will submit our report, maybe, in a month’s time to the High Court, and then it will be disclosed to the public.

items.statement: PNGRB open access committee recommendations pending; matter sub-judice in Delhi High Court.
items.quote: The committee is still to give their recommendation. It's an internal committee constituted by PNGRB. Further, you must appreciate that the matter is sub-judice under Delhi High Court and the discussions are going on.

items.statement: Final dividend of Rs. 18 per share approved; total FY25 dividend Rs. 30 per share (300% of face value).
items.quote: I am happy to announce that the Board of Directors has approved a total final dividend of Rs. 18 per equity share for this financial year. The total dividend for the year, including interim dividend already paid, is Rs. 30 per share, that is 300% on the face value of Rs. 10 per equity share.

items.statement: CNG vehicle additions in FY25 were 98,215, highest ever; scheme added 624 vehicles at Rs. 32-34 crores cost.
items.quote: And if you see overall conversion for the year, this is highest in the history of MG L, that is 98,215 number of conversions happened during the year against around 77,000 the last year.

items.statement: Capex breakup: ~Rs. 300 crores CNG, ~Rs. 500 crores PNG including pipelines, ~Rs. 200 crores pipelines, ~Rs. 100 crores replacement.
items.quote: As Rajesh mentioned, around Rs. 300 crores will be for CNG , around Rs. 500 crores will be for P NG, including pipelines. Pipelines will be another Rs. 200 crores and OPEX will be around Rs. 100 crores. Replacement CAPEX, around that number broadly.

items.statement: LNG trucking potential seen; 10-12 more stations needed in Maharashtra; Savroli selling 4 tons/day.
items.quote: We see a very good potential . As we keep on adding the stations we are getting the customer. Presently we have three main customers, one is Concor and GreenLine, as well as some other company. And going forward, we see that at least another 10 to 12 stations in Maharashtra itself will be required to cater to the demand from trucking .

items.statement: Term gas portfolio: ~1.27 mmscmd Henry Hub linked, 0.1 mmscmd Brent linked; HPHT ~0.6 mmscmd.
items.quote: Around 1.27 mmscmd is Henry Hub linked and 0.1 mmscmd is Brent linked.

items.statement: Industry discussing excise duty elimination on CNG and inclusion of natural gas in GST with government.
items.quote: In fact, our regulator PNGRB has also been following it up with ministry for, one, elimination of excise duty on the CNG, as well as LCNG also. And second is the inclusion of gas in the GST.

items.statement: Loan book target of INR1.5 lakh crores for FY26 maintained; may revise upward if PMAY 2.0 or Urban Challenge Fund disbursements materialize
items.quote: We had kept a target of INR1.2 lakh crores for the last financial year, and we had achieved INR1.25 lakh crores. So the target will remain INR1.5 lakh crores for the next financial year.

items.statement: Long-term loan book target of INR3 lakh crores by 2030 retained; may revise higher next year if opportunities unfold
items.quote: We had kept a long-term target of INR3 lakh crores loan book by 2030 and INR1.5 lakh crores loan book by FY '26.

items.statement: NIM improved from 3.18% to 3.22% in FY25; expected to sustain around 3.25%-3.3% with potential further cost of funds reduction
items.quote: We are maintaining our NIM rather improving from 3.18% to 3.22% during last financial year. And I think we will be remaining around these figures only, maybe around 3.25%.

items.statement: NIM guidance for next 2 years at 3.25%-3.3% as rate cuts may add a few basis points but viability focus limits upside
items.quote: We will be maintaining these levels. We had improved from 3.18% to 3.22%. So 4 basis points we had improved. So we are expecting some rate cuts. So another few points increment will come towards the NIM also. And I think it will be around 3.25% or 3.3%, not more than that.

items.statement: Cost of funds reduced by 35 bps from 7.1% to 6.75% in FY25; targeting another 10-15 bps reduction in FY26 via repo cuts, 54EC bonds, zero coupon bonds
items.quote: We had improved our total cost of fund from 7.25% to -- sorry, 7.1% to 6.75%. So it is a reduction of 0.35 basis points.

items.statement: Launched 54EC capital gain exemption bonds and INR5,000 crores zero coupon bonds approved; expect meaningful cost benefit in 2-3 years
items.quote: The government has also approved this zero coupon bond also this year. So it is around INR5,000 crores zero coupon bond. So this will further add to contributing towards this reduction in cost of fund.

items.statement: Committed pipeline of slightly over INR2 lakh crores from sanctions in FY25 and FY26; INR8 lakh crores MOUs signed over 5-year horizon
items.quote: We have a committed pipeline of slightly more than INR2 lakh crores, which we had sanctioned in last financial year and this financial year.

items.statement: Strong infrastructure demand from PMAY, metro, Urban Challenge Fund (INR4 lakh crores investment, INR2 lakh crores PPP), state-level Viksit programs
items.quote: In the last budget, the Government of India has launched Urban Challenge Fund also, which will be projecting around INR4 lakh crores of the investment, and INR1 lakh crores will come from the Government of India as a subsidy or grant.

items.statement: Infrastructure lending at 70% (60% urban infra + 10% affordable housing under harmonized list); targeting RBI's 75% IFC mandate by FY26
items.quote: Presently, we are just touching 70%. So the RBI mandate is only for the 75%. So in 70%, it is urban infrastructure, 60% that you had told. And another 10% is coming from the affordable housing.

items.statement: Net NPA at 0.25%; INR2,000 crores gross NPA targeted for resolution in 18 months; INR800 crores already have NCLT orders; INR400-500 crores recovery expected in FY26
items.quote: We are committed to resolve all these kind of NPAs in 18 months and all efforts are made. And we are continuously coming out of different model and modalities and the mechanism that how to resolve these kind of assets.

items.statement: Private sector PPP/HAM lending to be selective with rated entities, strong concessionaire agreements, third-party appraisal, no volume targets
items.quote: We will be very, very selective in terms of the entities, in terms of the project or segment and in terms of the concessionaire agreements and the comfort that how the revenue flow will come and what will be the fallback arrangement.

items.statement: Added 63 new employees to build capacity for private sector lending and digital transformation; opex increase partly due to recruitment and reclassification
items.quote: In the meantime, we had taken around 63 new employees to create that kind of capacity and capability within the company.

items.statement: No capital infusion needed given 50% CRAR and <6% debt-equity; government unlikely to infuse but other options exist if required
items.quote: I don't think so, Madam because whatever ratios or whatever projections that we are making, we are keeping this in our thoughts that we should not -- because government will not infuse generally, it is not a trend.

items.statement: Borrowing mix: 50% fixed-rate domestic bonds, 50% variable (repo/MCLR-linked); plan to raise more fixed-rate bonds and retire high-cost term loans as rates fall
items.quote: 50% of my borrowing is fixed rate borrowing by way of domestic bonds. And 50% of my borrowing is kind of variable, which is linked to repo or which is linked to the MCLR of the concerned banks.

items.statement: Asset reset period 1-3 years; slight time lag in passing on rate cuts but quarterly IPLR review ensures gradual transmission
items.quote: Yes. There is always a slight time lag between the -- I mean, passing on the increase -- I mean, increase in cost of borrowing or decreasing cost of borrowing scenario. There is a slight time lag in that.

items.statement: Project Spring target: EBITDA margins for Wires & Cables consistently in 11%-13% range over near to mid-term
items.quote: Our guidance, as a part of Project Spring, is on EBITDA and we've given the guidance that over the near to mid-term we expect the EBITDA margins in the cables and wires business to be consistently in the 11% to 13% range.

items.statement: Project Spring target: FMEG EBITDA margins to reach 8%-10% by FY30
items.quote: Looking ahead, the FMEG segment is expected to continue its upward trajectory aligned with our Project Spring goals of achieving 1.5x – 2x industry growth and improving EBITDA margins to 8% - 10% by FY30.

items.statement: Project Spring target: Export contribution to increase to 10% of revenue from current 6% by FY30
items.quote: Under Project Spring, we have anyways laid out a guidance that we would want to increase the contribution of exports to the overall revenue to 10% from the current 6% that we saw in FY25.

items.statement: Wires & Cables EBIT margin 15.1% in Q4 FY25, up 140 bps sequentially on operating leverage and product mix
items.quote: EBIT margins for the Wires and Cables business came in at 15.1%, improving by 140 basis points sequentially. This performance was supported by better operating leverage and a favorable product mix.

items.statement: Domestic Wires & Cables volume growth mid-teens YoY in Q4 FY25; cables volume higher teens, wires high single digit; FY25 volume growth also mid-teens
items.quote: Regarding the mix of value versus volume is concerned, the volume growth within the domestic cables and wires for the quarter YoY was around mid-teens, with the remaining growth coming from value. Within that, cables grew faster than wires. Cables volume growth was in the higher teens while volume growth for wires was in high single digit.

items.statement: Strong demand across power generation (renewables), real estate, infrastructure; expects consistent growth for next many years
items.quote: We have seen an improvement as far as sales to the power generation side is concerned, but this is something that will continu e at least for the next few years. As we are aware, at least on the green power side, we have taken a very aggressive target of reaching 500 GW of power generation through renewable sources and we are roughly at around 200 GW of renewable power generation. So, definitely i

items.statement: No material impact from US tariffs seen; 10% tariff across geographies maintains status quo; India may benefit vs other Asian exporters if tariffs rise
items.quote: Lastly, we don't see any material impact as of now because of the tariffs which are being levied. As of the current status, 10% tariffs are levied across all these geographies which export to US and that means it's status quo as compared to what it was a couple of months back. Even going ahead, post the completion of the 90 day period, if you look at the tariffs which are expected to get levied, I

items.statement: Working capital cycle 49 days in Q4 FY25 (temporary dip due to raw material in transit); normalized steady range 50-55 days
items.quote: Our working capital cycle improved to 49 days in Q4FY25, primarily due to a temporary reduction in inventory days as some of the raw material purchases are currently in transit. On a normalized basis, we expect the working capital cycle to return to a long-term steady range of 50 to 55 days.

items.statement: Net cash position ₹24.6 billion; proposed dividend ₹35/share (26.3% payout), targeting 30% by FY30
items.quote: We have further strengthened our balance sheet with net cash increasing to ₹ 24.6 billion, reflecting continued focus on efficient cash flow management. In line with our capital allocation priorities, we have proposed a dividend of ₹ 35 per share, resulting in a dividend payout ratio of 26.3%. This is a step forward towards our Project Spring target of 30% payout ratio by FY30.

items.statement: Management decided against providing specific guidance for FY25-26 due to global uncertainties around traffic regimes.
items.quote: Given the global uncertainties surrounding traffic regimes that could substantially impact enterprise and OTT communication spending, we have decided against providing specific guidance for FY25-26.

items.statement: Direct margins temporarily diluted in Q4 FY25 due to focus on COGS synergies with Proximus Group.
items.quote: In Q4 FY25, we accelerated our synergy initiatives with the group, while our primary focus was on COGS, the cost of goods sold synergies, which temporarily diluted our direct margins or gross profit.

items.statement: Management expects meaningful improvement in direct margins in FY26 as cross-sell synergies ramp up.
items.quote: We are confident in our ability to capitalize on high margin cross-sell opportunities in FY26. These strategic initiatives should significantly improve Route Mobile's direct margin profile moving forward.

items.statement: Operating costs increased in FY25 due to strategic integrations with Proximus Group including investments in robust systems and processes.
items.quote: Our o perating cost increased notably in FY25 due to strategic integrations with Proximus Group including investments in more robust systems and processes, one-time incentives, and competitive compensation packages to retain top talent

items.statement: New product initiatives grew 38% year-on-year in FY25, expanding beyond A2P SMS into IP-based messaging and email.
items.quote: Our new product initiatives have continued to thrive, demonstrating an impressive 38% year-on-year growth in FY25.

items.statement: Revenue contribution from Tier-1 CPaaS partners increased from 10% in FY24 to 19% in FY25, primarily from low-margin COGS synergies.
items.quote: Revenue contribution from Tier-1 CPaaS partners increased from 10% of total revenue in FY24 to 19% of total revenue in FY25, primarily from low margin COGS synergies resulting from related party transactions.

items.statement: Exceptional charge of Rs. 28 crores taken in Q4 FY25 due to a major global technology company phasing out a key platform and shifting to alternate channels.
items.quote: Regarding the exceptional item for an MNO contract, we have delivered over $100 million in annual value with strong ROI for Route Mobile, even after accounting for the exceptional charge. This charge was triggered in Q4 when a major global technology company began phasing out one of their key platforms while shifting to alternate channels for authenticator and notification service.

items.statement: Borrowings increased to Rs. 450 crores for a six-month period to meet supplier payment obligations; expected to retire in 2-3 months.
items.quote: This was taken kind of only for a six-month period. Essentially again, at the backdrop of a contract where we had to kind of make the payment to a supplier. And it would have entailed a lot of cash pooling. So, we have kind of created a security in India. And then through some treasury, we have some positive carry in terms of the cash deposits that we have. So, from that perspective this loan will

items.statement: Board recommended final dividend of Rs. 2 per share, bringing full-year dividend to Rs. 11 per share, exceeding previous guidance.
items.quote: In recognition of our solid performance, our board has recommended a final dividend of Rs. 2 per share, bringing the full-year dividend to Rs. 11 per share, which exceeds our guidance that we had doled out previously.

items.statement: Company maintains dividend payout ratio of 20% of annualised PAT and will continue scouting for bolt-on acquisitions.
items.quote: From a capital allocation standpoint, we will continue to scout for bolt-on acquisitions to enhance the capabilities of the platform, and we shall continue to maintain our dividend payout ratio of 20% of the annualised PAT.

items.statement: Management expects gross margins to meaningfully improve from current levels and steady around historical levels as cross-sell synergies ramp up in next few quarters.
items.quote: As the cross-sell synergy starts to ramp up, Swapnil, you will see that improvement coming through. I mean whenever we start to kind of start hitting those cross-sell numbers you will see meaningful improvement coming through. We anticipate in the next few quarters, we will definitely see meaningful improvement there.

items.statement: Strategic partnership deals won previously expected to contribute meaningfully in FY26.
items.quote: In t he past, I think we have won a few large deals. Unfortunately, some of them were not kind of contributing meaningfully during the year gone by. But some of those strategic partnerships that we have won, in FY26 you will see some meaningful kind of contribution from some of those strategic partnership deals that we have won

items.statement: Advances and deposits with telcos are short-term; one telco dispute in arbitration; expected to unwind over next few months and clear by next financial year.
items.quote: So, I mean they are mostly short term in nature and I think for one of the telcos, I mentioned in the notes we have also a legal dispute right. I mean that is now kind of gone into an arbitration. So we will share more light as and when we have more color on that arbitration proceedings

items.statement: FY26 AUM growth guidance of 30-35% with deposits growing faster and CD ratio below 100%
items.quote: So far as our overall book growth is concerned, we will continue to work with the guidance of 30% to 35%, something that we have been targeting for the last couple of years. Equally, on the deposit side, we expect to grow faster.

items.statement: FY26 secured mix target of 55%, GNPA <5%, NNPA <3%, credit cost 1%
items.quote: So secured mix is something that we'll target in the range of 55%. And so far as the GNPA and NNPAs are concerned, we will target a GNPA of somewhat less than 5%, NPA less than 3% and a credit cost of 1%.

items.statement: FY26 ROA guidance 1.5-1.6%, ROE 11-12%
items.quote: So for ROA, we will be somewhere between 1.5%, 1.6%, and that translates to an ROE of anywhere between 11% to 12%.

items.statement: FY26 net credit cost guidance of 1% excluding CGFMU premium; total credit cost including premium 1.75-2%
items.quote: So we are considering a 1% credit cost on a net basis for FY26.

items.statement: Technology investment of ~INR 200 Cr for migration to Finacle core banking platform
items.quote: We have done a huge investment in tech around closer to INR 200 Cr moving from profile to Finacle and which what gave us visibility in terms of our entire MSME journey is a 1-minute pre-approval journey.

items.statement: Digital deposit channel at INR 350 Cr with 30,000+ customers and INR 3 Cr daily run rate
items.quote: Currently, the deposit sourced through the digital channel stood at INR 350 Cr with over 30,000 granular retail customers and a daily run rate of about INR 3 Cr.

items.statement: Cost of funds increased to 7.8% from 7.3% YoY; cost-to-income ratio elevated at 70.6%
items.quote: Our cost of funds stood at 7.8%, up from 7.3%. Our cost-to-income ratio stand elevated currently at 70.6%.

items.statement: CGFMU premium locked at 1% for first 3 years; may rise to 1.25% in worst case after 3 years
items.quote: For the first 3 years, it doesn't go up. The rates are locked in. Based on the portfolio performance and the claims that we make, the rates will go up in the next cycle after the first 3 years.

items.statement: MFI collection efficiency expected to normalize and credit costs to stabilize by Q3 FY26
items.quote: Despite these challenges, the collection efficiency of MFI is expected to return to normalcy and credit costs are expected to stabilize by the third quarter of FY26.

items.statement: CGFMU claims of INR 460 Cr cover 100% of net NPA; INR 360 Cr expected in FY26, balance in FY27
items.quote: Not all of the INR 460 Cr will come in the financial year, about INR 360 Cr is expected to come in the current financial year. But what this essentially means is that my entire net NPA is covered under the credit guarantee scheme.

items.statement: April collection efficiency dipped 50-100 bps vs March; guardrails implemented Nov 2024, new-to-bank JLG near zero
items.quote: As of now, while March looked good across at 99% plus collection efficiency on current, April has not been maintaining the same momentum. And it is not any particular state which showed up. Across the board, there has been almost a 50 basis to 100 basis points reduction.

items.statement: Karnataka current bucket collection efficiency still ~300 bps below other states; Tamil Nadu stable so far
items.quote: It has not c ome back to anywhere closer to 99% in terms of current bucket collection efficiency. It's still kind of 300 basis points lower compared to the other states

items.statement: ARC sale of INR 80 Cr principal outstanding secured portfolio realized INR 31 Cr; used INR 20 Cr floating provision
items.quote: If you look at the ARC book that got sold, we had a principal outstanding of around INR 80 Cr and net of NPA provisions, it was around INR 50-odd Cr. So essentially, on that INR 50 Cr, we got around INR 31-odd Cr -- INR 30-odd Cr as purchase consideration.

items.statement: FIG book exposure to Aviom Financials (NCLT) fully provided; expect substantial realization and write-back
items.quote: We had one loan to Aviom Financials. That particular name has currently got into NCLT and the CIRP process. However, as things stand today, so we have provided 100% as a matter of caution and conservatism. But given how the thing is progressing, we expect substantial realization and a provision write-back in due course.

name: Aptus Value Housing Finance India Ltd

items.statement: Expect to outperform industry growth by about 2x in FY26
items.quote: We target to outperform the underlying industry growth yet again by about two times this year.

items.statement: Target export share of consolidated revenue at 14-15% by FY28
items.quote: A key focus of our strategy is the expansion of our global footprint with the target to increase our share of exports and our consolidated revenues to 14% to 15% by FY28.

items.statement: Current order book at around 85% of forecasted FY26 revenues
items.quote: With our current order book at around 85% of the forecasted FY26 revenues, we are well equipped to capitalize on these emerging opportunities.

items.statement: Plan additional capex of Rs. 40-45 crores in FY26 to increase capacity at Bangalore plant
items.quote: Due to significant new business opportunities, we plan to invest an additional capex of around Rs. 40 to 45 crores during FY26 to increase production capacity at our SJS plant in Bangalore.

items.statement: Total capex allocation of Rs. 150-odd crores for FY26 and Rs. 220 crores over three years
items.quote: If I say in a number point of view , Rs. 150-odd crores for FY26. And if I talk about three year scenario, close to Rs. 220 crores capex allocations we are going to do.

items.statement: SJS Decoplast expansion of Rs. 100 crores on track for H1 FY26 commissioning, Rs. 30 crores spent so far
items.quote: We allocated Rs. 100 crores for the expansion and this expansion is in progress at this moment. And we are hopeful that in H1 it will get completed.

items.statement: Cover glass capex of Rs. 40 crores allocated over FY26 and FY27, commissioning targeted by end of FY26
items.quote: On the cover glass, we have allocated the capex for Rs. 40 crores which is going to happen during this year and the next year.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin at 26.1% in Q4 FY25, 26.4% for full FY25
items.quote: EBITDA grew 27.1% to Rs. 2,032 million with a margin of 26.4% , and margin expansions by 129 bps.

items.statement: Expect two-wheeler industry growth in high single-digits and passenger vehicle growth in mid single-digits in FY26
items.quote: Largely, let me summarize, it depends on customer-to-customer, but overall, we expect the two -wheeler growth this year to be in high single-digits and the passenger vehicle growth to be mid single-digits.

items.statement: New generation products contribution doubled from 13% in FY21 to ~28% in FY25
items.quote: Contribution from new generation products in FY21 was 13% of our total revenue, and now it has more than doubled to close to about 28% of our total revenue in FY25.

items.statement: No tariff notifications received from customers; India at lower end of tariff spectrum vs competitors
items.quote: As I have answered earlier, so far we do not have any notification from any customer . And as I have said earlier, these tariffs, I think India is at the lower -end of the tariff spectrum.

items.statement: Hero MotoCorp awarded business across multiple models in April 2025; Hero buys ~Rs. 250 crores of decals and logos annually
items.quote: Hero currently buys about Rs. 250-odd crores of decals and logos , so we hope to win a significant share of that business.

items.statement: Stellantis programs worth ~Rs. 300 crores over 7-8 years, supplies starting Q2 FY26
items.quote: So it's close to about Rs. 300 crores business over the next seven to eight years. And supplies for the first models will start from Q2 of this year and they gradually ramp up.

items.statement: Whirlpool orders to start supplies from Q2 FY26 over next 4-5 years
items.quote: No, that should again start from this year. So, we will start supplies again by about Q2. So that, yes, we will start this year and continue over the next four, five years.

items.statement: SJS Decoplast expansion targets doubling turnover to ~Rs. 320 crores
items.quote: So close to Rs. 320 crores kind of a turnover we can able to generate with the new expansion.

items.statement: Actively looking at acquisition opportunities in US by end of FY26/FY27 after tariff clarity
items.quote: So, by next year is when we think that we will actively work on an acquisition. At the moment, we are collecting gunpowder.

items.statement: KFC net store additions guided at 60-80 per year medium term; Pizza Hut net additions capped at 20-25 per year max
items.quote: In the previous quarter call, we said KFC we can look at opening 70 to 80 stores or anywhere between 60 to 80 stores, that guidance still stands and that's a medium term guidance, not just for this particular year. I think we can continue to add 60 to 80 stores. For Pizza Hut we said our restaurant expansion strategy will be extremely cautious and that's what we continue to follow. So, we don't se

items.statement: KFC restaurant EBITDA margins expected to hold at current levels with low single digit SSSG; improvement possible if SSSG exceeds 5-6%
items.quote: I think holding onto the current level margins would be a good achievement. And for holding the current level margins we will require some SS SG even if it means low single digit SSSG. And I think that's what our immediate task would be, to get back into positive SSSG territory

items.statement: Pizza Hut restaurant EBITDA expected to remain low single digit for next 12 months as brand rebuilds from 42k ADS
items.quote: In the immediate scenario when I look at the coming year, I think it would still be range bound to a flattish kind of to low single digit restaurant EBITDA which we experienced last year.

items.statement: KFC new store capex ~Rs 2.1 crore; Pizza Hut new store capex ~Rs 1.35 crore; total FY25 capex ~Rs 265 crore including refurbs and tech
items.value: KFC 2.1 cr, Pizza Hut 1.35 cr per store
items.quote: If I come down to the breakup, in terms of the new store, the KFC is still in the range of Rs. 2.1 crore and Pizza Hut is in the range of Rs. 1.35 crores for per store.

items.statement: KFC full year restaurant EBITDA margin 17.3% despite -4% SSSG; Q4 consolidated restaurant EBITDA margin 12%
items.quote: despite the negative SSSG and the operating deleverage as a result, still our EBITD A margins were healthy at 17.3% and we crossed a significant milestone of 500 restaurants during the year, thereby doubling our count over 3

items.statement: Pizza Hut Q4 restaurant EBITDA negative 4.6% due to pullout of mass media advertising and lower ADS
items.quote: Gross margin dropped by 70 basis points and on back of the increased value and promotional offerings, this combined with low ADS and increased marketing spends although below the line but we continue to spend behind additional marketing as well meant that the restaurant E BITDA was impacted which came in at 4.6

items.statement: Sri Lanka full year restaurant EBITDA margin 15.4%, highest in 3 years; Q4 at 14.8%
items.quote: Slide # 47 which gives a 4 -year trend clearly seen the business has made a strong comeback and has delivered the highest restaurant EBITDA margin in the last 3 years at 15.4%.

items.statement: Demand environment remains neutral/tight with heightened competitive pressure; KFC SSSG trend flattish currently
items.quote: The demand situation continues to be neutral. It's not improved or it is not worsened off over the last three or four quarters. So, it's still a tight demand situation and then coupled with heightened competitive pressures has meant that growth has been difficult to come by.

items.statement: Pizza Hut mass media advertising paused in common markets due to disagreement with sister franchisee; resolution expected in couple of quarters
items.quote: We believe that this difference we should be able to resolve in the next couple of months. Having said that, one of the pillars of our strategy was a continuous innovation pipeline.

items.statement: KFC own delivery channel grew 3x aggregator growth in Q4, now ~10% of KFC delivery revenue
items.quote: Our own platform growth was 3x the growth which we experienced on the aggregator platform so that was a big positive for us.

items.statement: Sri Lanka store additions accelerated to high single digits for next 1-2 years after turnaround
items.quote: Earlier we were looking at a low single digit restaurant addition. I think now we can look at high single digit restaurant addition at least in the coming year, maybe next 2 years as well.

items.statement: KFC gross margin held relatively stable with small QoQ drop; value impact offset by product composition tweaks
items.quote: Actually, when you look at QoQ there we would have dropped very small amount of gross margin over there in case of KFC. Also, there are always an opportunity where on few product compositions or can we do some tweaking so that we can hold on to gross margin.

items.statement: Free cash flow may dip into cash reserves in FY26 due to renewal fees and major refurbishments
items.quote: We don't expect the cash flow to be positive coming here. We expect will marginally dip into our resources of cash.

items.statement: Corporate cost growth kept to single digits vs 13-14% revenue growth; target corporate cost growth at 2/3 to 3/4 of revenue growth
items.quote: Typically, the kind of thumb rule which we use is can the corporate cost grow at a two-third to three-fourth of the overall revenue growth. Our revenue growth last year was at a consol level 13%-14%. And yes a single digit growth was a good outcome.

items.statement: 70% of store additions in last 2 years in Metro/Tier 1 cities; same mix expected for next 2 years
items.quote: 70% of our stores which we added even in the last 2 years are in Metro and Tier I cities. I think that ratio and mix will continue even going forward at least for the next 2 years.

items.statement: Consolidated top line expected to grow at least high single-digit in FY26 with much stronger bottom line growth
items.quote: On a consolidated basis, we expect at least a higher single-digit growth in financial year '26 in top line and a much stronger growth in the bottom line.

items.statement: Bronze bushing business expected to grow at least 30% in FY26 over FY25
items.quote: I expect this business to continue to grow strongly, clocking at least about 30% growth in financial year '26 over '25.

items.statement: Capex of INR78 crores in Q4 FY25 and INR209 crores for full FY25 at consolidated level
items.quote: The company has incurred a capex of INR78 crores in the last quarter at consolidated level and INR209 crores for the whole financial year 2024-'25.

items.statement: Solar division expects healthy top line growth in FY26 based on orders on hand and in pipeline
items.quote: We are expecting a healthy growth of top line in the current financial year in this division based on orders on hand and in pipeline.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 engineering margin improved due to higher sales, lag in price pass-through, better product mix, cost control and financial income
items.quote: For the quarter and year ended, margin has improved, as explained by Vishal mainly on account of increase in sales, lag in price pass through, better product mix, better cost control and financial income improvement.

items.statement: Benefited from steel price reduction pass-through with lag in Q4 FY25; pass-through mechanism continues for FY26
items.quote: we have seen some benefit of price red uction, which has come through specifically on the steel side and that is being pass through to customers. So we have seen some lag a nd specifically I would mention that quarter 4, that lag was a little bit

items.statement: Early signals of revival in industrial demand seen in Q4 FY25; hopeful trend continues in coming quarters
items.quote: We have also started getting early signal of revival in industrial demand in quarter 4 and we are hopeful that this trend will continue and become more distinctly visible in coming quarters.

items.statement: Bronze bushing turnover exceeded INR100 crores in FY25; stamping business growing decently with value-added products coming
items.quote: I'm extremely delighted to inform you that our bronze b ushing business has really grown significantly in this financial year and we have recorded a turnover in excess of INR100 crores in this division for financial year 2025

items.statement: One-time impairment of INR95 crores in standalone and INR28 crores consolidated for Romania investment due to weak Europe demand and customer offtake reduction
items.quote: we have made a onetime impair ment provision of around INR95 crores in the value of our investment in Romania in our standalone books, which has translated into a net onetime provision of around INR28 crores in consolidated financial statement for FY 2025

items.statement: Solar division wrote off INR20 crores bad debt and made INR5 crores ECL provision; confident of reversing ECL
items.quote: In this quarter, after critically evaluating the recovery possibilities of old sticky debts of two of our major customers, we have written off a bad debt of around INR20 crores. We have also made an ECL provision of around INR5 crores as per Ind AS provisions, but we are quite confident of reversing the ECL part of the same going forward.

items.statement: Japan customer sales flat but signals indicate offtake likely to increase in coming quarters
items.quote: Further, the sales to Japan -- Japanese customer look flat and we are getting signal from key Japan-based customer indicating that their offtake is likely to increase in coming quarter.

items.statement: China subsidiary performance satisfactory in Q4 FY25; positive contribution expected to continue
items.quote: The performance of our China subsidiary has remained satisfactory in quarter 4 and has, therefore, positively contributed both in terms of EBITDA as well as PAT level for quarter 4 and FY '25. Going forward, we anticipate this positive contribution to continue from our Harsha China division.

items.statement: Romania operations cannot continue at current level; long-term strategy being formulated over 2-3 months
items.quote: Very obviously, the fact that we have provided for impairment would mean that, yes, the Romania operations cannot continue at the current level in this form. So give us maybe 2, 3 months more, and we'll get back to you.

items.statement: Working capital cycle improved to 126 days at March '25 from 144 days previous quarter and 142 days March '24
items.quote: Overall working capital cycle at consolidated level remains around 126 days for the year-end March '25 against the 144 days in the previous quarter and 142 days in the previous year March '24.

items.statement: Order book at Rs.14 crores as of 31 March 2025; L1 pipeline of Rs.400+ crores active and progressing
items.quote: While our order book, as of 31st March 2025 stood at approximately Rs.14 crores, our L1 pipeline opportunity of Rs. 400+ crores continue to stay active and in progress in the right direction with recent domestic additions as well.

items.statement: Emergency procurement tenders intended to close in early Q2 FY26 with 12-month delivery timeline
items.quote: The initial timeline that we understand this opportunity came with was to potentially close in the early part of the second quarter, that was the intended timeline for closure of order delivery to the industry.

items.statement: R&D spend of Rs.76.5 crores in FY25 expected to continue at similar level for next fiscal year
items.quote: Hardik last year we infused roughly about Rs.76 crores of fresh capital in R&D in our ongoing projects for the, at least coming year on the visibility would be to stay on the similar line

items.statement: Q4 FY25 gross profit Rs.7.3 crores at 36% margin; FY25 gross profit Rs.53 crores at 33% margin
items.quote: For the quarter, gross profit stood at Rs.7.3 crores with a gross profit margin of 36%. For FY'25 gross profit stood at Rs.53 crores, with a gross profit margin of about 33%.

items.statement: New emergency procurement cycle for counter insurgency and counter terrorism operations in tendering phase in Q4 FY25
items.quote: The industry started to regain momentum at the end of the year, with the new emergency procurement cycle for counter insurgency and counter terrorism operations going into the tendering phase in Quarter 4

items.statement: US tariff uncertainty and country-of-origin restrictions driving exploration of substantial product transformation in the US
items.quote: The tariff uncertainty and certain country of origin restrictions in the procurement programs are also driving us towards exploring substantial transformation of our products in the US.

items.statement: SWITCH UAV certified by DGQA as Fit for Indian military use in Q4 FY25; SWITCH v2 launched with 25% better flight time and range
items.quote: After extensive usage by our forces, our SWITCH UAV has been certified by the DGQA as Fit for Indian military use. SWITCH is the only UAV in its class to get this approval.

items.statement: Revenue target of Rs.200 crores by FY27 with Rs.20 crores factored from a planned 100-bed hospital acquisition
items.quote: For 2027 all numbers are expected, numbers are mentioned in circular Vision 2027. Slide #10 you if you could refer, it has expected PBT, expected EBITDA and PAT margin, everything is given there, sir.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target of 21% to 25% driven by cancer unit improvement and cost control in existing hospital
items.quote: EBITDA margin we are looking for 23% to 25%. With the improvement in the cancer unit, our EBITDA will improve drastically and in the existing hospital also we are trying to bring down the cost control very significantly.

items.statement: Cancer hospital ARPOB target of Rs.45,000 to match HCG benchmarks
items.quote: Sir, for cancer hospital, we are targeting to match with the HCG. HCG is having around 45,000 ARPOB and we would like to match that number because to achieve that target we need to create a similar kind of comprehensive cancer care spectrum of services to provide.

items.statement: Super Speciality hospital occupancy target of 70% from current 61%
items.quote: In the multispeciality hospital we are looking for a capacity utilization of 70% because that 70% will give us a good boost to the revenue.

items.statement: Cancer hospital occupancy target of 50% from current 30%
items.quote: In the cancer hospital if we achieve 50%, our revenue targets will be met rather we will be reasonably advanced of that.

items.statement: No significant CAPEX required for growth; infrastructure in place to achieve Rs.300+ crores revenue without further addition
items.quote: We are not looking for any fundraising and significant CAPEX investment because the infrastructure we have built is poised to achieve that target.

items.statement: Plan to acquire 100-bed hospital and add 50 beds across existing hospitals to reach 500 total beds by FY27
items.quote: Sir, we are targeting to add 100 beds, another hospital we want to acquire because when we have fund available, when we have things, it is in the pipeline to acquire 100 bed hospital and bed capacity another 50 beds will be added in the existing both the hospitals.

items.statement: Linear accelerator currently delivering 20 radiations per day, targeting 80 per day
items.quote: At present, we are delivering approximately 20 radiations per day. And this number has to go from 20 to we are targeting that we should be at least 80 radiations per day.

items.statement: Employee cost growth expected to moderate to not more than 20% annually over next two years after 30% jump in FY25
items.quote: It will not jump like that. So, as it is said it jumped to around 30%. We believe that it should be not more than 20% in the coming days.

items.statement: Trade receivables increased due to 92% cashless patients in cancer hospital under government schemes; payments delayed 3-4 months
items.quote: In the cancer hospital, we have 92% cashless patients, and cashless patients are either from Ayushman Bharat or government sponsored schemes. So government response for these schemes money comes when government allocates funds.

items.statement: Land dispute resolved; High Court removed company as party and stated judgment will not impact hospital land
items.quote: High court threw us out from the list of parties. So we are not a party in the case. The case is continued to be heard in the high court, but we are not a party and high court has explicitly mentioned that any judgment in this proceeding will not have any bearing on the Asarfi Hospital.

items.statement: Cancer hospital building trust through health talks across 10+ districts; added DM Hemato Oncologist to expand services
items.quote: We are organizing lots of health talks to the neighboring districts aggressively; yesterday itself. We organized at least four health talks, one in Ranchi, two in Hazaribagh and one in Dhanbad.

items.statement: Cancer hospital revenue driven 60% from non-admitted patients (radiation, medical oncology); bed occupancy not reflective of revenue
items.quote: 60% of the revenue comes from patients who are not admitted to your hospital. So that does not reflect things.

items.statement: Eye unit equipment sold to SharpSight; now renting facility to SharpSight who operates it with rotating doctors
items.quote: We partnered with our SharpSight and sold the eye unit equipments to SharpSight so that asset became their asset and now we are charging rent for the facility which we have provided them.

items.statement: Food delivery GOV growth guidance for FY26 is 18% to 22% year-on-year, currently trending towards lower end
items.quote: We have spoken about an 18% to 22% kind of year-on-year growth guidance, and we are towards the lower end of that range.

items.statement: Instamart contribution margin breakeven targeted within three to five quarters, could happen in December 2025 or June 2026 quarter
items.quote: As I said, we are seeking flexibility over two more quarters, it could happen in December, it could happen in the June quarter of the next calendar year.

items.statement: Instamart AOV growth guidance upgraded to high-teens growth for coming year
items.quote: We have continued to guide that we will be doing double digit. If you have observed that we have now upped this guidance, we expect that over the coming year we will be able to deliver high teens growth on the AOV.

items.statement: Capex cycle peak is behind, significant reduction expected going forward; per dark store capex not more than Rs. 80 lakhs
items.quote: We do believe that a large part of the overall CAPEX cycle that we had started for this deployment journey is now behind us, and going forward you should see that reducing in a significant way.

items.statement: Added 314 stores in Q4 FY25; future store additions to be growth-driven and graded, not city-expansion driven
items.quote: We have added 314 stores last quarter, as well as we have been increasing our warehouse footprint, and that has led to the overall capex deployment.

items.statement: Instamart contribution margin peak investment behind; expect quarter-on-quarter improvement from here as network utilization increases
items.quote: Having said that, the peak of the contribution margin investment is behind us. As you have seen, our network has expanded very rapidly over the H2 of last financial year, which means there's a certain amount of underutilization of the cost that is sitting into our P&L which will start decreasing quarter-on-quarter from here on.

items.statement: Maxxsaver economics at same ballpark as core; fulfillment cost advantage from higher AOV offsets discount given to customers
items.quote: Structurally, the Maxxsaver option which kicks in for majority of the customers at greater than Rs. 999. So, the economics overall is not very different. There is obviously a discount that we give to the customer. But the fulfillment cost advantage that w e get out of a higher order value allows us to be at the same ballpark

items.statement: Food delivery demand improved in February and March vs January; Bolt contributes 12% of order volumes and shows incrementality
items.quote: Bolt has grown at a faster clip and contributes 12% of overall order volumes today.

items.statement: Instamart added 2.8 million MTU in Q4 FY25, more than previous six quarters combined; cohort quality and retention tracking well
items.quote: If you have seen our numbers, just in the last quarter we have added more users as compared to the last six quarters, right, we added 2.8 million MTU.

items.statement: Megapods show highest profitability at maturity due to higher AOV and throughput; Maxxsaver drives incremental AOV and SKUs
items.quote: Matured Megapods which have come up in places where they were already mature, it has actually the highest profitability for us. So yes, if you look at maturity of the pod and the Megapods existing that is there, our probability is actually quite good, because AOV is higher as well as the throughput is high.

items.statement: Competitive intensity in quick commerce stable from existing players but new entrants expected; customer acquisition costs elevated but showing signs of improvement
items.quote: I think from the existing quick commerce players we have not seen any magnitude of going up or down in the recent past. At the same time, there is the expectation of newer set of competition coming in, but enough is not known yet to be able to give you specific guidance on that.

items.statement: Strong balance sheet with Rs. 6,700 crores cash; food delivery run-rating ~Rs. 1,000 crores EBITDA; comfortable on cash burn runway
items.quote: Currently we have a very strong balance sheet. As you see, Rs. 6,700 crores and the food delivery business and the dine-out business also turning profitable which continue to accrue to the treasury balance.

items.statement: Out-of-home (Dineout) business turned profitable; steady-state target of 4-5% EBITDA margin; will index on growth investment in near term
items.quote: We do expect that this business, at a steady state, again, can deliver in the ZIP code of 4% positive EBITDA for us.

items.statement: No implicit market structure assumption (e.g., number of players) in contribution breakeven guidance
items.quote: No, there is no such implicit assumptions in these.

items.statement: Management reaffirmed three-year EBITDA target of Rs 1,800-2,200 crore by FY28 and said they remain on track.
items.quote: From a three-year standpoint, we are not changing the guidance that we had given earlier. And we feel confident and remain on track to achieve that.

items.statement: FY26 capex expected at Rs 950-1,000 crore, mostly for Zone-4 projects.
items.quote: Based on our current plan, we expect the capex in FY26 to be about 950-1000 crs.

items.statement: Maintenance capex estimated at Rs 150-200 crore in FY26; rest for new Zone-4 initiatives.
items.quote: I guess the maintenance CAPEX and CAPEX related to some of the initiatives which are there on the existing product should be in the range of Rs. 150 crore to Rs. 200 crore or so.

items.statement: Long-term contracts for nitric acid, polymer application with global major, and US specialty polymer intermediate performing well; other supply contracts vary with market conditions.
items.quote: I think the 20-year purchase agreements that we have for nitric acid continues to perform exactly as per contract, no issues on that front. The other project that we have, which is where sort of our profitability is ensured, right, it's the polymer application with a global major, I think that continues to run very well.

items.statement: Cost optimization initiatives largely implemented in FY26 but EBITDA accrual, especially from hybrid power, will flow fully from FY27.
items.quote: From an implementation point of view, bulk of it w ill be done in FY ‘26. From an EBITDA accrual of that saving initiative poin t of view, it will go into, I think the full approvals will happen into next sort of, not in this financial year but the next financially

items.statement: Net debt expected to reduce by Rs 200-300 crore in FY26 as capex intensity declines and working capital unlocks cash.
items.quote: So directionally, I guess, we would have peaked out. We expect the number to be lower. We are expecting some unlocking of cash flow from working capital as well. So, plus the CAPEX intensity is also going down. So directionally, I expect the number to be lower by maybe Rs. 200-300 crore kind of range.

items.statement: Agrochemical intermediate pricing remains weak due to Chinese overcapacity; US tariffs may create mixed impact across product portfolio.
items.quote: We are seeing volume recovery for sure, but given the amount of over capacity that exists in China, that incr emental volume growth is also served by marginal pricing, and that's where we are not seeing uptick on pricing/margins at this stage

items.statement: Volume growth driven by existing assets; Zone-4 commissioning in Q3-Q4 FY26 but meaningful volume contribution only from FY27.
items.quote: This year we are pushing for volume growth from the existing assets which are already stabilized and ramped up.

items.statement: MMA market development targeting full capacity utilization over next two years; geographic diversification into US and Europe progressing.
items.quote: Over the course of the next two years we are targeting to utilize that capacity and that's where I think we will remain focused.

items.statement: US tariff impact is mixed: positive for non-exempt products competing with China (e.g., MPD), neutral-to-positive for exempt products if India sourcing increases, negative for MMA due to added cost. Second/third order effects to play out ov
items.quote: At current level, based on our best judgm ent, we can say it's a mixed impact on AIL. Certain products are definitely seeing positive traction, whereas for certain products we are trying to adjust the pricing to ensure that the tariff impacts are absorbed by both sides in a fair

items.statement: Customer decision-making showed holding pattern due to tariff uncertainty but returning to regular business over last few weeks; tariff issues expected to settle in 2-4 months.
items.quote: Over the last few weeks, we have also started seeing people coming back, and sort of moving on with respect to regular business. In general, we are anticipating the tariff issues to settle down over the course of the next two to four months.

items.statement: Energy application volumes grew 21% QoQ; non-energy base business (Nitro Toluene, NCB, Ethylation) grew 14% QoQ; agrochemical inventory stabilized, dyes/pigments/polymer additives demand positive.
items.quote: Volumes for Energy applications grew 21% Q-o-Q driven by our strategy to diversify and widen the customer base and geographical spread. On the other hand, our base business has shown good volume recovery in chains such as Nitro Toluene, NCB, and Ethylation-based products.

items.statement: Renewable PPAs with Cleanmax and Prozeal on track; one contract to deliver within calendar year, second by end FY26 or early FY27, lowering operational costs.
items.quote: These agreements are on track, with one of the contracts to start delivering within this calendar year, and the second one is expected to begin by end FY26 or early FY27.

items.statement: Tax rate expected to remain in mid-single digits in FY26 due to high depreciation from ongoing capex cycle.
items.quote: We will continue to remain lower and subdued on the tax rate. I know this year we have been negative on the tax rate level, I expect it to be somewhere close to mid-single digit next year.

items.statement: Working capital days targeted at 70-80 days gross in FY26; trade payables may increase Rs 100-200 crore with volume growth.
items.quote: So it should be somewhere between 70 to 80 days on a gross basis. We will have to work out some numbers, but yes, it should be that way.

items.statement: ARPOB growth projected at inflation rate for mature hospitals; Indore may exceed inflation for one more year due to case mix optimization
items.quote: As I was saying that the projection for ARPOB growth should be inflation-linked. Thane and Pune, both are mature d hospitals. So besides inflation, there is no other lever for ARPOB growth. Indore may be slightly higher than inflation because for maybe one more year, it has a second lever that is of case mix optimization that is more tertiary work

items.statement: New Pune hospital 500 beds, capex ~INR500 crores excluding land; land on 10-year lease with purchase option after year 3
items.quote: So the new Pune hospital is supposed to be 500 beds in size. We think that the capex incurred for that project should be somewhere in the tune of INR500 crores excluding land.

items.statement: Dombivli hospital construction on track, commissioning expected Q1 FY27 with 250 beds in Phase 1
items.quote: The Dombivli Hospital construction is progressing as per plan with an expected commissioning within a year in Q1 of FY '27.

items.statement: Cash position INR600 crores (INR325 crores new debt + INR275 crores reserves) available for land purchase or strategic acquisition
items.quote: As you see on our balance sheet today, our cash position stands at about INR600 crores, comprising of INR325 crores from the new debt and INR275 crores from our existing cash reserves.

items.statement: Thane additional floor expected to improve EBITDA margins incrementally as fixed costs already covered
items.quote: Yes, ideally, if and when this floor does come up, we definitely think that it should contribute on a unit level a little more to the EBITDA margins because most of the fixed costs are taken care of and the added capacity in terms of manpower, power, etc., does not need as much fixed cost now.

items.statement: Indore added 78 beds commissioned Jan 2025; 11-bed ICU ready but will operationalize based on demand; Thane reconfigured: removed 22-bed economy ward, added 2 OTs, second MRI, second cath lab, expanded Daycare/chemo 14 to 22 beds, new OPD c
items.quote: We executed a substantial expansion project, adding 2 additional floors to the existing hospital building, resulting in 78 new beds. These beds were commissioned on 1st January 2025. Furthermore, we have constructed an 11-bed ICU, which is now ready for commissioning, but will be operationalized based on occupancy demand.

items.statement: No senior doctor attrition at Thane despite new competitor hospitals; doctor supply and population growth in Thane support demand for all providers
items.quote: Aashita, so yes, so far, not a single one of our senior doctors has moved out and stopped association with us. So we continue to report 0 attrition at the senior consultant level. Going forward also, I don't perceive that to be a major risk factor.

items.statement: Mira Road land acquired, at post-purchase regulatory stage (7/12 updation); architectural drawings to start shortly
items.quote: In Mira Road, the land has been acquired, and we are at the post-purchase regulatory stage of 7/12 updation, etc., and we will start working on the architectural drawings for that project shortly.

items.statement: Acquisition strategy unchanged: Western India focus, flagship hub model, greenfield preferred; will acquire only if quality and value justifiable; no target multiple
items.quote: Yes. So there is no change in thought process on any front. A, to begin with, Western India remains the focus. B, full service flagship hub model continues to remain the focus. C, greenfield continues to remain a preferred choice. D, on the acquisition and brownfield front, like we have always said, if a good opportunity at a good value does present itself, we are not averse to it, but we will ins

items.statement: No specific 3-year revenue guidance; Dombivli Phase 1 (250 beds) FY27, Pune Phase 1 (250 beds) couple years later; both hospitals 500 beds total
items.quote: I wouldn't want to get into financial specific guidance after 3 years. But on the occupancy front, I can give you some color to understand that next financial year, Dombivli should get inaugurated and that should add about 250 -odd beds to our capacity in P hase 1, which can be ramped up over the next couple of years as the capacity expands and then Pune a couple of years after that

items.statement: FY26 double-digit revenue growth and EBITDA margin maintained at FY25 level
items.quote: Yes, we believe that FY26 double-digit growth is possible as well as maintaining the margins.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin target 25%+ and double-digit sales growth despite gRevlimid cliff
items.quote: on our current modelling, we will continue to have, based on what we have guided, sales double-digit growth and then EBITDA & RoCE 25% and above at this point of time

items.statement: FY26 capex expected in similar range as FY25 (₹2,699 crores)
items.quote: We believe, at this point of time, it would be in the similar range for FY26 as well.

items.statement: Generic semaglutide launch targeted for calendar 2026 in markets where IP allows
items.quote: So we are gearing up to launch it during the calendar '26, in all the markets that the IP landscape will allow us to launch.

items.statement: Abatacept biosimilar Phase III ongoing, filing targeted end of calendar 2025
items.quote: We were planning to submit the product somewhere in the end of this calendar year, end of '25, to be ready to launch the intravenous (IV), immediately after patent expiration.

items.statement: NRT business full-year FY26 revenue run rate ~₹2,400 crores (double Q4 run rate)
items.quote: Yes. Certainly, give or take, that would be the range.

items.statement: NRT business EBITDA margin zone of 25%
items.quote: So, for this business, earlier we have also spoken, our EBITDA margin is in zone of 25%.

items.statement: India business high double-digit growth expected in FY26 driven by new products and innovation
items.quote: So overall, between new products, innovation, dealing with those big brands that do not do well, we believe, that we will have a high double-digit growth in India next year.

items.statement: US price erosion very low single-digit in FY25, most products exhausted erosion potential
items.quote: the price erosion that was in the US was relatively low, primarily, as most of the products, I believe, exhausted the potential of the price erosion. So , it's normally when there is no price erosion in United States, it's not always a goo d sign. But, in our case, it was a very low single -digit price erosion within the fiscal

items.statement: No US manufacturing footprint; will not build specifically for tariffs but open to right asset
items.quote: As a company, we would love to have a footprint in the United States. It just has to be the right asset. We are always looking for an asset, but we are not going to do, at this stage, specific activities to build footprint.

items.statement: Committed to no supply disruption in US regardless of tariff scenario
items.quote: What I want to emphasize is that under any scenario, we will not create shortage of suppl y or supply disruption to the US market

items.statement: gRevlimid sales likely to stop few months before January 2026 cliff to avoid shelf stock adjustments
items.quote: So, likely that we will stop few months before that.

items.statement: Canada semaglutide market ~$1.8B (~10M pens) with high growth potential
items.quote: The market is around $1.8 billion, which suggests that it's around, give or take, 10 million pens.

items.statement: Semaglutide synthetic route for injectables, semi-synthetic for oral; preparing for both limited and high competition scenarios
items.quote: We believe that the synthetic route can be approved for the injectable, for the pens. And the semi-synthetic route is going to be used for the oral product.

items.statement: R&D spend to remain ~8.5% of sales; SG&A ~28% of sales in FY26
items.quote: Yes, yes, R&D and SG&A will be in the similar zone. I think the SG&A now is like somewhere 28% of the sales, R&D is 8.5% would be in the similar zone.

items.statement: Total project capex for 6.2 mt expansion including Kundanganj Line-III is Rs 4,759 crore
items.quote: Rs.4,759 crores is the number including Kundanganj Line-III.

items.statement: FY26 volume growth expected in line with industry at 6-8%
items.quote: This year industry is expected to grow maybe between 6% and 8%. We should be in line with industry if not better.

items.statement: FY26 net debt expected around Rs 3,000 crore with debt-to-EBITDA below 2x
items.quote: As of now, we expect it to be in the vicinity of Rs. 3,000 crores. But in terms of net debt-to-EBITDA, it definitely should be below two for this financial year.

items.statement: Debt-to-EBITDA not expected to exceed 2x over next two years
items.quote: The next two years, I do not see my debt-to-EBITDA exceeding much beyond two.

items.statement: Kundanganj Line-III (1.4 mt) commissioning in Q2 FY26; Maihar Line-II, Gaya Phase-I, Prayagraj grinding by CY27
items.quote: By calendar year '27 we are expecting Ma ihar Line-II, Phase-I of Gaya, Prayagraj and of course Kundanganj Line-III is expected in the second quarter of this financial year

items.statement: Green power share to rise from ~25% to 36-37% in next two years
items.quote: So going forward you can see that our green power is going to increase in next two years time to around 36 %, 37%.

items.statement: Power and fuel cost on downward trend around Rs 1,000/ton; gradual decline expected
items.quote: So power and fuel cost combined together you can see the trend already. It is in a downward tren d of Rs.1,000 per

items.statement: Q4 realization up ~7% QoQ driven by price hikes in North and East regions
items.quote: If you look at in the Quarter 4 across the country mostly the price in the North region gone up and the east also gone up

items.statement: Q1 FY26 realization remains same as Q4 FY25 average
items.quote: Ongoing almost remains same. There is no much variation.

items.statement: No veracity to reports of mining ban near Chittorgarh Fort; case progressing per Supreme Court process
items.quote: We have no such information on this. That statement was made, but we have not found any veracity and we will be surprised if such position is taken

items.statement: No immediate plans to sell non-strategic equity investments; internal accruals sufficient for capex
items.quote: Those are not strategic investment for us, but currently we do not have any plans, we feel that we have got enough internal accruals to cater to CAPEX requirement

items.statement: Bikram coal mine meaningful production from FY27; Marki Barka from FY28
items.quote: In terms of coal mines, Bikram coal mine, in Q3 of this year we are expecting to start that coal mine, but meaningful production will start from next financial year only. As regards the other coal mine, which is Marki Barka, that we expect to start only in FY28.

items.statement: RMC business strategy being finalized; clearer picture by next quarter
items.quote: We are still firming up our strategy. We have made a beginning in UP. We are finalizing our strategy. Hopefully by next quarter we should be able to give you a clearer picture on this.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin was 23.5% in Q4 FY25 and expected to increase 3-4% as prices move toward reference price of INR135/mm
items.quote: In the last quarter, we earned 23.5%, where the price was INR127.6 and we are increasing the price to the level of reference price, which is INR135 or so. So obviously, we are going to have some incremental EBITDA coming in, in the financial year. So, somebody had asked in the call earlier, whether 3% to 4% increase can be expected. So , we said yes.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA per quarter expected to rise to INR90+ crores from INR77 crores in Q4 FY25
items.quote: No, we will be having significant EBITDA positive because the EBITDA from Indian operations has been about, say, INR77 crores in the quarter 4, which is expected to rise to at least INR90-plus crores.

items.statement: Expansion capacity revised upward from 500 TPD to 600 TPD, project cost to be finalized next month, commissioning targeted Q3 FY27
items.quote: So the answer to your question is that we had taken a visit to China to understand the availability of latest glass manufacturing equipment. And we -- it is coming around that a furnace instead of being 250 tons, it is likely to be 300 tons. So instead of 500 tons, it looks like 600 tons.

items.statement: Board approved enabling resolution to raise up to INR500 crores via equity or convertible instruments for future opportunities
items.quote: The Board has also approved further raising of funds through the issuance of instruments of security, including equity shares or any other security convertible into equity shares, including warrants in one or more tranches for an amount not exceeding INR500 crores.

items.statement: Domestic demand robust with module manufacturing capacity at 90+ GW expected to reach 150 GW by March 2027, installations expected at 40-45 GW annually
items.quote: We expect the installations to rise to 40 to 45 gigawatts annually going forward.

items.statement: Blended margins for roll-up next year can be 300-400 bps higher than Q4 FY25
items.quote: Yes, we can assume that safely.

items.statement: Domestic selling prices now close to reference prices of INR135-140 per mm per sq meter, up from INR127.6 in Q4 FY25
items.value: INR135-140 per mm per sq meter
items.quote: The company's domestic selling prices are now close to the level of the reference prices, landed value at port of discharge of around INR135 to INR140 per millimeter per square meter.

items.statement: Realization moving toward reference price; recent transactions at or near INR135/mm, stock clearance completed in December
items.quote: So on the marginal basis, is it fair to say recent transaction are happening at 135 price? Ashok Jain: Or less, yes. And the stock is not a problem. In December itself, we had cleared all the

items.statement: Solar glass demand expected north of 50 GW vs domestic supply of 30 GW after new 15 GW capacity additions, leaving large import substitution opportunity
items.quote: And as we foresee the demand to grow to about 40 gigawatts to 45 gigawatts going forward in terms of installations, the module or the glass demand will be north of 50 gigawatts. So, there is a huge surge in demand, which is expected and new capacities of about 15 gigawatts are coming in India from glass perspective. So even if that is fully utilized, we will still have only 30 gigawatt supply as a

items.statement: Demand mix shifting to 2+2mm bifacial glass (60-70% of demand) from 3.2mm, increasing glass consumption per module by ~25%
