items.quote: Now almost 60%, 70% of the demand is converted to 2 plus 2. And when you say the demand, it is now split in the mix right now by 2:1 or like that. But when you do it 2 plus 2, then the gigawatt will be slightly lower. Because you consume almost 25 kg glass in 1 module in bifacial, 2 plus 2 as against 20.5 kg in a 3.2 module.

items.statement: German subsidiary monthly burn rate ~INR9 crores (EUR 900k); cold end restart may cut EBITDA losses by 50% but fixed costs remain
items.quote: So the loss is about, say, EUR 900,000 per month as of now, so almost INR8.5 crores to INR9 crores.

items.statement: German furnace restart depends on government incentives; cold end operations to resume by importing annealed glass in near future
items.quote: We shall observe the developments over the next weeks and take further steps relating to the possibility of resumption of glass production. In the meantime, we are evaluating resuming production in the cold end by importing annealed glass and processing it at the GMB plant in the near future.

items.statement: Preferential issue raised INR204.42 crores (INR100 cr from promoters, INR104.42 cr from warrants); INR185 cr used to repay GMB loan, balance for expansion
items.quote: A total sum of INR204.42 crores was received towards the issue, comprising INR100 crores from promoters against shares and INR104.42 crores towards 25% amount against warrants. INR185 crores from this amount has been utilized to repay the loan liability of our step-down subsidiary, GMB.

items.statement: Definitive anti-dumping duty imposed on solar glass from China and Vietnam for 5 years till Dec 2029, supporting domestic supply chain
items.quote: I'm happy to announce that the Ministry of Finance has on Friday, 9th May announced a definitive antidumping duty on all imports of solar glass originating in or exported from China and Vietnam, which shall remain valid till 3rd December 2029 for a period of 5 years from the date of issue of the preliminary duty notification.

items.statement: Captive 16.5 MW solar-wind hybrid plant expected to commission in Q2 FY26, raising renewable energy share to 65-70% of electricity demand
items.quote: We shall also see the benefits of an additional 16.5 megawatt solar plus wind hybrid power plant, which is expected to be commissioned during second quarter financial year '26. This will not only save costs for us, but will also enable us to meet a significantly higher portion, which is 65% to 70% of our demand for electricity from captive sources of renewable energy.

items.statement: Domestic welding volumes were flat for FY25; export volumes grew; overall revenue growth ~5% with declining steel prices
items.quote: So the domestic market has been at the end of the year fairly flat on that account. The export market has obviously had a little volume growth.

items.statement: International business grew >25% in FY25; USA and Australia remain big focus for coming years
items.quote: The international business continued to have robust growth at more than 25%.

items.statement: Services (FPED) segment expected to breakeven by H1 FY26 after closing ONGC Uran project; targeting Rs. 50-60 cr of smaller projects to breakeven
items.quote: We expect by H1 that this will be completely behind us and we would have closed down and commissioned it directly and all of that. We do not feel that there are any significantly large savings significant on the losses front left. It will be fairly flattish as we go through the next 6 months in terms of closing this out on a breakeven kind of level.

items.statement: FPED order book built to 70-80% of Rs. 50-60 cr breakeven target
items.quote: And we started building up our order book to anywhere around 70%, 80% of that level already.

items.statement: FY26 capex expected within 15-20% of FY25's Rs. 40 cr (i.e., ~Rs. 32-48 cr) for new consumable lines and plant upgrades
items.quote: I think we will be within the region of that up down minus 15%, 20% as far as it goes. It should be about 15%-20% up down from that because there are still upgradations that we have to do looking at the long term plans, looking at the new lines we want to add and stuff like that.

items.statement: Investing in flux-cored wire, stainless/nickel consumables, EV/solar welders, and high-spec welding equipment to enrich product basket
items.quote: We remain focused on improving our product mix, a basket with richer products. And that is where high-end welding consumables, whether they are related to nickels and other stainless steels and stuff like that are coming into play, is what we are adding into our basket going forward.

items.statement: Bare minimum operating margin target is 10%; expects incremental bottom-line benefit as topline grows
items.quote: It's a bare minimum as far as I am concerned is 10%. It has to be little bit better than that and there will be no how to make it better than that. It's a question of executing.

items.statement: New management team passing through steel price changes faster; not worried about large steel price movements
items.quote: I think we are just going to be a lot more brutal about passing things on a lot faster and having the strength to do that and I think that is exactly where the management changes are coming and I am seeing that that they are doing it effectively.

items.statement: ONGC Uran project 80% complete on ground, 70% revenue recognized; remaining execution over next 3-4 months; project margins below original expectations
items.quote: As far as UNGC order goes, I think on the ground, I would say we are close to about 80% of the project being done. As far as revenue goes, about 70% revenue down, 80% on the ground, 80%-85% going through this period of quick commissioning over the next 3-4 months.

items.statement: Will not take large EPC projects; future FPED orders limited to ~Rs. 15-20 cr with limited scope exposure
items.quote: We will not take on such large projects at all. We will only take on projects where the design and scope is within a limited understanding of us. Most of our order book will be very limited to up to about Rs. 15, Rs. 20 crores.

items.statement: Expects robust growth from railways, thermal, defence, general infra, heavy engineering; growth to be tempered post-COVID
items.quote: We do believe sectors such as railways, thermal, defense, general infra, heavy engineering to remain on a fairly robust growth path going forward from here. So I don't think you can expect any irrational type of growth at all.

items.statement: Internal mandate to double revenue over next 4 years by outperforming market growth
items.quote: We have got a mandate internally that we would like to be able to double our revenue over the next 4 years. And that means outperforming the market growth rate, of course.

items.statement: International exports grew ~20-25% in FY25 on Rs. 122 cr base; FY26 growth expected but more muted
items.quote: I can just tell you without telling you too much that like I said about 20%-25% growth on last year's numbers and we are looking at growth going forward. A little more muted and that may not be on the 20%-25%, maybe little more muted in that but in that time, it is for sure.

items.statement: M&R (ex-Fontech) products moved to welding products division; ~15-20% of Fontech portfolio transferred; like-to-like M&R revenue down 5-8% in last 6 months
items.quote: On the products that encompass M&R that are in the M&R group 1:1, on that front we would have seen in the last 6 months anywhere between a 5% to 8% drop on certain restructurings that we are going on.

items.statement: 3D printing business not feasible for long-term investment; dynamics changed too much
items.quote: I don't think it's feasible to invest long term in that business. And right now, I am not going to say anything more than that right now. I am just going to keep that with me. I don't think it's feasible. We have been through a lot of it. We figured a lot of it out. I think the dynamics changed too much around us. I don't think it's a long term sustainable investment from the Ador Group.

items.statement: FY25 capex of ~Rs. 40 cr spent primarily on new consumable lines (flux-cored, import substitution) at Silvassa, Raipur, Bangalore plants; operational from Q4
items.quote: Rs. 40 crores of CAPEX primarily went in new consumables additions or new lines to be done like I said stabilizing a little bit of all that. I think most of it was on that account. Most of it is on the consumable lines plants. Most of it is in plants in Silvassa, in Raipur. We have a little bit going forward Bangalore this year, has many plants.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin expanded by over 500 bps to 20.05% in FY25 driven by new models, value engineering, supply chain streamlining, and operating leverage.
items.quote: There has been decent expansion in EBITDA margin by more than 500 bps at a consol level and more than 400 bps at a standalone level. There has also been Y-o-Y gross margin expansion on account of, as guided earlier launch of 17 new models as well as value engineering and substantially streamline the supply chain in addition to operating leverage and economies of scale.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin improved by over 400 bps to 24.25% in FY25.
items.quote: And on standalone basis, EBITDA margin stands at 24.25%, that is more than 400 bps improvement.

items.statement: Channel inventory is slightly higher than last year at the same time, but season still has 7-11 weeks remaining in key regions.
items.quote: This inventory that is there in the channel at this moment is slightly higher than what we had at the same time in the last year.

items.statement: Summer 2025 started with robust demand in South India, but post-March weather turned mild and erratic, muting performance so far.
items.quote: However, post 31st March, as all summer -related industries are witnessing, and we are no exception, we are facing mild and erratic weather. However, due to several initiatives, of course, vis -a-vis previous year, it is muted performance so far.

items.statement: Adjacent categories (tower fans, kitchen cooling fans, water heaters) and LSV together now contribute decent double-digit percentage of standalone revenue, up from low single digits.
items.quote: Currently, in the interest of competition, we do have the numbers. But what I can broadly say adjacent category, LSV put together on a stand-alone basis itself, which was earlier in a small single-digit percentage is now decent double-digit percentage.

items.statement: Impairment of ₹50 crores taken on equity investment in Climate Technologies Australia per auditor recommendation; non-cash, below-the-line item.
items.quote: Our total equity investment as well as loan given to Climate Technologies Australia is substantial, out of which small part as recommended by auditors as per Ind-AS, as well as accounting standard amounting to about ₹50 crores to take as an impairment.

items.statement: Pathways write-off of close to ₹50 crores during the year; legal progress made with Power of Attorneys and equitable mortgage on 13 properties in Delhi/NCR.
items.quote: Giving further update on Pathways, on which during the year, we have taken total write -off of close to ₹50 crores, out of which very small amount of ₹49 lakhs has been recovered so far.

items.statement: Consolidated capital employed decreased to ₹248 crores (monthly average) from over ₹300 crores despite higher revenue, driving ROCE to 101%.
items.quote: Coming to capital allocation at a consol level, total capital employed in the business based on monthly average capital deployed is ₹248 crores versus previous year in excess of ₹300 crores. So capital deployed is lower despite increase in top line and bottom line, translating into ROCE in core business 101%.

items.statement: Board recommended final dividend of ₹8 per share (400% of face value); total FY25 payout ₹178 crores, 84% of consolidated profit vs guidance of at least 60%.
items.quote: The Board has recommended final dividend of ₹8, a face value of ₹2 that is 400%. In all, this amounts to total payout , during FY '25, ₹178 crores, which is 84% of the consolidated profit vis-a-vis our stated guidance of at least 60 % payout.

items.statement: IMPCO Mexico to acquire technology transfer and 9 IPRs from GSK China for ~₹43 crores; net ~₹40 crores to be used for loan repayment to Symphony.
items.quote: IMPCO Mexico is going to buy technology transfer as well as 9 IPRs from GSK China, which were specifically developed for IMPCO Mexico. And in new scenario, it has been found worthwhile to sell to IMPCO Mexico. The transaction value is about ₹43 crores.

items.statement: GSK China loans to Symphony expected to be fully repaid by end of FY26 from profitability and IPR sale proceeds.
items.quote: And hence, net of expenses close to ₹40 crores, which GSK will receive from IMPCO will be utilized towards repayment of loan to Symphony . And in addition to that, we expect that from profitability and cash accruals of GSK China by end of FY '26 or around that, the loans to Symphony should be completely paid off.

items.statement: IMPCO Mexico and Climate Technologies Australia put on block on April 12; investment banker appointed with milestones; process just begun.
items.quote: On 12th of April, we decided and finalized to put IMPCO Mexico and Climate Technologies, Australia on block. So it's less than a month since we have decided. We have appointed the investment banker with a specific milestone. So, process has just begun.

items.statement: US market inquiries surged from top retailers due to China tariffs; 8-week lead time prevents full supply this season but shipping some quantity.
items.quote: We already have some serious inquiries from the large U.S. buyers, including the top retailers. They wanted us to supply a sizable quantity in this season, which would be starting pretty soon. Now unfortunately, because of the 8 weeks of lead time and the production time that is required, we won't be able to meet that requirement, but we are definitely shipping some quantity this year.

items.statement: No forward-looking numbers provided for top line, margins, or profitability per IR policy; outlook shared only as qualitative factors.
items.quote: Again, as per our IR policy, we are not giving or sharing any forward -looking numbers, whether for the quarter or for the year, whether in terms of the top line, profitability margin or profitability. So our outlook will be more about qualitative factors.

items.statement: Gross margin expanded 73 bps to 49.75% on standalone basis due to new models, value engineering, and supply chain improvements.
items.quote: Gross profit margin % stands at 49.75%, up by 73 bps, and absolute amount-wise, it is up by 51% at ₹588 crores.

items.statement: Exports grew to ₹117 crores (10% of standalone revenue); strong growth in Middle East, Africa, Europe; Sri Lanka recovered; Egypt/Sudan challenged by remittance issues.
items.quote: So domestic turnover is ₹1,065 crores and the export is ₹117 crores. Nrupesh Shah: So broadly, you can say that, 90% is domestic and 10% is export

items.statement: FY26 capex expected at Rs 950-1,000 crore, bulk for Zone-4 completion
items.quote: Based on our current plan, we expect the capex in FY26 to be about 950-1000 crs.

items.statement: Zone-4 capex to complete in FY26; multipurpose and calcium chloride plants to start Q3 FY26
items.quote: Zone-4 staggered commissioning will happen throughout let's say Q3, Q4 of this financial. Especially the multipurpose plant, the calcium chloride plant is expected to start up in Q3.

items.statement: No specific FY26 revenue/EBITDA guidance; reaffirmed three-year EBITDA target of Rs 1,800-2,200 crore by FY28
items.quote: We have set out a strategy for the three years and I think the only thing I can confirm is we remain on track to deliver that three-year numbers.

items.statement: Cost optimization implementation in FY26; full EBITDA accrual from hybrid power projects expected from FY27
items.quote: From an implementation point of view, bulk of it w ill be done in FY ‘26. From an EBITDA accrual of that saving initiative poin t of view, it will go into, I think the full approvals will happen into next sort of, not in this financial year but the next financially, especially the hybrid projects which are expected to contribute also significant value. They will start accruing to the bottom line f

items.statement: Volume growth expected to continue in FY26 driven by existing asset utilization; no significant volume from new Zone-4 assets until FY27
items.quote: This year we are pushing for volume growth from the existing assets which are already stabilized and ramped up.

items.statement: US tariff impact mixed: positive for non-exempt products competing with China (e.g., MPD), neutral-to-positive for exempt products if India sourcing increases, negative for MMA due to added cost
items.quote: At current level, based on our best judgm ent, we can say it's a mixed impact on AIL. Certain products are definitely seeing positive traction, whereas for certain products we are trying to adjust the pricing to ensure that the tariff impacts are absorbed by both sides in a fair

items.statement: Net debt peaked at ~Rs 3,500 crore; expected to decline by Rs 200-300 crore in FY26 on lower capex and working capital release
items.quote: Directionally, I guess, we would have peaked out. We expect the number to be lower. We are expecting some unlocking of cash flow from working capital as well. So, plus the CAPEX intensity is also going down. So directionally, I expect the number to be lower by maybe Rs. 200-300 crore kind of range.

items.statement: Renewable PPAs with Cleanmax and Prozeal on track; one to start in CY2025, second by end FY26 or early FY27
items.quote: These agreements are on track, with one of the contracts to start delivering within this calendar year, and the second one is expected to begin by end FY26 or early FY27.

items.statement: Maintenance capex Rs 150-200 crore in FY26; remainder for new Zone-4 initiatives
items.quote: I guess the maintenance CAPEX and CAPEX related to some of the initiatives which are there on the existing product should be in the range of Rs. 150 crore to Rs. 200 crore or so. Beyond that, everything will be for the new initiatives at Zone-4 is going to be a bulk of that.

items.statement: Working capital days targeted at 70-80 days gross in FY26; trade payables may rise Rs 100-200 crore with volume growth
items.quote: So it should be somewhere between 70 to 80 days on a gross basis. We will have to work out some numbers, but yes, it should be that way.

items.statement: Tax rate expected at mid-single digits in FY26 due to high depreciation from capex cycle
items.quote: We will continue to remain lower and subdued on the tax rate. I know this year we have been negative on the tax rate level, I expect it to be somewhere close to mid-single digit next year.

items.statement: Long-term contracts performing as agreed: nitric acid 20-year purchase agreement on track, polymer application with global major running well, advanced specialty polymer intermediate ramping up
items.quote: I think the 20-year purchase agreements that we have for nitric acid continues to perform exactly as per contract, no issues on that front. The other project that we have, which is where sort of our profitability is ensured, right, it's the polymer application with a global major, I think that continues to run very well, no changes on that front and there is another contract which we had with a US

items.statement: FY26 volume growth guidance of 20% to 25%
items.quote: Apollo Pipes has laid down solid foundation for 20% to 25% volume growth for FY '26.

items.statement: Target 25% ROCE in next 2 years
items.quote: However, we are confident of achieving 25% ROCE in next 2 years as we increase our sales volume at 25% CAGR with margin improvement.

items.statement: FY25 capex INR166 crores; residual capex INR100 crores to reach 260,000 tons capacity by FY26 end
items.quote: In FY '25, we incurred a capex of INR166 crores after INR250 crores in the previous year. Our capacity has increased to 2,32,000 tons, which shall further increase to 2,60,000 tons by the year-end FY '26. The residual capex would be INR100 crores to achieve this capacity.

items.statement: Equity infusion of INR110 crores from Omani fund; INR28 crores received in April, balance over next 17 months
items.quote: On top of it, we will have equity infusion of INR110 crores from an Omani's fund against which INR28 crores already credited in April with balance coming in the next 17 months.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin target 10% to 12% in next 2-3 years from current 8.5%
items.quote: And the margins, which right now are at 8.5%, they will inch up to around 10% to 12%, right, in the next 2 to 3 years.

items.statement: Kisan EBITDA margin expected 5% in FY26, 8% to 9% in 2-3 years
items.quote: We believe that in FY '26, these margins could inch up to around 5%. And in FY '27, there will be further improvement of 200, 250 bps. So as we see that in next 2, 3 years, the company has a capability to generate 8% to 9% EBITDA margins easily.

items.statement: Three new revenue drivers: oPVC, Window Profile, Varanasi plant
items.quote: I'm pleased to tell you, that we have 3 additional revenue drivers, which are oPVC product segment, Window Profile product segment and Varanasi plant.

items.statement: JJM/HDPE segment weak; no substantial recovery factored in FY26 plan
items.quote: And for FY '26, we have not factored in any substantial volume recovery in HDPE pipes for JJM.

items.statement: Agri pipe demand showing double-digit growth momentum continuing in Q1 FY26
items.quote: So agri has done well so far, right? Last year, agri volume had double-digit growth for us. So far in Q1, we are seeing the same momentum.

items.statement: Window Profile product launch scheduled for June 2025
items.quote: So Udit, the product launch is lined up for June of 2025, right, which is next month.

items.statement: oPVC TAM estimated at INR7,000-8,000 crores annually; expect 5% revenue contribution in 2-3 years
items.quote: So the market analysis, what we had done before investing into oPVC segment, we believe that INR7,000 crores, INR8,000 crores worth of annual sales can be generated through replacement of ductile iron pipes with oPVC, right?

items.statement: Window Profile capex ~INR60 crores; 80-85% already spent
items.quote: So, window project, the capex is expected to be somewhere between around INR60 crores. And we have already done almost 80%, 85% of the expenditure.

items.statement: H1 FY26 volume ~40-45% of annual; H2 ~55-60%
items.quote: Our trajectory, like how it has been in earlier years, it should be like 40%, 45% in H1 and 55% to 60% in H2, right?

items.statement: PVC industry declined ~5% in FY25 due to real estate/infra slowdown and resin price volatility
items.quote: We believe that the overall PVC piping industry would have declined by about 5% in FY '25.

items.statement: Net cash INR46 crores at consolidated level; working capital cycle 36 days; operating cash flow to EBITDA 65%
items.quote: At a consolidated level, we have net cash of INR46 crores despite heavy capex spends. Our working capital cycle remained prudent at 36 days, which resulted in operating cash flow to EBITDA of 65%.

items.statement: Apollo Pipes EBITDA spread target increase of at least INR1,000 per ton vs FY25
items.quote: EBITDA spreads like for Apollo Pipes should be INR1,000 per ton at least higher than what it was in FY '25.

items.statement: Biocon Biologics expects to launch 5 new biosimilars in the next 12 to 18 months including Stelara, Bevacizumab, Aspart, Aflibercept, and Denosumab.
items.quote: The 2 products that we just talked about even in the opening remarks, actually, Kiran did cover all of them. We've launched Stelara biosimilar, which is one of them. The other one is we've got approval for bevaci zumab. We talked about Aspart just to Amey's question. So that's the third one. We discussed the Aflibercept settlement and the launch in July. We launched that in Canada. We have a clear

items.statement: Biocon Biologics expects to launch one biosimilar product per year from FY25 to FY30.
items.quote: Nitin, in the past, we've said that -- I mean, apart from the bunching up that has happened in the current time period because of whatever reasons, we've said that from '25 to '30, we saw ourselves launching a product a year, which is what you're seeing us do now.

items.statement: Biocon Biologics plans to spend about USD 100 million over the next couple of years, primarily to enhance capacities in Malaysia.
items.quote: On the Capex side, like what you said, Surya, we expect to spend about USD 100 million over the next couple of years. After which, it's expected to get moderated down. Large part of this money will go to enhance the capacities in Malaysia, which, for us, is very rewarding given the global demand that we are seeing for the product.

items.statement: Generics business plans to spend another USD 50 million next year, after which major capex programs end and only maintenance capex remains from FY27.
items.quote: For Generics, again, we'll be looking at another USD 50 million next year. And I think with that majority of our ongoing Capex programs come to an end and it will be only small bit of maintenance Capex from FY '27 onwards.

items.statement: Biocon Biologics has over 70% market access with U.S. payers for Yesintek (Ustekinumab) covering over 100 million lives.
items.quote: We have over 70% market access with the payers in the U.S. at the beginning of the start. With that comes the opportunity for us to continue to pull the product through in the U.S. We are very bullish on our market share. We haven't really been able to state that directly yet as we're starting to work with physicians and pulling it through. But we have over 100 million lives that are covered in th

items.statement: Biocon Biologics expects incremental gross margin and EBITDA contribution from new launches to be higher than existing business, providing operating leverage.
items.quote: I think as the launches do come in, the incremental gross margin on those launches is going to be higher than the existing business. So some kind of operating leverage as well as gross margin improvement is expected. We're not giving the guidance, but directionally, you are right.

items.statement: Pricing for Yesintek (Ustekinumab) in the U.S. remains stable with no significant net selling price compression expected.
items.quote: The pricing situation remains stable. We're certainly in a good position. As you know, in the United States, it is somewhat the economics. But clearly, the customers have seen the s cience behind this. Also, we built tremendous relationships with the payers and also the health care providers. So the pricing remains stable at this point as we go through the rest of the year. We don't see much chang

items.statement: Biocon Biologics is witnessing a surge in global demand for insulins and is well-positioned with global scale manufacturing capacities.
items.quote: We are witnessing a surge in global demand for our insulins. Given our global scale manufacturing capacities, we are well placed to capitalize on this large opportunity.

items.statement: Biocon Biologics has doubled drug product manufacturing capacity in Malaysia with a new facility brought online, and is expanding drug substance capacity twofold.
items.quote: We've just brought online another drug product facility in Malaysia, which increases our capacity of manufacturing drug product twofold. So it's a doubling of capacity that we have just completed, and we will go through the regulatory approval process to bring that product to patients. We are also in the midst of the capacity expansion, which will again twofold increase our capacity in Malaysia fo

items.statement: Board has constituted a committee to evaluate strategic options including a possible merger of Biocon Limited and Biocon Biologics due to IPO market volatility.
items.quote: Given the market volatility that we are seeing on the IPO front, I think the Board was of the opinion that we should look at other strategic options, which also includes evaluating a merger. So at this point in time, the Board has constituted a committee. We will evaluate all strategic options and then get back to you in a few months with what the Board recommend -- I mean what the committee recom

items.statement: Biocon Limited intends to raise INR 4,500 crores via QIP and private placement; first tranche expected to complete by mid-June to meet financial obligations from structured debt put options.
items.quote: I think what we have announced is that we intend to raise INR 4,500 crores through a combination of QIP and private placement, and we have sent out a shareholders' notice last week towards the same. We have started discussing with our bankers and investors and lawyers about the whole process. We expect to complete the first tranche, which we will decide the quantum of that first tranche in a few w

items.statement: Generic Liraglutide launch in Europe planned for Q1 and Q2 FY26; U.S. target action date in second half of calendar year 2025.

items.quote: the discretionary spend in high-tech space continues to be, I would say, tepid for a simple reason that on one hand, t here is a significant amount of spend happening in building the infrastructure and data pipelines, etc., for their AI -related initiatives. items.statement: GCC offerings targeting mid-market tech companies ($500M-$5B) for innovation/R&D-led setups of a few hundred people, not large-scale back-office

items.statement: Investing in go-to-market, sales leadership, AI/cloud capabilities, and delivery capacity; SG&A temporarily lower due to AR provision true-up but sales hiring continues
items.quote: We are obviously investing in go-to-market. We are investing in sales team. We are also investing in building capacity and capability, deeper capability around AI and cloud.

items.statement: April-May seeing decision-making brakes release as companies internalize tariff impacts and resume necessary business spending
items.quote: Once you realize that, okay, this is how it is happening, and this is what is the impact on us and this is how we are going to deal with it. Once all that happens, then you start releasing the brakes and start doing what is necessary for your business.

items.quote: If decision making gets delayed, it will delay the realization of revenues for us. And hence it can create a delay in finally that ramp up that earlier Nikhil was asking.

items.quote: Well, this is 50 net addition, despite the reduction in some of the revenues as you've seen. So, if you look at it that way, our gross addition has actually been quite healthy. In fact, one of the highest in preceding last seven or eight quarters.

items.quote: We have been selected as one of the key strategic partners to develop those connectors. items.statement: Interim dividend of INR 6 per share declared for FY25

items.statement: Europe revenue growing at same pace as US; revenue mix across geographies expected to remain stable with US-India corridor as primary channel

items.quote: Most of the product engineering business is discretionary spent. It is a project based, project to project type of business. And hence, to say that there is a significant portion of annuity in there is not right.

items.quote: Today we actually work with over 10 different private equities focused on the mid-market segment. And we are continuing to develop our book of business with private equities. On the larger ISVs or enterprise ISV front, we've seen some success.

items.statement: FY26 guidance: ~15% top-line growth, ~25% EBITDA growth, ~50-65% PBT growth
items.quote: Going forward, we look forward to a top line growth of about 15%, EBITDA growth of about 25% and PBT growth of about 65% for the next year.

items.statement: Confirmed FY26 guidance of 15% sales growth, 25% EBITDA growth, 50-65% PBT growth
items.quote: So yeah, we are we are hoping to have a 15% top line growth, 25% EBITDA growth and about a 50 to 65% PBT.

items.quote: The general demand scenario in the pigment business is not very robust. It's improved a bit, but again now with the uncertainties and the tariffs and all of course there may be some inflationary impacts and hence there could be slightly tepid demand going forward as well.

items.quote: capacity utilization on the AZOs was about 64% for last year for the yellows and red put together and we are hoping to improve that to about 85 percent, 80 to 85% this year

items.quote: See for the next year as I indicated as of now we believe H2, we should be able to deliver EBITDA margin between 16% and 17%.

items.quote: So, this margin should grow 2% to 3% year on year. So, if you are looking for a three-year perspective, definitely the margin may inch towards 27-30% depending upon how the license works and how the Purple Fabric comes.

items.statement: Capex investment around $20 million (Rs.160-170 Cr) for FY26, similar to last year
items.quote: Capex investment on capitalisation will be around same as last year, we aimed for 140. This year should see the same figure, 20 million dollars. Therefore, 20 million dollars will be my Capex investment, while Rs.160-170 Cr will be my Capex investment on the product side, which will be capitalised.

items.statement: Purple Fabric currently 10-15% of funnel, growing; most deals include Purple Fabric component
items.quote: As of now, the funnel has a 10 to 15% component from Purple Fabric. More components are getting built up, so that's how you can look at it.

items.statement: Strong demand for AI-driven transformation deals combining eMACH.ai and Purple Fabric across insurance, lending, payments, trade finance
items.quote: There's a big trend on AI, plus eMACH.ai. So, the complete deals are there eMACH.ai deals and the AI deals.

items.statement: Not accepting outcome-based revenue models; will consider later
items.quote: We are not accepting this. We don't want to take that risk right now. We will do it later.

items.statement: Central1 acquisition profitable in first month (March), high single-digit profit margin, value-accretive
items.quote: Even though we started operating Central1 on the 1st of March, we only had one month of revenue, and it was profitable. It's not a very high profitability, but it's not a loss either. There was a profitable high single-digit profit in the new business we acquired.

items.statement: Purple Fabric target Rs.1,000 Cr business in next three years; Rs.5,000 Cr aspirational
items.quote: We are quite sure of Rs.1,000 Cr. We are now in the last 4-5 months, we built up the entire use cases or business cases to make it Rs.1,000 Cr business in for next three years for Purple Fabric.

items.statement: Core cost base stabilised at Rs.500 Cr/quarter; with Central1 Rs.550 Cr; overall Rs.560-570 Cr including AI investments
items.quote: our core business has stabilised at ₹ 500 Cr, with an additional ₹ 50 Cr for Central1, making it ₹ 550 Cr. With some extra costs, the overall structure could be ₹ 560–570 Cr

items.statement: Plan to add 25-30 stores annually with focus on Uttar Pradesh expansion
items.quote: We plan to add 25-30 stores annually with a sharp focus on expanding our presence in Uttar Pradesh, where we see significant potential.

items.statement: Store addition guidance may increase to 30-35 stores, update expected after another quarter
items.quote: Yes, it can go upward, which we will keep you updated after another quarter or so.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected to be maintained between 8% and 10%
items.quote: However, these stores were started in this quarter itself. So it has come down, but still we will maintain that our EBITDA margin will be something between 8% and 10%.

items.statement: SSSG expected to remain in double digits over next 3-4 years
items.quote: I think our SSSG will be in double digits. This is all I can say, Vijay, very firmly that SSSG will be in double digits because what we have seen in past and what we are in fact, what is happening right now is we are having high double digit SSSG.

items.statement: Average store size increased to 4,500 sq ft from 4,000 sq ft, new stores at 5,500 sq ft driving higher capex and working capital
items.quote: So in fact what you said that the biggest contributor is that we are opening larger format stores. So stores have now, average store size has become 4500, which was 4000 previously.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 demand slow in April due to unseasonal rains but growth in single digits; bullish on second half of May and June
items.quote: I have already told that demand has been slow, but despite that Aditya Vision is in growth, our company and we are seeing that, yes, this thing happens once in a while, most of the years in fact past year. When summer starts slowly, it again builds up later in the quarter. So we are quite bullish about this second-half of May and the full next month.

items.statement: April typically contributes ~25% of Q1 revenue, with sales peaking in May and June
items.quote: So safely, you can think that 25% off entire quarter sale, you can think about that, but it is not strictly that. So 25% sale will come from April.

items.statement: Room AC contributes 45-50% of Q1 revenue; focus on compressor products this quarter
items.quote: It is about around 45%-50%.

items.statement: Gross margin declined 22 bps for FY25; Q4 decline slightly higher due to 50% of new stores opening in Q4
items.quote: Actually, we believe in a basket way of gross margins and gross margin in this Financial Year has gone down by 22 bps. And we think that for the quarter it has come down by slightly more, but please do understand that most of our, in fact, around about I will tell you the exact figure, 14 out of 30 stores that has been opened in Q4.

items.statement: Inventory buildup to Rs 698 cr due to compressor supply uncertainty and government restrictions; temporary and expected to normalize within a month
items.quote: This year, in addition to our usual planning, we took a more cautious approach and built up more inventory due to uncertainties surrounding compressor supply. As a result, we accelerated inventory accumulation to safeguard against any potential disruption and stock out situations and ensure readiness for a strong start in the ensuing Q1.

items.statement: UP store throughput per store similar to Jharkhand; target 200 stores in UP in 2-3 years vs 112 in Bihar
items.quote: If Bihar can accommodate 112 stores, Vijay, so we can fairly well assume that in next, let us say, 2-3 years then we can have 200 stores in UP, the size and the kind of population it is, we will definitely aim to have double our store count in UP compared to Bihar because that is the potential for UP.

items.statement: No national marketing strategy needed; culturally similar regions allow original marketing approach
items.quote: We will not like to spend our money in vain, stakeholder's money that way. In fact, right now, if national, there is no need for any national marketing strategy. We are in Bihar, Jharkhand and UP as I have been telling all the time that culturally, these are almost same in nature. So our marketing strategy also remains original in nature.

items.statement: Global product volumes grow 5-6% CAGR; India grows 8-10% CAGR
items.quote: Globally -- you can say that all products together average 5% to 6% is okay globally. But in India it is a little bit higher, maybe 8% to 10%.

items.statement: JNPA SEZ facility total capex around INR700-750 crores over 18-24 months
items.quote: That we had already told earlier that it is around total INR750 crores, but it will happen stage -wise as we go along.

items.statement: FY25 consolidated capex INR125 crores, mainly INR110 crores for JNPA land procurement
items.quote: So on a consol basis, it has come because it includes also on the SEZ some maintenance capex, something on the R&D side. So it includes everything.

items.statement: U.S. Phase 1 initial equity infusion INR45 crores for procedures and land part, full capex not yet finalized
items.quote: It is only for the initial equity to start with the procedures and to do certain things.

items.statement: Existing export volumes will shift to JNPA SEZ Phase 1 quickly; U.S. Phase 1 capacity will fill fast due to ready customers
items.quote: And secondly, when we are talking about JNPA, there also the first phase is going to be very quick because we already have sizable exports here.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA margin 22.6%, down from prior year due to raw material, logistics, utility cost pressures
items.quote: The EBITDA margins for FY '25 stood at 22.6%.

items.statement: Raw material prices rose from Q2 FY25 through Q4 FY25; passed on where no long-term contracts, absorbed where 1-year contracts existed
items.quote: Wherever there were no long-term contracts, we passed on. But wherever there were long-term contracts, we had to bear that additional cost.

items.statement: Raw material prices have stabilized but not come down; future direction uncertain due to import duty and geopolitical factors
items.quote: As of now the prices have not come down, but it has stabilized. So I don't know whether the prices will come down because it totally depends upon government.

items.statement: Domestic demand strong across all product segments; export momentum renewed across global markets
items.quote: Demand in the domestic market remains strong across all our product segments. On the export front, we saw renewed momentum across global markets.

items.statement: U.S. Phase 1 will make same products currently exported from India; Phase 2 to include mix of existing and new products
items.quote: Initially, the first phase is making the same products which we are currently exporting from Indian plant.

items.statement: U.S. expansion risks: hiring right local talent, regulatory compliance, cultural differences; mitigated by conservative Phase 1 capacity
items.quote: We are a little bit cautious because we don't have experience of running the plant in U.S. with U.S. regulations and U.S. systems and all that.

items.statement: No debottlenecking at Patalganga plant as it would compromise safety parameters
items.quote: We can't do any debottlenecking because it will straight away hamper the safety parameters.

items.statement: Expansions to be funded by mix of internal accruals and debt financing; open to debt
items.quote: We are open, and we will be taking certain debt. So our project will be funded both with a good amount of mix of internal accruals and the debt financing.

items.statement: Cash and long-term deposits total ~INR1,150-1,200 crores; to be used for SEZ, U.S. expansions and potential M&A
items.quote: Yes. Yes, around that amount only, yes. So that has been invested in various periods, 3, 6, 9 and 12 months.

items.statement: Badlapur unit resumed full operations in Q3 FY25 after fire at adjacent facility; insurance claim lodged, expected to conclude soon
items.quote: We resumed full operations at our Badlapur manufacturing unit in Q3 FY '25.

items.statement: Gujarat land acquisition cancelled; government refunded earnest money deposit; no other land proposals in India currently
items.quote: You are talking about the Gujarat land, that we have already said that we are not going to get it. Government has told us clearly.

items.statement: Expect NBFC AUM to grow around 20% in FY26 with better visibility quarter-on-quarter
items.quote: So, we expect this year the AUM to grow by around 20% but we would have better visibility as we go down the year, Quarter-on-Quarter.

items.statement: Plan to increase secured AUM to 75% over next three to four years from current 64%
items.quote: Currently, I think by the end of this year it was about 64% roughly and in the next three to four years our plan is to increase secured AUM to 75% and we are working on that.

items.statement: Expect NBFC spreads or margins to be better in FY26 due to higher yields and lower cost of finance
items.quote: we expect spreads or margins to be better because we are working on increasing our yields on our asset book as well as there are certain tailwinds in terms of the cost of finance

items.statement: GNPA increased to 3.55% from 2.22% last year; large accounts in GNPA being monitored for recovery
items.quote: GNPA numbers for us also increased to 3.5 5% as compared to around 2.2 2% last year. So, but if you compare with the industry, our delinquencies and the credit quality is much better

items.statement: Bullish on stock broking due to under-penetrated market, new SEBI chairman seen as friendly, FPI selling stopped
items.quote: India is the fastest growing economy in the world and stock market still is very under penetrated. So, there is a huge s cope and we are very bullish and positive about it

items.statement: DP AUA added Rs 36,413 crore in FY25 (46% growth); over 1 lakh new Demat accounts opened
items.quote: In broking DP AUA, asset under administration , we added Rs. 36,413 crores in our DP AUA during FY’25 marking a 46% growth. Over 1 lakh new Demat accounts were opened.

items.statement: Expect recovery in GNPA/NNPA during FY26 but timing uncertain quarter to quarter
items.quote: It is very difficult to comment whether it would happen in quarter one or other quarters, but we are expecting the recovery during the year.

items.statement: Fair value loss of Rs 9.32 crore in Q4 due to mark-to-market on investment portfolio; expected to improve as markets recover
items.quote: Since markets were down in march quarter, there is some negative balances but as the market improves this will be better in future.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA growth guided at 12% to 15% in FY26 over FY25 base
items.quote: On a standalone basis, we are guiding an EBITDA growth of around 12% to 15% in FY'26 over the higher base of FY '25.

items.statement: CDMO/CMO revenue estimated to grow 30% to 40% in FY26
items.quote: On the back of strong manufacturing capabilities and sound R&D setup , the CDMO/CMO revenue is estimated to grow around 30% to 40% in FY'26.

items.statement: FY26 capex guided at Rs. 400 to 450 crores
items.quote: Yes, I think FY'26, overall the CAPEX number is around Rs. 400 to 450 crores total capex that we will end up doing in FY'26.

items.statement: Capex breakup: Atali remainder ~Rs. 200 cr, Xanthine ~Rs. 100 cr, plus maintenance and R&D
items.quote: Yes, total CAPEX is broken into the remainder of Atali CAPEX, which is almost around Rs. 200 crore remaining there and some CAPEX of Xanthine product around, we have to spend close to Rs. 100 crore plus there and then other maintenance CAPEX and other R&D CAPEX.

items.statement: CDMO 30-40% growth guidance based on booked orders and visibility; large part already in system
items.quote: 30%-40% guidance we have given based on the orders that we have and the visibility that we have. In CDMO/CMO, we are already in May and most of the businesses are in Q3-Q4 deliveries. We already know what we are supposed to make and what we are supposed to give. We have large part of this number already booked in the system as orders.

items.statement: Atali greenfield project mechanical completion expected end of current quarter; phased operationalization, full ramp-up by end of FY26
items.quote: The greenfield project at Atali , Gujarat is in final stages of completion. The mechanical completion is expected to finish around the end of this current quarter. It's planned to get operationalized in phases and the full ramp-up is expected by the end of this financial year.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expanded to 26% in Q4 FY25 from 23% in Q4 FY24; full year FY25 EBITDA Rs. 464 cr, up 20% YoY
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter was Rs. 146 crores, a 24 % increase YoY. EBITDA margins expanded to 26% up from 23% in Q4 FY'24. For the full year FY'25, we achieved an annual EBITDA of Rs. 464 crores growing by 20 % YoY

items.statement: API & Intermediate growth driven by regulated markets; export-backed demand continues
items.quote: Yes, I think overall growth in API is driven by regulated markets and growth in export market or export backed market basically. Even if we are giving to India but ultimately the c ustomer is exporting the products to regulated markets only , so that is where our focus has been and that's where we have been more and more successful in pushing our product and in future also the same will continue

items.statement: No threat to API business from US tariff uncertainties; APIs exempt from duties
items.quote: Yes, overall direct US export is not very significant as such in overall total revenue, but API is exempt from all these duties. We don't anticipate APIs will come under duty because if there is any impact I think it will be more on th e formulation front not on the API front

items.statement: Borrowings likely to increase by Rs. 100-125 cr in FY26; debt-equity ~0.23-0.25
items.quote: So next year in current year, think the borrowing is likely to go up by about Rs. 100 crores to Rs. 125 crores, which would basically mean debt equity of roughly in the range o f 0.23 to 0.25.

items.statement: CDMO commercial projects contribute 75-80% of sales; 33 commercial projects, ~70-75% contributed revenue in FY25
items.quote: So bulk of our sales is coming from phase -III onwards, you know. So currently, Phase-III and commercialization product would constitute to be 75% to 80% of overall value of sales and smaller amount from the early phases.

items.statement: Xanthine revenue potential Rs. 1,000-1,250 cr at optimal utilization with pharma/regulated mix shift
items.quote: I think the range would be from Rs. 1,000 crore to Rs. 1,200 crore in any number, would be the growth area of Xanthine. I think we can go up to 1 ,000 to 1,250 depending on how fast we are able to get commercial and how the price is sustained for the other market.

items.statement: FY26 revenue guidance of around Rs. 700 crores and PAT of Rs. 44-45 crores
items.quote: So, in Q1 for the full fiscal year, I am still hopeful that we will achieve a top line of around Rs. 700 crores and the bottom line would be around Rs. 44 crores to Rs. 45 crores.

items.statement: FY27 revenue target of Rs. 1,000 crores and PAT of Rs. 55 crores remains intact
items.quote: Yes, Kunal. So, see, as and when we get nearer to the subject , my guidance has to be more on the side of truth. Whatever I have spoken, my whole thing is that, yes, Rs. 1,000 crores is what we are looking at for FY ‘27 and Rs. 55 crores bottom line is what we are looking for .

items.statement: Three-year target of over Rs. 1,000 crores revenue with 25% top-line and 20% bottom-line CAGR over five years
items.quote: At a three-year pace we would be wanting that there should be stronger demand . We should be going up the top line of more than Rs. 1,000 crores. And on a five-year plan, it's too long to comment, but the consistent 25% of sales on top line growth should remain with the bottom-line approach to follow on the same lines, 20% bottom line should get up year-on-year.

items.statement: No new factory CAPEX needed as gold price doubling has already doubled rupee capacity of existing 2-ton plant
items.quote: Right now CAPEX plan, so the factory that we were supposed to plan about a 4-ton factory or a 5 ton factory. So if you understand that at that time, during the IPO, the price was Rs. 50,000 a gram. And we had 1 ton capacity. So now the price is Rs. 1 lakh a gram, so already in the same CAPEX we were already achieving the same amount.

items.statement: Two new retail stores (Surat in Q3 FY26, Rajkot in Q1 FY27) primarily on lease model; CAPEX amount not finalized
items.quote: in Q3 of this financial year, and another one will be in the Q1 of the next financial year, that is what the plans are. Palash Kawale: Okay. And what is the total CAPEX for these two stores? Harit Zaveri: We are primarily looking for a lease model, but let's see if there is any plans for the CAPEX, we will surely let the investors know about

items.statement: Job work revenue of Rs. 8.5 crores in Q4 FY25 vs guided Rs. 5-6 crores due to advance Akshay Tritiya orders
items.quote: So see, job work demand we have already received in advance in Q4 of this year, so the guided figure was Rs. 5 crores to Rs. 6 crores, we have done Rs. 8.5 crores.

items.statement: Margins expected to remain in line with current levels; no business model change anticipated
items.quote: So the structure then, the business model that we are preparing, the margins should be in line. If there is any business model change or something , there will be a very concrete intimation. But as of now there is nothing like that.

items.statement: Gold price escalation to Rs. 1 lakh/10g causing demand postponement but not denial; consumers adjusting grammage
items.quote: On the quarter, the escalation of prices going to the tune of Rs. 1 lakh for 10 gram has certainly made the walk -ins relatively slow. The demand has postponed. Why I am saying the demand has postponed is that the occasional buyers will buy jewellery if not at one then the other point of time.

items.statement: April sales flat despite +30% Akshay Tritiya day; demand postponed due to gold volatility but wedding-driven occasion demand remains intact
items.quote: We have seen a (+30%) growth on the sales side for that day, but that should not conclude the overall month, the overall month still went flat. On the quarter, the escalation of prices going to the tune of Rs. 1 lakh for 10 gram has certainly made the walk -ins relatively slow. The demand has postponed.

items.statement: B2B volume growth expected at 7-8% annually; capacity sufficient for higher demand if it materializes
items.quote: Certainly I expect the volume to be on the B2B side to grow, but it will be on a single digit side. So let us say we should be able to grow by around 7 % to 8% by volumes in terms of B2B side.

items.statement: Retail revenue target Rs. 400 crores (same-store) to Rs. 500 crores (total) in FY26; Rs. 600-700 crores in FY27; long-term B2B/B2C volume split seen at 50:50
items.quote: I think what we are anticipating is that retail should go about Rs. 400 crores this year , the same store sales growth will be Rs. 400 crores in retail this year and overall retail should be about Rs. 500 crores. And next year it will be around Rs. 600 crores to 600 and Rs. 650 crores, Rs. 700 odd crores in retail itself for the upcoming.

items.statement: Plan to raise debt at 1:1 debt-equity ratio over coming years to fuel growth and improve ROE/ROCE
items.quote: We are 100% on our side of raising debt. We expect to raise the debt to the tune of 1:1 ratio, maybe not in full this year, in the coming year. But surely the fund debt raise plans are there, and debt raise will fuel the growth for the coming years, it will improve the ROE and ROCE.

items.statement: Equity raise considered after debt-funded infrastructure is in place for next growth phase
items.quote: Equity, see, right now the first aim is to fuel the growth as much as we can by debt . And then once we have a right kind of infrastructure and stuff in place for the robust next jump, we are sure that equities getting money and raising funds are part and parcel of operations .

items.statement: Income tax order of Rs. 25 crores for bonus share issuance appealed; management calls it baseless and expects no financial impact
items.quote: So income tax matter, they have ordered us for Rs. 25 crores of income tax appeal for issuance of bonus shares when we were a Private Limited Company. I think that order we have already filed across CIT appeal. We particularly think that it's a very baseless order and we have filed our replies into CIT appeal.

items.statement: Employee fraud (Rs. 25 lakh provision taken); perpetrator jailed, gold largely recovered, insurance claim filed
items.quote: So Mr. Om Shukla, who did the fraud, is right now behind bars. He did not get bail. The internal controls and the locks which was there, we have submitted to the insurance Company. We have got a positive feedback. And CCTV footages and everything is very much available.

items.statement: Interest rate expected to drop to 9.5-9.75% consolidated after CRISIL upgrade to BBB+ from current 9-10.25% spread
items.quote: And with this rating upgrade, we are hopeful that I think the interest rate should be in the range of around 9.5% or 9.75% at max on a consolidated basis.

items.statement: FY26 and FY27 will be quite transformational for overall P&L
items.quote: I think FY '26 and FY '27 will be quite transformational for our overall P&L.

items.statement: Chhatrapati Sambhaji Nagar greenfield facility to start coming on stream sometime next year
items.quote: Sometime next year, you should see it starting to come on life, but exact timeline we'll share a little later.

items.statement: Adjusted gross margin improved 1,000 bps YoY to almost 19% in FY25
items.quote: Overall, AGM adjusted gross margin for us was up 1,000 bps compared to the previous year, 9% to almost 19% and this led to an EBITDA improvement.

items.statement: Adjusted gross margin without subsidy improved 1,800 bps YoY in FY25
items.quote: There was an 1,800 bps year on year improvement in adjusted gross margin when you look at it without subsidy being factored in.

items.statement: COGS per unit reduced 19% YoY to INR 120,700 in FY25
items.quote: Our COGS per unit saw a very strong reduction in FY25. They were down from 148,900 to 120,700 in FY25, a 19% reduction over the course of a year.

items.statement: LFP battery packs generally 15-20% cheaper than NMC globally
items.quote: LFP generally tends to be 15%-20% cheaper compared to NMC globally, most reports will call it out.

items.statement: Very bullish about EV adoption in FY26, growth stronger than FY25
items.quote: So, very bullish about EV adoption in FY '26.

items.statement: Software attach rate reached 88% in FY25, contributing over 600 bps to revenue
items.quote: But with a very strong performance in Q4, software has ended up at an 88% attach rate for our sales over the course of the entire year.

items.statement: Rizta now majority of sales, 450 seeing some cannibalization but settling at healthy base
items.quote: Rizta is already the majority of our sales and is still in many ways a young product.

items.statement: Store count increased 69% YoY to 351 in FY25, added 86 stores in Q4 alone
items.quote: Overall for the full year, our store count was up 69%.

items.statement: Operational capacity up to adding almost two stores per day
items.quote: Today, our operational capacity is up to adding almost two stores per day.

items.statement: Subsidy reduction from INR 10,000 to INR 5,000 has roughly 3% revenue impact, ability to absorb given cost reduction trends
items.quote: For Athers P&L, that's a roughly 3% impact on revenue, something that, given the strong trend of cost reduction, we have a strong ability to absorb.

items.statement: India-produced cells may not bring big cost advantage near term, likely flat to marginally up on pricing
items.quote: I believe India produced cells may not necessarily bring a big cost advantage in the near term because frankly it's going to be hard to beat China's massive scale and pricing structures overall.

items.statement: Hosur plant produced 21,000 units in October 2024 vs 10,000 in October 2023
items.quote: Festive '24, October '24, we did 21,000 units out of that plant.

items.statement: EL low-cost scooter platform in mid-term, motorcycle platform work begun but product guidance still time away
items.quote: Ahead of this is the EL product line that we have talked about in our prospectus, which is a low-cost scooter platform.

items.statement: New format stores breakeven in few quarters vs several years for older format
items.quote: Today the new format stores that we open breakeven at a much smaller timeline. They are down from taking several years to get to steady state and years to profitability to literally down to a few quarters now.

items.statement: PLA plant capex Rs 2850 crore gross, Rs 1750 crore net after 50% government subsidy
items.quote: The 80,000 tonne capacity of our PLA plant is on track for commissioning by Q3 F Y27 with a capex of Rs. 2850 crores (gross) or net figure is Rs. 1750 crores accounting for government subsidy of 50

items.statement: PLA plant expected to generate Rs 2000 crore annual revenue and ~35% EBITDA margin
items.quote: The facility will produce 100% bio-based PLA using sugar as feed stock and is expected to generate around Rs. 2000 crore annual revenue, and hopefully, since it's the first time we are entering into this business, that's why the word hopefully, EBITDA margin of ~35%.

items.statement: Current sugar price around Rs 41/kg expected to maintain, marginal uptick possible
items.quote: So right now, as we have informed you, our price is around Rs.41/kg. I think this is what has been prevailing in this quarter, approximately around this range. So, I would say that this price level should definitely maintain. And the rest would depend on the government's policy for next year. So, if at all, we'll see a marginal uptick in the coming months.

items.statement: Cane crushing expected to see marginal uptick next season and decent uptick thereafter
items.quote: If I am to hazard a guess and please mark my language, it says hazard a guess. Next season probably we will see some uptick and thereafter a very decent uptick.

items.statement: No ethanol price increase for juice and B-heavy routes despite FRP revision; government understood the issue, expects FRP linkage restoration next year
items.quote: For 2024-25 ethanol year, while diversion of sugarcane juice and B-heavy molasses is permitted, so the restriction on quantum was lifted but there was no price increase given. This marks a shift from the government's prior practice of aligning ethanol prices with changes in FRP making sugar diversion for ethanol unattractive. If this persists, it could undermine the government's E30 blending progr

items.statement: Red rot variety Co-0238 reduced to 6% of cane; new varieties acclimatizing well, yield enhancement expected if weather supports
items.quote: Now we only have as also forecasted previously, now we have only 6% of 0238 which is affected by red rot. All the other varieties are very healthy and all the new varieties which are also put into the stream are acclimatizing well and now hopefully we should see some yield enhancement if weather is on our side definitely and even if weather is not on our side, we should see the lowest drop.

items.statement: Grain ethanol capacity up to 5.5 crore litres; maize price stable, company expects to make money using own energy source
items.quote: I would say, because you need some shutdown time, more Rs. 5-5.5 crore liter. So, maize is equal to balancing factor post juice in Maizapur. We have one single capacity. Two, maize price has not reduced, it remains stagnant. What I did is give a comparative between what the OMC buys maize ethanol at and juice ethanol at. That is what I did. Just to sort of drill down the logic that if one is looki

items.statement: Aim to reach around Rs.15,000 crores annual pre-sales in about three years' time
items.quote: What we are largely looking at is on a more three -year plan in which our aim is to reach ar ound Rs.15,000 crores in about three years’ time

items.statement: Planning to launch around Rs.14,000 crores of new launch phases or new projects in FY26, largely in Q3 and Q4
items.quote: So as you know, we mentioned we are planning to launch around Rs.14,000 crores of new launch phases or new projects. Largely, this is up in the Q3 and Q4.

items.statement: Added projects having GDV of more than Rs.25,000 crores in FY25, taking total GDV close to Rs.70,000 crores
items.quote: Added projects having GDV of more than Rs.25,000 crores, taking the total GD V of company close to Rs.70,000 crores

items.statement: Construction spend was about Rs.1,600 crores in FY25
items.quote: So we had a very healthy collection of almost Rs.2,706 crores, construction spend was about Rs.1,600 crores.

items.statement: Raised USD 33 million with Mitsubishi Estate Company for development of Birla Evara, Bengaluru via 51:49 equity JV
items.quote: In other updates, we have raised US D 33 million with Mitsubishi Estate Company for the Development of Birla Evara, Bengaluru.

items.statement: Demand continues to be very strong with massive hunger for right pricing, location, brand, design and sizing
items.quote: Amit, demand continues to be very strong. I have always maintained that the right pricing, right location and combination of right brand, right design, right sizing, I think the market continues to have massive hunger or demand for such kind of products.

items.statement: Exploring redevelopment space in a meaningful way to unlock asset-light deals and expanding commercial real estate portfolio for annuity income

items.statement: Dividend payout ratio maintained at ~95% in FY25, expected to continue

items.statement: Aspires to achieve highest ever revenue and profit in coming FYs

items.statement: FY26 AUM growth target 14-18% with MFI 8-12% and retail finance balance

items.statement: FY26 NIM guidance 12.6-12.8%

items.statement: Q4 FY25 NIM 12.7%, FY25 NIM 12.9% in line with revised guidance
items.quote: NIM remained healthy at 12.7 % for Q4 FY25 while 12.9% for F25, in line with our revised guidance.

items.statement: Portfolio yield 20.4%, interest spread 10.3%, cost of borrowing stable at 9.8% for seven quarters

items.statement: Sanctions in hand INR 3,618 crore and INR 4,664 crore in pipeline
items.quote: Additionally, we have sanctions in hands of INR 3,618 crore and INR. 4,664 crore worth sanctions in pipeline.

items.statement: New-to-credit borrowers increased to 40-43% in recent quarters; unique borrower count rose from 26.3% to 31.1%
items.quote: We added 2.61 lakh borrowers in Q4 FY25, of which 43% were new -to-credit, with the FY25 new borrower addition count at 7.49 lakh. The New-to-credit % trend has increased from 30 -35% to 40-43% levels over the past couple of quarters.

items.statement: Retail finance AUM INR 1,543 crore (5.9% of total); unsecured INR 1,100 crore, secured business INR 240 crore, home loans INR 110 crore
items.quote: Our 'Evolve with Customer' strategy is helping deepen our customer engagement, with Retail Finance reaching INR 1,543 crore, contributing 5.9% of the AUM, compared to 2.7% a year ago.

items.statement: Karnataka PAR accretion expected to normalize by end of Q1 FY26; ex-Karnataka new PAR accretion largely normalized

items.quote: We have taken INR 479 crore accelerated write off in FY25 of non -paying loan accounts with 180 plus DPD, resulting in additional credit cost of INR 151 crore. The total write-off of FY25 stood at INR 1,124 crore.

items.statement: Target mid-single digit growth for both Spencer's and Natures Basket in FY26 driven by online and same-store growth
items.quote: We want to target mid-single digit growth as far as Spencer's and Natures Basket is concerned, driven by online in both parts of the business, but also driven by same store growth in both the businesses.

items.statement: Spencer's FY25 EBITDA Rs 53 crore (3.1% of sales) vs breakeven in FY24; consolidated EBITDA Rs 60 crore vs Rs 14 crore
items.quote: EBITDA for Spencer's for the full year to be Rs. 53 crores versus breakeven last year. So, I think this EBITDA represents about 3.1% of sales and gives us confidence that that's the right trajectory for Spencer's.

items.quote: the slight depletion in gross margins, 90 basis point s depletion in gross margins which we experien ced in FY ’25, that is going to be built back and the team is quite confident of getting to levels which are going to be closer to the 30% mark as far as Natures Basket is

items.quote: The year-on-year Q4 of FY ‘25 versus FY ‘24 we saw 58% year-on-year user growth, which is close to 70,000 monthly transacting users. Our order growth ha s been in the order of 47%. So , we do an average of about 1.8 lakh bills per

items.statement: Net debt ~Rs 860 crore; exploring equity raise but market cap not supportive; will refinance maturing debt using available credit lines
items.quote: The debt position obviously remains high and we are aware of that. items.statement: No plans to liquidate any business part; Spencer's, Jiffy, and Natures Basket all integral to growth plans
items.quote: No, there are no plans to liquidate any part of the business. We have three parts of the business, w e have the Spencer’s business, we have Spencer’s online, which is Jiffy and Natures Basket. And all three are integral to our plans of driving top line

items.statement: Spencer's FY25 revenue Rs 1,700 crore vs Rs 2,049 crore (-17%) due to 47 store closures; LFL flat
items.quote: revenue from operations for Spencer's for FY '25 are Rs. 1,700 crores versus Rs. 2,049 crores in FY '24, which is a 17% decline.

items.statement: Natures Basket out-of-store share 13% currently; target 18% in FY26 via app relaunch and phone delivery

items.quote: Operational EBITDA, if you see for the stand-alone quarter 4, it stood at Rs.235.6 crores, basically resulting in a double-digit operational EBITDA of 12.3%.

items.statement: Robust tender pipeline excluding HVDC, strong domestic demand from renewables, transmission, data centers

items.quote: We said we have a potential of future addressable market is in the range of Rs.2,000 crores per year.

items.quote: About QIP proceeds, we talked about very clearly and two-thirds of that we used in our expansion capex. And then the rest 25% is our capex corporate usage and 10% is working capital.

items.quote: Data center is one of our key growth segments and we call it the high-growth segment and we are very well positioned.

items.statement: Gross margins 38-40%, operating margins improving through product mix, export and service growth

items.statement: Capacity expansions across all four business units: transformers, high voltage, grid automation, grid integration
items.quote: We are expanding our manufacturing capabilities, capacities in all the four business units.

items.statement: Reciprocal tariff impact uncertain, maintaining vigil to minimize impact on export growth momentum

items.statement: Full-year FY25 orders at record Rs.18,173.8 crores, up 228% year-on-year
items.quote: For the full year, orders reached a record of Rs.18,173.8 crores, as you can see from the slide, up by 228%.

items.statement: Material cost at 61.6% of total income in Q4 FY25, personnel expenses 7.5%, other expenses 16.6%

items.statement: CMC business PBT positive with reasonable EBITDA margin, scope for improvement

items.quote: we have, of course, announced our foray, we are working on a green powe r initiative, where we are looking at a hybrid of solar and wind, which will come in from next year, and that will have significant cost savings

items.quote: As far as the CAPEX guidance is concerned, we have our Chile project, which will have about $30 to $35 million of CAPEX expenditure. Then we have our Dahej debottlenecking project which is ongoing and apart from that we have about $5 to $6 million of maintenance CAPEX every year.

items.statement: Maintained healthy blended gross margins of ~57% despite raw material volatility and global uncertainties
items.quote: We have been able to maintain healthy blended gross margins of approximately 57% in-line with last year, in spite of raw material volatility and global uncertainties as witnessed during the year.

items.quote: So our guidance remains firm, it's only a time difference that has come in between Q4, some of the orders which is expected to come out in Q1 and Q2 going forward. So there is no loss, but more of a deferment that's come through.

items.quote: Yes, so on the tariff we don't see any impact on our business in the US, because all our competitors manufacture outside of the US. items.quote: About Rs.30 crore is the

items.quote: launches even in Tommy as a brand. We'll be bringing our first PP Brand Concepts Limited (BCONCEPTS) Q4 FY25 Post Earnings Conference Call May 19, 2025 Luggage. items.quote: No. So what we are looking at is 12% to 13% , kind of a volume growth in FY'26.

items.quote: THF can do close to INR90 crores of business in this FY'26, and Ariba can do close to INR50 crores. So that's the target that both brands have for FY'26.
