items.statement: Delhi next phase launch may not happen in FY27, could take longer
items.quote: It may not happen in FY '27. It may take longer than that.

items.statement: Focus on embedded margins in 5-figure range annually rather than just sales volume
items.quote: we clearly want to be in a situation where our embedded margins on an annual basis continue to be in the 5-figure range , and the sales that supports it

items.statement: Dahlias currently at INR 1 lakh+ per sq ft carpet, Camellias at INR 2 lakh, gap to close
items.quote: right now, we are at almost about lakh plus on carpet. So right now, that's where we are. And just to tell you what Camellias is about now 2 lakhs on carpet.

items.statement: Cyber City rental re-rating potential from INR 125-135 to INR 160-170 per sq ft
items.quote: We have the current rental for the minimum space that is vacant and for the term expiries is in the ballpark of about INR 125 to INR 135. And that if you say, compare with Downtown 4, which is the la st building or to say, Atrium Place, which we have just leased, which is in the ballpark of INR 160 to INR 170

items.statement: Development business now zero-leverage, removing down-cycle debt pressure
items.quote: Also, structurally, we are now a zero-leverage company on the development business. So that entire pressure that we used to have earlier of being caught in a down cycle with no debt. So that is gone now.

items.statement: Strong housing demand in Gurgaon driven by end-users, NRIs, and rental yield investors
items.quote: housing demand for quality products is continuously there. And also what is happening in Gurgaon today has become a very solid investment option too.

items.statement: Management expects significant growth in FY26, combining domestic private and export markets, and believes 40% growth in the Freight Car Division is possible.
items.quote: Combining domestic, private and export, we feel 40% in the FCD division is possible to be achieved.

items.statement: Capex for FY26 will be similar to FY25, focusing on improving infrastructure.
items.quote: Yes, we will be mainly focusing on improving the infrastructure. So our CAPEX will be like the last year only.

items.statement: Bright Power (Infra-Electrical) order book stands at Rs 1,600-1,900 crore as of March 31, 2025.
items.quote: Bright Power book is about Rs. 1,900 crores.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin for FY25 was 10.3%, up from 9.5% in FY24, driven by operational efficiencies despite infra segment losses.
items.quote: See, our margin for the year 2024 -25 has been 10.3%. So , that is as Sudipta has said, it is up from 9.5% to 10.3%, which is last year 9.5% to 10.3%.

items.statement: Private sector orders yield higher margins than government orders due to design-to-delivery value chain involvement.
items.quote: Yes, obviously it is the private sector where margin is higher. But we have to have a combination because in the private sector your receivable takes some time.

items.statement: Government targets 1.5 lakh wagons over next 3-4 years; Texmaco has 15,000 annual capacity and aims to capture fair share.
items.quote: As part of this expansion, approximately 1.5 lakh wagons are expected to be delivered in the next three to four years. With a consolidated annual production capacity of 15,000 wagons, Texmaco is ready to capture its fair share of this demand.

items.statement: Private wagon share rose to 35% of 10,612 wagons delivered in FY25 (~2,000 units); target is to shift revenue mix to 60% domestic / 40% export in near term.
items.quote: On year basis it was 35% of 10,600. So, over and above, if you specifically ask, so it may be around 2,000 something.

items.statement: Wheelset supply from RWF remains uncertain for the near term though supplies improved significantly in the last week; geopolitical disruptions persist.
items.quote: I will not say it has gone completely, and it has become good, no. The first quarter may look , I mean, it may remain for another few days.

items.statement: No fund raise discussed; CARE Ratings upgraded long-term and short-term facilities to CARE A and CARE A-1 respectively.
items.quote: CARE Ratings upgraded company's long-term and short-term facilities to CARE A and CARE A-1 respectively.

items.statement: Merger of Texmaco West Rail and transfer of Infra-Rail/Green businesses expected to receive final approval by January 2026.
items.quote: We are currently filed the scheme with the Stock Exchanges. We got some queries which we have replied. We are working with the NOCs, and we are expecting final approval in January 26.

items.statement: Jindal Rail (Texmaco West) contributed revenue >Rs 900 crore and PBT >Rs 125 crore in FY25.
items.quote: Jindal Rail turnover was more than Rs. 900 crores, and the PBT was about more than Rs. 125 crores.

items.statement: One-off provisions of Rs 20-25 crore taken in Q4 FY25 for slow-moving debtors and future studies.
items.quote: So, we have some one-time expenses, one-off expenses of about Rs. 20 crores to Rs. 25 crores, which includes provisions and some study we have done for the future.

items.statement: Global Capability Center in Faridabad to commercialize Trinity Rail partnership and global sourcing within FY26; Nevomo MagRail pilot expected within FY26.
items.quote: the commercialization of the whole process, the transaction level you can see in this financial year itself.

items.statement: Foundry casting revenue ~Rs 750 crore; hi-tech components >Rs 50 crore in FY25, booked under Freight Car Division.
items.quote: Our foundry casting revenue is about Rs. 750 crore plus and for other small hi-tech components is more than Rs. 50 crores.

items.statement: Nymwag facility to operate as boutique/premium unit targeting ~2,000 wagons mean output across multiple geographies.
items.quote: if I have to say the mean, it will be around 2000.

items.statement: Management aims for at least 25-30% reduction in new vertical losses (₹162 crs in FY25), targeting ₹40-45 crs savings.
items.quote: We believe it should get fixed, coupled with a stringent control on costs. So at least a 25%, 30% reduction in this, if not more, we are internally aiming for more, but that's the kind of reduction we are minimum aiming to bring it.

items.statement: Management targets ₹25-30 crs cost reduction at platform level, with benefits visible from Q2 FY26 and full impact in H2 FY26.
items.quote: We are looking at a potential ₹25 to ₹30crs cost reduction and measures have already been taken. I mean it's something that we reflected in last month and have put it under execution. And I also mentioned that clearly, the benefits will start coming in, in the later part of the year from Q2 onwards.

items.statement: Management expects aggregate savings of around ₹50 crs from new vertical loss reduction, platform cost cuts, and tail vertical restructuring in FY26.
items.quote: But can we not achieve ₹50crs out of these initiatives all put together, I think we feel positive we should be able to achieve as an aggregate number out of all of these things.

items.statement: Management guides for mid-teens GMV growth in FY26, citing 14% order book growth in dollar terms and positive factors like UK FTA and US tariffs.
items.quote: So I think we are walking in with a 14% order book growth in dollar terms over the same period last year. So mid-teens is what we are walking into it.

items.statement: No immediate capex needed for Knit Gallery acquisition; existing 3.5-acre land and 2,200 machines can double capacity at small incremental cost as UK-India FTA ramps up.
items.quote: There is 3.5-acre land that is already there under a long-term arrangement in Knit Gallery facility. We have no immediate need for any capex. There are about 2,200 machines in Knit Gallery. As the India-U.K. FTA ramps up, there is this lever that at a small incremental cost, we can double up the capacity.

items.statement: Excluding agency business, gross margin improved by 45 bps in FY25; adjusted EBITDA margin (ex-new vertical investments) was 5.2% vs 4.9% in FY24.
items.quote: Excluding agency business, our gross margin has improved by 45 basis points. We reported an EBITDA of ₹457crs with a margin of 3.6%. However, if we were to adjust this for our investments made in new verticals, we clocked EBITDA margins of 5.2% versus 4.9% in the last year.

items.statement: Management targets gradual ramp-up towards 3% PAT margin by FY27 (from ~2% currently) via mid-teens growth, new vertical profitability, lower incremental investment, and cost austerity.
items.quote: We're just at about 2%. And we have been in this call talking about levers of a mid-teens' growth, coupled with investments in new verticals expected on one hand to become in the journey of profitability, also lesser incremental investment, lots of cost austerity measures as well. So no one can say with certainty that will we get to 3. But I think the measures, the levers are underway to see that

items.statement: UK customers represent near $1 billion GMV in order book across apparel, general merchandise, and home categories.
items.quote: With the recent acquisition of Knit Gallery, we are now well positioned to scale up sourcing volumes for our existing marquee U.K. customers who already represent near $1 billion in GMV that we currently have in order book from them.

items.statement: Sourcing as a Service GMV was $730 million for FY25, translating to ~$18 million revenue.
items.quote: So for the full financial year as far as our Sourcing as a Service business is concerned, we did a GMV of $730 million, which translates into revenue of close to $18 million in this financial year.

items.statement: US retailers paused buying in Q4 due to tariffs, postponing orders; major accounts like Walmart, Target, American Eagle, Ralph Lauren, and TJ Maxx have opened PDS accounts.
items.quote: But with the tariffs suddenly coming in, most of the retailers have paused the buying that we saw the impact in the Q4 order book as well. So one of the factors our losses in Q4 were there and not reducing is because the North America business that was supposed to come in for shipping in Jan, Feb, March and even beginning part of this quarter, has now been postponed to a little bit in the future m

items.statement: Agency business (including Ted Baker) declined due to retail partner bankruptcies; Ted Baker revenue was $61M in FY25 vs $63M in FY24, with agency revenue only in first few and last months.
items.quote: Ted Baker, the total revenue that we did was around $61 million, including both wholesale and agency business, which was a tad lower than what we did in the last financial year. Last financial year, it was $63 million. This year, it's $61 million.

items.statement: Working capital days increased to 17 in FY25 due to growth, business mix changes, trade terms, and Bangladesh disruptions; management targets reduction to low single digits in FY26.
items.quote: Net working capital days increased to 17, largely -- and this was largely on account of changes in business mix and terms of trade. We are working on and are pretty confident that we should be able to contain and reduce our working capital days in fiscal '26.

items.statement: Matalan revenue reduced from £134M to £89M in FY25; relationship being cautiously scaled down due to credit risk.
items.quote: one of our key markets, clocked a growth of 6%. This is mainly due to one of our customers, U.K.-based Matalan. The revenue to Matalan reduced from 134 million in FY '24 to 89 million in FY '25. This particular customer is served by Design Arc, which is one of our large verticals. We have decided to cautiously scale down this relationship because of the credit risk involved

items.statement: ₹430 crs raised via QIP; ₹278 crs deployed for debt repayment and ₹24 crs for Knit Gallery acquisition in May; remainder earmarked for strategic growth and general corporate purposes.
items.quote: With the ₹430crs raised from our recent QIP, we have already deployed ₹278 crs towards debt repayment. And in May, we further deployed ₹24crs towards the Knit Gallery acquisition and the remaining funds earmarked for strategic growth and general corporate purposes.

items.statement: New sourcing geographies (Egypt, LatAm, Africa, India) take 3-6 months to set up teams, 12-24 months to reach critical mass and profitability; office cost ~$0.5-0.7M/year.
items.quote: So setting up teams and offices for PDS is our strength, the ability to attract the best talent is our strength. It's just that when the customer starts visiting, it takes 12, 24 months for business to become sizable and from there it becomes profitable.

items.statement: Rock phosphate purchased at 15-20% lower levels for coming season; prices since improved to 5-7% correction but still considered cheapest
items.quote: As far as r ock phosphate that you spoke about , we have bought the product at lower levels of at least 15% to 20% for coming this season. And from thereafter, now I see that the 15%, 20% correction which was there, that has still improved to 5 % to 7% level

items.statement: Expects 20% volume growth in Fertilizer segment in FY26 driven by phosphatic fertilizer shortage and higher SSP subsidy
items.quote: In this particular year, we believe, looking at the present situation of the phosphatic fertilizers globally, in my opinion we should be able to achieve at least this target what we had planned for the last year. So, I still see that there would be 20% increase in fertilizer business as far as this particular season is concerned.

items.statement: Bangladesh exposure only 4% of total business; developing alternative markets in Vietnam, Indonesia, Sri Lanka, Egypt
items.quote: Right, it is hardly 4% of the total business. Even after there is internal disturbance also, we have not seen much impact on the business, and still my confidence level is that this will not have major impact on our relationships with Bangladesh.

items.statement: Commissioned additional 3.8 MW DC solar plant (total 9 MW DC); initiated 10 MW DC solar plant in Nanded under Open Access Scheme
items.value: 9 MW DC total; 10 MW DC planned
items.quote: During the quarter, we commissioned an additional 3.8 megawatts DC solar power plant, taking the total solar capacity to 9 megawatts DC, and parallel site development at Unit-6 is also progressing as planned. We have also initiated work on a 10 megawatts DC solar plant in Nanded for our captive consumption under the Open Access Scheme.

items.statement: Dropped caustic soda plant investment after review; pursuing other opportunities instead
items.quote: Last time also we mentioned this that we have dropped this, because it is always better to review your decisions; and very importantly, we need to take very conscious decisions, any such decisions which is good for the Company on a longer-term business. I personally believe that we can always review our decisions, and after reviewing the decisions we found that caustic is not so great, so we got s

items.statement: Promoter equity transfer to mother part of family trust creation for long-term succession planning
items.quote: We are in the process of making a family trust. So the equity transfer to my mother is a part of the process for our entire equity transferring to the family trust for a long-term succession plan, for a better stability and this long-term sustainability.

items.statement: Management does not give explicit guidance but hopes to sustain ~28% average annual growth seen over the last three years.
items.quote: So, I would hope that this is a new normal for the company or in that range. And this is what we try to achieve going forward.

items.statement: About 35% of the South African deposit insurance platform remains to be executed; a good handful of RFPs are in play.
items.quote: So, I would say maybe about 35% is still left to be executed. And we are working on a number of other deals which are in the pipeline as well.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved to ~17% in FY25 from ~15% in FY24; other expenses rose ~25% YoY to INR44.89 crores due to sales, marketing and partner payments.
items.quote: I think the EBITDA margin on a year-to-year basis there is a small increase. It's about 17% versus 15%.

items.statement: Software development costs for new revenue streams (e.g., Malaysian e-invoicing) are capitalized; other R&D is expensed.
items.quote: Whenever we build new products from which we expect to generate revenue, this is a policy to capitalize those expenses.

items.statement: Disclosure management and voluntary ESG reporting are growing pipelines; cross-sell to 6,000+ customers is in motion but sales cycles are longer without mandate urgency.
items.quote: We see disclosure management certainly as a high-touch, more value-add, deeper driver of growth.

items.statement: SupTech ~49% of revenue; RegTech expanding beyond XBRL mandates into disclosure management and sustainability; TaxTech turning around after product investments.
items.quote: If you look at the current pie, the SupTech is maybe contributing up to 49%.

items.statement: FERC Phase 2 and ESG mandate timelines uncertain due to legislative and political factors; SupTech RFP decisions can be delayed.
items.quote: There is a lot of, I would say, external f actors, political factors that are playing out as we speak globally. So, I will not comment on when that will

items.statement: Disclosure management commands a significant price premium over traditional XBRL compliance products.
items.quote: We see there is traction and a lot of demand for the disclosure management as a product as well as we are able to demonstrate value and hence charge more compared to what we have traditionally done.

items.statement: ARR ~INR75 crores; recurring revenue share expected to rise; Qatar Central Bank deal smaller and faster to implement than South Africa.
items.quote: Anyway, if you look at the ARR of the company, that has already gone up. We are at about INR75 crores of ARR roughly.

items.statement: Expect revenue growth to accelerate to 12-15% in FY26 from 8.5% in FY25, with double-digit growth targeted for FY26
items.quote: we are very confident that if markets sort of support a little bit, we will hit our aspiration of 12% to 15% and surely, higher than 8.5% that we have delivered in FY 25

items.statement: Target EBITDA margin expansion of 100 bps annually going forward
items.quote: We are confident of increasing margins by 100 bps every year going forward.

items.statement: Capex remained near INR 100 crores in FY25 with asset-light approach
items.quote: And with our asset-light mindset, capex has remained in the expected range of close to INR 100 crores.

items.statement: Net square foot addition of 1.22 lakh sq ft in FY25, targeting 1.5 lakh+ sq ft in FY26
items.quote: In FY26 in our view, should go up to more than 1.5 lakh square ft., and we want to look at a CAGR of between 12% to 15%, more like 15% for square foot expansion.

items.statement: Retail discounting reduced ~2% in Q4 FY25, driving 270 bps GP margin improvement
items.quote: Discounting reduction of nearly 2% in retail, this is a key achievement of this quarter and is a reflection of the strength of our brand portfolio and the quality of execution.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 showing uptick in like-to-like and growth rates in first 45 days
items.quote: Whatever we witnessed in the first 45 days of quarter 1, we have witnessed some uptick in our like-to-like and growth rates.

items.statement: Adjacent categories (footwear, innerwear, womenswear) now >20% of revenue, growing ~20%+
items.quote: We are seeing these categories reaching more than 20% of revenue share with healthy growth of around 20%.

items.statement: Growth dependent on market conditions and wholesale channel recovery
items.quote: While a lot of growth is linked to external market condition and business does get influenced by economic reality, we are confident of continuing uptick in revenue growth.

items.statement: ROCE crossed 20% in FY25, up ~400 bps YoY; debt reduced ~INR 75 crores
items.quote: We are delighted to report that AFL crossed the milestone of generating more than 20% return on capital employed this year, and we hope to continue to impr ove upon this as we move ahead

items.statement: Medium-term guidance: consolidated revenue CAGR ~75% over next 3 fiscals, Operating EBITDA CAGR ~45%, Operating EBITDA margin stabilizing at 11% by FY28, PAT CAGR ~40% with PAT margin ~5% by FY28, ROCE >18%
items.quote: Over the next 3 fiscals, we anticipate consolidated revenue to grow at a CAGR of approximately 75%, driven by the phased commissioning of the Bokaro greenfield project and our organic growth. Operating EBITDA is expected to grow at a CAGR of 45% over the same period with the Operating EBITDA margin stabilizing at 11% by FY '28 as we progressively integrate the new and existing business lines.

items.statement: Greenfield investment in Bokaro for downstream processing and coated/plated steel, total INR 803 crores over 24 months, Phase 1 operational by end FY26, qualified under PLI 1.1 Scheme
items.quote: Lastly, in a decisive step, the company has initiated a greenfield investment in Bokaro, focused on downstream processing and manufacturing of coated and plated steel. With a total investment of INR 803 crores over the next 24 months, Phase 1 of the facility is expected to be operational by the end of FY '26.

items.statement: Debt expected ~INR 500 crores out of INR 800 crores project outlay for Bokaro expansion over next 24 months
items.quote: In terms of the debt for Bokaro, our total project outlay over the next 24 months is expected to be about INR 800-odd crores. And our debt is expected to be in the range of INR 500 crores out of that.

items.statement: Core conversion business EBITDA margin stable at 23-24%; consolidated margin to moderate to 11% by FY28 due to raw material costs >80% of revenue in new downstream model
items.quote: Historically, our conversion business model has delivered Operating EBITDA margins in the mid-20s, owing to very limited raw material exposure. With the transition to an integrated downstream steel processing model, our cost structure will change. Steel inputs will now form a part of our cost structure, resulting in raw material costs comprising over 80% of the Revenue. Accordingly, consolidated O

items.statement: Long-term contracts with key customer renewed through FY29
items.quote: First, we successfully renewed our long-term contracts with our key customer, extending it through FY '29. This reaffirms the trust placed in us and our role as a dependable partner in the steel ecosystem.

items.statement: Pipes and Tubes utilization improved substantially in Q4 FY25 from ~174k tonnes out of 534k tonnes capacity; healthy growth expected to pick up faster
items.quote: So the Quarter 4 numbers are there, you will see a substantial improvement in the utilization of Pipes and Tubes. And this is slower than we had expected. And therefore, we had scaled out our number. But we are seeing a healthy growth that we are hoping it picks up even faster.

items.statement: Bokaro Phase 1 starts with Color Coated segment (highest value-add), then expands backwards; Defense and Solar products to follow from same plant
items.quote: We are doing like the first phase is only the Color Coated Segment. So what is happening is we are starting with the highest value add and going backwards, right, as we expand.

items.statement: Input cost variation largely transferable to customers in value-added downstream processing; not upstream steel production
items.quote: In this sector, most of the input variation is transferable to the customers. So there is very little component that one has to absorb when you're talking about value-added.

items.statement: Core steel servicing business revenue potential ~INR 850 crores at 60-70% utilization of Pipe and Tube capacity; EBITDA margin 23-24% stable state
items.quote: If the only place where we are left to ramp up is the pipes and tubes, if that ramps up to the capacity, we expect maybe INR 850 crores or thereabout.

items.statement: Bokaro expansion capacity scaled to 700,000 tonnes from earlier 1 million tonnes; will revisit later
items.quote: So we will revisit it as and when the time comes. But as of now, we are sticking to the 700,000 number.

items.statement: Trading revenue of INR 12.5 crores in Q4 FY25 from HR/CR/GP coil trading for Bokaro market insights; negligible margins, one-quarter only, not more than one quarter in FY26
items.quote: The decline in operating EBITDA margin from 24.5% in Quarter 3 FY '25 to 21.2% in Quarter 4 is primarily due to a revenue of INR 12.5 crores from HR, CR, GP coil trading. This activity was undertaken to gain market insights as part of our preparation for the upcoming Bokaro project and generated negligible margins.

items.statement: Cash Conversion Cycle improved to 56 days in March 2025 from 96 days in March 2024; Net Cash from Operating Activities INR 125 crores in FY25
items.quote: Notably, our Cash Conversion Cycle improved significantly to 56 days in March '25 from 96 days in March '24. This improvement was driven by disciplined working capital management, specifically more efficient inventory utilization aligned with our ongoing capacity expansion and a sharper focus on maintaining lower trade receivables.

items.statement: Net Debt INR 120 crores as of March 2025, up from INR 99 crores in FY24 due to long-term borrowings for capacity expansion; Cash and Cash Equivalents INR 41 crores
items.quote: Net Debt as of March '25 stood at INR 120 crores, up from INR 99 crores in FY '24, primarily driven by an increase in long-term borrowings to support ongoing capacity expansion.

items.statement: Finance cost ~INR 1.3-1.4 crores in Q4 FY25 due to debt repayments and capitalization; expected to return to INR 3-4 crores per quarter going forward
items.quote: So I think it will surely increase to reflect the borrowings. This is also lower because of certain paybacks that we have completed in Quarter 4, certain debts which have been paid back and new loans which have been taken are still low.

items.statement: Bokaro project expected IRR 25%+ and payback not exceeding 5 years; registered for PLI 1.1 Scheme benefits
items.quote: So we expect IRR of 25% plus and a payback not exceeding maybe 5 years.

items.statement: Board recommended final dividend of 0.43 rupees per share for FY25 subject to shareholder approval
items.quote: We are also delighted to announce that the Board has recommended a final dividend of 0.43 rupees per share, subject to shareholder approval.

items.statement: Targeting double-digit revenue growth in FY26, specifically 10%-15%
items.quote: We are expecting a double digit in the revenue growth in FY26, that we will achieve this double-digit.

items.statement: If FY27 order inflow target of INR20,000 crores is achieved, revenue growth could exceed 15%
items.quote: In FY27, if we are achieving projects worth INR20,000 crores, then naturally more than 15% should be there.

items.statement: Order book stood at INR24,346 crores at end of Q4 FY25; 30 projects worth INR14,370 crores under execution as on date
items.quote: Moving on the update on the order book, at the end of Q4 of the order book stood at INR24,346 crores. As on date, the company has 30 projects worth INR14,370 crores that are under execution.

items.statement: FY26 order inflow target is INR20,000 crores across highways, railways, metro, power transmission, ropeway, hydro, tunnel, logistics and telecom
items.quote: The target of this year's order booking is around INR20,000 crores. In the highway sector, there is INR11,500 crores. In the railway, there is 2,000 crores. In the metro, there is INR1,000 crores In the railway and metro, there is 3,000 crores In the power transmission, there is INR2,000 crores. In the ropeway and hydro and tunnel, there is INR3,500 crores. And in logistics and telecom, there is I

items.statement: Expect margins to remain flat at 12%-13% for FY26 and FY27 due to competitive pressure and escalation issues
items.quote: Look, we should still consider the margin as flat. So, there are a lot of things, one is the pressure of our competition, and apart from that, the prices in the market, the way there are escalation issues, we have flat expectations on that.

items.statement: FY25 capex was INR135 crores including corporate office; FY26 capex targeted at INR100-125 crores with INR40-50 crores for corporate office
items.quote: 2025 capex in machinery is in the range of INR70 crores, INR80 crores. But then we are building our corporate office as well. So, total capex which has to be including that corporate office building and machinery is around INR135 crores. INR135 crores, INR134 crores. And for next year, we are targeting another INR100 crores, INR125 crores not more than that.

items.statement: Equity requirement for operational HAM projects is INR2,875 crores pending over next 3 years; targeting INR1,000 crores in FY26 and INR1,000 crores in FY27
items.quote: The balance promoter contribution required to be made for the operational HAM projects is INR2,875.23 crores of which we are expecting a co ntribution of INR1,000 crores in the fiscal year 2026

items.statement: Bidding at up to 46% below estimated cost persists, which is concerning; government has imposed additional performance security for low bids
items.quote: Also, the instances under bidding up to 46% continue to persist. This is although concerning and we are continuing to keep a close watch.

items.statement: Diversifying portfolio across roads, railways, metro, tunnels, power transmission, distribution, ropeway, logistics, telecom; recently added OFC/telecom sector
items.quote: We will continue our strategy of diversifying and balancing our portfolio across various markets and sectors and take the company back to double-digit growth in current financial year '26.

items.statement: Government capital investment outlay for infrastructure increased to INR11.21 lakh crores in Union Budget 2025-26; highway investment projected to grow 1.4x between FY26-FY29
items.quote: As the Central Government continues to focus on infrastructure development, this is evident from the fact that the capital investment outlay for the infrastructure has been increased to INR11.21 lakh crores in the Union Budget of '25, '26.

items.statement: Competitive pressure and escalation issues keep margin expectations flat; no margin growth targeted
items.quote: We are looking at the margin on which we are working now. It is difficult for us to increase the margin. First of all, there is still a lot of underfeeding. So, we are looking at such a margin in the competitive market.

items.statement: InvIT dividend income targeted at INR225-250 crores annually; four operational HAM assets eligible for transfer to InvIT after one-year track record
items.quote: In InvIT, the income that will come, that woul d be in the range of IN R225 crores to INR250 crores on yearly basis

items.statement: BOT project Agra-Gwalior equity commitment INR1,075 crores; appointed date expected by Q3 FY26 (Dec-Jan); initial equity deployment ~10% (INR100 crores) in FY26
items.quote: For Agra-Gwalior, that is BOT projects, we have signed a concession agreement recently, so it takes time, it's a BOT-DBF-BOT project, which takes time of another six months for getting financial closure and all other prerequisites done. So maybe for that Agra-Gwalior, we will be receiving that appointed date in the Q3 quarter.

items.statement: Comfortable deploying INR1,000 crores equity annually in BOT projects; targeting INR2,000-4,000 crores BOT order inflow per year out of INR11,500 crores highway target
items.quote: We can take INR3,000 crores to INR4,000 crores BOT on a yearly basis, where we are comfortable putting INR1,000 crores of equity on a yearly basis.

items.statement: Full-year consolidated PAT margin expanded 5 percentage points from 2% to 7% in FY25.
items.quote: Our margins have moved by 5%, from 2% to 7% for the full year.

items.statement: Renewals contribution margin now estimated at 77-80% due to smarter cost allocation including claims and service costs.
items.quote: At this point, what I would say is, it's somewhere between 77% to 80%, that is where we are.

items.statement: Core business EBITDA margin ~16% for FY25 (12-month rolling); new initiatives EBITDA margin -9% (12-month rolling), both inching up.
items.quote: Right now, the 12-month ruling situation is core is at 16% and new is at -9%. But both are inching upwards clearly, and I think that is what is important

items.statement: Health insurance fresh premium growing 4-5x industry rate; term growing at 12-15% industry rate but PB growing multiples of that.

We are planning that probably the first two quarters of the new financial year will also

items.statement: UAE insurance premium grew 76% YoY and turned profitable; management confident profitability is sustainable.
items.quote: Our UAE insurance premium has grown 76% YoY, and there is a bit of a positive surprise there. That business has turned profitable and I feel confident it's turned profitable kind of forever.

items.statement: Credit business adjusted EBITDA margin 7% for FY25; new initiatives 40% of disbursements for year, 70% for Q4.
items.quote: The adjusted EBITDA margin of the business is 7% for the year.

items.statement: Health insurers focused on combined operating ratio; PB channel attractive due to lower claims and OpEx; no change in economic structure seen so far.
items.quote: clearly now health insurers, like other general insurers, are focused on the combined operating ratio. I think on that basis, if I were to summarize what Yashish said, our channel comes out on a fairly attractive end of the spectrum, and because of that, I think the pressu res obviously will always be there for everyone. But I think those pressures are much more manageable, and at least so far, we

items.statement: Credit strategy: expand secured lending (home loans, LAP, auto), build savings on Paisabazaar for better underwriting, invest in tech-led collections to scale unsecured supply.

We will also start savings area to deepen our understanding about a consumer, and that also allows for better understanding of our customer's risk and means sharper under

items.statement: Q4 contribution margin expansion driven by flat call centre costs vs Q2-Q3 growth and year-end incentive reversals; structural drivers are renewables growth and fresh health negative margin.

So that is the other reason why the margin has expanded because the growth in call centre cost was lower this quarter as compared to the first three quarters.

items.statement: Motor and two-wheeler insurance returned to above 30% growth after period of subdued growth.
items.quote: We have seen other parts of our business -like motor, two-wheeler and travel returning to the above 30% growth which it wasn't for some time.

items.statement: Expect product growth levels to sustain at mid to high-teens in FY26
items.quote: Notwithstanding, I would say, mixed and challenging market conditions, we expect the product growth levels to sustain at mid to high-teens.

items.statement: ESOP charges on steady state basis will be Rs. 5 crores to Rs. 5.5 crores every quarter
items.quote: On a steady state basis, this charge will be in the range of Rs. 5 crores to Rs. 5.5 crores every quarter.

items.statement: Full year adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 136 bps to 11.7% in FY25
items.quote: The impact of all the above led to an adjusted EBITDA expansion of 136 basis points to 11.7% and a YoY increase of 25.9% for the year, to end at Rs. 285 crores.

items.statement: Q4 adjusted EBITDA margin reached 13%, up 183 bps YoY, the highest ever
items.quote: Adjusted EBITDA margins expanded 183 basis points YoY, and we ended the year with a 13% margin in Q4.

items.statement: Gross margins range bound at 58.3% for FY25 vs 58.8% in FY24
items.quote: Gross margins have been range bound and for the year, were at 58.3% versus 58.8% in FY 24.

items.statement: Operating expenses as percentage of revenue down 187 bps in FY25 despite 121 bps higher A&SP spend
items.quote: On the cost side, operating expenses as a percentage to revenue were down 187 basis points, reflecting a very clear operating leverage. This reduction, I must call out, is after the conscious 121 basis points higher investment in A&SP spends.

items.statement: Category growth in water, cleaning, air has decisively inflected to mid to high-teens
items.quote: The categories in which we operate, water, cleaning, etcetera, all have decisively inflected in the trajectory enabled by our own innovation and interventions, increased category visibility and activity and greater recognition by consumers on the importance of health and hygiene.

items.statement: Robotics segment growing 100% YoY for last 3+ years, expected 75-110% in next few years
items.quote: Robotics as a segment has been growing by 100% YoY for the last 3 years or more and we expect that rate to be in the same ballpark of between 75%, 80% to 100%, 110% in the next few years as well.

items.statement: Premium portfolio grew faster than average high-teens product growth in FY25
items.quote: our premium innovations have delivered much higher growth than even what we had estimated. And we now have best -in-class products across th e entire suite of the portfolio

items.statement: Third-party service providers remain a challenge; interventions include call masking, QR code filters, tiered AMCs, consumer campaigns
items.quote: First, I would say, at a very basic level, the first port of call was to make sure that the customer data does not go to these particular players. And hence, we had put in call masking, 1.5 years back.

items.statement: Net surplus of Rs. 284 crores at year-end excluding lease liability
items.quote: Our net surplus at year-end, excluding lease liability, was Rs. 284 crores.

items.statement: A&SP spends grew 25% YoY in FY25 (121 bps increase) and will sustain as business grows
items.quote: Our spends and our investments in advertising and promotion, will sustain as we grow our categories and grow our business.

items.statement: Service revenue showing green shoots after volume growth in AMC unit sales last year
items.quote: we are now seeing green shoots in terms of service revenue. We believe that our interventions in driving filter innovations, building a filter go-to-market, co-opting and partnering our offline network of technicians and business partners, strengthening our D 2C intervention, will augment this growth

items.statement: Vacuum cleaner category adoption accelerating; market size forecast for 2028 now expected in FY26
items.quote: To give an illustration, in vacuum cleaner, what the study forecast as a market size for 2028 will now be happening in FY 26. So, we are almost 2 to 3 years ahead in terms of the category growth compared to the initial estimate and the prognosis.

items.statement: Air purifier growth more than 3x-4x faster than industry estimate per Technopak study
items.quote: Air purifiers for instance, albeit of a small base, we grew significantly faster, more than 3x to 4x faster as compared to the industry growth rate estimated by the independent study.

items.statement: Capex intensity expected to remain stable and slowly taper towards long-term target of 3.5% to 4% of revenue
items.quote: We anticipate going forward that Capex intensity in the business will continue to remain largely stable and slowly taper its way towards our long- term targets of between 3.5% and 4%.

items.statement: Capex expected to hit long-term 4% range in FY27 due to excess automation equipment from Ecom acquisition
items.quote: I think there is a fair bit of chance that in FY27, we will be able to start hitting our long-term Capex targets on the back of excess automation equipment that we will acquire in Ecom acquisition.

items.statement: PTL service EBITDA margin expanded from 3.8% in Q3 FY25 to 10.8% in Q4 FY25, a 700 bps improvement
items.quote: The big change obviously is in the Part Truckload business where service EBITDA margins have grown from 3.8% in Q3 FY25 to 10.8% in Q4 FY25, an expansion of 700 basis points.

items.statement: PTL yields increased to Rs. 11.3 per kg in Q4 FY25 from Rs. 10.9 in Q4 FY24, driven by renegotiation of poor Spoton-era rates and customer confidence
items.quote: Overall, yields have gone up, I think to about Rs. 11.3 per kilo of freight delivered compared to, I think, Rs. 10.9 in Q4 of FY24.

items.statement: PTL growth runway remains large as nearly 80% of industry is unorganized; Delhivery will continue to exploit this headroom profitably
items.quote: The reality is that Delhivery is effectively organizing this industry. And as long as, whatever, nearly 80% of this industry continues to remain unorganized, there's very, very large headroom for growth for Delhivery in this space.

items.statement: Express Parcel margin decline from 18% to 16% is entirely due to parcel mix changes in weight and distance, not structural; expects return to 18% as pricing overhang clears
items.quote: It is entirely down to parcel mix. It's not just the mix in terms of clients, it's also the mix in terms of weight and distances, both of which also have an impact on overall profitability.

items.statement: Ecom Express integration risk is materially lower than Spoton due to 100% customer overlap, smaller relative scale (40% of volumes, <20% of tonnage), and no new technology needed
items.quote: The risks of the integration are also materially lower. As we've discussed in the note that we've put up, there are a couple of key reasons why this is the case.

items.statement: Ecom Express volume retention assumption was conservative at 30%; actual volumes trending higher in March, April, May with organic uptick and customer migration
items.quote: Our assumption was that we would retain close to about 30% of the volumes of the Ecom Express standalone network. From the time that the deal was under consideration up to now in May, we've already seen an organic uptick in the volumes of Delhivery's standalone Express Parcel network.

items.statement: Rs. 300 crore integration cost for Ecom Express acquisition includes lease liabilities with lock-ins and operating losses during rollback; already factored into purchase consideration
items.quote: Our purchase consideration already includes or factors in about Rs. 300 crores of integration costs. These have been considered, and we anticipate that we should be well within this envelope.

items.statement: Rapid commerce dark stores: 18 stores in 3 cities as of Q4 FY25; older stores at 350-400 orders/day; targeting 50 stores in FY26; breakeven at 700-800 orders/day in 4-5 months per store
items.quote: We are in three cities as of this quarter and about 18 dark stores. In terms of orders per dark stores, the older dark stores are now clocking at about 350 to 400 orders per day, while the newer ones, of course, have a certain ramp up time.

items.statement: Working capital days close to target in Express Parcel and PTL; 2-3 days improvement possible in each; Supply Chain Services has significant room; overall 1-2 days improvement expected over 2-3 years
items.quote: I think there is still room to reduce working capital days in these two businesses by two to three days for each of them. However, in our Supply Chain Services business, we have a significant room for improvement.

items.statement: Delhivery Direct on-demand local service launched in Ahmedabad, Delhi, Bombay; expanding to Bangalore in 45 days; supply creation phase causes initial burn, profitability improves at couple thousand orders/day per city
items.quote: We also intend to go live in Bangalore and in Bombay over the next 45 days. So some of these are also SMEs coming into that platform.

items.statement: Management does not provide specific numerical forecasts but expects to continue historical growth trajectory excluding one-time large orders
items.quote: We will keep on doing the same because that is the practical way of doing things. If we just add those one-time orders and then think on top of that how much we want to grow and everything, it becomes really unrealistic.

items.statement: Gross margins dropped to 17% in H1 FY25 due to large one-time orders but recovered to 23-24% in H2; management expects margins to stabilize at H2 levels
items.quote: if you see our gross margins in H1, they were around 17 %, so they have dropped because of those big orders. If you see in H2, we have again main tained our regular 23%, 24% gross margin levels, which we generally are happy with

items.statement: EBITDA margins have declined from ~16% in FY22 as B2B mix increases; management expects margins to stabilize at some level with 0.5-1% fluctuations
items.quote: Of course, everybody knows as this is not the secret, the second thing is also not the secret that ok ay it will go down only up to a certain level, because after that the margins should stabilize, let's say, give or take 0.5% or 1% here and there

items.statement: Added over 50,000 new SKUs in FY25, primarily small low-cost items; launched 186 proprietary products under Robu 2.0 (development boards, drone parts) and 650 products under Orange brand
items.quote: We have added over 50,000 new schemes for new products. So, I just want to highlight one thing here. Though this 50,000 as the number looks very big, but we all have to understand that these are primarily small and low cost items that we have added.

items.statement: Robu 2.0 strategy focuses on filling market gaps with proprietary products rather than replacing existing vendor products; targets categories with pricing between cheap low-quality and expensive premium options
items.quote: we found a gap where we felt that, okay, we can make the modules in India and we can provide a o ne-year warranty, the quality should be good. But the price we can keep right in the middle where there is a customer base who would like to procure these

items.statement: Healthy demand for product offerings continues; electronics becoming bigger part of daily life and government manufacturing policies are key growth drivers
items.quote: The overall year was marked by healthy demand for our product offerings. And we are optimistic that this demand will continue. As we always say, electronics is becoming a big part of life day by day, as well as the alignment of government policies for manu facturing in India

items.statement: Investing in IT infrastructure enhancement and strengthening supplier partnerships for Robu 1.0; doubled R&D efforts for Robu 2.0 proprietary product development
items.quote: Robu 1.0, we are investing in our IT infrastructure enhancement as well as we are strengthening our supplier partnerships to optimize the procurement as well as reducing lead times

items.statement: Inventory increased to Rs. 55-56 crores from Rs. 24 crores due to SKU expansion and timing of shipments; management expects inventory days to increase slightly but margins on new products compensate for inefficiencies
items.quote: So primarily because we have added these products, we expect our inventory days to go slightly up. However, you have to understand, this is a different category of products, and these products have other margins.

items.statement: No current plans for equity dilution; promoter stake at ~69% with no minimum threshold discussed; debt decisions based on category-level ROI exceeding interest cost
items.quote: As of today, we really do not have any plans for dilution, of course, even if we had it would be really stupid to say it loud on this call. But yes, to be very frank, we do not have it as on today.

items.statement: Marketing spend target maintained below 2.5% of online revenue; domestic exhibition participation enabled by revenue growth
items.quote: The marketing state, generally our target is to maintain it below 2.5% of the overall revenue, the online revenu e that is the internal number

items.statement: Corporate sales grew from ~5% in FY20 to ~50% currently; B2B orders are repetitive for production-based requirements but one-time for R&D/lab setups
items.quote: Five years from that moment, today our corporate sales are almost 50% , half of our business. We have strong corporate support or corporate sales team, key account mana gers to support corporate customers

items.quote: We have distribution for many of these things. We are authorized distributor for over 250 brands. However, we are not exclusive distributor for most of them.

items.quote: So, the average order value is around Rs. 4,600 which was around Rs. 4,000 last year, okay. And like before a year ago, like before a y ear to that it was Rs. 4,900

items.statement: Payable days decreased to 18 from 30+ days; management attributes to situational timing of shipments rather than structural change; credit terms with international principals remain difficult
items.quote: So generally we always want to have th e credit from our suppliers, which is whatever based on 30 days, 45 days, 60 days, whatever. In our case, more often than not, we are importing these products

items.quote: I think this time PAT level if you see around 7%. But yes, we are always trying to improve it or at least maintain that.

items.statement: No specific SKU count targets for Robu 2.0; strategy is revenue-driven focusing on categories with market demand and margin potential
items.quote: So, our thought process is more revenue driven rather than the number of SKUs driven, even in Robu 2.0. So right now our key metrics for Robu 2.0 is making the products, launching them in the market and get the first response from the market.

items.quote: we are planning to invest about INR1,000 crores in some of the upcoming projects from Q3 FY '26

items.quote: we are not necessarily going to be bound by development of only logistics-related assets. So we will continue to look at other asset classes

items.quote: I think that's the last event and I think it should not be coming going forward

items.statement: Company is debt-free with INR165 crores cash as of March 2025
items.quote: your company is now debt-free. The cash and cash equivalent is INR165 crores

items.quote: So if I add it up the current value of the land bank, which is not generating any rent for us right now is about INR480 crores? Jatin Chokshi: Yes

items.statement: FY26 presales target INR12,500 crores, over 20% growth
items.quote: In the forthcoming year, we expect the sales number to cross INR12,500 crores, which is more than 20% growth over the current year.

items.statement: Medium-term presales growth target 20%+ annually
items.quote: We message that achieving a 20%-plus growth rate in terms of presales over a medium-term basis is an achievable target.

items.statement: FY26 collections target INR6,000 crores, 35% growth
items.quote: For the coming year, our guidance is to achieve INR60 billion in terms of collections, which is, again, a 35% growth in terms of collections vis-a-vis the current year.

items.statement: Net debt to operating cash surplus not to exceed 0.5x
items.quote: We'll make sure that at no stage our net debt to OCF will not cross 0.5x of the surplus being created by company.

items.statement: FY26 business development spend INR1,200-1,500 crores
items.quote: We do intend to redeploy anywhere between INR1,200 crores to INR1,500-odd crores in terms of fresh business development.

items.statement: Early-stage portfolio 39.3M sq ft with GDV INR575B+

The balance, 60%, which is at a land stage right now, which is roughly 24.6 million

items.statement: FY25 adjusted gross margin 31%, EBITDA margin 14.5%
items.quote: Signature Global adjusted gross profit margin has been also improved to 31% in FY '25 from 28% in FY '24, while adjusted EBITDA margin has improved to 14% in FY '25 from 11% in FY '24.

items.statement: Embedded EBITDA margin on new sales ~35%
items.quote: Whatever sales are being done are happening at -- with an implied EBITDA of 35%.

items.statement: FY25 average realization INR12,457/sq ft, up 6% YoY
items.quote: The company's average sales realization has also improved to INR12,457 per square feet in FY '25 from INR11,762 in FY '24.

items.statement: Like-for-like price rise 15-20% in Sector 37D and 71
items.quote: You may very comfortably assume at least a 15% price rise and almost closer to a 20% price rise in Sector 71 vis-a-vis -- for Phase 2 launches, which vis-a-vis the launch which we did previous year.

items.statement: 70%+ inventory absorption within months of launch
items.quote: about Signatureglobal ( 70% plus inventory is getting absorbed within short span of time. I would say at launch itself, that trends to be a little scary only, but yes within a couple of months, a few months

items.statement: Focus on mid-income housing INR2-4 cr ticket across 3 Gurugram micro-markets
items.quote: Our focus area is getting more into this early mid-income segment. Price points starting from lets say about -- we were little less than INR2 crores and going up to, let's say, INR3.5 crores to INR4 crores.

items.statement: Delhi expansion on hold pending policy clarity from new state government
items.quote: Till the time we don't get absolute clarity on the developability of the underlying land, which one can acquire, will not put in capital.

items.statement: Planning 15% to 20% overall growth for FY26
items.quote: On the growth side, we are planning somewhere around 15% to 20% growth overall.

items.statement: Expect positive ROA by second half of FY26
items.quote: We expect that the positive ROA will be achieved by second half of FY '26 and this year will be a consolidation year with medium growth in business and improved operational numbers.

items.statement: Expect turnaround to profitability by Q3-Q4 FY26
items.quote: We hope by second half of the current fiscal, we will be able to turn around. On a quarterly basis, we will be turning around to somewhat in Q3 and Q4.

items.statement: Comfortable operating at net interest margin around 8% with higher secured loan book
items.quote: So, we will be comfortable operating with a higher secured loan book at a net interest margin of somewhere around 8%.

items.statement: Board approved adding 38 branches in FY26, majority in unbanked rural locations
items.quote: Yes, as per the Board approval, we are adding 38 branches in the financial year, and majority are in the unbanked rural locations and rural locations.

items.statement: Secured loan disbursements stood at INR5,832 crores in Q4 FY25, up 167% YoY
items.quote: During the quarter, we achieved strong traction in secured lending. Secured loan disbursements stood at INR5,832 crores in Q4 FY '25, marking a 167% increase over INR2,187 crores in Q4 FY '24.

items.statement: Net interest margin declined to 6.9% in Q4 FY25 from 10% in Q4 FY24 due to portfolio mix shift and excess liquidity
items.quote: Net interest margin for Q4 FY '25 came down to 6.9% down from 10% in Q4 FY '24 due to the following factors. The shift in the composition of our loan portfolio mix, strategic decision to have excess liquidity and controlled growth in loan book and delinquencies in the high-yielding Micro Loan book.

items.statement: FD rates reduced by 50 bps and savings bank effective rates moderated by around 70 bps
items.quote: On the liability front, F D rates were already reduced by 50 basis points and SB effective rates have been moderated by around 70 basis points by the decision of ALCO

items.statement: Provision coverage ratio strengthened to 80.5% in Q4 FY25
items.quote: The provision coverage ratio also strengthened, standing stable at 80.5%, reinforcing our commitment to demonstrate better asset quality.

items.statement: Technical write-off of INR345 crores in Q4 FY25 and INR1,225 crores for full FY25
items.quote: As a strategy, the bank has done technical write-off of advances amounting to INR345 crores in Q4 and cumulatively by INR1,225 crores in FY '25 to clean up the NPA book.

items.statement: Expect microfinance stress normalization by second half of FY26
items.quote: The reverse trend has already started as we see from the market as well as on our book. So, we are hopeful of reversing the trend by second half of the current fiscal.

items.statement: Secured loans constitute 52% of total loan book as of FY25, up from 29% in March 2024
items.quote: As on FY '25, secured loan constitute of 52% of our total loan book, a marked improvement from 29% as of March 2024.

items.statement: Target to increase secured assets share to 70% by March 2027
items.quote: In line with our long-term strategic road map to increase the share of secured assets to 70% by March 2027, we are pleased to report substantial progress on this front.

items.statement: Expect recovery momentum to build in second half of FY26 supported by favourable macroeconomic conditions
items.quote: While it may take a couple of quarters to definitely mark the bottoming out of curr ent sectoral stress, the ongoing situation is gradually improving. We expect recovery momentum to build in the second half of the year, supported by favourable macroeconomic conditions alongside continued operational discipline and fiscal prudence

items.statement: No specific FY26 guidance given; order book and capacity envelope provide visibility
items.quote: No, no. I mean, look, I think you know what is the planned delivery of all the new expansion capacities. So, you know what is that order book also. items.statement: Total estimated capex over next three years is INR125,000 million for Mission 2028
items.quote: Including these ongoing expansion plans and the new initiatives announced today, as part of our mission 2028, our total estimated capex over the next three years is going to be INR125,000 million.

items.statement: Bulk of 4.8 GW cell and 5.6 GW module line capex in current financial year; BESS and inverter capex phased
items.quote: So, in terms of the capex, the 4.8 gigawatt cell line and the 5.6 gigawatt module line, the bulk of the capex will be incurred in the current financial year because we are anticipating completion by end of this financial year or early next year. For the other businesses, capex will be incurred in a scaled manner. A phased out manner because we are anticipating a phased ramp-up of the battery energ

items.statement: Ingot/wafer capex ~INR400 cr/GW; BESS capex ~INR600 cr for 12 GWh; Inverter capex ~INR100-150 cr
items.quote: So you're right. I mean, in terms of ingot and wafer, the expected capex on a per gigawatt basis is about INR400 crores. So for 10 gigawatt, that would be about INR4,000 crores.
