And for inverters, the cap is would be about INR100 to INR150 cr

items.statement: Order book of 5.3 GW for 12-15 months; pipeline similar or slightly higher
items.quote: So the blended basis, the order book is for about 12 to 15 months and if you look at the order book it is about 5.3 odd gigawatt, which is the order book which is shown on slide number 23.

items.statement: DCR demand envelope very strong; ~65 GW government target over next two years from Surya Ghar, Kusum, CPSU schemes
items.quote: Between these three schemes, the total demand as per the government targets is about 65 gigawatts over the next two years. Even if we take a slightly realistic and more conservative number, there is likely to be very strong demand over the next two years.

items.statement: ALMM on cells from June 2026 will open corporate and IPP segments to DCR
items.quote: And then, of course, with ALM cells being implemented from June 2026 onwards, there will be more market segments, namely the corporate segment, as well as the IPP segment opening up in the next two years.

items.statement: Cell captive consumption ~50% now, expected to reach 100% by 2027 as market becomes fully DCR
items.quote: But also just to add to that the share of captive consumption for cells will go up over a period of time over the next two years because like I said by 2027 the entire market is expected to be almost I would say 100% DCR. So we will go from 50% captive consumption 100% over these two years.

items.statement: Current pricing: DCR modules $0.24-0.25/W, non-DCR $0.17/W, cells domestic $0.14-0.15/W, export lower
items.quote: The DCR modules, the general pricing is around $0.24 to $0.25. Non-DCR modules are at about $0.17. For sales, again, there's a little bit of a variation depending on whether sales are being sold in the Indian market or exports. In the Indian market, prices tend to be around $0.14 to $0.15. Export market prices are a little lower.

items.statement: Expect to maintain margins over next year given order book visibility; no specific margin guidance
items.quote: Insofar as we have the visibility and the order book, which is already committed for the next year, we should be able to, by and large, maintain our margins. But, we are not able to give any guidance as such.

items.statement: Target fixed asset turnover of 2.2x-2.5x by end of capex program
items.quote: But we are expecting, based on all this capex, fixed asset turnover of about between 2.2x to 2.5x by the end of this implementation program.

items.statement: US market uncertainty due to tariff changes and trade treaty negotiations; wait-and-watch approach
items.quote: So I think the problem is that these changes have been coming so thick and fast that everybody is kind of really sitting back a little bit and just trying to make sure they understand the market landscape. Of course, there is also a trade treaty with the US in under negotiation. So I think both from the customer side in the US, as well as the supplier side for us, I think it is better to wait a li

items.statement: 2 GW wafer JV with SAS Taiwan targeting FY27 commissioning; land acquired for 10 GW
items.quote: Yes, so the plan is to commission the 2 gigawatt in FY '27. We have already acquired the land and it's well aligned with what we have targeted to commission this line. This is with the Taiwanese company SAS, which is a JV. And it's a 2 gigawatt line.

items.statement: BESS entry via cell-to-pack + EPC in two 6 GWh phases (FY27, FY28); upstream later if policy supports
items.quote: On BESS, we are getting into to start with a cell-to-pack manufacturing line along with EPC offerings to our IPP customers. And we will be doing this in two phases. The first phase would come up in FY27, and the second in FY28. Each is going to be a 6 gigawatt hour capacity.

items.statement: Capex to be funded via internal accruals and cash; peak leverage ~1.4-1.5x debt/equity, ~2x debt/EBITDA
items.quote: Our expectation is that the total leverage will peak out at about 1.4 to 1.5 times in terms of debt to equity and about two times in terms of debt to EBITDA. So both of which we feel are fairly conservative numbers and easily manageable in the context of the larger industry parameters.

items.statement: 1.4 GW module line commissioned May 16; 1.2 GW TOPCon cell line commissioning next month; 4.8 GW cell + 5.6 GW module on track
items.quote: it's already commissioned as we announced in the opening remarks. And the 1.2 gigawatt TOPCon cell line is getting commissioned next month, which is well in time compared to the data which we had shared in the last quarterly results. We had said it would be commissioned by June 26, and it is on track. On the 4 plus 4, which has now become 4.8 and 5.6, that's enhanced capacity. This is also well on

items.statement: Management expects 15% to 18% revenue growth and 13% to 15% EBITDA margins going forward.
items.quote: continuing the same pattern, we would look at anywhere between a 15% to 18% growth and in between the 13% to 15% EBITDA margins is what we are hopeful of.

items.statement: Capex for FY26 expected at Rs 35-50 crore for adding 250-300 cars and retiring 150-200 cars.
items.quote: Average, I would say around Rs. 35 to Rs. 50 crores depending upon, so lot of our CAPEX is also opportunistic in terms of if some really good opportunity comes in where we feel that it makes sense to invest in our own cars, then we will not shy away from that.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 EBITDA margin stable at ~15% despite competition; CCR mix rose from 37% in Q1 to 45% in Q4 aiding margins.
items.quote: We successfully maintained a stable EBITDA margin of approximately 15% despite rising competition putting pressure on our margin.

items.statement: Strong demand from GCCs, top consultants, and return-to-office trends across IT, BPO, and GCCs driving growth.
items.quote: The rising demand for corporate events, executive travel, on-demand engagements, and of course, the accelerated return to office for the IT and BPO and GCCs has continued to be a cornerstone of our success.

items.statement: CCR revenue share increased from 37% in Q1 to 45% in Q4 FY25; management targets 50-50 mix long term.
items.quote: We have seen in the last few quarters, wherein our proportion of CCR business has risen from 37% in the first quarter to 45% in the last quarter.

items.statement: Onboarded 188 new clients in FY25; total client base ~1,250 in FY24; top 25 clients contribute 48% of revenue.
items.quote: Over the course of the year, we on boarded 188 new clients. This is now a strong validation of a brand's growing credibility and execution strength.

items.statement: Management sees no applicability of gig-worker pension norms as vendors are contracted one-to-one, not gig platform.
items.quote: As far as I know, we are not a gig platform in anyway and where we have one-to-one contracts with our vendors who provide us the services in full.

items.statement: Board recommended final dividend of Rs 2.5 per share for FY25 (~25% of PAT); evaluating inorganic opportunities with cash pile.
items.quote: the Board of Directors and its meeting held today has considered and recommended a final dividend of 2.5 per equity share for the Financial Year ended March 31 st 2025.

items.statement: International revenue grew from Rs 5 crore to Rs 9 crore in FY25; targeting Middle East, Europe, USA, Southeast Asia for exponential growth.
items.quote: the year before we did Rs. 5 crores of international business, this year we have done approximately Rs. 9 crores. So we have seen a good base being built now and we hope to take it higher exponentially this year.

items.statement: Targeting 5% revenue share from exports in FY26
items.quote: We are confident of growing exports meaningfully and are targeting a 5% revenue share from our exports in FY '26.

items.statement: Seamless tube plant capex estimated at INR167 crores with 120,000 tons per annum capacity
items.quote: The total capex for this plant is estimated at INR167 crores, with a capacity to produce 120,000 tons per annum.

items.statement: New extrusion line equipment arrival June 2025, production likely Q2 FY26
items.quote: Equipment arrival is June '25, with production likely to commence in Q2 FY '26.

items.statement: New extrusion technology reduces costs while selling prices remain stable, enhancing margins
items.quote: With the new technology, while selling prices remain stable, costs reduce, which directly enhance our margin.

items.statement: Extruded axle realization benefit estimated at 5% to 6%
items.quote: The overall price benefit that we have on the realization value is close to 5% to 6% that would be the benefit that would be there.

items.statement: Tipping jacks launch by H2 FY26, average realization Rs 1,15,000 per unit, targeting 300-400 units in H2 FY26 and 800 per month eventually
items.quote: The average realization would be Rs 1,15,000 per tipping jacks. This is the basic value. And we are hoping that in H2 of this FY '26, we sell, at least, 300 to 400 tipping jacks or we sell at least, I would say, 800 tipping jacks for the Indian market.

items.statement: April volumes holding strong, consistent with FY25 exit momentum
items.quote: As we step into FY '26, we have seen a steady start to the year, with April volumes holding strong, consistent with the momentum we saw at the close of FY '25.

items.statement: CV market Q1 FY26 good, OEMs pre-buying ahead of October mandate, production volumes strong
items.quote: Q1 has been good, of this year. The reason is that, you know, the OEMs are going in for a mandate in the month of October. And they would be producing these vehicles with air conditioning on all their cabins from the month of July itself.

items.statement: Trailer axle capacity 4,500-5,000 per month currently, rising to 7,500 then 10,000 with new extrusion line
items.quote: 7,500 numbers, firstly. And then we can also go up to 10,000 numbers.

items.statement: Seamless tube plant commercial production expected Q3 FY27, meaningful contribution from FY28
items.quote: The commercial production for this is expected to begin in Q3 FY27, and the business will contribute meaningfully from FY28.

items.statement: No material impact anticipated from tariffs as exposure limited to European OEMs with rigorous validation
items.quote: We do not anticipate any material impacts from the tariffs as our current exposure is largely limited to European OEMs who have onboarded us following a rigorous validation process.

items.statement: Exports need to reach ~15% revenue share to meaningfully drive margin expansion
items.quote: That would be approximately when the exports reach at around 15%. Is when we feel that it would enhance our margins further.

items.statement: Close to 75% of IPO proceeds deployed, balance 25% to be fully utilized within current financial year
items.quote: We would like to inform you that close to 75% of the IPO proceeds have already been deployed by us and the balance 25% will also be fully utilized within the current financial year.

items.statement: Trailer market volumes reduced 3-5% in FY25, but company axle volumes grew from 31,000 to 32,500
items.quote: If we look into our overall business on this axle and suspension, in terms of value we had done INR269 crores of revenue in FY '24. And in FY '25, we have done INR274 crores revenue. The axles more or less have been quite similar. We've sold close to 31,000 axles in FY '24 and we've sold close to 32,500 axles in FY '25.

items.statement: Shift towards air suspensions growing in FY25, full axle range developed from 12-ton to 18-ton except car carrier axle under development
items.quote: Only in the suspension, we feel that the shift towards air suspensions are growing. That is one shift that we've been able to see. Plus, the overall presence with all the product mix now that we have, except the only car carrier axle that is under development, we've developed the entire range of axles and suspensions right from the 12-ton to the 18-ton.

items.statement: Targeting top 5 customer concentration at 55-56% by end of FY26 from current 59%
items.quote: We would like it to be at close to 55%-56% by this year.

items.statement: Management will not provide quarterly or FY26 guidance due to market immaturity; expects to grow faster than the 12% outsourced TAM growth rate with earnings growth faster than revenue growth.
items.quote: I just want to highlight that it's not a mature enough market where I can give you that type of guidance, which is why I will continue to refrain from giving guidance about future performance.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 EBITDA margin reached 31.2%, up from 21.7% in Q4 FY24 and 30.5% in Q3 FY25; full-year FY25 EBITDA margin was 29.7% versus 24% pro forma FY24.
items.quote: EBITDA margins have gone from the 24% pro forma that we had in FY24 to now Q4 FY25 has come in a little off of 31% EBITDA.

items.statement: Adjusted EBITDA margin (ex-ESOP) was 32.8% in Q4 FY25; employee benefit expense fell to 51.8% of revenue from 57.3% in Q3 FY25 and 60.8% in Q4 FY24.
items.quote: If you look at adjusted EBITDA, which excludes ESOP cost, that's still at 32.8% for the quarter.

items.statement: No explicit capex guidance; cash flow used for debt repayment and potential small outcome-oriented deals, not large acquisitions.
items.quote: We might have some uses of capital periodically in these type of unique outcome orientation deals where we might be able to participate in the outcomes that we create for our customers.

items.statement: Signed five major platform deals in Q4 FY25: Sky Lakes (mid-size health system, full care enablement platform + hospital RCM), Western Washington Medical Group (full platform), Platinum Derm (PE-owned dermatology platform, full platform), O
items.quote: Sky Lakes has actually committed to the entire IKS Care enablement platform for their employed physician base.

items.statement: Pipeline at all-time high across three segments (mid-size health systems, large health systems, independent medical groups); buying cycles still immature, conversion rates not predictable.
items.quote: The pipeline seems to suggest that we are at an all-time high in terms of where the pipeline stands.

items.statement: Cross-sold IKS platform features to four large health system customers in AQuity install base; AQuity customer count reduced from 850 to ~700, targeting 550-600 by end of FY26.
items.quote: I'm happy to report that we've been able to cross-sell features of the IKS platform to four significantly large health system customers in the AQuity install base.

items.statement: Outcome-based pricing model (percentage of customer revenue) combined with tech-led autonomy drives margin superiority; Medicaid reimbursement growth contraction seen as tailwind, not headwind.
items.quote: IKS built a business model where our pricing was outcome based. We get paid as a percentage of the customer's revenue.

items.statement: Competitive intensity rising due to $45B equity investment in point-solution vendors (2021-2024); management believes platform breadth and deep data relationships provide moat.
items.quote: Second, naturally, that's going to create competitive intensity. And so, yes, we should expect significant competitive intensity backed by large pools of capital in these spaces.

items.statement: Net debt reduced from INR860 cr (FY24) to INR560 cr (FY25) despite INR139 cr Palomar performance guarantee; target is minimal leverage.
items.quote: If you look at our net debt position, again, we have been able to bear it down quite significantly. If you look at FY24, we ended the year at INR860 crores. From there, we have been able to bring it down to INR560 crores.

items.statement: Effective tax rate expected to rise to 21-22% in FY26 from 19% in FY25 due to loss of SEZ tax break.
items.quote: Please expect ETR for the next year to be around 21% to 22%, because we will be loosing some tax breaks on one of our SEZ units.

items.statement: Headcount reduced from 13,241 (FY24) to 12,661 (Q4 FY25) driven by AQuity model transformation (onshore to offshore) and tech deployment; non-linear revenue-to-headcount growth to continue.
items.quote: Headcount, you will note that we were at 13,241 at the end of last year. From there, in Q4 FY25, we ended the year at 12,661.

items.statement: Ramp-up for full-platform deals typically 4-7 months; single-feature implementations 3-4 months.
items.quote: Typically what happens is full-platform execution takes somewhere between 4 to 7 months, give or take, depending on the size of the customer.

items.statement: Targeting at least 50% top-line growth and at least 100% PAT growth for FY26 on a full-year basis
items.quote: Yes. So, on our top-line, we've already, during the last call, we've already given quite considerable growth trajectory, at least 50% plus top-line growth from what we see today. That's one way we are targeting. On a PAT level, we are targeting at l east 100% growth from where we are today for the next year on full year

items.statement: Expecting ramp-up from Q1 FY26 with sizable growth in H2 due to product launches and approvals in September-October
items.quote: Yes. So, we feel there is a ramp up going to happen from Q1 itself, but it will be sizable on the second half of this year because of certain product launches, certain approvals that are expected, certain niche products that are going to be approved in the mon th of September-October timeframe

items.statement: Capex for FY26 is INR250 crores
items.quote: We have that in the presentation, 250 crores.

items.statement: Planning to launch around 31 ANDA products in regulated market and 23 CDMO-CMO products in FY26
items.quote: As of now, we are planning to launch around 31 ANDA products in the regulated market in FY '26 and 23 CDMO-CMO products in the current financial year.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin sustainable in 24-26% range annually; regulated market EBITDA margin upwards of 40%; emerging market EBITDA margin target 15-16% in next two years
items.quote: We continue to maintain our margin in the range of 24% to 26% sustainable on annual basis, which we have been doing so far.

items.statement: Regulated market EBITDA margin consolidated upwards of 40%
items.quote: No, they would be upwards of 40%.

items.statement: Emerging market EBITDA margin at about 7% currently, likely to improve significantly next year, targeting 15-16% in next two years
items.quote: We have also delivered on our strategy of improving the profitability in the emerging market busin ess with EBITDA margin at about 7% curren t y ear, which is likely to improve significantly in the next year.

items.statement: Seeing healthy growth in regulated market business with good visibility for next year from existing portfolio, pipeline, and CDMO contracts in hand
items.quote: Our existing portfolio and the pipeline in the own product segment coupled with the contracts in hand on CDMO-CMO segment gives us a good visib ility for the next year in the regulated market as we speak.

items.statement: Emerging market portfolio to reach 650+ registered products by end of FY27; shift towards niche molecules and changed go-to-market strategy to drive higher realizations and profitability
items.quote: With the current product pipeline, we intend to have a portfolio of 650 plus registered products across all emerging markets by the end of FY '27. We expect the shift in our product portfolio towards more niche molecules and the change in our go-to-market strategies to lead to considerable increase in the realizations.

items.statement: Revenue mix to remain steady at ~70% regulated, ~30% emerging markets on annualized basis
items.quote: We will continu e to have about 70% revenue coming from regulated market and about 30% revenue coming from emerging market.

items.statement: US FDA-approved manufacturing facility in the US insulates from tariff risk; only one product sourced from China with two years API inventory; pharma currently exempt from tariffs
items.quote: Our US FDA-approved manufacturing facility located in the U.S., through wh ich we cater to our regulated markets, gives us a considerable advantage versus players who d o not have the manufacturing footprint in the U.S. Hence, we should be insulated from any ta riff-related risk which other manufacturers might face.

items.statement: Equalization and most-favored-nation pricing policies likely targeted at innovators; generic packaging differences (blister vs bottle) make equalization complex; company expects to be fine
items.quote: Now, when we talk about equalization, now equalization is you can only equalize w hen the product, product packaging, product franchise is equivalent to it is sold in oth er markets. Most of the products that are sold in the US and other markets, they do not have the same packaging. Europe is all blister packaging, most of it is blister packaging. US is all bottle packaging, right?

items.statement: Injectable capex in US planned for end of FY26; oral solids expansion ongoing with third line installing, fourth planned; India greenfield site for semi-regulated and regulated support being finalized
items.quote: Currently, as we speak, the capex will be planned sometime end of this year. We are increasing our oral solids capacities. As I mentioned in my opening remar k, we already got two installed lines. We are getting third line installed as we speak and four th line is being planned

items.statement: New API facility 100-120 MTPA capacity; production commenced March 2025; targeting US FDA trigger by Q2 CY26; strategic for backward integration, not a separate business vertical
items.quote: Yes, so the new facility is about 100 to 120 metric ton product ion capacity. We have already started production, but it will be in a full scale probably in about a month's time, the new facility. We expect in Q2 CY26 for US FDA trigger for our API facility

items.statement: CDMO-CMO portfolio at 22 products with 69 in pipeline; strong order book and visibility; only 4-5 players in US with end-to-end capability for controlled substances
items.quote: Our portfolio now stands at about 22 products. We have around 69 products in CDMO-CMO pipeline as of March 2025 at various levels of which many of them wi ll be commercialized in the fisc al y e ar as w e wi ll keep on adding our

items.quote: We have acquired 14 ANDAs from Dr. Reddy's, one from Breckenridge. This takes our portfolio to about 61 ANDA products, of which large number of ANDAs have potential o f c a t e r i n g t o l a r g e government contracts in the U.S., giving us an edge to enhance our market share.

items.statement: Management expects 30-35% YoY revenue growth over the next three years.
items.quote: Together with these, we believe that 30% to 35% YoY should be a very reasonable growth target that we have kept for ourselves.

items.statement: Management expects 3-4% profitability enhancement through margin-accretive offerings over the next three years.
items.quote: We believe that our strategic investments in infrastructure and product development, backed by our 30 plus years of technical know-how, position us to capture an expected CAGR of 30%, 35% over the next three years, while enhancing profitability by 3% to 4% through margin accretive offerings.

items.statement: Capex spend was INR 69 lakhs as of March 31, 2025, against planned INR 51 crores; procurement started in May after facility redesign.
items.quote: As of 31st, March, we had shown a spend of approximately, I think, INR 69 lakhs only versus INR 51 crores of CapEx spend approximate INR 51 crores of CapEx spend.

items.statement: Mambattu facility scaled up from 5 to 10 tanks; specialty gas plant also redesigned; completion target remains October 30, 2025.
items.quote: the Mambattu facility was designed for five tanks as a five-tank facility. We have scaled it up to a 10-tank facility. The helium plant also, the specialty gas plant also, initial designs were different. Then, now basically, as you come into the current year and as you see the opportunities coming in front, so you will reengineer and rechange the design to suit what would now appear to be a better

items.statement: Current EBITDA and PAT margins are excellent for a non-molecule manufacturer; new facilities expected to enhance margins significantly from next year.
items.quote: Currently, EBITDA margin and the PAT margins are much higher than for a company like us, not physically currently manufacturing the molecule. These are excellent EBITDA and PAT margins that we have right now. No one in the similar grouping would enjoy these kind of margins, number one.

items.statement: New Mambattu facility dedicated to HFO blending; specialty gas unit for semiconductor, fiber optic, medical and defense gases; helium sales to start immediately on commissioning.
items.quote: This facility is not like the other four facilities because it's going to be designed only for HFO and HFO blending. All the next generation, as the quota starts kicking in and as all companies after, say, 2027, all the companies will start switching over to new products, '26, '27. They will start moving to HFO.

items.statement: HFO demand expected to grow phenomenally from next year as industry shifts from HFCs; semiconductor gases, helium, argon, NFC seen as sunrise segments with 7-10 year growth runway.
items.quote: HFO currently don't have that much reach or scale of volume. But now from next year, it is expected to grow phenomenally. So, this gives us opening to the new businesses that are going to start now.

items.statement: Cost fluctuations managed via high inventory levels and advance planning; raw material mostly sourced from China due to global supply concentration; cost pass-through easier in aftermarket (70% of current sales) than OEM contracts.
items.quote: So usually, it all boils down to having higher inventory levels at the correct pricing. So you have your raw materials stocked up. So that allows you to offset any short-term fluctuations.

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions (e.g., Pahalgam incident) have subdued a strong start to FY26; China supply concentration remains a structural risk; quota cuts can spike prices 25%+ suddenly.
items.quote: This current, little border issue that after Pahalgam that happened, unfortunately, it has had its ripple effect on business. It's not that it's not, without totally without consequence. So from what was a sterling quarter that was starting off, it got subdued very badly, number one.

items.statement: Backward integration planned for 1-2 molecules (e.g., R32) using fluorspar from Mexico/Vietnam to reduce China dependence; forward integration via 6 pan-India locations enables just-in-time delivery and 1/3 logistics cost vs peers.
items.quote: But in the core segment also, we would like to go in for backward integration where we go into manufacture of at least one or two of the molecules. So focus is there also and we are working on that also.

items.statement: Honeywell distributorship is perpetual non-exclusive but functions as exclusive; HFO sales restricted to Stallion in India giving first-mover advantage.
items.quote: It's sort of perpetual only. There's no renewal. Meaning, it's that's more paperwork. So we've been with Honeywell 20 years. 2006 till date, we are with Honeywell.

items.statement: Cash cycle improving via vendor financing/bill discounting (e.g., Dow via Citibank no-recourse); new customers on 120-160 day terms, average currently 90 days.
items.quote: Now we moved all of them into vendor finance and discounting. So the payment cycle should improve significantly, but currently, they are at 90 days average.

items.statement: Current sales mix: 70% aftermarket, 30% OEM; will shift to 100% OEM for new HFO and specialty gas segments initially.
items.quote: Currently, aftermarket reliance is 70%, OEM is 30%. Now when we start with the Specialty Gas segment and the HFO segment, again, we will move 100% back to OEM because HFO, there's no aftermarket, it's all OEM.

items.statement: HPC business targets minimum 15% year-on-year growth and aims to double in about four and a half years
items.quote: And the target is that we should be double of where we currently are, at this rate in about four and a-half years' time.

items.statement: Ethnic Foods category targets 8% to 10% growth and aims to recover market share
items.quote: we should not only be able to arrest it, but we will continue to grow between 8% to 10% growth that we have set for ourselves.

items.statement: Edible Oil segment targets 2% to 4% EBITDA margin range, aiming for higher end
items.quote: we target, for example, in the Edible Oil segment this year we have done overall 4.64%. And we have stated that the range of margins is 2% to 4%.

items.statement: Food business targets 8% to 10% EBITDA margin
items.quote: Food margin 8% to 10%, we should pretty much definitely meet.

items.statement: HPC business targets 16% to 18% EBITDA margin with 200 bps expansion expected in Q1 or Q2 FY26
items.quote: somewhere around the Q1 or Q2 of FY '26 is what we are estimating that we should start to see some results. So the idea is that somewhere around next fiscal that we should see in the 1st Quarter or 2nd Quarter, I think we should start to see the impact of 200 basis points expansion in the margin.

items.statement: Oil palm plantation targets 0.5 million hectares over next five years with 40,000 hectares in FY26 and 125,000 hectares in FY27
items.quote: this year the target is that we should do 40,000 hectares, next year the pick-up will be 125,000 hectares, and thereafter it will continue on that same momentum trajectory.

items.statement: Oil palm plantation expects 10% year-on-year revenue growth in FY26 and minimum 25% year-on-year growth from FY28 onwards
items.quote: each year we are expecting that this revenue to grow close to about 10% year-on-year, as the more plantations come in. And the momentum will pick-up in fiscal '26-'27 when we expect what the pick-up in the plantation driver that we took two years back, some of that should start coming on-stream. And '27-'28 onwards, we should see minimum 25% growth year-on-year on the oil palm plantation side.

items.statement: Edible Oil volume growth expected at 2% to 3% in FY26
items.quote: On Edible Oil, though, the growth that we see in volumes is typically between 2% and 3%, and we are pretty confident of getting it back this year.

items.statement: Regular capex targeted at Rs. 125-150 crores per year; Rs. 1,000 crores anticipated over two-year window in years four and five
items.quote: large part of our CAPEX, the regular CAPEX spend that we have is close to about Rs. 125 crores to Rs. 150 crores per year is our targeted CAPEX, which is required for the routine sort of maintenance cost and addition of few machines here or there. In year three and four we are expecting almost over two years' window, we will invest close to about Rs. 1,000 crores of spend we are

items.statement: HPC segment Q4 FY25 EBITDA margin was 15.74%
items.quote: As an update on the HPC business, the quarterly revenue for the HPC business segment amounted to Rs. 728.48 crores and the EBITDA margin was 15.74%.

items.statement: Oil palm plantation FY25 EBITDA margin was 16%, expects consistent 16% to 18% range
items.quote: this year, in FY '25, our revenue from palm plantation business was Rs. 1,263 crores, the EBITDA was Rs. 203 crores, which is 16%, and this is in comparison to Rs. 951 crores FY '24 and Rs. 156 crores EBITDA. As we maintain that it is always generally a pretty consistent annuity business for us, and in general we are able to maintain the margin construct. So we are pretty confident of this being i

items.statement: Food & FMCG segment FY25 EBITDA margin was 8.35%, down from 13.18% in FY24 due to high commodity prices
items.quote: This year also we did about 8.35% margin overall on the Foods portfolio, FMCG. So, we are pretty much in the range of what we have projected. But yes, you are right that it has dropped from 13.18% last year to 8.35%, but this would be more a temporary phase, we are expecting for us to tide over it.

items.statement: Urban demand expected to recover from second half of fiscal year due to income tax relief and falling food inflation; rural demand remains strong
items.quote: We are optimistic about the demand revival in the Food,FMCG and HPC categories in both rural and the urban India. The falling cost basket of Food inflation, along with lower taxes and other supportive government policies is likely to aid a recovery in mass market urban demand. This impact should be visible from the second half of the fiscal year.

items.statement: High commodity prices (palm oil up 30-40%, wheat up 12%, sugar up 2-5%, paddy up 5-8%) squeezed Food margins in FY25
items.quote: One is very clearly the high commodity prices. So palm oil, for example, this year was almost elevated between 30% and 40% almost through the year. The sugar prices were up between 2% to 5%, the wheat prices were up 12% last year. Similarly, we saw at the wholesale level, the commodity inflation, the paddy prices were up between 5% to 8% consistently.

items.statement: ESOP cost for FY25 was ~Rs. 122 crores (Rs. 10 crores per month)
items.quote: This year we have debited near about Rs. 122 crores, Rs. 10 crores per month as ESOP cost for the fair valuation adjustment of ESOPs into the cost.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin target ~20%+ similar to FY25, subject to market conditions

items.statement: Pellet order book ~45 days; early Q1 had price jump but end Q1 prices back to Q4 levels
items.quote: So usually, we have an order book of almost 45 days. So early Q1, there was a price jump, but end of Q1, there'll be again a price low. So you can consider Q4 and Q1 prices on the same level for pellets, more or less.

items.statement: FY25 consolidated EBITDA margin 22%, PAT margin 15%; net cash INR863 cr as of March 31, 2025
items.quote: Despite challenges, EBITDA margin and PAT margin stood strong at 22% and 15%, respectively. The company has a net cash of INR863 crores as on March 31, 2025, with healthy balance sheet.

items.statement: Imported coal landed cost Q4 ~INR11,750/t; Q1 ~INR11,500/t; Q2 onwards sharp drop ~10% due to international correction

items.quote: See, you have to consider region-wise, if you see the Eastern market, which is Bengal and Odisha, there is oversupply of pellets because of additional capacity being installed, plus limited sources of fines available, which is mainly the Odisha market. items.statement: New structural rolling mill commissioned (1.5 lakh tons FY26); PGCIL approval for MS grade obtained, HT grade inspection done, approval expected by June

We hope to get their approval by end of this quarter, which is June. And from July onwards, we will offer the entire range of PGCIL-approved products in the market to our end consumers.

items.statement: Ari Dongri mine EC expansion (2.35 to 6Mt) delayed due to third-party report requirement; confident of approval by Q3 FY26; Boria Tibu mine to resume end of May

items.statement: No plan B needed for Ari Dongri EC; third-party report expected by first half June, then public hearing and mining plan filing

items.quote: Yes. This INR300 crore borrowing, which we have proposed and took the approval of the Board is in order to manage the cash flow. In that, our actual requirement may not be there to the extent. We may draw some amount, we may not draw.

items.quote: So FY '27, we are targeting the entire capacity. So right from 2.35 million, so we're targeting about 4 million of iron ore and 1.5 million of BMQ for my beneficiation plant from FY '27. Plus FY '27 will also give us the entire volume of the new pellet plant.

items.statement: New steel plant at Tilda to be greenfield section mill (light to medium then medium to heavy); land allotment expected in 4-6 weeks, EC by Q2 FY26

items.statement: Capex guidance of INR 190 crores for FY26
items.quote: We are expecting to have a capex spend of about INR 190 crores for FY '25-'26.

items.quote: Our PBT stood at 18.2% of product sales in FY 2024 -25, and we maintained healthy EBITDA margins of 22.8% for Q4 FY 2024-25 and 22.1% for the year.

items.quote: We are expecting to have a capex spend of about INR 190 crores for FY '25-'26. This would be more towards expansion of our Oragadam plant and introduction of some lines at some of the other plants for export support and all that.

items.quote: This regulatory shift has opened a significant opportunity for retrofitting existing vehicles through the aftermarket channel, and we anticipate strong T-EBS/T-ABS adoption via this route in FY 2025–26.

items.quote: going forward with the 2 entities, we expect to see continued improvements in both EBITDA, PBT, yes; as well as higher growth with the demerged entities.

items.statement: Capex expected to double from current INR130-150 crores in current financial year and continue for next 2 years
items.quote: We are expecting that to double in the current financial year and continue with that with for -- probably for the next 2 years.

items.quote: if you look at FY '24, our EBITDA margins for automotive was around 18%. And industrial was around 17%. So we kind of expect similar numbers for FY 24-25.

items.quote: cash flow down mainly due to net working capital change in this quarter, but it will -- we expect that to come back strongly by next quarter and next year.

items.quote: We expect margins to show stability in this financial year from, you know, the current delivered numbers and we hope to bring the margins slowly back towards the delivered earlier numbers.
