items.statement: Aspire to double sales over next 3 years and inch closer to $1 billion company ambition
items.quote: As stated earlier, we want to double our sales as a company over the next 3 years and inc h closer to our ambition of being a $1 billion company

items.statement: Capex outlook for FY26 around Rs.200 crore, majorly in Pipes (40%), Parador (20%), Walls (20%), Roofs and Construction Chemicals (20%)
items.quote: So not factoring in any inorganic or any major new plant that we may get on to. But given the plans that we have, it's in the zone of a bout Rs.200 crore for this year

items.statement: OPVC Phase 1 capex Rs.35-40 crore, revenue potential north of Rs.100 crore, capacity ~5,000 tons per annum
items.quote: Capex will be in the zone of about Rs.35 to 40 crore for just Phase 1. This does not include the cost of technology acquisition and so on.

items.statement: Chennai AAC Block Line 2 commissioned, doubling capacity to 4 lakh cubic meters per year, capex Rs.40-45 crore
items.quote: So, by the time this is completed, it will be in the zone of about Rs.40 crore to Rs.45 crore.

items.statement: Parador order pipeline remains strong, early gains from strategic push into newer markets
items.quote: Parador's order pipeline remains strong, and we are beginning to see early gains from our strategic push into newer markets.

items.statement: Parador steady-state operating margin target 8-10% at pre-war revenue levels; Q4 FY25 annualized run rate ~EUR 160 million with margins 4-5%
items.quote: For us, the steady-state margin and if we start replicating the revenue numbers that we were doing pre-war situation is in the 8% to 10% range at an operating margin level.

items.statement: Roofing margin goalpost 15-16% first; FY25 at 12-13% range; 18-20% too far currently
items.quote: I think the first psychological milestone to cross is 15%, 16%. And all of it, I would say, and without qualification is to do with the prevailing price conditions and the competitive nature of the market.

items.statement: OPVC operating margins expected in mid-teens
items.quote: These are much better than the traditional PVC pipes. So, we should be in the mid-teens as far as the operating margins for that particular segment is concerned.

items.statement: PVC resin prices near decadal lows; inventory losses Rs.15 crore in FY25; antidumping duty and BIS standards may support price recovery
items.quote: We did, and you would recall, in this year, at an aggregate level, the price erosion has been north of 10%. And hence, yes, there were inventory losses to the tune of about Rs.15 crore at an aggregate level.

items.statement: Roofing prices dropped 1.5-2% in FY25; demand sentiment flat, volumes similar or slightly better but prices not encouraging
items.quote: So there has been a drop of about 1.5% to 2%.

items.statement: B2G demand showing green shoots with orders flowing in UP under Amrut 2.0; JJM revival expected in FY26 with increased government allocation
items.quote: In fact, in some segments in some states, there are orders flowing in. So, for instance, the state of UP, not in the traditional JJM, but the Amrut 2.0, which is a similar scheme, but more towards the urban areas, that has picked up.

items.statement: Pipes mix: CPVC 30%, PVC 55-57%, value-added 10%; target CPVC + value-added 37-40%
items.quote: So, I would say between CPVC and value-added, we are still at about the 37% to 40% range, and that's the right mix for us to continue in our portfolio.

items.statement: Parador commercial share 12-14% in FY25 (growing), non-Central Europe sales 18-20%
items.quote: So commercial will still be about, if I'm not wrong, in the 12% to 14% range and growing because the same number last year was lower. Non-Central European sales will be in the zone of about 18% to 20%.

items.statement: Cautious on FY26 due to macroeconomic, tariff and geopolitical uncertainties across India, Europe and global markets
items.quote: As we enter FY26, w e remain cautious of the prevailing macroeconomic tariff and geopolitical uncertainties across India, Europe and the global markets

items.statement: Internal IRR benchmark 18-20%, payback 3-4 years for capital deployment
items.quote: We normally monitor payback of 3 to 4 years and IRR is in the range of around 18% to 20%.

items.statement: Mid-single digit revenue growth expected for FY26 given industry headwinds and climatic uncertainties
items.quote: We are looking for mid single digit level growth this year given the industry headwinds and the uncertainties of the climatic situation.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin guidance maintained at around 25% for FY26
items.quote: We would be looking at in the range of around 25%.

items.statement: Effective tax rate expected around 23% for FY26
items.quote: the effective tax rate should be around 23%.

items.statement: FY26 capex guided at Rs. 800-900 crore, similar to FY25
items.quote: FY25-26 CAPEX should be in the range of around Rs. 800 - Rs. 900 crore

items.statement: Capex split: ~Rs. 100 crore for PI Health Sciences pharma business, balance for Ag-Chem manufacturing
items.quote: broadly in the Rs. 800 - Rs. 900, when you look at it to around Rs. 100 crore would be in the PI HS, the pharma business and the balance will be in the manufacturing in the Ag-Chem business.

items.statement: Order book estimated around $1.3 billion plus as of Q4 FY25
items.quote: Est around 1.3 billion USD plus, but we don't have exact number in front.

items.statement: Gross margin guidance for FY26 at 50-52% depending on product mix
items.quote: this will remain around 50% - 52% depending on the final product mix that we are able to achieve.

items.statement: Pharma business built with gross margins of 60-65%, operating leverage to improve profitability with scale
items.quote: the business is built with gross margins of around 60%-65%. And with the scale up of the revenue, the operating leverage will start kicking in and we should have better profitability at the bottom-line too.

items.statement: Price softening in Ag-Chem exports due to input cost reductions passed through to customers
items.quote: there is obviously some price softening and that is on the basis of input cost softening. So over last 1 to 1.5 year, post COVID, input prices have come down and given our business model of CSM Exports, where these input cost improvements are also passed through and therefore the pricing of some of these existing products have also come down

items.statement: Domestic branded business targeting 15-20% growth (2x industry average) over next 2-3 years
items.quote: we are looking at a 15%-20% growth which is 2x of the industry average growth.

items.statement: Export business expected to pick up from H2 FY26 with new product launches
items.quote: we believe that from H2, the export business would start picking up well with the launch of our new products and the growth in those areas.

items.statement: Biologicals revenue target of 5x in 5 years from current ~Rs. 250 crore to Rs. 1,000-1,200 crore
items.quote: today we are at something around Rs. 250 crore right now. This would probably move up to 5x, it will be Rs. 1,000 to Rs. 1,200 crore in the next 5 years.

items.statement: New products contribute 15-18% of Ag-Chem exports; biologicals 18-20% of domestic agri-brands
items.quote: When we are talking about new product launches and their contribution to our Ag-Chem export business is around 15% to 18%. And similarly, the biologicals business to our Ag-Chem brands business accounts for around 18% to 20%.

items.statement: Pharma EBITDA breakeven not expected in FY26; positive trends seen over FY26-FY28
items.quote: Definitely, it will take time over next few years because as we are scaling up , the developmental spend will also go up. So while EBITDA breakeven is on the horizon, but it will definitely take more time, not in FY26.

items.statement: Two multi-product plants under construction; one expected to commission this year, next by March next year
items.quote: we are doing our CAPEX with two multi -products plants which are under construction. We expect to commission one this year, maybe the next in the beginning of March next year.

items.statement: Expect 30-40% revenue increase and 80-90% EBITDA improvement from existing complex over 3-4 years as renovations complete
items.quote: From the existing complex that we are currently operating, we expect a 30% to 40% increase in revenue as we see the renovation being completed, which could lead to almost an 80% to 90% improvement in the EBITDA.

items.statement: Target 3x FY25 EBITDA within 3-4 years including contribution from new 200-key Madhapur hotel
items.quote: Having said that, we also, in the same 3-4 year timeline, we are looking at opening our next hotel, which is in Madhapur, which is a 200-key inventory, in which case we can see our EBITDA from that also contribute to this and potentially even go to about 3x of what we have reported for this financial year.

items.statement: Plan INR120 crores capex over next 2-3 years for Marriott upgrades, convention center expansion, Courtyard completion, and F&B renovations
items.quote: The first, we expect a capex renovation of about INR120 crores over the next two to three years. This is mainly for the upgradation of Marriott, which is a 295 room hotel. The upgradation of the convention center, which is about 10,000 square feet, which will be converted to a 20,000 square feet convention center.

items.statement: Expect capex payback within 2-2.5 years based on HVS Anarock study projections
items.quote: And based on the reports that we've received and EBITDAs that we expect to have once the renovation is entirely completed, this amount that we are infusing as capex is possibly going to be returned within two to two and a half years.

items.statement: Plan QIP of INR100-120 crores for Madhapur hotel; prefer minimal debt on books
items.quote: But having said that, because we also have another project in Madhapur planned, we are looking at another QIP exercise which would raise another INR100 crores to INR120 crores into the company.

items.statement: May add INR50 crores debt over 3-4 years; target net debt/EBITDA ~1x at INR100 crores EBITDA
items.value: INR50 crores additional debt; ~1x net debt/EBITDA
items.quote: So, the debt level which is currently on the books of the company is about INR50 crores. So, we possibly maybe have to add another INR50 crores of debt over the next 3 years, 4 years. And we expect once the renovation to be completed and all three projects, all three properties are operational, to have EBITDA close to INR100 crores. So, that's possibly putting the ratio at about 1 is to 1.

items.statement: Expect EBITDA margin to breach and sustain above 30% post-renovation; new Madhapur hotel to drive margins higher
items.quote: Particularly with the renovation in mind, we've managed now to get closer to the 30% mark. And in fact, once the renovation is completed and our ADRs further improve, we only see this EBITDA margin, breaching that 30% mark.

items.statement: Phase 1: Add 56 rooms, spa, gym, rooftop bar at Courtyard; Phase 2: Expand Marriott convention center to 20,000 sq ft, upgrade 168 rooms; Phase 3: Upgrade 4 F&B outlets, executive lounge, Altitude venue, lobby, 127 rooms at Marriott
items.quote: Phase 1 of this plan will include the addition of 56 new guest rooms to be added to the courtyard by Marriott, along with a spa, gym, and a bar. Phase 2 will consist of the upgradation of 168 rooms of Marriott and Convention Center in Marriott to 20,000 square feet from present 10,000 square feet.

items.statement: Signed operating agreement for new 200-room hotel on 7,000 sq yards in Madhapur, Hyderabad; construction start pending land conversion and approvals
items.quote: Further strengthening our partnership with Marriott, we have recently signed a new operating agreement with Marriott Hotels India Private Limited, along with other related ancillary agreements for the upcoming hotel project in Madhapur, Hyderabad. The proposed property spans approximately 7,000 square yards and is expected to feature around 200 rooms.

items.statement: Marriott ADR INR6,864 (+1.66% YoY); Courtyard ADR INR6,758 (+2.15% YoY); expect significant ADR growth post-renovation flowing to EBITDA
items.value: Marriott ADR INR6,864; Courtyard ADR INR6,758
items.quote: For the Marriott property, the average daily rate stood at INR6,864, marking a year-on-year growth of 1.66%. At Courtyard, the ADR was INR6,758, reflecting a 2.15% increase.

items.statement: Courtyard RevPAR declined 6.29% YoY due to ongoing renovation temporarily affecting availability and operational efficiency
items.quote: And Courtyard reported a RevPAR of INR4,908, reflecting a decline of 6.29%, but this is largely attributable to the ongoing renovation work, which temporarily affected the property's availability and operational efficiency.

items.statement: Long-term goal to reach 1,000 rooms; actively evaluating brownfield, distressed assets, and commercial conversions in Tier I cities (Bangalore, Goa, Pune, Chandigarh)
items.quote: High level objective of the company in the future in the long term goal is to reach 1,000 rooms.

items.statement: Revenue guidance of Rs. 925-930 crores for FY26, representing ~15% growth
items.quote: I think the guidance what we had given is a 15% increase in revenues should be around Rs. 925 crores, Rs. 930 crores for this year.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 18-20% for FY26
items.quote: Yes. We stand to maintain 18% to 20% our margin guidance, we stick to that.

items.statement: Capex of Rs. 50 crores planned for FY26 across sinks, fabrication and built-in appliances
items.quote: So, for the current year we have envisaged CAPEX of about Rs. 50 crores which includes expansion of overall from sinks to fabrication to built in Appliances.

items.statement: Signed deal with US major retail chain via KARRAN for additional 150,000 quartz sinks across 1,800+ US stores
items.quote: As informed earlier through a press release, a key highlight for Q4 '25 had been a significant deal with a US major retail chain through our customer KARRAN, which is going to add additional capacity and supply of 150,000 quartz sinks across spread 1800 plus stores across United States.

items.statement: Quartz sink capacity utilization at 67%, targeting 85-90% within 3-4 months by restarting 250,000 unit plant
items.quote: What would be the challenge? I think the biggest challenge we see is to now build the capacity from currently which we are utilizing 65% and to start manufacturing 85% to 90% within 90 days of time. As you know, with the downward trend, we

items.statement: Stainless steel sink operations running at 80%+ capacity, strong demand in domestic and export markets
items.quote: The segment continues to witness robust demand. Our current operations are running at the capacity of already 80-plus-percent, demand of the high qualities of sinks in Indian and export market.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 EBITDA margin improved to 17.5% from 16% in Q4 FY24, driven by cooling MMA prices and freight costs
items.quote: I think if I am not mistaken, our CFO would probably say, I think that has improved, Anand, from 16% to 19%, right, EBITDA, for Q4? Anand Sharma: Yes, 16% to 18%.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA margin 17.3%, marginally impacted by higher MMA prices, export freight, manpower and marketing spend
items.quote: EBITDA margin for FY'25 stood at 17.3%, marginally impacted due to higher MMA price, which is our primary raw material, increase in export freight cost, some additional manpower cost which we build for capacity elevation, and marketing spend for our domestic business.

items.statement: No significant tariff impact expected on sinks as no reciprocal duty applies; 10% baseline duty on all US imports
items.quote: So I think that now everybody is getting 10% duty attraction to anything imported into the US. But we do not see any significant increase in the tariffs as there is no reciprocal duty on sinks.

items.statement: United Granite US subsidiary turned profitable at 2-3% margin in Q4, targeting significant improvement in coming quarters
items.quote: We were about negative 8% to 10%, and we have now crossed the breakeven, I think we are at about 2% or 3% profit now. Coming quarters, I think we see a significant improvement in the margins moving forward.

items.statement: Revenue target of Rs. 3,000 crores for FY26, implying ~17% growth; conservative basis 17% doable, aim to improve
items.quote: Yes, very much, Bino , because we have done Rs. 2,600 crores. So we are very optimistic that we are very much on track for the Rs. 3,000 crores.

items.statement: Corporate growth target above 17.5-18% YoY for next 3 years; US growth higher due to small base
items.quote: For the company by itself, we are giving a year-on-year growth of anything above 17.5%, 18% year-on-year growth as a corporate.

items.statement: Teva facility revenue trending Rs. 400-500 crores in FY26 based on current run-rate; aim to hit Rs. 1,000 crores eventually
items.quote: So we are looking at somewhere around between Rs. 400-odd crores to Rs. 500-odd crores. This is the trend as on today.

items.statement: FY25 capex Rs. 173 crores for Goa facility scale-up; FY26 capex expected $8-10 million (lower than FY25) for debottlenecking
items.quote: So last year, of course, we did CAPEX of Rs. 173 crores. And I think this year also, the CAPEX we will continue to incur. It will be lower than last year, but I think we should be somewhere between, say, $8 million to $10 million overall.

items.statement: EBITDA margin FY25 20.2% vs 21.1% FY24; expect to maintain or improve historic EBITDA; target 21-22% once operating leverage from Goa facility kicks in H2 FY26
items.quote: See, I think definitely, we can do 21%, 22% EBITDA margin once this kind of operating leverage gets in.

items.statement: Gross margin expanded 407 bps to 56.4% in FY25 driven by better product mix and lower raw material prices
items.quote: The gross profit was at Rs. 1,479 crores, up 29.8% year-on-year. Gross margin increased by 407 basis points to 56.4% in FY '25.

items.statement: If tariffs >10%, will pass on to customers; retailers have publicly stated prices will rise; US manufacturers also face raw material tariff costs
items.quote: But most likely, if it is 10% or anything above 10%, we will definitely work on passing it down. And we will still be competitive compared to the domestic manufacturing in the U.S. because they will also have the brunt of raw material tariffs.

items.statement: No pre-buying in Q1 FY26; uncertainty in March-April slowed orders; US base small so high % growth; UK and Europe aggressive growth plans
items.quote: No, not exactly. There's no prebuying in quarter 1. The U.S. tariff is a universal question, honestly, I don't think anyone has the right answer for that.

items.statement: OTC segment crossed Rs. 2,000 crores in FY25; OTC share may rise to 85% of revenue; commercialized 58 SKUs in FY25, 79 in pipeline; ~70 launches by September
items.quote: It may grow, Nitin, honestly, because we are very strong in OTC. So like I have always said, it may grow, and you may see OTC having maybe 85%.

items.statement: Tariff uncertainty remains; if disproportionate tariffs applied, will pass through; US recession risk acknowledged but not expected; working capital days 125-135 sustainable
items.quote: But then again, that's only my opinion. I do believe that if the tariffs are disproportion in any nature, it will be passed down to customers and clients.

items.statement: Debt-free with Rs. 704 crores cash; pursuing European M&A targets €30-40m each; keeping ~Rs. 400 crores for acquisitions, capex ~Rs. 100 crores, rest for working capital
items.quote: We continue to remain debt-free and the cash balance stood at Rs. 704 crores as of 31st March of 2025.

items.statement: Teva facility utilization ~200M units Q4 FY25, trending 350M units in Q1 FY26; target 450-500M in H1, 600-700M thereafter; 50% capacity (4B units) in 6 months, full 8B units by late FY26 or early FY27
items.quote: So the last quarter, Q4, we didn't do the volumes as expected. We were somewhere around 200 million units being generated. But this year, this first few months, we are trending around 350 million tablets.

items.statement: R&D spend FY25 2.2% of revenue (Rs. 57.9 crores); expect 1.9-2% of revenue going forward; Q4 spike due to US/UK filings
items.quote: Moving on, we do expect the R&D expenditure to remain between, say, 1.9% to 2% on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Freight cost as % of sales 5% in FY25 vs 4% FY24; stabilized now, expected to return to 4% in FY26
items.quote: So if I see like freight cost as a percentage to sales, so in FY '25, it was around 5% as compared to 4% in FY '24. So we ended up paying like more in FY '25 as a whole. But yes, now it has stabilized, and I think it will come back to 4% in FY '26.

items.statement: Dividend recommended Rs. 0.8 per share (80% of face value); India Ratings upgraded long-term debt to IND AA- from IND A+
items.quote: As a part of our commitment and enhancing shareho lder value, I am pleased to announce that the Board has recommended a dividend of Rs. 0.8 per equity share, representing 80% of the face value per share

items.statement: Targeting 20-25% top line growth for FY26
items.quote: Yes. So I'm really grateful that you all have taken the time out to listen to my diatribes and lecture, but I'm really grateful to you all. And I hope I could give some idea about our business and where we are today and where we are going. And looking forward to your support and I'm very I mean, I would like to sign off on an optimistic note as far as we are concerned. I'm quite optimistic about t

items.statement: INR 15 crore capex for new Bangalore facility; inauguration planned 31st May with commercial production soon after
items.quote: Our new facility at Bangalore will be a largest and most modern for the company. We'll be going into the latest technologies in welding and painting to improve the offerings to our customers. The inauguration of this facility is planned on 31st May and commercial production soon thereafter.

items.statement: No order booking visibility; business depends on customer monthly schedules and new component wins
items.quote: In our case, you don't get the order booking. I see, whatever is the existing business that you are doing for it's like an OEM supply. So that there is open ended orders and there are just schedules which they lift month on month.

items.statement: OEM gross margins unlikely to improve; EBITDA margin expansion driven by operating leverage on fixed costs, not margin expansion
items.quote: I would say that the gross margins for OEM business that we are doing, this is I do not see the possibility of improvement of this margin. These are already quite good margins compared to many of the -- many of our peers that we look at.

items.statement: Cannot pass through non-raw material cost increases; rely on productivity gains and volume growth to protect margins
items.quote: Any other cost, whether they are consumer, whether they are any other terrestrial cost, the costumer that's will not, we cannot pass on. See, the way out is either to increase your volume or to improve productivity.

items.statement: Mining segment showing traction now; electrification/solar transformer demand projected but not yet materializing
items.quote: So mining, yes, they are very, very bullish both in India and overseas. Worldwide, of course, because of more mining, because of copper, because of all these battery related chemicals that have to be all taken out of the ground and all that.

items.statement: Earthmoving/construction equipment ~60-65% of revenue; exports ~11% currently, targeting higher share via Caterpillar aftermarket and new Bangalore facility
items.quote: The highest revenue is coming from the construction equipment or earthmoving sector, what we in the industry call as yellow goods, so which are used for infrastructure projects, road dams, mining, et cetera. So that is our biggest area of business. And that, I think, must be constituting about 60% of the turnover of the company. 60%, 65% of business comes from that sector.

items.statement: Human capital shortage is critical industry challenge; investing heavily in training and process R&D to differentiate
items.quote: And so I think what I am seeing is that the industry is really struggling as far as human capital is concerned. And it's a kind of a hidden thing. Nobody talks about it surprisingly, but the real challenge is the human capital.

items.statement: Launching retail cut steel parts and tube processing from Baroda plant in June; lower margin but high volume, software-driven model
items.quote: Instead of doing B2B OEM business, I want to start retail kind of business from there. And that facility is also going on, I mean, in the same premises, but that is a separate vertical, which will go on stream now shortly in this month June.

items.statement: Auto sector expected to grow 6-8% in FY26 on stable macros, revival in infra spend, normal monsoon, easing rates and higher disposable incomes
items.quote: Auto sector is expected to grow at 6-8% in FY26 on the back of stable macroeconomic conditions including revival in infrastructure spend , normal monsoon , easing interest rate scenario and increase in rural and urban disposable incomes.

items.statement: Capex outlay of roughly INR900 crores in FY26 to complete ongoing projects worth INR1,400 crores across PCR, TBR and ASLTR
items.quote: This year we will be spending roughly around INR900 crores, and we will be completing all our existing projects.

items.statement: Ongoing projects worth Rs.1,400 crores across PCR, TBR & All Steel Light Truck Radial (ASLTR) segments are progressing well
items.quote: Ongoing projects worth Rs.1,400 crores across PCR, TBR & All Steel Light Truck Radial (ASLTR) segments are progressing well.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expanded to 10.2% in Q4 FY25 from 9.1% in Q3 FY25, improvement of over 110 bps QoQ
items.quote: EBITDA margins during Q4 were recorded at 10.2% as against 9.1%, representing an improvement of over 110 basis points over the previous quarter.

items.statement: Raw material prices declined ~2.5% QoQ in Q4; management sees stabilization with a bias towards marginal decline in forthcoming quarters
items.quote: Raw material, we have seen right now on quarter -on-quarter basis from the previous quarter, around 2.5% decline. Going ahead, we are seeing stabilizing of raw material prices with a bias towards marginal decline in forthcoming quarters.

items.statement: CV segment saw positive momentum in Q4 FY25; trend expected to continue in Q1 FY26 due to pre-buying ahead of mandatory AC cabin norms from June 2025
items.quote: Commercial Vehicle (CV) segment saw a positive momentum in Q4FY25 and the trend is expected to continue in the 1st quarter of next financial year on account of pre-buying of CVs as the new regulations for AC cabins is becoming mandatory in June 2025.

items.statement: Revenue mix of high rim sizes improving consistently and growing at double-digit in PCR; XF, XM, XD series improving mix in commercial segment
items.quote: As part of our premiumization efforts, in the replacement market, revenue mix of high rim sizes is improving consistently and growing at double-digit in PCR and in commercial segment also XF, XM and XD series tyres are improving the product mix.

items.statement: US tariff uncertainty impacted Mexico exports in Q4; only ~3% of consolidated revenue exposed to US tariffs; strategy to grow domestic, Brazil and LATAM sales to minimize impact
items.quote: So what I'm trying to tell you is that the exposure to the total revenues to U.S. tariff is minimal. It may not be more than 3%.

items.statement: Net debt reduced by INR238 crores in Q4 to INR4,081 crores; leverage ratios net debt/equity 0.82x and net debt/EBITDA 2.4x as of 31 March 2025
items.quote: Net debt stood at INR4,081 crores for the quarter as against INR4,319 crores in the previous quarter. So there is a reduction of about INR238 crores during the quarter 4.

items.statement: Cavendish revenue INR1,034 crores in Q4 (+18% YoY) and INR3,991 crores in FY25 (+9% YoY); run rate ~INR1,000 crores/quarter
items.quote: For Q4, there was a revenue of INR1,034 crores from Cavendish. And for the financial year, it was INR3,991 crores, almost about INR4,000 crores. So the run rate quarterly as of now is about INR1,000 crores.

items.statement: Mexico PCR expansion project of USD 27 Mn progressing well, expected completion by end of CY2025
items.quote: Our PCR expansion project of USD 27 Mn is also progressing well and is expected to be completed by the end of CY2025.

items.statement: Board announced dividend of Rs.3 per equity share (150%) for FY25
items.quote: The Board has announced a dividend of Rs.3 per equity share, i.e. 150%.

items.statement: Scheme of amalgamation of Cavendish (CIL) with JK Tyre approved by SEBI, now with NCLT
items.quote: The scheme of amalgamation of CIL with JK Tyre is progressing well and has already been approved by SEBI and the matter is now with NCLT.

items.statement: EV bus share at 7% of total bus industry; expected to reach 10% with government policy support; EV passenger car production estimated at 1.33 million units (~20% of PV) by 2030
items.quote: EV bus es are contributing 7% in the total bus industry, and we are expecting that this will go further to 10% by intervention of various government policies. So, we are expecting a growth. Overall, in the EV space we are expecting a growth in the passenger car vehicle production, which by 2030, we are estimating around 1.33 million units, which is approximately 20% of the total passenger vehicle

items.statement: Capacity utilization for FY25 at 78% consolidated; radial tyres over 85%
items.quote: Capacity utilization for FY '25 was at 78% on a consolidated basis. However, capacity utilization of radial tyres remained high at over 85%.

items.statement: Target minimum 30% revenue CAGR over next 5 years and exceed Rs. 5,000 crores revenue by FY 2030
items.quote: Paramount is further targeted to grow its topline with the CAGR of a minimum of 30% over the next 5 years also, and we hope to exceed Rs. 5,000 crores in revenues by FY 2030.

items.statement: Plan Rs. 150 crores Phase-1 capex for Narmadapuram greenfield plant targeting commercial production within FY26
items.quote: We are looking at roughly Rs. 150 crores of CAPEX in Phase-1 for the Narmadapuram facility.

items.statement: Target commercial production at Narmadapuram plant within FY26, possibly Q4 FY26 or Q1 FY27
items.quote: The Company is targeting to begin commercial production in this plant within FY '26.

items.statement: Pending order book of over Rs. 650 crores as of 31 March 2025, split roughly equally between domestic and export
items.quote: The Company has a pending order book of around more than Rs. 650 crore as on 31st March 25 comprising of domestic cables roughly more than Rs. 328 crores and export of the similar amount around Rs. 325 crores.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 EBITDA margin fell to 6.6% from 9%-9.2% in Q4 FY24 due to volume push and working capital trade-offs
items.quote: EBITDA during this quarter is 33.5% with a margin of 6.6% as against Rs. 29.9 crores with a margin of 9%-9.2% in the same quarter of the previous year.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA margin slightly down to 8.5% from 9% in FY24
items.quote: EBITDA margin is little bit down that is from 9%-8.5% as against previous year.

items.statement: Revenue growth (47%) lagged volume growth (57%) due to declining metal prices over past two years
items.quote: Metal prices have shown a downward trend in the past 2 years. Not only this year, in the previous year also, the metal prices have been coming down, basically commodity prices that test their peak during FY '23.

items.statement: Target US exports to constitute around 40% of total revenues in coming years via distribution network
items.quote: The Company targets US exports to constitute around 40% of its total revenues in the coming years, mainly through our distribution network in the US.

items.statement: Power cables share rose to 59% of Q4 FY25 sales from 45% in Q4 FY24; domestic power cable sales grew 106% YoY in Q4
items.quote: Power Cable sales constitute around 59% of the total Company sales in this quarter against 45% for Q4 of the previous year.

items.statement: US currently imposes 14%-15% import duty; reciprocal tariffs could alter competitive position vs Vietnam, Cambodia, South Korea
items.quote: Currently, their duty imposed is around between 14%-15% depending on the exact product.

items.statement: If India faces negative tariff treatment vs competitors, exports could be impacted; otherwise strong market position expected to hold
items.quote: Unless India is treated very negatively by the US government in comparison to the countries that are competing with us. If that happens, yes, there could be a problem.

items.statement: Company became debt-free in FY25; working capital days reduced from 155 to 101 days; operational cash flow turned positive Rs. 104 crores
items.quote: The Company has become debt free in the Financial Year '25 and we have liquidated all our debts and obligations during this year.

items.statement: Narmadapuram plant targets Rs. 1,000 crores revenue within 3 years at asset turn of ~6x; will make power cables up to 132 kV initially
items.quote: Asset turn could go up to 6 roughly because we will be looking at getting revenues of around Rs. 1,000 crores from this facility within the next 3 years.

items.statement: Expect PBT CAGR to be much higher than 30% revenue CAGR, potentially 60%+, after tax normalization post Q2 FY26
items.quote: Common sense tells us, I am not making an announcement or a projection, but a common sense is that if my CAGR in revenue is 30%, my CAGR in PBT should be at least 60%.

items.statement: Existing two plants can support up to ~Rs. 2,000 crores revenue; new greenfield needed beyond that
items.quote: We have been doing CAPEX consistently in the past 2-3 years and we hope that we should be able to achieve something up to around Rs. 2,000 crores from these 2 plants.

items.statement: Revenue guidance for FY26 revised to Rs 1,900-1,950 crore, implying 12-14% growth
items.quote: We are recalibrating ou r outlook and currently expect to achieve revenue in the range of Rs. 1,900 crore to Rs. 1,950 crore in FY '26 translating to a top -line growth of 12% to 14% for the year

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance for FY26 around 13%
items.quote: So, we see like a flat, Quarter 1 is flat. May be further improvement from Quarter 2 and for the full year, we are expecting near about around 13% in the margins.

items.statement: Capex for FY25 was Rs 165-170 crore, largest in two decades
items.quote: Capital expenditure for Financial Year '25 stood at approximately Rs. 165 crore to Rs. 170 crore primarily directed towards machinery upgrades and new product development in alignment with our long-term growth strategy.

items.statement: Capex guidance for FY26 around Rs 170 crore
items.quote: Looking ahead, we anticipate a capital expenditure of around Rs. 170 crore in the upcoming financial year, as we contin ue to build capabilities and support our expanding business pipeline

items.statement: Order book stands at Rs 9,000 crore executable up to FY29, 82% from four-wheeler (PV 50%, CV 32%)
items.quote: Currently our order book is around Rs. 9,000 crore. And here what we are seeing, the major increase which we are seeing is from the passenger vehicle and the commercial vehicle. And if I bifurcate, so passenger vehicle contributes 50% and commercial vehicle 32%.

items.statement: FY25 gross margin 47.8% vs 51.5% in FY24; EBITDA Rs 198 crore, down 1% YoY
items.quote: gross margin for Financial Year '25 was 47.8% compared to 51.5% in the last year. EBITDA for Financial Year '25 was Rs. 198 crore, a 1% decline o n a year-on-year basis

items.statement: Aluminum price changes 100% passed through to customers, no margin impact
items.quote: So, actually this is 100% passed on to the customer. So, there is no impact on the margins.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 was worst quarter; recovery in Q4 and further recovery expected in coming quarters
items.quote: Yes Devang, you rightly said, Quarter 3 we all feel was the worst quarter for us, and now we have made the r ecovery. And we are seeing the further recovery in the coming quarter

items.statement: US tariff uncertainty and potential US recession in H2 CY25 causing customer decision delays
items.quote: The noise around the U.S. tariffs is proving to be a deterrent. There is heightened uncertainty given the fast pace of development and news flow around these tariffs and counter tariffs being proposed.

items.statement: Global research firms projecting 9% volume decline in USA and 6% in Europe for current year
items.quote: The latest research report, which we are seeing from the global companies, they are still showing the 9% reduction in the volume in the USA and 6% in the Europe.

items.statement: New order wins in FY25 to fetch Rs 1,600 crore revenue over next 5 years; some EV orders reduced per customer guidelines
items.quote: If you see like in '24 -'25, what orders we have got, it will fetch us the revenue of Rs. 1,600 crore in the next 5 years. But what happened is some of the orders which we have got for electric vehicles, the EV veh icles, so that we have reduced based on the new guidelines from the

items.statement: FY26 growth driven 5% from new order wins, rest from existing platform ramp-up
items.quote: So, from the new order win, around 5% growth will be from the new order wins and remaining from the natural growth of the existing part.

items.statement: Capacity utilization target ~80% in FY26 and FY27
items.quote: We are seeing in the next year and year after, we will be having the capacity utilization of around 80%.

items.statement: FY26 capex largely funded from internal accruals; small debt increase possible
items.quote: So, maximum will be from the internal accruals, but I think there will be a small increase in the debt, but not a major increase from this CAPEX because some money we will realize from this improvement in the working capital cycle.

items.statement: Incremental effective sales from Plant II sterile facility expected to begin in Q2 FY26
items.quote: As such, for this year, I think it would be safe to say that any incremental effective sales from this plant would only begin in the second quarter this year.

items.statement: Europe business expected to return to INR300 crore level in FY26
items.quote: Coming to Europe, our normal base for Europe used to be around INR300 crores. And this year, it got impacted because of inability to supply, etcetera, of solid orals. And I expect it to go back to the INR300 crore level in the coming year.

items.statement: Other expenses targeted to be arrested at INR120 crores per quarter
items.quote: As of now, I think we are doing close to INR140 crores on other expenses, but I am hopeful in another quarter to be able to arrest it at INR120 crores.

items.statement: Warren Remedies OTC toothpaste sales expected to grow in double digits
items.quote: So I expect this to create good demand. And from here on, I expect Warren Remedies base sales to also grow in a good fashion, at least in double digits.

items.statement: Warren Remedies breakeven expected in FY27
items.quote: I think safe to say '27.

items.statement: Capex for FY26 limited to routine maintenance; most capex work at finishing stage
items.quote: While your question about the plan for this particular financial year '24 -- '25-'26, we don't intend to spend much on capex. We have controlled capex. And most of the capex work is almost at finishing stage in all sites.

items.statement: Additional depreciation of INR9-10 crores per annum from new asset capitalization
items.quote: So about INR9 crores to INR10 crores would be the additional depreciation on the new assets.

items.statement: Sufficient orders in hand for international business
items.quote: As of now, we have sufficient orders in hand and feel confident th at we'll be able to do that

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin at 6% for FY25 vs 13.7% in FY24
items.quote: Consolidated EBITDA to net sales for the year is 6% at INR993 million compared to 13.7% at INR2,443 million.

items.statement: Rock bottom of losses reached; improvement expected from Q2 FY26
items.quote: Yes, I believe we are at the rock bottom of the losses. And from here on, I don't expect any further deterioration.

items.statement: Remediation costs at INR4 crores per quarter; updates to continue until December
items.quote: So we spent close to INR4 crores per quarter on remediation expenses. And this has happened for all 4 quarters this year.

items.statement: Domestic formulation business grew 8.5% in FY25; legacy products showing healthy double-digit growth except Febrex Plus and ATM
items.quote: If you look at the consolidated picture of India business performance, you will see that we have grown at more than 8.5%, which is at par or even better than the industry growth.

items.statement: New products contribution to growth at 4.5% vs industry average 2.5%; Cylopam added INR25 crores incrementally
items.quote: Today, at IRL, our contribution of new products to total growth is in excess of 4.5%, which is way higher than the industry average of 2.5%.

items.statement: US FDA warning letter on sterile Plant II; remediation updates to be completed by July-August 2025
items.quote: last updates, most of the updates on the remediation would be completed by July or August this year. So I think as a site, we have to be ready any time after that

items.statement: R&D spend maintained at ~5% of sales; being selective on pipeline investments
items.quote: No, we are not planning to increase or decrease, but we are maintaining it at 5%. Even on a lower top line this year, in absolute terms, it has come down because we are now being a little bit more picky about the products we take up.

items.statement: No specific revenue or earnings guidance provided
items.quote: In line with our usual practice, we would not be sharing specific guidance on revenue or on earnings projections.

items.statement: Print EBITDA margin expanded ~400 bps YoY in FY25
items.quote: With a margin expansion, also, of ~400 basis points.

items.statement: Print margin expansion driven by newsprint savings and advertising yield improvement
items.quote: Yes, cost has substantially improved because if you remember last year was a year of heightened newsprint pricing and therefore most of the margin expansion is attributed to the savings in newsprint that's come through.

items.statement: Hindi print ad revenue declined due to high government spending base in prior year
items.quote: Hindi has not done well because of a large revenue from government in the base. Last year, prior to the national election, there was a fair bit of spend happening from the Government and so most, vernacular players, especially Hindi players, you would see have had a substantial revenue coming from the Government.

items.statement: English print ad revenue grew 3% YoY in FY25
items.quote: In English we have seen growth, because Government was not such a substantial component, and we've called out the growth in critical segments in our deck - as to which are the segments that contributed.

items.statement: Radio revenue grew 30% YoY to INR 204 cr driven by on-ground events
items.quote: On the top line, you can see the quarterly numbers grew 72% to INR 82 cr, and on a full year basis to INR 204 cr, which is an increase of 30%.

items.statement: Radio margins remain soft due to higher cost structure of scaled events
items.quote: Unlike the core FCT revenue, where every increase in revenue falls to the bottom line because of the fixed nature of the business where the cost is mostly on the statutory fees side, when we go into the non-FCT streams of revenue, there is bound to be a related cost also associated with it.

items.statement: OTTplay targeting break-even by end of FY26 but may invest more if scaling fast
items.quote: We expect to keep up the momentum on the growth side, given that, it's still a very nascent business from that perspective and hopefully by the end of this year, we should be in a break-even situation. But it depends, if we scale fast enough, we may invest more on the business as well.

items.statement: Digital revenue grew 38% YoY to INR 212 cr led by OTTplay and Shine
items.quote: On a full year basis to INR 212 cr, which is an increase of 38%.

items.statement: Digital losses narrowed from INR 114 cr to INR 102 cr while revenue scaled
items.quote: From INR 154 cr of revenue last year, Digital revenues have grown to INR 212 cr, while the losses we have reduced from INR 114 cr to INR 102 cr.

items.statement: Electric mobility investment is ad-for-equity with no cash deployment
items.quote: It is not a cash investment, it is an AFE investment, so there is no cash being deployed for that investment.

items.statement: Net cash position exceeds INR 1,000 cr as of March 31, 2025
items.quote: If you see the net cash position, we have as of 31st March, cash in excess of INR 1,000 cr on the books.

items.statement: Ad-for-equity portfolio on fully diluted basis north of INR 1,000 cr
items.quote: Broadly, I will give you that number this year also. So , look, what I give you every year on a fully diluted basis our investment position will be, north of INR 1000 cr.

items.statement: Print advertising yield improved through price corrections and category mix
items.quote: Basis a mix of categories and absolute price increases there has been an overall yield improvement in advertising revenue despite growth not being that strong and therefore that has also contributed to the margins.

items.statement: Radio industry revenues remain challenged; regulatory changes needed for margin recovery
items.quote: The revenues still remain a challenge largely for the industry. So, while we are at it and we will see some level of growth, we believe the larger growth will come in line of non -FCT initiatives.

items.statement: Annual plan is a growth plan; investments in future-looking businesses to continue
items.quote: We've already drawn our annual plan, which is a growth plan and basis which we will strive to do our best to get greater performances . And investments in future looking businesses that will create long-term sustainable value for all shareholders is something that we are at, and we will strive to do our best.

items.statement: Operating profit margin guidance of 2.3% to 2.5% for the immediate future, with potential upside from software mix shift over time.
items.quote: We have been talking about between 2.3 % to 2.5% of operating profit. We will be happy if we are able to stay in this consistently, but definitely, as I have said, because of the focus on the software and this thing - subscription vertical, we think this can go up in future, but I think for now we should stay with between 2.3 to 2.5%.

items.statement: Gross margins expected to be broadly stable; mix change and larger TSG deals may pressure weighted margins.
items.quote: I think we should be able to maintain this. I mean, there can be some mixed change, but otherwise, broadly, we should be able to maintain this.

items.statement: Software portfolio (hyperscaler, SaaS, security) at ~15% of revenue, targeting >20% in 2-3 years; TSG and Endpoint Solutions mix also expected to rise.
items.quote: Today it's 15. We should be more than 20 and higher as a percentage of our total business. Clearly, the Technology Solutions Group as a mix also should be higher because that's the part of the business you have already seen it's grown between 25% and 30% over the course of the quarter and high double digit during the year.

items.statement: Saudi Arabia expected to deliver strong double-digit growth for the next three years driven by AI infrastructure, cloud, and PC penetration catch-up.
items.quote: We do expect a good strong double-digit growth coming back in Saudi both in the coming year and future years. Because all parts of the market as I mentioned earlier, it's not just the infrastructure side.

items.statement: Quarterly capex expected to stabilize at Rs. 40-60 crores per quarter.
items.quote: Our CAPEX, Rucha, has always been limited. And this CAPEX is more specific and that too has happened more in ProConnect because of the new businesses that they had got, but otherwise it will range between Rs. 40 crores to Rs. 60 crores per quarter.

items.statement: Paynet divestment proceeds of INR 626 crores (US$74M) received; used to repay Arena debt, significantly reducing interest and finance costs.
items.quote: Out of the sales proceeds, a large part of this has been used to repay Arena's debt position, resulting in significant reduction in interest and finance costs. This should have a positive impact in the Arena performance in the upcoming quarters.

items.statement: Tariff changes and geopolitical tensions are key uncertainties being closely monitored; potential supply chain disruptions from manufacturing diversification.
items.quote: The uncertainty from the tariff changes and the geopolitical tensions in many of our geographies are areas we are closely watching, and we will respond as needed.

items.statement: Cloud/software resell margins 5.5-6%; professional services margins 20%+.
items.quote: So, see, somewhere between 5.5 and 6, so it is on the higher side, is what we appropriate from the pure resell and the subscription model. And there is additional margins to be had on professional services, which can be anywhere from around 20% plus.

items.statement: Tax rate guided at 25-27% for FY26 (closer to 27%) due to UAE tax rising to 15% under global minimum tax.
items.quote: So, we expect next year , the tax rate should range between 25 % to 27%, maybe closer to th is thing, 27%.

items.statement: Large deals in TSG (servers, storage, data centers) are <20% of revenue; run-rate business ~80%.
items.quote: It's hard to comment because the deals happen every quarter and I would say the large deals will be less than 20% of our business. The run rate should definitely continue to be around 80%.

items.statement: Arena business worst decline over; credit card segment still declining due to high rates, expecting flattening in coming year.
items.quote: We believe the worst in terms of decline is over. Having said that, the credit card business continues to show a decline because of the high interest rates. And IP is most impacted by that. So, that's largely in the consumer and mid-market space. But while we don't see a growth coming back in the coming year, we see flattening out of growth.

items.statement: One-off depreciation of Rs. 5 crores in Q4 from digital platform transition write-off.
items.quote: Again, for your earlier question, the one-off depreciation on account of this digital platform this quarter is about Rs. 5 crores.

items.statement: Factoring and interest cost for Q4 FY25 at Rs. 110 crores (vs Rs. 186 crores YoY, Rs. 155 crores QoQ); full-year FY25 at Rs. 531 crores (vs Rs. 706 crores FY24).
items.quote: Regarding interest and factoring cost for the quarter both put together is about Rs. 110 crores vis-à-vis Rs. 186 crores Q4 last year and Rs. 155 crores in Q3 current year.

items.statement: Final dividend of Rs. 6.8 per share declared for FY25, similar to FY24, constituting ~40% of profits excluding Paynet gain.
items.quote: We had deliberations at the Board yesterday, and we are happy to declare Rs. 6.8 per share of final dividend for the year ended 31st March 2025. The dividend amount for FY '25 is similar to FY '24 dividend, and this constitutes nearly 40% of our total profits for the year without considering the one-off impact on account of Paynet divestment.

items.statement: Blends business expected to grow ~20% CAGR over next 2-3 years with EBITDA margins in high teens moving toward 20% as they mature
items.quote: Essentially, we should grow that blends business by about 20% going forward in the next 2 to 3 years. And the EBITDA margins will improve in some of the geographies because there is a certain threshold. So it will be in the high teens, the EBITDA margin.

items.statement: Vanillin plant capacity utilization target of 100% within next 2 years from current 45-50%
items.quote: In the next 2 years, we want to take it up to 100% as the market development gets better. The idea is to take it, go 100% in the next 2 years.

items.statement: Discontinued operations cash burn to reduce to INR 8 crores per quarter for next couple of quarters then INR 4-5 crores annually
items.quote: Yes. So, the idea is that this INR8 crores a quarter is for the next couple of quarters at max, because after the closing procedure is completed in a way which complies with all regulations and safety laws, we will -- in those -- in that locality or in that plant, we will have no employees there really, workers there apart from a couple which are required statutorily. So, the cash burn over a peri

items.statement: No significant capex planned; only maintenance and minor debottlenecking to sweat vanillin plant first
items.quote: So, right now, we are not looking at any significant capex because we need to first also sweat our vanillin plant. So, no significant capex, it's just maintenance and some odd debottlenecking and that kind of...

items.statement: Consolidated gross margin expected in 45-55% range depending on product mix and market behavior
items.quote: So when you balance it, you kind of say that it will be in the region of 45% to 55% in that zone. You end up at based on product mix, based on how the market is behaving. But that's the region where we are, essentially playing on.

items.statement: Vanillin prices in U.S. around $15/kg, Europe 20-25% lower; current booking range $13-15/kg; European prices may rise 10-15% after 131% ADD confirmation
items.quote: The vanillin price, the difference will be about 20% or so, 20% to 25% because the ADDs are different between what is in Europe and what is in the U.S.

items.statement: Vanillin demand ramp-up delayed by U.S. inventory destocking; expect volumes from U.S. and Europe to grow over next 3-4 quarters as ADD duties take effect
items.quote: Essentially, that kind of gives Solvay and us some advan tage. And I suppose we'll get majority of the share of the market between Solvay being the market leader and us being a second player, we will see volumes growing from these 2 markets in the next 3 to 4 quarters, you'll see the growth coming

items.statement: Blends growth driven across all geographies (North America, LatAm, India, Europe, Middle East, Africa, Asia) with Vitafor contributing INR 85 crores in 9 months
items.quote: Overall, the Blends business has grown by around 17% to 18% year-on-year. So we have reached around INR878 crores as compared to INR747 crores in the last year. Of course, Blends business also increased -- includes CFS Vitafor, the new blend business, which we bought in Europe, Belgium, in our first quarter of this year. It's 9 months thing, but it also clicked around INR85 crores in this year

items.statement: Pricing pressure on all products except vanillin due to aggressive Chinese competition; tariff impacts uncertain but expected to balance out over time
items.quote: Yes, there's pricing pressure on all products. Santosh Parab: Except vanillin. Nirmal Momaya: Except vanillin right now because -- in 2 markets. But otherwise, there's a lot of pricing pressure coming from competition from

items.statement: Vinpai acquisition expected to close by July end; could lift blends growth from 20% to 25% CAGR; strong cross-selling interest across geographies
items.quote: So, I think the regulatory procedures, I think corporate actions and all that required to be done should be completed in the next 2 months, and that should be done by July end. In terms of growth potential, yes, Vinpai does have a fantastic growth potential because of the categories of products that they are in are substantial categories and with some differentiated technology, it's well positione

items.statement: Aroma ingredients revenue reached INR 176 crores in FY25; ramp-up to continue with U.S. and EU anti-dumping duties on Chinese vanillin
items.quote: The total contribution of revenue from Aroma has been around INR176 crores in FY '25. And we -- this ramp-up will go -- will come or increase in the subsequent quarters with anti-dumping duty action in U.S. and you would be aware now that even European Union has levied a preliminary duty of 131% and it will be finalize d in next few months

items.statement: Net debt improved from INR 564 crores to INR 492 crores after successful rights issue in Jan 2025
items.quote: You know that our equity has increased because we had a successful rights issue in Jan '25. We have been able to control the overall debt position. The net debt position has improved from INR564 crores to INR492 crores.

items.statement: Core business revenue grew ~15% YoY to INR 1,666 crores; core EBITDA improved to INR 208 crores (12.5% margin)
items.quote: So, the total growth what we have seen in revenues on an annual basis are continuing or the core business has grown by almost 15% year-on-year. We also had an improved EBITDA of core business of around 12.5%. That's around INR208 crores in '25 as compared to INR184 crores of the comparable business in the last year.

items.statement: Vanillin cost of production currently $9.5-10/kg at 45-50% utilization; expected to drop below $9 at 70-75% utilization
items.quote: As we told you that because this average utilization is at 45%, that's the reason why it is high. When we -- as we go beyond 70%, 75% of breakeven, this should come down to sub $9.

items.statement: DHA/Omega products in pipeline; potential significant revenue jump in FY26 if contracts finalize in next 3-4 months
items.quote: Of course FY '25, you won't see a massive jump, but there are some projects in the pipeline and some contracts that are being negot iated. If they come to fruition, which we should know in the next 3 to 4 months, then in FY '26, you could see a big jump in that

items.statement: Lockheed Martin battery project: first battery installed, awaiting feedback; no orders or timeline yet
items.quote: No, nothing on update about Lockheed right now. It's on -- they've installed the first battery. They're waiting for some feedback. So, no orders at this point of time.

items.statement: Hospital revenue growth expected at 14-15% for FY26 with 5-6% ARPOB growth and balance from volume
items.quote: So, revenue-wise, we expect to grow around 14% -15%, similar number. And this time last year, the year we have completed, we have seen 9% type of ARPOB growth and balance growth is coming from the volume. So I'm expecting it will be the reverse this time, around 5%, 6% in the ARPOB growth and the balance is from the volume side.

items.statement: Hospital EBITDA margin expansion of ~200 bps expected in FY26 similar to FY25
items.quote: Yes, yes. So we are quite confident. And last year also, we have demonstrated 2% margin improvement and similar thing we are expecting this financial year. So we are quite confident on that.

items.statement: Diagnostics revenue targeting double-digit growth in FY26
items.quote: So, the brand change effect is now behind us, and we are seeing a double-digit type of growth number in the diagnostic business henceforth.

items.statement: Diagnostics EBITDA margin targeting 23% then 25% in a couple of years on net revenue
items.quote: It should be around 23% ultimately and then moving towards 25% in a couple of years' time.

items.statement: FY25 capex was approximately INR 700 crores for capacity expansion and medical infrastructure
items.quote: Just to highlight, our capital expenditure in financial year '25 stood at approximately INR 700 crores, reflecting our confidence to further scale up operations both in terms of capacity expansion and augmenting medical infrastructure.

items.statement: Brownfield expansion funded through internal accruals with no incremental debt
items.quote: Yes. So there will not be any incremental debt for brownfield expansion. It will be funded through internal accruals. So there will be no incremental impact.

items.statement: Bed capacity of ~4,024 at end of FY25; targeting ~1,000 bed additions in FY26
items.quote: Yes. So, we ended fiscal 2 5 with a bed capacity of around 4,024 because we have taken out certain beds also in the Richmond Road. And we will be adding around, how much, almost 1,000 beds in the current time.

items.statement: Hospital EBITDA margin improved to 20.5% in FY25 from 18.6% in FY24
items.quote: The hospital business operating EBITDA margins have improved from 18.6% to 20.5% in financial year '25 with an EBITDA of INR 1,339 crores.

items.statement: Diagnostics EBITDA margin (ex-one-offs) improved to 22% in FY25 from 19.6% in FY24
items.quote: Excluding one -offs, primarily related to rebranding expenses, the operating EBITDA margin stood at 22% in financial year '25 versus 19.6% in financial year '24.

items.statement: ARPOB grew 9% to INR 2.42 crores per annum in FY25 driven by key specialties
items.quote: Our hospital business recorded a 9% increase in ARPOB for the yea r, reaching to INR 2.42 crores per annum. This growth was primarily driven by the revenue gains in our key specialty areas such as oncology, neurosciences, cardiac sciences, gastroenterology, orthopedics and renal sciences, which together achieved a 16% year-on-year growth and contributed 62% to the overall hospital business revenue

items.statement: Hospital occupancy improved to 69% in FY25 from 65% in FY24; occupied beds up 5% to 2,838
items.quote: Hospital occupancy improved to 69% in financial year '25 compared to 65% in financial year '24. This translates into occupied bed increas ing by 5% to 2,838 compared to 2,700 beds in financial year '24.

items.statement: Key specialties (oncology, neurosciences, cardiac, gastro, ortho, renal) grew 16% YoY and contributed 62% of hospital revenue in FY25
items.quote: This growth was primarily driven by the revenue gains in our key specialty areas such as oncology, neurosciences, cardiac sciences, gastroenterology, orthopedics and renal sciences, which together achieved a 16% year-on-year growth and contributed 62% to the overall hospital business revenue s.

items.statement: Legal and legacy costs consuming ~1% of EBITDA margin; expected to continue in FY26 and reduce from FY27
items.quote: Yes. So the legal and other legacy cost is taking away almost 1% of our EBITDA margin. A nd I will say that will continue till we're able to resolve these court cases because there is still 1 court case pending in Delhi High Court where the regular hearing is happening.

items.statement: Raised INR 1,550 crores via NCDs in Dec 2024 to acquire 31.52% stake in Agilus; FHL now holds 89.2%
items.quote: In December 2024, we raised INR 1,550 crores through the issuance of non -convertible debentures. Leveraging these funds, along with internal accruals, we have consolidated our stake in Agilus by acquiring 31.52% stake from our private equity investors. As a result, FHL now holds 89.2% equity stake in Agilus.

items.statement: Acquired Fortis brand and trademarks for INR 200 crores; saves ~0.3% EBITDA margin on hospital revenue
items.quote: Recently, the company successfully acquired the 'Fortis' brand and trademarks, for a consideration of INR 200 crores.

items.statement: Manesar hospital at 40% occupancy with 90 beds commissioned; targeting 50%+ occupancy by end of FY26 and breakeven before that
items.quote: Regarding Manesar, we are currently operating, Neha, at about 40% occupancy, but we have commissioned only 90 beds. Another 120 beds we will commission as the occupancy levels go up. We expect that on the entire bed capacity, which is 120 plus 90, we will have about 50% occupancy by the end of this year. The exit should be at least 50%-plus occupancy.

items.statement: Revenue growth of around 15% on FY25, targeting INR6,500-6,600 crores for FY26
items.quote: So we are expecting a top line growth of around 15% on FY '25. That should be around INR6,500 crores to INR6,600 crores for FY '26.

items.statement: Order book as on 31st March 2025 stood at INR22,238 crores
