items.quote: We also saw a healthy increase in ARR of 11% to 13% versus FY24, which resulted in a good RevPAR growth of 14% to 16%.

items.statement: Oberoi Grand renovation to take ~12 more months for partial opening (two-phased); Wildflower Hall managed for 6 months or until bidding concludes; legal costs continue until court proceedings conclude.
items.quote: As far as the Oberoi Grand is concerned, the plan is still... the renovation was for 18 months. We're already six months through that. So, we'll open in about 12 months from now. And that'll be a partial opening. It's a two-phased renovation.

items.statement: Surplus funds of roughly Rs 1,000 crore as of March 31, 2025, providing strong position for future growth and expansion.
items.quote: We ha ve roughly 1,000 crores of surplus funds at the end of March 31 st 2025, which gives us a good position for future growth and expansion, which we are looking across the hotel segments

items.statement: International revenue Rs 131 crore, EBITDA Rs 36 crore, grew 10% YoY; Middle East impacted by Israel-Palestine conflict but now stable; Marrakesh and Mauritius performed well.
items.quote: So if I look at the international category, we had a contribution to the revenue around 131 crores and 36 crores in EBITDA. We grew by 10% in terms of revenue, and seen similar growth in EBITDA from our international category.

items.statement: London subsidiary investment of ~Rs 240 crore mostly done; additional small infusions expected by year-end; long-term goal to bring in 49% partner closer to hotel opening.
items.quote: So there will be some additional requirements which will come through, but most of the investment, at least for current year, is done. There will be some few additions which will be made towards the end of this year, but not a sizable one.

items.statement: Oberoi Grand closure impact roughly Rs 70 crore revenue and Rs 43 crore EBITDA for the year.
items.quote: So, for the year, the impact is roughly, and Vineet can give you the exact number, but it's roughly 70 crore on revenue and 43 crore on EBITDA.

items.statement: Inbound tourism forecasted to grow 15% next year driven by global connectivity and India's improving profile; air traffic grew ~9% in Q4.
items.quote: As per Government of India's forecast, the inbound tourism is forecasted to grow by 15% in next year driven by, global connectivity and India's profile which is bound to improve in the coming year.

items.statement: Q4 occupancy 81-82% (up from 81% last year); industry RevPAR grew ~16%, Oberoi/managed hotels grew 22% (Oberoi 24%, Trident 22%).
items.quote: When we look at the Q4 occupancy, both occupancy as well as ARR were higher than last year, with the occupancy going from 81% to 82% for Q4 as a whole.

items.statement: Mashobra deconsolidation resulted in one-time exceptional gain of Rs 115 crore; advance against equity of Rs 136 crore and book value of ~Rs 141 crore expected to be recovered based on court proceedings.
items.quote: We have given the control back to the government. Due to that, we had a one-time exceptional gain of Rs 115 crores, which came in the books for Q4, resulting in a 109% increase over last year impact.

items.statement: Internal target is double-digit volume growth, but no official guidance given.
items.quote: But despite this, I can say that our internal targets, which we have kept for our team are definitely a double-digit growth. I would not like to give that as a guidance because, as I said, as a policy, we don't give guidance.

items.statement: Focus on margin recovery through cost cuts, pricing, and product mix.
items.quote: So our focus would be on recovery of margins. As far as the overall scenario goes, we definitely see growth, but I would avoid giving any specific percentage.

items.statement: CPVC volume grew 17% year-on-year and 7% quarter-on-quarter.
items.quote: So Shravan, year -on-year, CPVC volume has grown by 17%. And quarter -on-quarter, it was roughly around 7%.

items.statement: CPVC expected to see double-digit growth ahead.
items.quote: And we see in CPVC definitely a double-digit growth going ahead.

items.statement: Confident of improving margins independent of ADD and BIS.
items.quote: Independent of ADD and BIS, we are confident of improving the margins. I would not again like to place a number on that, but margin definitely, we see a margin improvement.

items.statement: Adding 50,000 tons capacity, with 25,000 already done in Q4 FY25 and the rest in next couple of months.
items.quote: See capacity increase incremental will continue to happen with 25,000, we added. our total project is 50,000 addition to capacity, which within this quarter or early next quarter, we'll complete that 50,000. Partly 25,000 has already happened during Q4 '25 . The remaining is happening in the next couple of months.

items.statement: Pipe capacity will increase from 420,000 to 470,000 tons.
items.quote: 420,000 will go to 470,000. 50,000 is currently enough. So it will be 520,000.

items.statement: Recent PVC price increase of INR2.5 per kg due to strong demand, not ADD.
items.quote: No, sir, this price increase, which has happened in the last week has nothing to do with ADD. This is basically because of strong demand from the market for the last couple of months.

items.statement: If ADD imposed, PVC prices could recover by INR3 to INR6 per kg.
items.quote: But INR3 to INR4 is something, which I think is definitely -- which can go through. So as I said, it can be anywhere between -- so if you want to place a range, it can be between INR3 to INR6.

items.statement: April and May saw strong demand, but monsoon may slow it down.
items.quote: Right now, in fact, April and May have been very strong months for us, both agri and non-agri. In fact, till the rain started a couple of years -- I mean, a couple of days ago, we have been completely sold out on inventory.

items.statement: Agri to non-agri mix was 67:33 in FY25.
items.quote: So FY '25, our agri to non-agri was 67%:33%.

items.statement: Agri volume grew 2% and non-agri 9% in FY25.
items.quote: Agri volume more or less 2% in terms of totality and non-agri around 9%.

items.statement: Industry PVC pipe growth expected at 8-10% CAGR over next 5-6 years.
items.quote: See, CAGR has always been about 8% to 10%, and there is no reason for that to change drastically either lower or higher. So we expect that close to double-digit trend to continue, both on agri as well as non -agri side.

items.statement: CPVC becoming commoditized, margins may soften but still better than SPVC.
items.quote: So today, the special status that CPVC enjoys, we believe that going ahead, it is getting more and more commoditized. On the manufacturing side, also a lot of players have got into CPVC. So the super margins, which prevailed at one time have already softened a bit.

items.statement: Excess cash may be returned to shareholders if not used for capex, but Board decision pending.
items.quote: Finally, if we don't have a very large capex, then it will be returned to the shareholders. But it's a Board's decision. So I would not like to specify anything right now.

items.statement: Expects around 20% revenue growth for FY26, plus or minus something.
items.quote: We are expecting around 20% growth plus/minus something. See, last year also, we were expecting certain businesses to click, but our growth is a lumpy growth.

items.statement: Margins expected at similar level to current.
items.quote: But right now, it is looking all at the similar level what we have today. So I think a fair assumption is to at about similar level of margins.

items.statement: Plans to invest INR 15-20 crores in relay manufacturing, scaling as demand grows.
items.quote: We plan to invest about between, let's say, INR 15 crores to INR 20 crores roughly and then scale up as the demand, whatever demand will be, but it is subject to lot of this number that I'm saying will be there will be a lot of changes due to the level of automation that we decide.

items.statement: Relay business peak revenue potential INR 70-100 crores.
items.quote: Maybe between INR 70 crores to INR 100 crores maybe roughly.

items.statement: Relay margins range 10-25% depending on customization.
items.quote: So margins can range from, let's say, between 10% to 25%, depending on the level of customization that you do.

items.statement: Adding new furnace by December, capacity to increase 6-7 times from calendar year 2026.
items.quote: So we have already ordered new furnace and our capacity will become almost 6-7 times of what we have today.

items.statement: Alloy business expected INR 20-30 crores this year.
items.quote: This year, we are expecting somewhere between INR 20 crores to INR 30 crores maybe for alloy.

items.statement: Alloy margins expected 12-20% this year.
items.quote: My expectation is, it should be somewhere between 15% to 20%, somewhere between or maybe you can consider between, let's say, 12% to 20% in between somewhere there, it should be during this year

items.statement: Quantum Magnetics production stopped due to China export restrictions; uncertain for current year.
items.quote: But currently, our production is stopped.

items.statement: Planning to fund large capex for rare earth magnets via debt-equity mix.
items.quote: And regarding the long-term, yes, we have to the capex required is quite large, and we will be we are planning how to fund that capex by way of debt equity, maybe a mix and that we are planning.

items.statement: EV demand from Western OEMs reduced; Indian EV outlook good.
items.quote: And the overall demand from them has only reduced, particularly I'm talking about American and European EV manufacturers. I mean their demand reduced, so their Tier 1 demand reduced.

items.statement: Not affected by US import duty; no change expected in US business.
items.quote: No, we are not affected by that import duty. Our product is customized product.

items.statement: Shift towards standardized products may lower margins.
items.quote: So as we move towards more and more standardized products, margins will come down.

items.statement: Export energy meters expected 5-10% growth over next 2-3 years.
items.quote: Today, what we are doing you can expect about 5%, 10% growth is all right.

items.statement: New plant operations expected in 2-3 years.
items.quote: In totality, I'm saying about 2 to 3 years, we should start some kind of operations in the new plant.

items.statement: Will stick to 20-25% growth guidance.
items.quote: We'll stick to the guidance of 20%, 25% growth. This year, why we couldn't achieve it is because few of our projects are stuck in the environmental clearances, which is having a stay from the Supreme Court of India since 1 year, which impacted the start of construction for all the projects.

items.statement: Target construction spend of INR650 crores for the financial year.
items.quote: And with respect to capex for construction, our target is to do construction of around INR650 crores for the financial year.

items.statement: Expect to sustain EBITDA margins around 24-25%, growing to 26-27% as new projects contribute.
items.quote: Yes, we should be able to sustain at around 24%, 25% in the coming quarters once the new projects start contributing, which we have acquired over the last 2 years. They will have higher EBITDA margins. So then we expect it to grow around 26%, 27% once those projects also start contributing to the revenue.

items.statement: Average pricing to increase to INR6,500-6,700 per sq ft on annual basis.
items.quote: It will be around INR6,500, INR6,700 on average so -- on a year-on-year basis. So this year, we did INR6,084 per square feet, which we expect it to go to around INR6,500 on a total financial year basis.

items.statement: Expect at least 5-7% price increase in Panvel, Taloja, Kharghar locations.
items.quote: How the price trends could be on a blended basis for the next year, we expect at least 5% to 7% increase in the prices for these locations because these are the hot destinations today.

items.statement: Construction halted until environmental clearance received; sales ongoing.
items.quote: So the construction is halted till we get the clearance, although sales is happening.

items.statement: Expect environmental clearance by Q2 or Q3, revenue recognition from Q4 FY26.
items.quote: So we expect it to be cleared by, say, Q2 or maybe October, basically, which is Q3. So once that is done, recognition can start in 1 or max 2 quarters. So we expected that recognition should happen from Q4 of FY '26. So fingers crossed.

items.statement: Comfortable with net debt up to INR750-800 crores; secured debt to INR500 crores.
items.quote: So as of now, we are at around INR685 crores of net debt and we'll be comfortable with the debt going to around INR750 crores, INR800 crores. So out of this INR685 crores, INR300 crores is unsecured loans, which is payable when and able. So balance the net debt, which is secured debt is only INR385 crores. So we'll be comfortable to sustain the secured debt to around INR500 crores. So that is comf

items.statement: Limited land acquisitions planned in FY26.
items.quote: With respect to more acquisitions. So we have not lined up many more acquisitions in this coming financial year. We feel we have enough land now to execute and implement the projects, which can give out good, positive cash flows to the company over the next 2 to 3 years. So limited investments will happen towards land acquisitions in FY '26 at least.

items.statement: New phase launches planned for existing projects in FY26.
items.quote: So we have phased -- new phase launches for FY '26 for the existing projects. So one of them is at Arihant Avanti in Shilphata where we'll be opening the third tower. There's also more launches planned -- lined up in Arihant Aspire Panvel, which is also one of our largest projects.

items.statement: Town Villas in design stage, start FY27 onwards.
items.quote: We are in the design stage at the moment for Town Villas, and it should take another 1 year for it to start. So it's all FY '27 onwards.

items.statement: World Villas sales to cover up in Q1 and Q2.
items.quote: But Q1 onwards, we started gaining momentum, and Q2, we'll really be able to cover up a lot because majorly this is -- I mean, today, we see a great weather with respect to World Villa sales and clients who are going are very much attracted to the greenery and the environmental development over there. So we'll be able to cover it up in the next 2 quarters, Q1 and Q2.

items.statement: Already spent a little more than Rs. 100 crores on graphite anode plant implementation.
items.quote: So in terms of implementation, a little bit more than Rs. 100 crores we have already spent and we have started committing against the main machinery.

items.statement: Graphite anode project capital will be a mix of debt and equity.
items.quote: It will be a mix of debt and equity.

items.statement: Approximately 11 million tons of new greenfield electric arc furnace capacities commissioned in last 18 months; another 25 to 30 million tons expected in next 18 months.
items.quote: We believe over the last 18 months or so, approximately 11 million tons of new greenfield electric arc furnace capacities have already been commissioned and in the next 18 months, this figure is likely to be in the region of another 25 to 30 million tons.

items.statement: Total new electric arc furnace capacities including last 12 months actual commissions of about 10, 12 million tons, it's more than 100 million tons.
items.quote: So from all the various data that we collect from different sources, the total new electric arc furnace capacities including the last 12 months actual commissions of about 10, 12 million tons, it's more than 100 million tons.

items.statement: International peers announced intent to increase electrode prices by about 15% to 20% in last 2 quarters; some price increases being absorbed.
items.quote: You are aware that given their high cost structur e and incurring significant losses, most of our international peers had announced their intent to increase electrode prices by about 15% to 20% in last 2 quarters. While we do see some price increases being absorbed in the market, we hope in the coming quarters the impact of significant closures of above capacities would help the industry to get ba

items.statement: Some price increase may be on the way, but wait for a quarter or two for clear direction; prices should increase towards second half.
items.quote: But what the sense we are getting at is that yes, some price increase may be on the way, but we have to wait for a while because the orders which we have on hand, of course, they have to be executed. So towards, let's say the second half, I think, and we hope that prices should increase.

items.statement: Needle coke prices have been stable in the last 3 quarters and expected to remain in same range for next 1 or 2 quarters.
items.quote: See, the needle coke prices have been stable. Needle coke prices have been stable in the last 3 quarters. Now they are also, of course, needle coke prices are tied to the electrode prices. So let's say in the next 1 or 2 quarters, we think they should be in the same range because the electrode prices are also going to be in the same range.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved from 16% in Q1 to 21% in Q3 to 27% in Q4, with full year average 21%.
items.quote: Our EBITDA quarter-on-quarter has been going up. It was 16% in Q1, which went up to 21% in Q3. And in last quarter, Q4, it was as high as 27%, with a full year average being 21%.

items.statement: Margin sustainability depends on pricing; cannot pinpoint 20% or 22%.
items.quote: See, it will all depend on the pricing. I mean what can I tell you? I mean, I can't pinpoint the number of 20%, 22%.

items.statement: US 10% import duties may impact business, but overall impact expected limited due to diversified sales footprint.
items.quote: The recent imposition of 10% import duties in the US, if not withdrawn, will have some impact on our business. However, given HEG's very well diversified sales, sales footprint across all major global markets, the overall impact is expected to be limited.

items.statement: US tariffs at 10% for now; real date is 9th July, uncertain whether it will come back to zero or remain at 10%.
items.quote: No, it is 10%. For the time being, it is 10% no t only from India, but from all over the world. So we will have to see, wait and se e. I mean, the real date is the 9th of July, when this 10%..until when it is 10%, we never know whether it will come back to zero or it will remain at 10% or… I mean, it's just speculation today

items.statement: New electric arc furnace capacities in western economies require big ultra-high power electrodes, where competition from China is minimal.
items.quote: No, most of these new capacities of electric arc furnaces which are coming up, these 100 million tons that we are talking about, these are all in the western economies. So obviously they are putting up large furnaces which will require bi g size electrodes which we call ultra high power and that's where the competition from China is minimal

items.statement: Domestic graphite anode demand expected 100,000 to 140,000 tons by 2030; first stage 20,000 tons, hope to double in next 4 to 5 years.
items.quote: I think by the year 2030 you will see a demand of between 100,000 tons to 140,000 tons based on the cell battery that will be produced in India. So we are looking at not only the global market but actually the India market itself would be mature enough to consume 120,000 tons of graphite anode powder. So our first stage, of course, we are starting with 20,000, but we hope that in the same location

items.statement: Demerger scheme filed with stock exchanges and authorities; expect all approvals by end of calendar year 2025.
items.quote: Our scheme has been filed with stock exchanges and all other relevant authorities, after which it will go to NCLT. We expect to get all the required approvals by end of calendar year 2025.

items.statement: Capacity utilization for FY25 close to 80% based on expanded capacity of 100,000 tons; hope to maintain or increase slightly in current year.
items.quote: Our capacity utilization for the year 2024-25 was close to 80% based on our expanded capacity of 100,000 tons and we hope to maintain this in the cu rrent year too, if not increase th is a little bit

items.statement: Focus on D2C, leisure, and retail; strong in corporate and student.
items.quote: The focus is on D2C, leisure and retail, because already we are strong in corporate and student.

items.statement: Launching multi-currency card variant shortly; sees it as big opportunity.
items.quote: We have launched the single currency card variant. We are shortly launching the multi-currency card variant and we are looking at it as a big opportunity both in terms of direct sales and channel sales.

items.statement: Will apply for PA-CB license within this quarter or before next quarter ends.
items.period: this quarter or before next quarter ends
items.quote: That is the idea that we will apply it within this quarter or max before the next quarter ends.

items.statement: Next 6-9 months focus on scaling Direct Card Issuance business.
items.quote: So next 6 months to 9 months, our focus will be on getting the Direct Card Issuance business into scale.

items.statement: Aim to increase platform usage from 50-60% to 80%.
items.quote: We need to see everything put together, but our idea is to slowly pivot from that 50%-60% level to the 80% level.

items.statement: Aim to card every student, take attachment rate to 100%.
items.quote: In fact, it has been a key focus for us to ensure that every student gets a card, whether the load is small or big, and that drive is on. Of course, today, you may say that is not 100%, but our aim is to take it to 100% levels.

items.statement: Aim to reach 80% of corporate business on platform.
items.quote: We have around close to 50% on the platform because bigger companies are more ready to get into the platform. There is some resistance by smaller companies. We are working on it, but our aim is to at least reach 80%.

items.statement: Student segment under pressure due to geopolitical situation and visa restrictions.
items.quote: As you are all aware, student segment is under a little bit of pressure because of the geopolitical situation.

items.statement: TCS guidelines impact business; ticket size reduced.
items.quote: One of the impacts which has been there for the last 1, 1.5 years has been the TCS guidelines where there is a TCS of 5% and 20% when it comes to personal remittances in travel.

items.statement: Corporate business not growing as fast as anticipated, still below pre-COVID levels.
items.quote: Corporate business where we have a key strength, is not growing as fast as we would have anticipated because it's still not reached the pre-COVID levels because of technology and collaboration through VCs etc.

items.statement: Leisure travel seen as biggest opportunity, validated by LRS numbers.
items.quote: We feel growth in leisure travel is the biggest opportunity as of now and it's als o validated by the LRS numbers

items.statement: FXC opportunity anticipated this year, pending RBI approval.
items.quote: Now this is something which has not still come through, but we are hopeful that this year it will come through, which will ensure that we have distribution reach through this network.

items.statement: Working on platform for seamless student fee payments.
items.quote: We are also working on a platform which will help the students fo r making the fees seamlessly and that's one activity w hich we are working on

items.statement: Working with tour operators and expense management companies like Zaggle.
items.quote: We are also working with leading expense management companies like Zaggle. We have also got some 200-300 agents who are working with us.

items.statement: Deferred tax reversal of Rs. 3 crores; remaining Rs. 2 crores to reverse next year.
items.quote: So still we have some deferred tax in the asset which is around Rs. 2 crores or so. So in the next year, when it will be utilized that time it will be reversed.

items.statement: Tax rate applicable is 22% plus surcharge, so 25%.
items.quote: It is 22%, right plus surcharge, so 25%.

items.statement: Standalone EMS and BTS to grow at blended rate of 25% to 28%.
items.quote: And we expect that growth momentum to continue , and basically at a standalone level both the EMS and the BTS part of the business should grow for us at a blended rate of somewhere in the range of about 25% to 28%.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue to grow 18% to 20%.
items.quote: Yes. On a consolidated basis, we will grow for 18% to 20%, and that is basically driven by a higher growth rate contribution from the standalone entity, which is at over the 25% level, whereas at the subsidiary level we would be roughly flat, I would say.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin of 10% possible.
items.quote: Yes. That should be definitely be possible at the consol level.

items.statement: Goal to improve consolidated EBITDA margin to around 12% in next two years.
items.quote: Yes. Definitely. I think that's our goal, to improve that from 10% to probably around 12% in the next two years.

items.statement: Targeting 18% to 20% CAGR for next three years.
items.quote: As we have been maintaining, we are targeting 18% to 20% CAGR for the next three years.

items.statement: Planning to invest Rs. 40 crores in standalone capex for FY26.
items.quote: Okay. We are planning to invest about Rs. 40 crores, that again only in the standalone, essentially to augment the capabilities and increase the capacities, both in the BTS segment as well as the EMS segment.

items.statement: Targeting Rs. 2,000 crores of order booking in next three to four years.
items.quote: The pipeline of orders is healthy, I mentioned this in the past, we are roughly looking at something in the range of about Rs. 2,000 crores of booking in the next three to four years, that's what we are targeting.

items.statement: Typical EBITDA margin for build-to-spec around 20%, EMS 10-12%.
items.quote: So, your typical EBITDA margin for build-to-spec can be in the range of 20% or so . And whereas on the EMS side of the business, it's more build-to-print, and that is typically in the 10% to 12% level or so.

items.statement: Canadian subsidiary loss; targeting resolution by September or sooner.
items.quote: So, there will be something that we are doing and we are targeting to have this completed by September or sooner.

items.statement: Space applications 40-50% of BTS order book.
items.quote: But at a high level, I would say, space applications are I would say in the range of somewhere about 40% to 50% of that part.

items.statement: Gross vs net accounting confusion will not continue in FY26.
items.quote: It will not continue. It is only for the last year. In FY '26, the confusion between gross and net accounting will not be there.

items.statement: Expects substantial revenues and billing from electronic intelligence program this year.
items.quote: And we expect this year that we will have substantial revenues and billing from this program as well.

items.statement: Order book executable over 15 to 18 months overall.
items.quote: And maybe at an overall basis something in the range of about 15 months or so, 15 odd months I would say, 15 to 18 months is what you can look at.

items.statement: Confident of achieving $450 million top line, 16% EBITDA, and 30% return on capital employed in FY26.
items.value: $450 million, 16% EBITDA, 30% return on capital employed
items.quote: We have given a guidance for 25-26 as part of our five year guidance that we did five years ago. We are quite confident that we will hit that that you know, I don't want to get into aggressive and conservative, but that's really our projection which is $450 million of top line revenue. 16% EBITDA and 30% return on capital employed.

items.statement: India expected to grow low to mid double digit if economy remains whole and no global tariff impact.
items.quote: So assuming India remains whole economically and there is no impact of tariffs globally. I expect India to grow double digit, but I would probably say low to mid double digit.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue growth expected at minimum same as last year's 9% if steady state.
items.quote: Will next year be better than this. Again, I don't want to put anything on the ground because a lot of uncertainties at the moment with respect to the US tariff and its impact. Rippling impact on the various economies. Of the world, assuming it is, everything comes back to a steady state. Nothing negative, and India continues to be a good story. We should be able to do this. Minimum do this same g

items.statement: Confident of hitting 16% EBITDA margin as one-time expenses won't repeat.
items.quote: As far as profitability is concerned, we will hit. We were already hitting close to 16% even this year manish. It is just that one-time expenses and clean up that we did that dropped out EBITDA. So what is going to happen is that is not going to get repeated. In next year. And therefore, we're quite confident that we'll be able to hit those numbers.

items.statement: Can absorb 10% tariff without impacting profitability due to motor plant savings.
items.quote: For 26 the assuming, 10% tariff we have like I explained to you, we will be able to absorb that 10% without any impact on our profitability, because the savings that we have from our motor plant and a few other initiatives that we kicked off almost couple of years ago for cost reduction is more than enough to absorb it.

items.statement: Can sustain current pricing and profitability up to 16% reciprocal tariff.
items.quote: And assuming they are going to make it in the worst-case reciprocal to that same percentage in this range, we are pretty much ok with all the cost reduction initiatives we can sustain our current pricing and our profitability.

items.statement: If US moves to 26% tariff, may need to increase prices or find other ways.
items.quote: But if they move to 26% like they originally did, then that could be we need to make a decision in terms of either increasing prices or finding other ways as we speak all our competitors.

items.statement: Portable compressors expected to remain subdued in current year due to market drop.
items.quote: Portables is a more a market structural thing. You know for three years there is a big growth and since the last couple of years there has been a significant almost a 30-40% drop in the market and we are feeling the effect of it and we expect this this portable to remain subdued in the current year as well.

items.statement: Stabilizer and Chinese-import-competing machines to be fully launched by Q3.
items.quote: Our machines for competing with the Chinese Imports are already working in the field and we are confident that by the third quarter both these products will be out in the market full-fledged and our earlier initiative called Project Everest for increasing our share of the market is going very well.

items.statement: Aftermarket share in India 27-28%, rest of world 13-14%, expected to improve.
items.quote: It's about 27-28% is on our revenue in India in the rest of the world, we are probably around 13 to 14% right now in both these percentages have to keep improving as we progress through the life cycle of life of the of the. Operation, I mean I we get more and more machines installed then there is more and more aftermarket coming in.

items.statement: Motor plant capacity not an issue; machines being installed after visa delays.
items.quote: So now that is opened up and the machines are getting installed. So we're quite confident. That we have the capacity. That's not an issue.

items.statement: Siemens railway business to see movement in Q3 and Q4, significant improvement next year.
items.quote: So I think we will see some movement of the business during the third and fourth quarter of this year. But I think next year we will see more of a significant you know improvement in the in that model of compressors and locomotives.

items.statement: Europe faces tariff uncertainty; will watch Q1 and adjust cost structure if needed.
items.quote: But the only caution here now is the Tariff other than that, we are not pretty strong wicket, right. But we are watching the situation very carefully. We are not going to invest anything more, right. What we are going to do is in response to any, if there is any challenges, we will look at cost structure changes, not in terms of you know this Willy nilly. reduction in cost, but structurally change

items.statement: US operations profitable on steady state basis excluding one-time clean-up costs.

items.statement: Q4 discounts and returns caused loss; will take adequate provisioning to make Q4 zero level.
items.quote: But we'll make sure that, again, this financial year, we take adequate provisioning to make at least at a zero level for fourth quarter.

items.statement: Expects 5-10 days reduction in debtor days from tying up with distributors.
items.quote: We expect 5 to 10 days of debtor days should come down going forward.

items.statement: Inventory will remain at current level plus/minus 5%.
items.quote: So, in that case, we don't see a very significant improvement in the inventory level, but it will remain at this level, plus/minus 5%.

items.statement: Tied up with Style from Landmark Group to supply 8,000-10,000 pieces in UAE.
items.quote: And we've also tied up with Style, which is from the Landmark Group in the UAE, to supply around 8,000 to 10,000 pieces of Monte Carlo products in the UAE market.

items.statement: Plans to shut down 150 MBOs in West Bengal and Northeast and open EBOs instead.
items.quote: And so, what we've taken a call is we are going to shut down these 150-odd MBO outlets and instead open our own exclusive brand outlets to service these markets.

items.statement: Sunroof JV revenues will start from FY27, not FY26.
items.quote: So Raghu, the revenues will not be in FY26. As we have committed before, the revenues will be starting from FY27.

items.statement: Flash Electronics revenue growth expected in mid-to-high double-digit percentage.
items.quote: So Raghu, the growth momentum in the revenue of Flash Electronics should be again in the similar range that they have been doing for the last few years. So, again, in the range of mid - to high double -digit percentage.

items.statement: Capex to remain INR 250-350 crores; Flash capex INR 50-100 crores.
items.value: INR 250 crores to max INR 350 crores
items.quote: Going forward, we see the capex to remain in the range of about INR 250 crores to max INR 350 crores. And as regards the capex in Flash is concerned, again, that should broadly be in the range of INR 50 crores to INR 100 crores only.

items.statement: Lifetime orders over INR 8,000 crores, with 25% from EV platforms.
items.quote: During the year, the Company booked lifetime orders exceeding INR 8,000 crores with approximately 25% of new orders coming from electric vehicle platforms.

items.statement: Highest-ever EBITDA margin of 11.6% in Q4 FY25.
items.quote: The Company reported highest-ever EBITDA of INR 153 crores, along with the highest ever margin of 11.6% for the quarter, demonstrating strong operational execution and the effectiveness of our strategic initiatives.

items.statement: EV sales were 8% of Q4 revenue and 7% for full year.
items.quote: In Q4, EV sales stood at about 8% of the Minda Corporation's total revenue and on a full year basis, it is approximately 7%.

items.statement: Digital clusters to grow to 40% of instrument cluster business in 18-24 months.
items.quote: So currently about INR 800 crores plus revenue of the Minda Instruments Limited, you can say the digital clusters contribute somewhere about 25% to 30% and, of course, this is expected to grow to somewhere about 40% or so in the next, let's say, 18 months to 24 months.

items.statement: PAT impacted by higher finance costs from Flash investment and increased depreciation.
items.quote: This was impacted by higher finance costs associated with the strategic investment in flash electronics and increased depreciation stemming from ongoing capacity expansion and technolog ical upgrades.

items.statement: Promoter investment at INR 550 per share; 25% in 2 weeks, 75% in 18 months.
items.quote: We are expecting the stock exchanges approval within this week, and 25% of the money should be received max within 2 weeks and thereafter, as per the terms, the balance 75% can be paid by the promoters within 18 months.

items.statement: Sensors revenue for FY25 is INR 250-300 crores, expected to grow.
items.quote: But for the current year, our sensors revenue is in the tune of about INR 250 crores to INR 300 crores. This is expected to grow further while we are localizing many sensors in India , and some of the new sensors are also going SOP in the next few quarters to come.

items.statement: Cross-selling with Flash to reach close to 3-digit number by FY27.
items.quote: And by FY27, we can see maybe close to a 3-digit number coming into cross-selling.

items.statement: Localization of Minda connectors to reach 20-25% in 18-24 months.
items.quote: Our target is to reach about 20% to 25% over the next 18 to 24 months. All efforts are in those directions.

items.statement: Debt to equity target reduced to 0.2x in 2-3 years.
items.quote: So, yes, the interest is how we can bring down the 0.5x debt to equity to about 0.2x in the next 2 to 3 years.

items.statement: Utilization currently at 65-80% across organization.
items.quote: But overall, we, as an organization, are currently working to the tune of about 65% to 80% of utilization. So different segments, different plants will have that variation.

items.statement: Flash Electronics FY25 revenue INR 1,537 crores, EBITDA margin 14.5%.
items.quote: In line with our estimation, Flash Electronics has delivered INR 1,537 crores for the full year. EBITDA at about INR 223 crores with EBITDA margin of 14.5% and EV revenue stands at 23%, which is a 92% growth on a Y-o-Y basis.

items.statement: Expect EBITDA margins in low 20s as initial goal, with established centers over 20% and emerging centers improving toward that level
items.quote: But is it good to say as the emerging centers also rack up, our margin, as we always indicated, will be in the low 20s. That is our initial goal.

items.statement: Expect more than 20% EBITDA margin in future from current portfolio, but new center operationalization may cause dilution until scale-up
items.quote: In our current portfolio, we should be expecting more than 20% in the future to come in the near future. However, as we operationalize new centres as part of our expansion initiative, overall we may see dilution till these centres scale up to steady state.

items.statement: Plan capex of INR286 crores in FY26 for network expansion and technology upgrades
items.quote: Looking ahead, we plan a capex of INR286 crores in FY '26 in line with our network expansion and technology upgrade plans.

items.statement: Capex of INR286 crores in FY26 includes ~INR100 crores maintenance capex and growth capex in existing centers and markets like Bangalore and Cuttack
items.quote: I think it is in the range of about INR 280 crores. We already invested a little over INR200 crores in last financial year. That includes close to about INR100 crores of maintenance capex and large growth capex within our existing centers and markets are in Bangalore and Cuttack.

items.statement: Aim to operationalize over 900 beds across network within next 3 years, including 350 beds fully invested but not yet operational
items.quote: As informed earlier, we aim to expand in our existing markets by operationalizing over 900 beds across networks within next 3 years, including this year's addition and 350 beds that are fully invested but not yet operational.

items.statement: Established centers at over 20% EBITDA margin, emerging centers at a little over 10%, blended near 18%; emerging centers grew revenue 32% and EBITDA 44% in Q4 FY25
items.quote: You would notice that we have over 20% margin in our established centers, showcasing the strength of the platform. However, our emerging centers are a little over 10%. Together, we are delivering close to about 18% margin.

items.statement: Expect EBITDA margins to improve as emerging centers scale toward established center margins, driven by operating leverage
items.quote: As our emerging centers continue to grow, which is again reflected in last year's performance, you will see that our revenue grew by 32% and our EBITDA has grown by 44% in the same quarter for emerging centers, reflecting an increase in EBITDA margin as well.

items.statement: ARPOB increased 4% YoY to INR44,236 in Q4 FY25; established centers ARPOB INR42,591 (+2.5%), emerging centers INR66,755 (+12.4%)
items.quote: On the pricing and efficiency front, for the quarter ended 31st March '25, ARPOB across our network increased by 4%, reaching to INR 44,236. Established center recorded an ARPOB of INR42,591 growing by 2.5%, while emerging centers delivered an impressive ARPOB of INR66,755, growing by 12.4%.

items.statement: Expect 7-8% ARPOB growth in FY26 driven by decreasing length of stay and high-end treatment modalities
items.quote: With continu ous decrease in length of stay in the hospital coupled with high end treatment modalities we expect 7% to 8% increase in ARPOB

items.statement: Chemotherapy sessions grew 24% YoY in FY25, indicating growing patient demand; outpatient footfall rose 13.8%
items.quote: In medical oncology, we saw a 24% growth in chemotherapy sessions, a clear indicator of growing patient demand. Our LINAC machine utilization remained steady at 60% in quarter 4 of FY '25 with acquisition of 2 LINACs with MGM Hospital over the last 12 months.

items.statement: Digital revenue doubled in FY25; launched HCG mobile app for appointments, virtual consults, reports; expect digital to become major revenue contributor
items.quote: Digital revenue for FY '25 has doubled over the past year, and we are committed to scaling this further. We launched our official HCG mobile app, a platform that enables to book appointments, consult doctor virtually, access reports and manage their care journey end-to-end.

items.statement: Medical oncology (chemotherapy) grew 24% vs other modalities; least profitable but highly return-accretive and least capital intensive
items.quote: You would see in Slide number 30, that our chemotherapy volumes have grown by 24%, which is higher than other modality. I would like to just inform the participants here that while we practice comprehensive cancer care and all the modalities are equally important for us. F rom a financial outcome perspective, medical oncology modality is least profitable, but highly return

items.statement: International patient revenue (3-4% of total) impacted by reduced medical visas for Bangladeshi patients due to geopolitical issues; expect suppression for next few months
items.quote: The biggest contributor to India, not just for HCG, but for all hospital players in terms of international business is Bangladesh. And as you know, because of geopolitical issues between our 2 countries, India has reduced drastically the number of medical visas that India grants to Bangladeshi patients.

items.statement: Primary equity infusion expected in coming months with new investor KKR; proceeds may reduce debt and interest cost, improving PAT
items.quote: And one other addition I want to add before you take is regarding the debt issue, we have communicated to the investors in the past that once the new investors, shareholders come, we will be looking at the possibility of primary equity coming into the system, and this will be decided in the coming few months.

items.statement: Plan to divest Milann fertility business this fiscal year after addressing partner competition issues and discussing with new investor KKR
items.quote: We have addressed this issue internally. We were just waiting for the new investor also to come. We have also discussed with them. So, we are definitely putting a proposal to divest. And hopefully, this will happen definitely this fiscal year, and we'll keep you updated.

items.statement: Effective tax rate expected around 30% for FY26
items.quote: I think we can expect about 30-odd percent to remain in that level during the next 1 year.

items.statement: Aims for annual sales of ₹25 crore in welding within two years.
items.quote: With this momentum, we aim to achieve annual sales of ₹25 crore within the next two years.

items.statement: Comfortable achieving ₹25 crore target in two years for welding.
items.quote: And as we have set a target of ₹25 crore in 2 years, I think we are very comfortable in achieving that.

items.statement: Plans to add 3 flux cored wire production lines costing about ₹3 crore.
items.quote: So, CapEx req uirement for Flux Cored Wire, I would say where we are currently hosting 3 production lines and we plan to go ramp it up with 3 more productions lines in the new near future, which will approximately cost us ₹ 3 crore.

items.statement: Each flux cored wire production line costs approximately ₹1 crore.
items.quote: We only need to invest in the production lines, which cost approximately ₹1 crore per line.

items.statement: Expects single digit growth in cored wire volumes.
items.quote: So, if steel production is moderate and not growing, I don't see our cored wires also doing too great -like a single digit growth is still expected due to the trust and the dependence that I mentioned, which is coming back to the existing players, the veteran players I see that happening now and which is why I can see a single digit growth in cored wires.

items.statement: Plans to scale flux-cored arc welding consumables from 70 to 100 tonnes monthly.
items.quote: Currently, we are selling approximately 70 tonnes of flux -cored arc welding consumables every month, and we have plans to scale this to 100 tonnes in the coming months.

items.statement: Aluminium business faces price mismatch and unethical environment.
items.quote: However, aluminium flipping coil business is facing major challenges with prices mismatch and unethical business environment.

items.statement: Global supply chain disruptions and low-grade business environment compressed margins.
items.quote: While we are scaling cautiously, global supply chain disruptions and low-grade business environment have significantly compressed margins across the industry.

items.statement: Invested ₹50 lakh in biotech pilot R&D facility.
items.quote: To date, we have invested ₹50 lakh, primarily for establishing a pilot R&D facility in Nagpur.

items.statement: Biotech pilot facility operational with 14 kg per batch capacity.
items.quote: The Solid State Fermentation (SSF) pilot facility, with a fermentation capacity of 14 kilograms in one batch, is now operational, and we successfully commenced the first production batch in May 2025.

items.statement: Targets scaling biotech batch capacity from 14 kg to 50 kg.
items.quote: We have built a 14 kg per batch capacity of space which we are standardizing and our target is to immediately take this 14 kgs to 50 kgs; and from those 50 kgs once we standardize the product and once we get the ideal activity of the product that is when I will be able to tell you the revenue scenario but we are confident with the amount of work that has been done in this one month, we are quite c

items.statement: Biotech fermentation cycle reduced from 6 days to 4 days, targeting 3 days.
items.quote: The fermentation cycle has been reduced from 6 days to now 4 days and we are looking at strategies to bring it down to 3 days.

items.statement: Biotech product activity increased 10-fold, targeting another 10-fold.
items.quote: We have already achieved 10 fold activity of the product from where we started only in a single digit per ML of product and we are confident to take this to another 10 fold activity.

items.statement: Expects clarity on aluminium business outlook by end of June 2025.
items.quote: We expect greater clarity on the aluminium business outlook by the end of June 2025, and we remain committed to making strategic decisions in the best interest of our long -term growth.

items.statement: Managing about 10 dealers across 5 states, plans rapid expansion.
items.quote: Currently we are managing approx. 10 dealers across 5 states and we plan to expand this network rapidly.

items.statement: Has 3 lines with total capacity of 250 MTs per month.
items.quote: We have currently 3 lines with a total capacity of 250 MTs per month.

items.statement: FY26 revenue growth expected at 25% with EBITDA margin 21% plus/minus 100 basis points.
items.value: 25% revenue growth, 21% EBITDA margins plus/minus 100 basis points
items.quote: In FY '26, we look forward to a 25% growth in revenues on a conservative note, with 21% EBITDA margins plus/minus 100 basis points.

items.statement: Average revenue growth of 25% year-on-year expected over next three years.
items.quote: Our consistent revenue growth over the past five years demonstrates sustained growth momentum and we remain confident in our abilit y to maintain this growth trajectory with an average growth of 25% year-on-y ear over the next three years due to multiple growth engines across various sectors

items.statement: Aerospace and defense sector expected to grow 80% in FY26.
items.quote: We anticipate a phenomenal growth of 80% from this sector in FY '26.

items.statement: Clean energy sector expected to grow 15-20% in FY26.
items.quote: We look forward to growth in clean energy at the rate of 15% to 20% in this sector including fuel cells, hydropower, battery storage systems and others.

items.statement: Nuclear sector revenue expected at Rs. 60 crores in FY26.
items.quote: To add to your point, like from Rs. 19 crores what we have done in FY '25, we are expecting to do Rs. 60 crores in FY '26.

items.statement: Products division expected to grow 20% in FY26.
items.quote: We recorded Rs. 148 crores revenue in products and other verticals, and we expect a 20% growth in this segment as well.

items.statement: Capex of Rs. 50-60 crores planned for FY26.
items.quote: See, right now, this year the basic minimum bottleneck areas, we are looking at about Rs. 50 crores to Rs. 60 crores of CapEx going in.

items.statement: Orders worth Rs. 720 crores secured in FY25, with Rs. 178 crores from aerospace and defense and Rs. 349 crores from clean energy.
items.quote: We have secured orders worth Rs. 720 crores in FY '25, for which Rs. 178 crores are from aerospace and defense which is a substantial improvement in this area and Rs. 349 crores of orders are from clean energy underlying our technological leadership in these sectors.

items.statement: Expecting Rs. 700-800 crores of orders from nuclear division over next one to two quarters.
items.quote: So, we are looking at anywhere between, I do not want to spell out individual numbers because of certain confidentiality, but we are looking at around Rs. 700 crores to Rs. 800 crores of orders flowing in over the next one, two quarters.

items.statement: Sequential improvement in EBITDA margins expected in FY26 due to operating leverage and scale-up.
items.quote: We anticipate a sequential improvement in EBITDA margins in FY '26 due to operating leverage and scale-up in production of new products developed over the past couple of years.

items.statement: Fuel cells business expected to grow 20% in FY26.
items.quote: But we will be growing at a rate of 20% compared to the last year what we have done. We have done around Rs. 450 crores plus last year, so we will do around 20% more this year.

items.statement: Diversification into aerospace and defense with higher margins to improve gross margins.
items.quote: But if you look at the way we are moving forward, we have diversified into the aerospace and defense sectors in a big way where the margins are much higher. So, basi cally the gross margins are also going to be higher in terms of these segments.

items.statement: Tariffs and external factors considered in guidance; confident in maintaining growth and margins.
items.quote: For example, the tariffs issue which is going on with the United States, we have considered all those factors in arriving at this particular growth percentage. And we feel that because of our diversification into various countries and exports, we are in a position where we are still able to maintain that growth and achieve the margins that what I have mentioned, 21%plus/minus 100 basis points.

items.statement: Working capital days target reduced to 200 days for FY26.
items.quote: And also, we would like to further try to reduce working capital for FY '26 to 200 days.

items.statement: Long-term contract with domestic companies for Rs. 20 crores per year over five years.
items.quote: The Company has also entered into long-term contract with some of the few domestic companies for execution of Rs. 20 crores year-on-year over the next five years.

items.statement: Expect 600 net store additions in FY26
items.quote: We expect a total of 600 net store additions in FY '26.

items.statement: Steady-state gross margin expected at 24.5% to 24.75% for pharmacy business
items.quote: Your other question on the steady -state gross margin, we would look at in the range of 24.5% to around 24.75% going forward.

items.statement: Private label share to grow ~1% per quarter going forward
items.quote: I think we will definitely be able to maintain the 1% growth pretty easily.

items.statement: Same-store sales growth expected at high single digits to low double-digits
items.value: high single digits to low double-digit
items.quote: I expect it to be, let's say, high single digits to low double-digit kind of number on the SSG.

items.statement: Added 10 warehouses in FY25, nearly doubling warehouse count
items.quote: As an update, we have added around 10 additional warehouses in the last financial year to enhance our availability at our existing outlet and further supporting our endeavour in new store expansion.

items.statement: Net store additions of 305 in FY25 (gross 398, closures 93)
items.quote: Over the past 12 months, we have added a net total of 305 stores, gross 398 store addition, and we closed down certain stores.

items.statement: Pharmacy operating EBITDA margin 5.2% in Q4 FY25, 4.5% for full year FY25
items.quote: The pharmacy operating EBITDA stood at INR769 million, representing 5.2%.

items.statement: Store-level EBITDA margin 11.5% for stores >12 months, 11.7% for >24 months, 8.2% for 13-24 months
items.quote: Revenue from these stores in Q4 was INR14,011 million, representing 95% of pharmacy revenue. These stores had a store level EBITDA margin of 11.5%.

items.statement: Private label pharma share 20.9% of GMV in Q4 FY25 vs 7.9% pre-launch in Q1 FY24
items.quote: In Q1 FY '24, prior to the launch, the share of private label pharma stood at 7.9% of total GMV compared to 20.9% during the current quarter.

items.statement: Diagnostics active plans grew to 157,000 covering 327,000 lives by March 2025
items.quote: As on 31st March, we had 157,000 active plans and covering 327,000 underlying lives.

items.statement: Private label sales 23.3% of total revenue (pharma 13.6%, non-pharma 9.7%) in Q4 FY25
items.quote: Private label sales for Q4 FY '25 constitutes 23.3%, pharma 13.6% and non -pharma 9.7% of our total revenue.

items.statement: Fill rates affected in remote areas due to warehouse constraints and high attrition in large cities
items.quote: Fill rates, definitely, they were affected, and they were affected largely in the remote parts of the states, which are getting supplied from the main warehouses.

items.statement: Tax rate below 25% due to Section 80JJAA deduction for new employment; expected to continue for 3 years
items.quote: On the income tax, there is a deduction which the company continues to claim. It's the Section 80JJAA, which is linked with the employment created for new employees.

items.statement: Franchisee pilot planned as part of 600 store additions; wholesale model where MedPlus acts as super distributor
items.quote: Part of the stores which we are doing will be franchisee. This will be like a wholesale kind of model where we sell the product to the store, and he then sells it downwards.

items.statement: Targeting 250,000 active diagnostic plans before expanding to other states
items.quote: We need the number to be closer to 250,000 for us to actually take the leap of expanding to other states and all.

items.statement: Planning to launch private label GLP-1 injectable around patent expiry March 2026
items.quote: I know it is coming out of patent, I think March '26. And I'm hoping that we should be ready on day 1 or maybe if not day 1, maybe month 1.

items.statement: Mid- to high-teens revenue CAGR (15-18%) targeted over next 3 years; no specific FY26 number given
items.quote: We have not put out a specific number for FY '26, but midterm growth of high -- mid- to high teens is very much on course, 15% to 18% growth in top line CAGR over the next 3 years is very much on course.

items.statement: RVL targets breakeven this quarter or early next quarter; aims for 20-22% of overall revenue in 3 years
items.quote: We definitely will have no loss in March 2026. That's the target that we are currently looking at. And with regards to your question over the next 3 years, my hope is that gradually at least it will contribute to about 20% to 22% of the overall revenue will come from this business.

items.statement: Acemoney targets 90,000 POS machines installed in FY26, up from 64,228 in FY25
items.quote: We have installed 64,228 POS machines in the last financial year and has set an ambitious target of 90,000 machines for the current financial year.

items.statement: Acemoney achieved 20%+ EBITDA margins in FY25, contributing positively to consolidated performance
items.quote: The rapid scaling has achieved healthy EBITDA margins of 20%-plus for the year, contributing significantly to the overall consolidated performance of the Radiant Group.

items.statement: MFI sector expected to bounce back with 15-17% AUM growth in FY26 after ~20% shrinkage in FY25
items.quote: The industry Sa-Dhan has put out an expectation that they expect the industry to bounce back and worst is behind them. And they expect about 15% to 17% growth in the industry AUM in the current year after a shrinking of about almost 20% last year.

items.statement: Cash in circulation at INR36-37 lakh crores supports continued cash dominance in rural areas; >50% retail outlets lack digital payments
items.quote: As you can see, the continuous growth in cash in circulation, I think it's already crossed INR37 lakh crores, indicates that cash will continue to be a dominant mode of payment in rural areas. As we realized in our Acemoney subsidiary, more than 50% of the retail outlets do not have any form of digital payment mechanism yet.

items.statement: RVL cash burn continues but not a concern; infrastructure largely shared with cash logistics; breakeven targeted this quarter or early next
items.quote: So these are the reasons as to why there is some amount of cash burn in that, which we're not unduly concerned about, and we are gradually moving quickly towards a breakeven situation in this quarter or in early next quarter.

items.statement: Added 86 new clients, 456 new end customers, 8,048 new retail touch points in retail cash management in FY25
items.quote: During this financial year, we added 86 new clients, 456 new end customers and 8,048 new retail touch points in our retail cash management business.

items.statement: April FY26 cash volumes better than March FY25; positive trend noted
items.quote: April numbers have been better than our March numbers. And March was the last month of the year -- financial year. So the positive trend that there has been an increase is very heartening.

items.statement: Cash van fleet of 7,000-10,000 nationally; significant growth opportunity with new contracts
items.quote: Cash van is, again, a very important segment. And currently, there are over 7,000 to 10,000 cash vans currently deployed all over the country. So it's a huge opportunity that we are looking at right now.

items.statement: Cash balance INR80 crores at end of FY25
items.quote: Cash balance, we have about INR80 crores of cash balance.

items.statement: Top line to grow 25% plus from current level.
items.quote: Once again, I tell you that it would be 25% plus from the current top line.

items.statement: Targeting at least 25% annual year-on-year growth and improving bottom line.
items.quote: So, on the constrained basis, if we say we are target, we are trying out to be working at least 25% annual year-on-year on that and improving our bottom line by adding up various other higher-margin products, and we are entering into retail segment also, and that will add on additional value.

items.statement: Demand expected to increase by 25%.
items.quote: And at the constrained, we are seeing that the demand would increase by 25%, but it would be much better than that I think.

items.statement: B2B margin around 4%, B2C around 9-10%, blended around 5%.
items.quote: As previously, we have defined that B2B margin would be somewhere around 4% and B2C would be around 9% to 10%. So blended margin, you can say that it would be somewhere 5%.

items.statement: Margins to improve gradually, reaching 5% in coming 2 years.
items.quote: We cannot define that it may reach to 5% in next year itself. But gradually, surely in coming 2 years, it will surely reach.

items.statement: Secured order book worth INR55-60 crores at Gem & Jewellery India International Fair 2025.
items.quote: Another key highlight of this year was a strong presence at the Gem & Jewellery India International Fair, B2B Expo of 2025, where we secured a significant order book worth INR55 crores to INR60 crores, a clear testimony to the growing preference for our design and craftsmanship among industry peers.

items.statement: New flagship showroom to launch in Q2 FY26.
items.quote: As a part of our expansion strategy, we are on track to launch a new flagship showroom in second quarter of FY '26.

items.statement: Planning 4-5 branches around FY28.
items.quote: After opening up our flagship showroom, anyway, beyond the coming financial year, somewhere around FY '28, we are planning of expanding into various different areas where we could open 4 to 5 branches.

items.statement: Planning 5-6 showrooms in retail segment in 1-2 years after flagship.
items.quote: And for the retail segment, initially, we are coming up with our flagship showroom. And after completion of that, say, in another 1 or 2 years, there is an expansion plan of 5 to 6 room on the retail segment.

items.statement: B2C share to increase by 10% after flagship store.
items.quote: If everything works right, as of the percentage would be improved by 10% addition for B2C.

items.statement: 15% of turnover is high margin, rest medium and high margin.
items.quote: We cannot define that separately, but you can say that somewhere total turnover of 15% is of high margin, and all others are regular margins and we are dealing with all handmade jewellery.

items.statement: Lightweight and fusion jewellery giving higher margin.
items.quote: And since the lightweight jewellery are fusioned with the latest designs and technology, obviously, it is giving a higher margin.

items.statement: Gold price increases cause short-term slowdown but demand picks up.
items.quote: Once the price is accepted by the crowd, then things start working at the same pace. So that is not a big issue.

items.statement: No decision on debt or equity for expansion; may use reserves.
items.quote: That has not been actually decided now till date because it will be a combination of debt and equity maybe. And the company is growing or out of its reserve profits also, it can grow.

items.statement: Inventory value around INR260 crores.
items.quote: Value-wise, we are having around some inventory of some INR260 crores.

items.statement: Debt to equity is 0.11.
items.quote: The current debt to equity is 0.11.

items.statement: Targeting over 15% organic growth in BSS segment for FY26
items.quote: We expect to achieve over 15% organic growth in the BSS segment for FY '26, which will further improve our margins.

items.statement: Aspiration to grow IFM segment revenue at 3x nominal GDP growth rate
items.quote: Our aspiration is to grow the IFM segment revenue at 3x of ; Nominal GDP growth rate

items.statement: Internal target of 15% IFM growth for FY26, may be higher
items.quote: 15% is what we really think that we can definitely get, and it may be higher.

items.statement: Consolidated margin expansion of 0.2-0.3% YoY from operating leverage plus mix shift benefit
items.quote: you will see margin expansion, as we have explained in the past, given our operational leverage, and that expansion will be between 0.2% to 0.3% year-on-year.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 PAT margin reached 4.7%, highest since listing
items.quote: In Q4 '25, we achieved our highest PAT margin since listing at 4.7%.

items.statement: FY25 consolidated EBITDA margin improved 90 bps to 7.3%
items.quote: EBITDA margin stood at 7.3% versus this year 6.4% in FY '24, an improvement of 90 basis points.
